cards.name: Flat
cards.desc: Solid blocks of color with no shadows, gradients or texture. Clean, modern and easy to read at small sizes.
cards.phrase: flat vector illustration, solid fills, no gradients or shadows

cards.name: 3D isometric
cards.desc: 3D objects drawn at fixed 30° angles with no vanishing point, so parallel edges stay parallel. Feels like a tidy game board or a miniature model.
cards.phrase: 3D isometric illustration, 30° angles, no perspective distortion, soft shading on each face

cards.name: Line art
cards.desc: Drawn only with lines of one consistent thickness, no fills. Light, precise and good for technical subjects.
cards.phrase: monoline line art, consistent 2px stroke, no fills

cards.name: Skeuomorphic
cards.desc: Imitates real materials such as brushed metal, leather or glass, with bevels and shadows, so digital things look like physical objects.
cards.phrase: skeuomorphic style, realistic materials, bevels and highlights like a physical object

cards.name: Neumorphism
cards.desc: Shapes look pressed out of, or into, the same material as the background, using a light shadow on one side and a dark one on the other.
cards.phrase: neumorphic soft UI, elements extruded from the background with soft light and dark shadows

cards.name: Glassmorphism
cards.desc: Translucent panels that blur whatever sits behind them, usually floating over bright color blobs. Feels layered and airy.
cards.phrase: glassmorphism, frosted translucent panels with background blur over soft color blobs

cards.name: Claymorphism
cards.desc: Chunky rounded 3D shapes that look like soft plastic or modelling clay, with gentle inner highlights. Friendly and toy-like.
cards.phrase: soft 3D clay style, rounded puffy shapes, matte material, gentle studio lighting

cards.name: Low-poly
cards.desc: Objects built from a small number of flat triangles, each with its own shade. Reads as crafted and geometric.
cards.phrase: low-poly style, faceted triangles with flat shading

cards.name: Hand-drawn
cards.desc: Slightly wobbly lines that look drawn by hand. Makes technical diagrams feel informal, approachable and "work in progress".
cards.phrase: hand-drawn sketchy style like Excalidraw, wobbly marker lines, casual

cards.name: Pixel art
cards.desc: Images built from a visible grid of square pixels with a tiny palette. Instantly reads as retro gaming.
cards.phrase: 8-bit pixel art, visible square pixels, limited palette

cards.name: Blueprint
cards.desc: Light lines on a deep blue grid with dimension marks, like an engineer's plan. Says "this is how it's built".
cards.phrase: blueprint style, white technical linework on a blue grid, dimension annotations

cards.name: Wireframe
cards.desc: Grey boxes and placeholder lines that show structure only, with no styling. Used to agree on layout before any visual design.
cards.phrase: low-fidelity wireframe, grey boxes and placeholder lines, no styling

cards.name: Front view
cards.desc: Looking straight at the front with no depth at all. Everything is shown at true proportions, like a flat facade.
cards.phrase: straight-on front view, orthographic, no perspective

cards.name: Perspective
cards.desc: Things shrink as they get further away and lines converge on a vanishing point. Feels cinematic and real.
cards.phrase: one-point perspective with a central vanishing point, depth receding into the distance

cards.name: Top-down
cards.desc: Looking straight down from above, like a map or floor plan. Great for showing how parts are arranged in space.
cards.phrase: top-down bird's-eye view, map-like layout

cards.name: Exploded view
cards.desc: The parts of a thing separated along one direction so you can see every layer and how they fit back together. Ideal for "what's inside".
cards.phrase: exploded view, layers separated vertically with dashed guide lines showing how they stack

cards.name: Cutaway
cards.desc: A slice removed from the outside so the inner layers are visible while the rest stays whole.
cards.phrase: cutaway illustration with a wedge removed to reveal the inner layers

cards.name: Elevation
cards.desc: Flat shapes made to float at different heights using shadows. Bigger, softer shadows mean higher up and more important.
cards.phrase: cards at different elevations, soft drop shadows indicating depth

cards.name: Depth of field
cards.desc: The subject is sharp and things behind it are blurred, pulling the eye to one spot. Tilt-shift is the miniature-model version of this.
cards.phrase: shallow depth of field, sharp subject, softly blurred background

cards.name: Monochromatic
cards.desc: Many shades and tints of one hue. Calm, cohesive and hard to get wrong.
cards.phrase: monochromatic palette, shades and tints of a single blue

cards.name: Analogous
cards.desc: Colors that sit next to each other on the color wheel, like teal, green and lime. Natural and pleasant.
cards.phrase: analogous palette of neighboring hues (teal, green, lime)

cards.name: Complementary
cards.desc: Two colors from opposite sides of the wheel, such as blue and orange. Each makes the other pop.
cards.phrase: complementary palette, blue paired with orange accents

cards.name: Pastel
cards.desc: Light, low-intensity colors with lots of white mixed in. Gentle, friendly and youthful.
cards.phrase: soft pastel palette, light and low saturation

cards.name: Muted
cards.desc: Colors with some grey mixed in so nothing shouts. Sophisticated and easy on the eyes for long reading.
cards.phrase: muted desaturated palette, dusty tones, nothing fully saturated

cards.name: High contrast
cards.aka: bold, black and white plus one
cards.desc: Very dark against very light, sometimes with one loud color. Punchy, readable and accessible.
cards.phrase: high-contrast palette, black and white with one bold yellow

cards.name: Neon on dark
cards.desc: Saturated glowing colors on a near-black background. Feels techy, nocturnal and energetic.
cards.phrase: dark background with glowing neon accents in magenta and cyan

cards.name: One accent color
cards.desc: Mostly neutral greys or whites, with a single strong color reserved for the thing that matters. Guides attention precisely.
cards.phrase: mostly neutral palette with a single accent color used only for emphasis

cards.name: Gradient
cards.desc: Colors that blend smoothly into each other. A mesh gradient blends several colors in soft organic patches.
cards.phrase: smooth gradient background blending purple into coral

cards.name: Duotone
cards.desc: An image reduced to just two colors, dark and light. Unifies mixed photos and feels graphic.
cards.phrase: duotone treatment, every image in deep navy and hot pink only

cards.name: Warm vs. cool
cards.desc: Warm colors (reds, oranges) feel close and energetic; cool colors (blues, greens) feel distant and calm. Use them to separate two sides of an idea.
cards.phrase: warm colors for the problem side, cool colors for the solution side

cards.name: Semantic color
cards.desc: Colors that carry a fixed meaning: green for good, amber for warning, red for problems. Keep them separate from the decorative palette.
cards.phrase: semantic status colors: green for success, amber for warning, red for error

cards.name: Hue
cards.desc: Which color it is: red, orange, blue and so on, as a position around the color wheel. Changing hue changes the color itself, not how strong or light it is.
cards.phrase: keep all colors within a narrow hue range around [color]

cards.name: Saturation
cards.desc: How pure or strong a color is, from gray to vivid. Low saturation feels calm and grown-up; high saturation feels loud and energetic.
cards.phrase: low-saturation palette with one fully saturated accent

cards.name: Value
cards.desc: How light or dark a color is, ignoring its hue. Artists say value does the work and color gets the credit: a picture with clear light and dark shapes reads well even in black and white.
cards.phrase: strong value structure: clear separation of lights and darks that reads even in grayscale

cards.name: Tints, tones & shades
cards.desc: A tint is a color mixed with white (lighter, softer). A shade is mixed with black (deeper, richer). A tone is mixed with gray (muted). Asking for "tints of one blue" keeps a palette unified.
cards.phrase: palette built from tints and shades of a single [color]

cards.name: Triadic
cards.desc: Three colors evenly spaced around the wheel, like red, yellow and blue. Playful and balanced; usually one leads and the other two support.
cards.phrase: triadic color scheme of [color], [color] and [color], with one dominant

cards.name: Split-complementary
cards.desc: One main color plus the two colors on either side of its opposite. You get the punch of complementary colors with less clash.
cards.phrase: split-complementary palette: [main color] with the two neighbors of its complement as accents

cards.name: Serif
cards.desc: Letters with small feet on the strokes. Reads as traditional, literary and trustworthy.
cards.phrase: elegant serif typeface for headings

cards.name: Sans-serif
cards.desc: Letters without the feet. Clean, neutral and the default for screens and interfaces.
cards.phrase: clean geometric sans-serif typeface

cards.name: Monospace
cards.desc: Every letter takes the same width, like code or a typewriter. Signals technical, precise, developer-ish.
cards.phrase: monospace typeface for labels and data, developer aesthetic

cards.name: Display type
cards.desc: A characterful font made for big sizes only. Gives a page its personality; never use it for paragraphs.
cards.phrase: bold expressive display typeface for the headline only

cards.name: Handwritten
cards.desc: Type that looks written by hand. Warm and personal; best for short notes and annotations.
cards.phrase: handwritten marker-style font for annotations

cards.name: Type scale
cards.desc: A fixed set of sizes that step up in proportion, so headings, subheadings and text always relate cleanly.
cards.phrase: clear type scale with distinct H1, H2 and body sizes

cards.name: Weight contrast
cards.desc: Mixing very heavy and very light weights of the same family. Creates emphasis without changing size or color.
cards.phrase: strong weight contrast, ultra-bold keywords next to light text

cards.name: Letter-spacing
cards.desc: The space between letters. Wide tracking feels airy and premium in caps; tight tracking makes big headlines punchy.
cards.phrase: wide letter-spacing on small uppercase labels, tight tracking on large headlines

cards.name: Eyebrow label
cards.desc: A small uppercase label above a headline that names its category, like "CASE STUDY" or "STEP 2".
cards.phrase: small uppercase eyebrow label above each heading

cards.name: Kerning
cards.desc: Adjusting the space between specific pairs of letters, like "AV" or "To", so a word looks evenly spaced. Matters most in logos and big headlines.
cards.phrase: carefully kerned headline with optically even letter spacing

cards.name: Leading
cards.desc: The space between lines of text. Tight leading suits big headlines; body text needs room (around 1.4 to 1.6 times the size) to be comfortable to read.
cards.phrase: tight leading on headlines, generous 1.5 line height for body text

cards.name: Type pairing
cards.aka: font pairing, heading and body fonts
cards.desc: Choosing two typefaces that work together, usually a characterful one for headings and a plain one for text. Contrast in style, harmony in proportion.
cards.phrase: type pairing: [serif] for headings with [sans-serif] for body text

cards.name: Drop cap
cards.desc: An oversized first letter that drops down into the first few lines of a paragraph. Signals the start of a story; feels literary and editorial.
cards.phrase: editorial layout with a large serif drop cap starting the first paragraph

cards.name: Line length
cards.desc: How wide a column of text is. Around 45 to 75 characters per line is comfortable; much wider and the eye loses its place.
cards.phrase: body text limited to about 65 characters per line

cards.name: Corner radius
cards.desc: How round the corners are. Sharp reads serious, softly rounded reads friendly, fully round "pill" reads playful.
cards.phrase: softly rounded corners on all shapes, pill-shaped buttons

cards.name: Geometric
cards.desc: Built from perfect circles, squares and triangles. Feels precise, modern and constructed.
cards.phrase: geometric shapes only: circles, squares and triangles with crisp edges

cards.name: Organic
cards.desc: Soft irregular curves that feel natural and hand-made. Takes the edge off technical content.
cards.phrase: organic blob shapes and flowing curves, nothing perfectly geometric

cards.name: Stroke weight
cards.desc: How thick the lines are. Hairlines feel delicate and technical; heavy strokes feel bold and graphic.
cards.phrase: consistent medium stroke weight on all lines and icons

cards.name: Grain
cards.desc: A fine speckled texture laid over flat color, like film grain or print. Adds warmth and a tactile, analog feel.
cards.phrase: subtle grain texture over flat colors, risograph print feel

cards.name: Background pattern
cards.desc: A faint repeating pattern of dots or lines behind the content. Signals "workspace" or "canvas".
cards.phrase: faint dot-grid background like a design canvas

cards.name: Solid vs. dashed
cards.desc: Solid lines show what is real or happening now. Dashed lines show what is optional, planned, async or a boundary.
cards.phrase: solid arrows for the main path, dashed arrows for optional or async steps

cards.name: Glow
cards.desc: A soft blurred halo of light around a shape, as if it emits light. Draws attention and adds atmosphere on dark backgrounds.
cards.phrase: soft glow around the key element, like light emission

cards.name: Minimalist
cards.desc: Only what is necessary, lots of space, restrained color and simple type. Calm and confident.
cards.phrase: minimalist: few elements, restrained color, lots of white space

cards.name: Swiss style
cards.desc: Strict grids, big bold sans-serif type set flush left, asymmetric layouts and a few flat colors, often red. Objective and timeless.
cards.phrase: Swiss International style: strict grid, bold flush-left sans-serif, asymmetric layout, red accent

cards.name: Bauhaus
cards.desc: Primary colors (red, yellow, blue) plus black, built from circles, squares and triangles. Bold, playful and architectural.
cards.phrase: Bauhaus style: primary colors, black, bold geometric shapes

cards.name: Brutalist
cards.desc: Deliberately raw: thick black borders, hard offset shadows, clashing flat colors, default-looking fonts. Loud and honest.
cards.phrase: neo-brutalist style: thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat bright colors

cards.name: Editorial
cards.desc: Like a quality magazine: big serif headlines, columns of text, pull quotes, considered photography. Feels authored and thoughtful.
cards.phrase: editorial magazine style: large serif headline, text columns, generous margins

cards.name: Memphis
cards.desc: Loud 1980s pattern style: squiggles, zigzags, confetti dots and triangles in pastels with black. Fun and chaotic.
cards.phrase: Memphis design style: squiggles, zigzags, confetti shapes, pastel colors with black accents

cards.name: Synthwave
cards.desc: 1980s retro-future: neon pink and purple sunsets, a glowing grid running to the horizon, chrome text.
cards.phrase: synthwave retro-futurist style: neon sunset, glowing perspective grid, purple and magenta

cards.name: Terminal
cards.desc: Green or amber monospace text on black, a blinking cursor, maybe scanlines. Signals code, systems and under-the-hood.
cards.phrase: terminal aesthetic: green monospace text on black, blinking cursor

cards.name: Vintage travel poster
cards.aka: WPA poster, National Parks poster, retro screen-print poster
cards.desc: The look of 1930s to 50s travel and parks posters, recently revived: big simple shapes, a handful of flat inks, halftone and grain for shading, and a strong sense of place.
cards.phrase: vintage travel-poster style: limited palette of flat screen-print inks, halftone and grain shading, bold simple silhouettes, warm paper texture

cards.name: Axonometric
cards.desc: The family of 3D views with no vanishing point. Isometric tilts all three axes equally; dimetric and trimetric tilt them unevenly for a more natural or dramatic angle.
cards.phrase: dimetric axonometric view, parallel projection, no vanishing point

cards.name: Three-quarter view
cards.desc: The object turned about 45° and seen slightly from above, so you see the front, one side and the top at once. The classic product-shot angle.
cards.phrase: three-quarter view from slightly above, showing front, side and top

cards.name: Low angle
cards.desc: The camera low on the ground looking up, so things tower over you. Makes a subject feel big, powerful or monumental.
cards.phrase: dramatic low-angle shot looking up at the subject

cards.name: Studio lighting
cards.desc: Soft, even light from big diffuse sources, like a photo studio. Gentle gradients, soft shadows, nothing harsh. The default for clean product and object renders.
cards.phrase: soft studio lighting from a large softbox, gentle gradients and soft shadows

cards.name: Rim light
cards.desc: Light from behind the subject that outlines its edge with a bright glow, separating it from a dark background. Moody and cinematic.
cards.phrase: strong rim lighting from behind, glowing edges against a dark background

cards.name: Contact shadows
cards.desc: The soft darkening where objects touch the floor or each other. Without it, 3D objects look like they are floating or pasted on.
cards.phrase: soft contact shadows and ambient occlusion so objects feel grounded

cards.name: Matte vs. glossy
cards.desc: Matte surfaces scatter light softly; glossy ones show a sharp bright highlight and reflections. One word changes how premium or soft an object feels.
cards.phrase: matte surfaces with no reflections (or: glossy with sharp specular highlights)

cards.name: Glass & translucency
cards.desc: See-through materials that bend and tint what is behind them. Makes an object feel light, precious or high-tech.
cards.phrase: translucent glass material with refraction, background visible and slightly distorted through it

cards.name: Chrome & metal
cards.desc: Mirror-like surfaces that reflect the sky and ground as bright and dark bands. Reads as futuristic, luxurious or Y2K.
cards.phrase: polished chrome material reflecting a bright sky and dark horizon

cards.name: 3D wireframe
cards.desc: A 3D object shown as the grid of lines that forms its surface, with no solid fill. Feels technical, digital and "under the hood".
cards.phrase: 3D wireframe mesh rendering, glowing grid lines, no solid surfaces

cards.name: Voxel art
cards.desc: Scenes built entirely from small identical cubes, like 3D pixels. Playful, retro and instantly readable.
cards.phrase: voxel art, scene built from small uniform cubes

cards.name: Diorama
cards.aka: isometric room, miniature scene, cutaway room
cards.desc: A small self-contained 3D scene, often a room with two walls removed, like a doll's house or museum model. Great for showing a whole system in one tidy box.
cards.phrase: isometric diorama: a miniature room with two walls cut away, objects arranged inside

cards.name: Floating objects
cards.desc: Objects suspended in mid-air with their shadow below them. Feels light, playful and a bit magical; good for hero visuals.
cards.phrase: objects floating in mid-air with soft shadows on the ground beneath

cards.name: Cel-shaded
cards.desc: 3D objects lit with a few hard bands of flat color and a dark outline, so they look hand-drawn or cartoon-like.
cards.phrase: cel-shaded toon rendering, hard-edged shadow bands and bold outlines

cards.name: Extruded type
cards.desc: Flat letters or shapes pushed out into thick 3D blocks. Bold, chunky and attention-grabbing.
cards.phrase: chunky extruded 3D lettering with visible depth

cards.name: Orbit / turntable
cards.desc: The camera circles around an object, or the object spins on a turntable, so you see it from every side. The standard way to show off a 3D model.
cards.phrase: slow 360° turntable rotation around the object

cards.name: Soft 3D render
cards.aka: C4D look, Blender render, global illumination
cards.desc: The polished, softly lit look of modern 3D software: smooth simple shapes, soft bounce light, gentle color gradients and a seamless backdrop.
cards.phrase: clean soft 3D render in the style of Cinema 4D or Blender, global illumination, seamless pastel backdrop

cards.name: Density
cards.desc: How much fits on screen at once. Comfortable layouts have room to breathe; compact ones pack in more rows for power users.
cards.phrase: compact, information-dense layout with tight row height (or: comfortable density with generous row spacing)

cards.name: Affordance
cards.desc: Visual cues that tell people what they can do with something: a button looks pressable, a handle looks draggable, a field looks typeable.
cards.phrase: clear affordances: buttons look pressable, draggable items show grab handles, inputs look editable

cards.name: Progressive disclosure
cards.desc: Show only the basics first and reveal advanced options when someone asks for them. Keeps screens simple without removing power.
cards.phrase: progressive disclosure: show the essential options first, tuck advanced settings behind an expandable section

cards.name: Empty state
cards.desc: What a screen shows before there is any data. A good one explains what will appear here and gives one clear first action.
cards.phrase: friendly empty state: small illustration, one line explaining what goes here, and a single primary button to start

cards.name: Skeleton screen
cards.desc: Grey placeholder shapes in the layout of the content that is about to load. Feels faster than a spinner because the page already has its shape.
cards.phrase: skeleton loading state: grey placeholder blocks shaped like the content, with a gentle shimmer

cards.name: Modal dialog
cards.desc: A box that appears over a dimmed page and must be dealt with before going back. Use for focused decisions or short forms.
cards.phrase: centered modal dialog over a dimmed backdrop, with a title, short message and two buttons

cards.name: Drawer
cards.desc: A panel that slides in from the edge of the screen for details or settings, while the page stays visible behind it.
cards.phrase: slide-over drawer from the right edge showing details, page dimmed behind it

cards.name: Toast
cards.desc: A small message that pops up briefly to confirm something happened, then disappears on its own.
cards.phrase: brief toast notification at the bottom of the screen confirming the action, auto-dismisses

cards.name: Tabs
cards.desc: A row of labels that switch between views of the same thing without leaving the page. The selected one is clearly marked.
cards.phrase: tab bar across the top of the panel with an underline on the active tab

cards.name: Breadcrumbs
cards.desc: A trail of links showing where you are in a hierarchy and how to step back up.
cards.phrase: breadcrumb trail above the page title showing the path back up the hierarchy

cards.name: Command palette
cards.desc: A search box that pops up on a keyboard shortcut and lets you run any command by typing its name. Loved by power users.
cards.phrase: command palette opened with ⌘K: search input on top, filtered list of commands with one highlighted

cards.name: Button hierarchy
cards.desc: Giving actions different visual weights so the main one is obvious: one filled primary button, outlined secondary ones, plain text links for minor actions.
cards.phrase: clear button hierarchy: one filled primary action, an outlined secondary, a text-link tertiary

cards.name: Interaction states
cards.desc: How a control looks in each situation: resting, hovered, focused by keyboard, pressed and disabled. Missing states make an app feel broken.
cards.phrase: design every interaction state: default, hover, focus ring, pressed and disabled

cards.name: Inline validation
cards.desc: Checking a form field as you go and showing the problem right next to it, in plain words, instead of a list of errors at the end.
cards.phrase: inline form validation: error message directly under the field in red, success check when valid

cards.name: Tooltip
cards.desc: A small label that appears when you hover or focus something, explaining what it does. A popover is the bigger, clickable version.
cards.phrase: small dark tooltip with an arrow appearing above the icon on hover

cards.name: Responsive layout
cards.desc: One design that rearranges itself for different screen sizes: several columns on desktop, fewer on tablet, one on a phone.
cards.phrase: responsive layout: three columns on desktop, two on tablet, a single stacked column on mobile

cards.name: Grid layout
cards.desc: Invisible columns that every element snaps to, so edges line up across the page. The backbone of most tidy designs.
cards.phrase: strict 12-column grid, elements aligned to column edges

cards.name: Bento grid
cards.desc: Tiles of different sizes packed into a neat rectangle, like compartments in a bento lunch box. Each tile shows one feature.
cards.phrase: bento grid layout, rounded tiles of varied sizes packed into a tidy rectangle

cards.name: Card layout
cards.desc: Repeated self-contained boxes, each with an image, title and text. Easy to scan and compare.
cards.phrase: card layout, equal cards in a row each with image, title and short text

cards.name: Hero section
cards.desc: A large opening block with a big headline, short line of text and one main button. The first thing anyone sees.
cards.phrase: bold hero section: large headline, one-line subhead and a single call-to-action button

cards.name: Split screen
cards.desc: The canvas divided into two halves, often image on one side and words on the other. Good for comparisons or pairing a visual with text.
cards.phrase: split-screen layout, image on the left half and text on the right half

cards.name: Masonry
cards.desc: Columns of items with uneven heights packed tightly, like bricks. Good for galleries of mixed shapes.
cards.phrase: masonry layout, columns of uneven-height tiles packed tightly

cards.name: Negative space
cards.desc: Deliberately empty space around things. Makes a design feel calm, premium and focused on what remains.
cards.phrase: generous negative space, few elements, lots of breathing room

cards.name: Visual hierarchy
cards.desc: Using size, weight and color so the most important thing is seen first, then the next. Answers "where does the eye go?"
cards.phrase: strong visual hierarchy: one dominant headline, a clear secondary level, quiet body text

cards.name: Rule of thirds
cards.desc: The frame split into a 3×3 grid, with the subject placed on a line or crossing point instead of dead center. Feels more dynamic.
cards.phrase: rule-of-thirds composition, subject placed off-center on a third line

cards.name: Asymmetric balance
cards.desc: One heavy element on one side balanced by several lighter ones on the other, without mirroring. Feels modern and intentional.
cards.phrase: asymmetric but balanced composition, large element offset by smaller ones

cards.name: Sidebar + content
cards.desc: A fixed navigation column on the left and a main work area that scrolls. Standard for apps and tools.
cards.phrase: app layout with a left sidebar for navigation and a main content area of panels

cards.name: Leading lines
cards.desc: A line in the picture, like a road, river, fence or reflection, that carries the eye from the edge of the frame to the subject.
cards.phrase: use leading lines: a road or reflection runs from the bottom of the frame straight to the subject

cards.name: Easing
cards.desc: How speed changes during a movement. Linear feels robotic; ease-in-out speeds up then slows down, like real objects.
cards.phrase: smooth ease-in-out transitions, nothing linear

cards.name: Spring
cards.desc: Motion that overshoots its target slightly and settles back, like a spring. Feels lively and physical.
cards.phrase: springy motion with a slight overshoot and settle

cards.name: Stagger
cards.desc: Items animate one after another with a short delay instead of all at once. Shows order and feels choreographed.
cards.phrase: staggered entrance, items appear one after another with a short delay

cards.name: Fade and slide
cards.desc: Something fades in while moving a short distance into place. The quiet default for new content arriving.
cards.phrase: elements fade in while sliding up a few pixels

cards.name: Morph
cards.desc: One shape smoothly turns into another. Shows that two states are the same thing, changed.
cards.phrase: shape morphs smoothly from one form into the next

cards.name: Pulse
cards.desc: A ring that expands and fades on repeat. Says "this is live" or "look here".
cards.phrase: subtle pulsing ring to show the element is live

cards.name: Flowing dashes
cards.desc: Dashed lines that move along a path, showing direction of travel. Great for data moving between boxes.
cards.phrase: animated dashed connectors showing data flowing along each arrow

cards.name: Parallax
cards.desc: Layers move at different speeds, near ones faster than far ones, giving a sense of depth.
cards.phrase: parallax effect, foreground layers move faster than background layers

cards.name: Build-up
cards.desc: A diagram appears piece by piece, in the order you would explain it out loud. Each step adds one idea.
cards.phrase: diagram builds up step by step, one component at a time in explanation order

cards.name: Micro-interaction
cards.desc: A tiny response to an action: a button squishes when pressed, then shows a check. Confirms that something happened.
cards.phrase: small micro-interactions on buttons: press feedback and a success state

cards.name: Proximity
cards.desc: Things placed close together are seen as a group. The single most useful rule for organizing a screen: spacing is grouping.
cards.phrase: use proximity to group related items: tight spacing within groups, larger gaps between groups

cards.name: Similarity
cards.desc: Things that look alike, by color, shape or size, are seen as belonging together, even when they are spread out.
cards.phrase: use similarity: items with the same role share the same color and shape

cards.name: Common region
cards.desc: Items inside the same boundary, like a box, card or tinted background, are seen as a group, even if they look different.
cards.phrase: use common region: wrap related controls in a subtle tinted container

cards.name: Continuity
cards.desc: The eye follows smooth lines and curves, so elements arranged along a path are read in order and as connected.
cards.phrase: use continuity: arrange steps along one smooth path so the eye follows them in order

cards.name: Closure
cards.desc: The brain fills in gaps to see a complete shape, so you can suggest a form without drawing all of it. Great for minimal logos.
cards.phrase: use closure: suggest the shape with partial outlines and let negative space complete it

cards.name: Figure and ground
cards.desc: We split every image into a subject (figure) and what is behind it (ground). Clever designs make the background itself form a shape.
cards.phrase: play with figure and ground: let the negative space form a second shape

cards.name: Contrast
cards.desc: A difference in size, color, weight or shape makes one thing stand out. Without contrast nothing leads; with too much, everything shouts.
cards.phrase: use contrast to make one element clearly dominant; keep everything else quiet

cards.name: Alignment
cards.desc: Lining elements up on shared edges creates invisible lines that make a design feel ordered and intentional.
cards.phrase: strict alignment: elements share left edges and baselines on a consistent grid

cards.name: Repetition
cards.desc: Reusing the same colors, shapes, spacing and styles across a design ties it together and makes it learnable.
cards.phrase: consistent visual system: repeat the same card style, spacing and accent across every section

cards.name: Rhythm
cards.desc: A pattern of repeated elements and intervals that the eye moves through, like a beat. Regular rhythm feels calm; progressive rhythm feels like movement.
cards.phrase: create a steady visual rhythm with evenly repeated elements and consistent intervals

cards.name: Symmetry
cards.desc: Mirroring a composition across a center line. Feels stable, formal and calm; asymmetry feels more dynamic.
cards.phrase: symmetrical composition mirrored around a central vertical axis

cards.name: Visual weight
cards.desc: Some elements pull the eye more than others: bigger, darker, more saturated or more detailed things are "heavier". Balance them like a seesaw.
cards.phrase: balance visual weight: offset the heavy dark element with several lighter ones on the other side

cards.name: Scale contrast
cards.aka: tiny figure, sense of scale, the small subject
cards.desc: Something very small set against something enormous. The size gap is the story: awe, loneliness, ambition or danger, depending on the mood.
cards.phrase: extreme scale contrast: a tiny subject dwarfed by an enormous shape that fills the frame

cards.name: Visual metaphor
cards.desc: The picture stands for an idea it never says out loud. A door in an empty field means a new start; sailing into the sun means leaving for good.
cards.phrase: built around one clear visual metaphor for [idea], shown without any text

cards.name: Visual noise
cards.desc: Too many elements competing for attention with no clear order. The fix is fewer things, clearer hierarchy and more space.
cards.phrase: reduce visual noise: remove non-essential elements, establish one clear hierarchy, add whitespace

cards.name: Tight spacing
cards.desc: Not enough padding inside containers or space between elements, so everything touches. Usually fixed by roughly doubling the spacing.
cards.phrase: increase spacing: generous padding inside containers and consistent gaps between elements

cards.name: Weak grouping
cards.aka: "it feels disconnected", "floaty", "I can't tell what goes with what"
cards.desc: Related items are spaced the same as unrelated ones, so nothing reads as a group. Fix it with proximity: tight within groups, wide between them.
cards.phrase: fix grouping: keep each label close to its value and add larger gaps between groups

cards.name: Misalignment
cards.desc: Edges that almost but don't quite line up. The eye notices even a few pixels. Snap everything to shared edges.
cards.phrase: fix alignment: snap all elements to a shared left edge and consistent grid

cards.name: Color overload
cards.desc: Too many saturated colors fighting each other. Pull back to neutrals and keep one or two accents for meaning.
cards.phrase: calm the palette: mostly neutrals with a single accent color reserved for emphasis

cards.name: No focal point
cards.aka: "it feels flat", "boring", "I don't know where to look"
cards.desc: Everything has the same size and weight, so nothing leads the eye. Make one thing clearly the most important.
cards.phrase: create a focal point: make the key element significantly larger or more colorful than the rest

cards.name: Poor legibility
cards.desc: Usually low contrast between text and background, text that is too small, or lines that run too long. Aim for dark text, real size and about 65 characters per line.
cards.phrase: improve legibility: higher text contrast, larger body size, line length around 65 characters, more line spacing

cards.name: Inconsistency
cards.desc: Mixed corner radii, icon styles, font sizes and colors that don't follow one system. Consistency is what reads as polish.
cards.phrase: make it consistent: one corner radius, one icon style, a fixed type scale and spacing system

cards.name: Heavy visual weight
cards.desc: Thick borders, dark fills and big shadows everywhere. Lighten borders, use tints instead of solid fills and let backgrounds breathe.
cards.phrase: lighten the visual weight: thin subtle borders, light tinted fills, fewer heavy shadows

cards.name: Dated styling
cards.desc: Trends from a past era: glossy buttons, heavy bevels, embossed text, busy gradients, stock clip-art. Flatter surfaces and calmer type read as current.
cards.phrase: modernize the styling: flat surfaces, subtle shadows, no gloss or bevels, contemporary sans-serif type

cards.name: No point of view
cards.desc: The default layout and safe choices any template would make. Fix it by committing to one distinctive decision: a typeface, a color, an unusual layout.
cards.phrase: give it a point of view: one distinctive typeface and color, an asymmetric layout, avoid template defaults

cards.name: Over-decoration
cards.desc: Gradients, shadows, borders, icons and effects stacked on things that don't need them. Remove decoration until something breaks, then add one back.
cards.phrase: strip back decoration: remove gradients, extra borders and effects that don't carry meaning

cards.name: Lopsided balance
cards.aka: "it feels unbalanced", "tipping over", "empty on one side"
cards.desc: All the weight sits in one corner and the rest is empty by accident rather than on purpose. Redistribute elements or make the emptiness intentional.
cards.phrase: rebalance the composition: distribute visual weight across the frame

cards.name: Flowchart
cards.desc: Boxes for steps and diamonds for decisions, joined by arrows. Answers "what happens next, and when does it branch?"
cards.phrase: flowchart with step boxes, decision diamonds and labelled yes/no branches

cards.name: Sequence diagram
cards.desc: Actors as columns with time running downward, and arrows for each message between them. Answers "who talks to whom, in what order?"
cards.phrase: sequence diagram with lifelines for each actor and numbered messages flowing downward

cards.name: Pipeline
cards.aka: data flow, process flow, assembly line
cards.desc: Stages in a row with arrows between them, where each stage transforms what it receives. Answers "what does the input become?"
cards.phrase: left-to-right pipeline diagram, each stage a box transforming the data, arrows between stages

cards.name: Layer stack
cards.desc: Horizontal bands stacked on top of each other, where each layer is built on the one below. Answers "what sits on top of what?"
cards.phrase: layer stack diagram, horizontal bands from foundation at the bottom to user-facing at the top

cards.name: Hub and spoke
cards.desc: One central idea with related pieces arranged around it. Answers "what connects to this one thing?"
cards.phrase: hub-and-spoke diagram with a central node and satellites around it

cards.name: Tree
cards.desc: A root that branches into children and grandchildren. Answers "how does this break down into parts?"
cards.phrase: top-down tree diagram showing parent-child hierarchy

cards.name: Network graph
cards.desc: Dots for things and lines for relationships, with no fixed hierarchy. Answers "how is everything connected?"
cards.phrase: network graph of nodes and connecting edges, key nodes larger and highlighted

cards.name: Swimlane
cards.desc: A flowchart split into horizontal lanes, one per person or system, so you see who does each step.
cards.phrase: swimlane diagram with one lane per actor, steps hopping between lanes

cards.name: Timeline
cards.desc: Events placed along a line in date order. Answers "what happened when, and how did we get here?"
cards.phrase: horizontal timeline with dated milestones, labels alternating above and below

cards.name: Venn diagram
cards.desc: Overlapping circles where the overlap shows what two or three ideas share.
cards.phrase: Venn diagram of overlapping translucent circles, shared area labelled

cards.name: 2×2 matrix
cards.desc: Two axes split the space into four boxes so items can be sorted by two qualities at once.
cards.phrase: 2x2 quadrant matrix with labelled axes and items plotted in each quadrant

cards.name: Funnel
cards.desc: Wide at the top, narrow at the bottom, showing how much survives each stage.
cards.phrase: funnel diagram with stages narrowing from top to bottom

cards.name: Annotated callouts
cards.desc: Short labels connected to parts of a picture by thin lines. Turns any illustration into an explanation.
cards.phrase: annotated callouts, short labels connected to parts by thin leader lines with dots

cards.name: Zoom inset
cards.desc: A big picture with one small area enlarged in a bubble beside it. Shows the forest and a tree at once.
cards.phrase: zoom inset: a small highlighted region magnified in a circle beside the main image

cards.name: Before / after
cards.desc: Two panels next to each other showing a state before and after a change. The difference is the message.
cards.phrase: side-by-side before/after comparison, same framing in both panels

cards.name: Small multiples
cards.desc: The same small chart repeated for each case, with identical axes, so differences jump out.
cards.phrase: small multiples: a grid of identical mini charts sharing the same axes

cards.name: Cycle
cards.desc: Steps arranged in a circle with arrows that come back to the start. Answers "what repeats?"
cards.phrase: cycle diagram with steps around a circle and curved arrows looping back

cards.name: Sankey
cards.desc: Bands that split and merge, where each band's thickness shows how much flows that way.
cards.phrase: Sankey diagram, band widths proportional to the amount flowing between stages

cards.name: Heatmap
cards.desc: A grid where color strength shows how much of something is in each cell. Good for patterns across two dimensions.
cards.phrase: heatmap grid, single hue from pale to saturated showing intensity

cards.name: Bar chart
cards.desc: Bars whose length shows an amount. The clearest way to compare categories; highlight one bar to make the point.
cards.phrase: clean bar chart, one highlighted bar, others in muted gray, direct value labels

cards.name: Line chart
cards.desc: Points over time joined by a line. Best for trends, growth and change; a soft fill under the line makes it an area chart.
cards.phrase: line chart of [metric] over time, soft area fill under the line, end point labeled

cards.name: Scatter plot
cards.desc: One dot per item, placed by two values. Shows whether two things move together, plus clusters and outliers.
cards.phrase: scatter plot with a faint trend line and outliers highlighted

cards.name: Sparkline & KPI
cards.desc: One big number with a tiny inline chart and a change indicator. The workhorse of dashboards: the headline first, the trend at a glance.
cards.phrase: KPI stat cards: big number, small label, green or red delta and an inline sparkline

cards.name: Donut chart
cards.desc: A ring split into slices of a whole. Fine for two or three parts; past that, a bar chart reads better.
cards.phrase: donut chart with three segments and the total in the center

cards.name: Stacked area
cards.desc: Several area charts stacked on top of each other, showing both the total over time and how the parts change inside it.
cards.phrase: stacked area chart of [parts] over time, soft distinct colors, total on top

cards.name: Treemap
cards.desc: Rectangles sized by value, nested by category. Shows what takes up the most space in a hierarchy at a glance.
cards.phrase: treemap of [items] sized by value, grouped by category with subtle borders

cards.name: Outline icons
cards.desc: Icons drawn with a single stroke weight and no fill. Light and modern; the default in most current apps.
cards.phrase: outline icons with a consistent 1.5px stroke and rounded joins

cards.name: Filled icons
cards.desc: Solid silhouette icons. Bolder and easier to spot at small sizes; often used for the selected state of an outline set.
cards.phrase: solid filled glyph icons, simple silhouettes

cards.name: Duotone icons
cards.desc: Icons in two shades of one color: a light base shape with darker details. Friendly and a bit richer than plain line icons.
cards.phrase: duotone icons: light tint fill with darker accent details in the same hue

cards.name: Line and offset fill
cards.aka: misregistered fill, line with color pop
cards.desc: An outline drawing with a flat color shape shifted slightly off it, like an imperfect print. Playful and hand-made feeling.
cards.phrase: line icons with an offset flat color fill shifted slightly behind the outline

cards.name: 3D icons
cards.desc: Small rendered 3D objects used as icons, with soft lighting and highlights. Eye-catching for landing pages; too heavy for dense UI.
cards.phrase: soft 3D rendered icons with glossy highlights and gentle shadows

cards.name: Sticker style
cards.desc: Illustrations with a thick white border and a small shadow, as if cut out and stuck on. Casual and fun.
cards.phrase: sticker-style illustrations with a thick white die-cut border and a soft drop shadow, slightly rotated

cards.name: Pictogram
cards.desc: Highly simplified symbols of people and objects meant to be understood instantly by anyone, in any language.
cards.phrase: pictogram style: ultra-simplified geometric figures, white on a solid colored square, like airport signage

cards.name: Spot illustration
cards.desc: A small illustration placed next to text to add warmth or explain an idea, without a full background or frame.
cards.phrase: small spot illustrations beside the text, no background frame, simple shapes in the brand palette

cards.name: Corporate Memphis
cards.desc: Flat cartoon people with tiny heads, long bendy limbs and unrealistic skin colors. Hugely popular in the late 2010s, now often seen as generic.
cards.phrase: Corporate Memphis style: flat people with small heads, exaggerated long limbs, non-realistic skin colors, blob shapes

cards.name: Mascot
cards.desc: A recurring friendly character that represents a product. Gives personality to empty states, errors and onboarding.
cards.phrase: friendly brand mascot character: simple rounded shape, big expressive eyes, used in empty and error states

cards.name: Watercolor
cards.desc: Transparent paint thinned with water, so colors bleed, pool and layer over each other.
cards.phrase: loose watercolor illustration, soft bleeding edges, transparent layered washes on textured paper

cards.name: Crosshatching
cards.desc: Shading with sets of parallel lines. More layers crossing each other means darker.
cards.phrase: pen-and-ink crosshatching, shading built from layered parallel lines

cards.name: Linocut
cards.desc: An image carved into a block, inked and pressed onto paper. Whatever was cut away stays white.
cards.phrase: linocut print style, bold black and white, visible carving marks and rough edges

cards.name: Halftone
cards.desc: Shading made from a grid of dots that get bigger in the dark areas and smaller in the light. How newspapers print photos.
cards.phrase: halftone dot shading, regular dot grid varying in size to create tone

cards.name: Screen print
cards.desc: Prints made one flat ink color at a time. The layers rarely line up perfectly, and that slight offset is part of the charm.
cards.phrase: risograph screen-print style, two or three flat inks, overlapping colors, slight misregistration and grain

cards.name: Collage
cards.desc: An image assembled from scraps of paper, photos and print, glued together.
cards.phrase: paper collage style, torn edges, mixed textures and cut-out shapes layered at angles

cards.name: Layered paper
cards.desc: Shapes cut from colored card and stacked in layers, each casting a small shadow on the one behind.
cards.phrase: layered paper-cut illustration, stacked cut-out layers with soft shadows between them

cards.name: Stippling
cards.desc: Shading made from many tiny hand-placed dots, packed tightly in shadows and sparse in light.
cards.phrase: stippling dotwork illustration, shading built from dense tiny dots

cards.name: Spot color separation
cards.aka: ink layers, color separations, flat inks
cards.desc: The image is split into a few solid inks, each printed as its own layer. Naming the exact inks, and what each one is used for, gives you tight control over the palette.
cards.phrase: flat color separation in [N] spot inks: [ink] for [use], [ink] for [use]; no blended gradients

cards.name: Lost and found edges
cards.aka: dissolving edges, soft vs hard edges
cards.desc: Some edges are crisp ("found") and others melt into what is behind them ("lost"). It makes light feel bright and lets a subject sink into its surroundings.
cards.phrase: lost and found edges: the subject's outline is crisp at the bottom and dissolves into the light at the top

cards.name: Misregistration
cards.desc: When the ink layers of a print don't line up exactly, leaving slivers of paper and color peeking out at the edges. A small amount reads as handmade and authentic.
cards.phrase: slight misregistration between ink layers, thin slivers of paper showing at the edges

cards.name: Overprint
cards.desc: Printing one ink on top of another so they mix where they overlap, making a third color for free. Designers plan these overlaps on purpose.
cards.phrase: overprinted transparent inks that mix into new colors where shapes overlap

cards.name: Wordmark
cards.desc: A logo that is just the name, set in distinctive type. Works when the name is short and memorable.
cards.phrase: wordmark logo: the name "[name]" in a custom [geometric / serif / rounded] typeface, no symbol

cards.name: Lettermark
cards.desc: A logo made from the initials of a long name. Compact and strong, but says little on its own until people know the brand.
cards.phrase: lettermark logo using the initials "[ABC]", bold and compact

cards.name: Monogram
cards.desc: Two or three letters woven together into one shape. Feels crafted, heritage and premium.
cards.phrase: interlocking monogram of the letters [A] and [B], elegant and symmetrical

cards.name: Pictorial mark
cards.desc: A simple picture of a real thing standing for the brand. Strong once known, and works at tiny sizes like app icons.
cards.phrase: pictorial logo mark: a simplified [object] symbol, works at 16px

cards.name: Abstract mark
cards.desc: A shape that represents nothing literal but carries a feeling: motion, connection, balance. Very ownable, but needs time to earn meaning.
cards.phrase: abstract geometric logo mark suggesting [idea], simple enough to draw from memory

cards.name: Emblem
cards.desc: Text and symbol locked together inside a shape, like a badge or crest. Feels official, traditional or outdoorsy; hard to shrink.
cards.phrase: emblem logo: badge shape with "[name]" around the edge and a [symbol] in the center

cards.name: Combination mark
cards.desc: A symbol and a wordmark used together, side by side or stacked. The most common logo type, because each half can also stand alone.
cards.phrase: combination mark: a simple [symbol] next to the wordmark "[name]", horizontal lockup

cards.name: Brand identity system
cards.aka: brand kit, style guide, brand guidelines
cards.desc: Everything that makes a brand recognizable beyond the logo: colors, typefaces, patterns, photo style and rules for using them. Asking for a "system" gets you consistency across many pieces.
cards.phrase: a brand identity system for [name]: logo, primary and secondary colors, type pairing, a graphic pattern and example applications

cards.name: Canvas
cards.desc: The woven cloth paintings are made on. A faint crisscross grid of threads shows through the paint, especially in thin areas.
cards.phrase: visible canvas weave texture showing through the paint

cards.name: Paper grain
cards.desc: The bumpy surface of good art paper. Light catches the little hills and pigment settles in the valleys.
cards.phrase: textured cold-press paper surface, visible paper tooth under the color

cards.name: Kraft paper
cards.desc: Unbleached brown paper with visible fibers. Feels handmade, eco and packaging-like.
cards.phrase: printed on brown kraft paper with visible fibers and flecks

cards.name: Grain shading
cards.aka: stipple shading, spray grit, noise shading
cards.desc: Shading made from a scatter of fine specks instead of a smooth blend. Popular in modern retro illustration; it reads as printed or hand-made rather than digital.
cards.phrase: flat shapes shaded with fine grainy stipple texture instead of smooth gradients

cards.name: Halftone gradient
cards.desc: A color fading into another through a field of dots that shrink as they go. The signature texture of printed posters and comics.
cards.phrase: halftone dot gradients for shading, dots shrinking toward the light, flat screen-print inks

cards.name: Distressed print
cards.desc: Ink that looks faded, scuffed and broken up, as if the poster has been in the sun for years. Adds age and authenticity.
cards.phrase: distressed vintage print texture, worn and speckled ink, slightly faded

cards.name: Linen & fabric
cards.desc: A fine soft woven texture, finer and more irregular than canvas. Feels warm, domestic and tactile.
cards.phrase: soft linen fabric texture as the background

cards.name: Concrete & plaster
cards.desc: A mottled grey mineral surface with tiny pits. Feels solid, industrial and architectural.
cards.phrase: raw concrete texture, mottled grey with small pits

cards.name: Wood grain
cards.desc: Long flowing lines and rings from a tree's growth. Warm, natural and crafted.
cards.phrase: warm natural wood grain texture

cards.name: Crumpled paper
cards.desc: Paper that has been scrunched and flattened, leaving soft folds and creases. Feels informal, lived-in or nostalgic.
cards.phrase: crumpled paper texture with soft creases and folds

cards.name: Brushed metal
cards.desc: Metal with fine parallel scratch lines from polishing, plus a soft band of reflected light.
cards.phrase: brushed aluminum texture with fine horizontal streaks and a soft sheen

cards.name: Grainy gradient
cards.desc: A soft color gradient with a layer of fine noise on top, which stops it looking plasticky and adds a print-like softness.
cards.phrase: soft grainy gradient background with visible fine noise

cards.name: Uncoated paper
cards.aka: matte stock, toothy paper, ink soak
cards.desc: Paper without a glossy coating. Ink sinks in, so colors are softer and slightly muted, edges are a touch fuzzy, and the paper fibers show. The opposite of a shiny magazine page.
cards.phrase: printed on uncoated matte paper: inks soaked in and slightly muted, soft edges, visible paper tooth

cards.name: Oil paint
cards.desc: Slow-drying paint that can be blended smoothly or laid on thick so the brushstrokes stand up off the canvas (impasto).
cards.phrase: oil painting with thick impasto brushstrokes catching the light

cards.name: Gouache
cards.desc: Water-based paint that dries flat, matte and opaque. Gives clean blocks of color with soft, slightly dry edges.
cards.phrase: gouache painting: flat matte opaque color shapes with soft brushy edges

cards.name: Pastel & chalk
cards.desc: Sticks of pure pigment rubbed onto textured paper. Colors are soft and powdery and break up over the paper's grain.
cards.phrase: soft pastel drawing on dark paper, grainy powdery strokes

cards.name: Charcoal
cards.desc: Burnt wood sticks that make rich, smudgy blacks. Great for quick expressive drawings with dramatic dark tones.
cards.phrase: expressive charcoal drawing, smudged soft shading and bold dark lines

cards.name: Colored pencil
cards.desc: Layers of light, directional strokes that build color slowly. Gentle, detailed and a little nostalgic.
cards.phrase: colored pencil illustration, visible directional strokes and paper texture

cards.name: Marker
cards.desc: Felt-tip markers lay down bold see-through color. Where strokes overlap the color gets darker, leaving visible streaks.
cards.phrase: marker rendering: bold translucent strokes with darker overlaps, over a black ink line drawing

cards.name: Airbrush
cards.desc: Paint sprayed as a fine mist, giving ultra-smooth gradients and soft glowing edges. Very 1970s and 80s.
cards.phrase: 1980s airbrush illustration: ultra-smooth gradients, soft glowing edges, fine spray speckle

cards.name: Ink wash
cards.desc: East Asian brush painting in black ink diluted to many greys. A few confident strokes suggest a whole landscape.
cards.phrase: sumi-e ink wash painting: grey washes, expressive black brushstrokes, generous empty space

cards.name: Spray paint
cards.desc: Paint from an aerosol can: bold fills, soft overspray halos and the occasional drip. Loud, urban and rebellious.
cards.phrase: spray-painted graffiti style: bold outlined lettering, soft overspray, paint drips on a concrete wall

cards.name: Digital painting
cards.desc: Painting done on a tablet with software brushes. Can mimic any medium; its own look is smooth blends, soft brushes and bright, glowing light.
cards.phrase: painterly digital concept art: soft brushes, smooth blends, glowing atmospheric light

cards.name: Impressionism
cards.desc: Painting the feeling of a moment of light rather than precise detail. Late 1800s France.
cards.phrase: impressionist painting style, short visible brushstrokes, soft dappled light, no hard outlines

cards.name: Pointillism
cards.desc: Pictures made entirely of small dots of pure color that blend into shapes when you step back.
cards.phrase: pointillism, image built from small dots of pure color

cards.name: Ukiyo-e
cards.desc: Japanese woodblock prints from the 1600s to 1800s showing landscapes, waves, actors and city life.
cards.phrase: ukiyo-e woodblock print style, flat color areas, bold outlines, stylized waves, indigo and cream

cards.name: Art Nouveau
cards.desc: Around 1890 to 1910. Decorative art inspired by plants and flowing natural forms, used on posters, metro stations and furniture.
cards.phrase: Art Nouveau style, flowing whiplash curves, floral ornament, arched decorative frame, muted olive and gold

cards.name: Cubism
cards.desc: Early 1900s. Objects broken into geometric facets and shown from several angles at once.
cards.phrase: cubist style, subject fractured into overlapping geometric planes seen from multiple angles, muted earthy palette

cards.name: De Stijl
cards.desc: Dutch movement from 1917. Reduced everything to straight lines, right angles and primary colors.
cards.phrase: De Stijl / Mondrian composition: black grid lines, white fields, primary red, yellow and blue blocks

cards.name: Constructivism
cards.desc: Soviet art and design from the 1920s. Art as a tool for a new society, full of energy and propaganda.
cards.phrase: Russian constructivist poster style: dynamic diagonals, red and black on cream, bold geometric type

cards.name: Art Deco
cards.desc: 1920s and 30s glamour. Machine-age geometry mixed with luxury: think grand hotels, ocean liners and cinema lobbies.
cards.phrase: Art Deco style: symmetrical geometric fans and sunbursts, stepped forms, thin gold linework on deep navy

cards.name: Surrealism
cards.desc: From the 1920s. Realistic painting of impossible, dream-like scenes, meant to tap the unconscious.
cards.phrase: surrealist scene: realistic rendering of a dreamlike impossible situation, empty landscape, long shadows

cards.name: Abstract Expressionism
cards.desc: Post-war New York painting where the act of painting itself is the subject. Big, raw and emotional.
cards.phrase: abstract expressionist style, energetic drips, splatters and gestural brushstrokes, no literal subject

cards.name: Pop Art
cards.desc: 1950s and 60s art that borrowed from comics, ads and packaging. Turns everyday commercial imagery into art.
cards.phrase: pop art comic style: Ben-Day dots, thick black outlines, flat primary colors, speech bubble

cards.name: Op Art
cards.desc: 1960s art that uses precise patterns to trick the eye into seeing movement, depth or vibration.
cards.phrase: op art optical illusion pattern, high-contrast black and white shapes that appear to move

cards.name: Classical
cards.desc: Based on ancient Greek and Roman temples, revived again and again for banks, courts and museums.
cards.phrase: neoclassical architecture: symmetrical facade, rows of columns, triangular pediment, pale stone

cards.name: Gothic
cards.desc: European cathedrals from the 1100s to 1500s, built to soar upward and flood the inside with colored light.
cards.phrase: Gothic architecture: pointed arches, tall spires, rose window, vertical soaring stone facade

cards.name: Art Deco architecture
cards.desc: The 1920s and 30s skyscraper look: luxurious, geometric and vertical, built in steps as the tower rises.
cards.phrase: Art Deco skyscraper: stepped setbacks, sunburst crown, strong vertical lines, gold geometric ornament

cards.name: Modernist
cards.desc: Early-to-mid 1900s. Ornament was stripped away, and the shape of a building came from what it does.
cards.phrase: modernist International Style architecture: white flat-roofed box on thin columns, ribbon windows, no ornament

cards.name: Brutalism
cards.desc: 1950s to 70s. Massive buildings in raw, unpainted concrete, honest about their materials and structure. Loved and hated in equal measure.
cards.phrase: brutalist architecture: massive raw concrete blocks, repeated deep-set windows, heavy cantilevered forms

cards.name: Mid-century modern
cards.desc: Postwar homes and furniture from about 1945 to 1970: modern but warm, built to bring the outdoors in.
cards.phrase: mid-century modern style: low horizontal lines, butterfly roof, walls of glass, warm wood and stone, mustard and teal accents

cards.name: Postmodern
cards.desc: 1970s to 90s reaction against plain modernism. Brings back color, humor and classical shapes, used ironically.
cards.phrase: postmodern architecture: playful oversized classical motifs, broken pediment, pastel pink and teal

cards.name: Deconstructivism
cards.desc: From the 1980s. Buildings that look fragmented, tilted or exploded, deliberately breaking the box.
cards.phrase: deconstructivist architecture: fragmented tilted volumes, colliding angles and curved metal surfaces

cards.name: Parametric
cards.desc: Buildings designed with algorithms, so forms can flow and curve in ways hand drawing never could.
cards.phrase: parametric architecture: flowing curved form, repeated ribs that gradually shift, smooth white surfaces

cards.name: Traditional Japanese
cards.desc: Wooden buildings designed around simplicity, natural materials and a close link to the garden.
cards.phrase: traditional Japanese architecture: exposed timber frame, shoji paper screens, deep eaves, natural materials, calm modular grid

cards.name: Establishing shot
cards.desc: A wide view that shows the whole setting, with people small in the frame. Answers "where are we?"
cards.phrase: wide establishing shot showing the whole setting, people small in the frame

cards.name: Medium shot
cards.desc: A person framed from about the waist up. Natural and conversational; the default for interviews and talking heads.
cards.phrase: medium shot framing the subject from the waist up

cards.name: Close-up
cards.desc: The face fills most of the frame. Shows emotion and creates intimacy.
cards.phrase: tight close-up on the face, filling the frame

cards.name: Extreme close-up
cards.desc: One small detail fills the whole frame, like an eye or a texture. Dramatic, tactile and attention-grabbing.
cards.phrase: extreme close-up macro shot of a single detail filling the frame

cards.name: Over-the-shoulder
cards.desc: Framed from behind one person's shoulder looking at another. Puts the viewer inside a conversation.
cards.phrase: over-the-shoulder shot: blurred shoulder in the foreground, the other person in focus facing camera

cards.name: Dutch angle
cards.desc: The camera tilted so the horizon is slanted. Signals unease, tension or something off-balance.
cards.phrase: Dutch angle: camera tilted so the horizon slants, uneasy tension

cards.name: Golden hour
cards.desc: The hour after sunrise or before sunset: low, warm, soft light with long shadows. Flattering, nostalgic and hopeful.
cards.phrase: golden hour lighting: low warm sun, long soft shadows, glowing amber tones

cards.name: Blue hour
cards.desc: The short time after sunset when the sky turns deep blue and city lights come on. Calm, cool and a little melancholy.
cards.phrase: blue hour: deep blue twilight sky, warm city lights just switching on

cards.name: High-key
cards.desc: Bright, even lighting with mostly white and light tones and almost no dark shadows. Feels clean, optimistic and fresh.
cards.phrase: high-key lighting: bright, airy, mostly white tones, minimal shadows

cards.name: Low-key
cards.desc: Mostly dark with a single hard light picking out part of the subject. Moody, mysterious and dramatic.
cards.phrase: low-key chiaroscuro lighting: mostly darkness, one hard side light revealing half the subject

cards.name: Silhouette
cards.desc: A subject shot against a bright light so it becomes a solid dark shape. Strong, graphic and anonymous.
cards.phrase: silhouette: subject as a solid black shape against a bright backlit sky

cards.name: Teal and orange
cards.desc: A common film color grade: shadows and backgrounds pushed toward teal, skin tones toward orange. Instant "Hollywood" look.
cards.phrase: cinematic teal-and-orange color grade, teal shadows, warm orange skin tones

cards.name: Analog film look
cards.desc: The texture of old film photos: grain, slightly faded colors, warm light leaks and soft contrast. Nostalgic and human.
cards.phrase: analog 35mm film look: visible grain, faded warm colors, soft contrast, light leaks

cards.name: Long exposure
cards.desc: The shutter stays open for seconds, so moving lights become smooth streaks and water turns to mist. Shows motion and the passing of time.
cards.phrase: long exposure photograph: smooth light trails streaking through a night scene

cards.name: Flat lay
cards.desc: Objects arranged neatly on a surface and shot straight down from above. Tidy and curated; knolling lines everything up at right angles.
cards.phrase: flat lay photo from directly above, objects neatly arranged on a clean surface

cards.name: Backlit
cards.desc: The light source sits behind the subject, facing the camera. Edges glow, the air looks hazy, and the subject drops toward silhouette. Warm, dreamy and a little nostalgic.
cards.phrase: backlit, contre-jour lighting: the sun directly behind the subject, glowing rim and soft haze

cards.name: Foreground, midground, background
cards.desc: Splitting a scene into a near layer, a middle layer and a far layer. Even flat illustrations feel deep when each layer is clearly separate.
cards.phrase: clear foreground, midground and background layers: [near thing] in front, [subject] in the middle, [scenery] behind

cards.name: Atmospheric perspective
cards.desc: Far-away things look lighter, bluer and lower in contrast because of air and haze. Fading the distant layers is the quickest way to add depth.
cards.phrase: atmospheric perspective: distant layers fade lighter and bluer with lower contrast

cards.name: Frame within a frame
cards.desc: Using something in the scene, like a doorway, window, arch or branches, to put a border around the subject. It focuses attention and adds depth.
cards.phrase: frame-within-a-frame composition: the subject seen through a [doorway, window, arch]

cards.name: Tight crop
cards.desc: Letting the subject run off the edges instead of fitting it neatly inside. Feels bold, close and confident; showing everything feels distant and safe.
cards.phrase: tight crop: the subject fills the frame and bleeds off the edges

cards.name: Aspect ratio
cards.desc: The width-to-height shape of the frame. It changes what fits and how it feels: wide is cinematic, square is calm, tall is phone-native.
cards.phrase: composed for a [16:9 / 4:5 / 9:16] aspect ratio

cards.name: Rule of odds
cards.desc: Groups of three or five look more natural and interesting than pairs or fours, because the eye can't split them into neat halves.
cards.phrase: group the [objects] in threes following the rule of odds

cards.name: Golden ratio
cards.desc: A proportion (about 1 to 1.618) that shows up in nature and classical art. As a composition guide, the subject sits at the tight end of a spiral.
cards.phrase: golden-ratio composition, subject placed at the eye of the spiral

cards.name: Telephoto compression
cards.desc: A long lens shot from far away makes distant things look huge and stacked right behind the subject. It's how photographers get a giant sun or moon behind a tiny figure.
cards.phrase: shot on a long telephoto lens, compressed perspective, enormous sun stacked behind the subject

cards.name: Wide-angle
cards.desc: A short lens that fits a lot in and stretches space: close things look big, far things look tiny, and lines rush toward the center.
cards.phrase: wide-angle lens, exaggerated perspective with lines rushing to the center

cards.name: Fisheye
cards.desc: An extreme wide lens that bends straight lines into curves and fits almost half the world into one round image. Playful, skate-video, 90s music-video energy.
cards.phrase: fisheye lens with strong barrel distortion and a curved horizon

cards.name: Lens flare
cards.desc: Bright light bouncing inside the lens, showing up as a streak and a line of soft colored circles. Signals "real camera" and sunny warmth, or sci-fi when overdone.
cards.phrase: subtle lens flare from the sun in the corner, soft circular ghosts and a horizontal anamorphic streak

cards.name: Stop-motion
cards.desc: Real objects moved a tiny bit and photographed one frame at a time. Slightly jittery, tactile and handmade, with real light and real materials.
cards.phrase: stop-motion animation look: handmade miniature set, felt and wood textures, real shallow-focus lighting

cards.name: Claymation
cards.desc: Stop-motion with soft modelling clay. Rounded, lumpy shapes, visible fingerprints and a warm, goofy charm.
cards.phrase: claymation style: chunky plasticine characters with visible fingerprints and soft waxy highlights

cards.name: Cel animation
cards.desc: Characters drawn with clean ink lines and flat colors, laid over a painted background. The classic Disney and anime look: crisp figures, soft painted world.
cards.phrase: traditional cel animation look: crisp ink-outlined flat-color character over a soft painted background

cards.name: Kinetic typography
cards.desc: Words that move, scale and snap in time with speech or music. The text itself is the visual.
cards.phrase: kinetic typography: bold words scale and slide in on the beat, one phrase at a time

cards.name: Motion graphics
cards.desc: Animated flat shapes, icons and charts, usually vector, with smooth easing and satisfying transitions. The language of product explainers and app animations.
cards.phrase: motion graphics style: flat vector shapes with springy easing, shapes morph and pop between scenes

cards.name: PBR
cards.desc: Materials that react to light like the real thing: metal reflects, rubber is matte, plastic has a soft shine. The standard for realistic 3D.
cards.phrase: physically based rendering with realistic materials: brushed metal, matte rubber, glossy plastic

cards.name: Hand-painted textures
cards.desc: Simple 3D shapes with lighting and wear painted straight into the textures: bright edge highlights, painted shadows, chunky shapes.
cards.phrase: stylized 3D with hand-painted textures, painted edge highlights and soft painted shadows

cards.name: Stylized realism
cards.desc: Believable lighting and materials on exaggerated, friendly shapes and bright colors. Real enough to feel solid, cartoony enough to feel inviting.
cards.phrase: stylized realism: chunky exaggerated shapes, saturated colors, soft realistic lighting and materials

cards.name: Ghibli-like painterly
cards.desc: Lush hand-painted worlds: towering cumulus clouds, deep blue skies, rich greens and cozy details, with simple characters set inside. Nostalgic, gentle and full of light.
cards.phrase: painterly anime landscape in a Ghibli-like spirit: towering cumulus clouds, lush greens, warm summer light, cozy details

cards.name: Game HUD
cards.desc: The information layered over gameplay: health and energy bars, a minimap, ammo or score counters. Clean HUDs stay in the corners and out of the action.
cards.phrase: game HUD overlay: health bar top-left, minimap bottom-right, minimal and out of the center

cards.name: Monochromatic
cards.desc: One hue in many lights and darks. Calm, unified and almost impossible to get wrong; contrast comes from value, not from color.
cards.phrase: monochromatic palette: tints and shades of a single [blue], separated by value only

cards.name: Analogous
cards.desc: Three or so hues that sit side by side on the wheel, like amber, orange and red. Natural and harmonious, the way a sunset or autumn leaves are.
cards.phrase: analogous palette of neighboring hues: [gold, amber and burnt orange]

cards.name: Accented analogous
cards.aka: analogous plus complement, warm palette with one cool accent
cards.desc: An analogous family with a single small accent taken from the opposite side of the wheel. The accent pops because it is the only one of its kind.
cards.phrase: accented analogous palette: [amber, gold and cream] with a single small [teal] accent as the only cool color

cards.name: Complementary
cards.desc: Two hues from opposite sides of the wheel, such as blue and orange. Each makes the other look stronger; use one as the main color and the other sparingly.
cards.phrase: complementary palette: [deep blue] dominant with small [orange] accents

cards.name: Split-complementary
cards.desc: One main hue plus the two hues on either side of its opposite. The punch of complementary colors with less clash, so it is easier to balance.
cards.phrase: split-complementary scheme: [blue] as the base, with [red-orange] and [yellow-orange] accents

cards.name: Triadic
cards.desc: Three hues evenly spaced around the wheel, like red, yellow and blue. Bright and playful; let one lead and the other two support.
cards.phrase: triadic color scheme of [red], [yellow] and [blue], with [red] dominant

cards.name: Tetradic
cards.desc: Two complementary pairs, making a rectangle on the wheel. Rich and varied, but busy; it works best when one color clearly dominates and the rest are muted.
cards.phrase: tetradic (double complementary) scheme, one dominant hue and three muted supporting hues

cards.name: Square
cards.desc: Four hues evenly spaced around the wheel. The most colorful of the classic schemes; it suits playful brands and needs a quiet neutral to rest on.
cards.phrase: square color scheme of four evenly spaced hues on a calm off-white background

cards.name: Achromatic
cards.desc: No hue at all: only black, white and grays. Feels editorial, architectural and serious, and lets texture and shape carry everything.
cards.phrase: achromatic palette: black, white and grays only, no hue at all

cards.name: Neutral plus one accent
cards.aka: achromatic with a pop, spot color
cards.desc: Mostly grays, off-whites or blacks, with one strong color reserved for the thing that matters. The most dependable way to direct the eye.
cards.phrase: neutral palette of warm grays with a single [cobalt] accent used only for the most important element

cards.name: 60-30-10 rule
cards.desc: Use the main color on about 60% of the area, a second on 30%, and an accent on 10%. A simple proportion that makes almost any palette feel balanced.
cards.phrase: follow a 60-30-10 split: [cream] 60% of the area, [forest green] 30%, [brass] 10% for accents

cards.name: Discordant
cards.desc: Colors that are “wrong” together on purpose, like pink with orange or acid green with red. Loud, fashion-forward and attention-grabbing when it is clearly intentional.
cards.phrase: deliberately clashing palette: hot pink against orange and acid green, bold and intentional

cards.name: Hue
cards.desc: Which color it is (red, amber, teal) as a position around the wheel. Shifting hue changes the color itself, not how strong or light it is.
cards.phrase: keep every color within a narrow hue range around [amber]

cards.name: Saturation
cards.desc: How pure a color is, from gray to vivid. Low saturation feels calm, grown-up and expensive; high saturation feels loud, young and energetic.
cards.phrase: low-saturation palette overall, with only [one element] fully saturated

cards.name: Value
cards.desc: How light or dark a color is, ignoring its hue. Value does the work and color gets the credit: an image with clear light and dark shapes still reads in grayscale.
cards.phrase: strong value structure: a few big light and dark shapes that read clearly even in grayscale

cards.name: Tints, tones & shades
cards.desc: A tint is a color plus white (soft, airy). A tone is plus gray (muted). A shade is plus black (deep, rich). Asking for “tints and shades of one teal” keeps a palette unified.
cards.phrase: build the palette from tints, tones and shades of a single [teal]

cards.name: Color temperature
cards.desc: Reds, oranges and yellows feel warm, close and energetic; blues and greens feel cool, distant and calm. Warm things seem to step forward and cool things recede.
cards.phrase: warm colors for the foreground subject, cool colors for the background so it recedes

cards.name: Warm-shifted & cool-shifted
cards.aka: biased hue, warm teal, cool red
cards.desc: Nudging a color toward the warm or cool side without changing what it is: a teal that leans green, a red that leans blue. It keeps a single accent in tune with the rest of the palette.
cards.phrase: warm-shift the [teal] toward green so it sits comfortably in the warm palette

cards.name: High key & low key
cards.aka: light key, dark key, tonal range
cards.desc: High key keeps nearly everything light, with few shadows: airy and optimistic. Low key keeps nearly everything dark with small pools of light: dramatic and intimate.
cards.phrase: high-key image: mostly light tones, soft shadows, airy and bright

cards.name: Simultaneous contrast
cards.aka: relative color, color interaction, Albers effect
cards.desc: The same color looks different depending on what surrounds it: gray looks warm on blue and cool on orange. It is why a color you picked alone can look wrong in place.
cards.phrase: test each color against its actual background; adjust for simultaneous contrast

cards.name: Vibrating colors
cards.desc: Two saturated complements of the same lightness placed edge to edge seem to shimmer at the border. Thrilling in op art and posters, painful for text.
cards.phrase: use vibrating complementary colors of equal lightness for an op-art shimmer (never for body text)

cards.name: Color weight
cards.desc: Saturated, dark and warm colors look heavier than light, cool, muted ones. A small patch of red can balance a large area of pale blue.
cards.phrase: balance color weight: one small saturated [red] shape offsets the large pale [blue] field

cards.name: Color roles
cards.aka: color jobs, assigned colors, color mapping
cards.desc: Assigning every color one job: background, main subject, shadow, highlight, accent. Roles are the single most effective way to keep a generated image or UI on palette.
cards.phrase: assign each color one role: [color] for [background], [color] for [subject], [color] for [shadows], [color] for [accents only]

cards.name: Limited palette
cards.desc: Painting everything with only three or four colors. Every mixture shares the same parents, so the whole image hangs together. The Zorn palette is just ochre, red, black and white.
cards.phrase: strictly limited palette of [four] colors; every tone mixed only from these

cards.name: Pastel
cards.desc: Light colors with lots of white mixed in. Gentle, friendly and young; needs one darker color for text and edges or everything floats.
