cards.phrase: soft pastel palette (light, low-saturation tints) with one deep [plum] for outlines and text

cards.name: Muted
cards.desc: Every color has some gray mixed in so nothing shouts. Sophisticated, calm and easy to live with; reads as considered and adult.
cards.phrase: muted, dusty palette; no color fully saturated

cards.name: Earth tones
cards.desc: Browns, ochres, terracotta, olive and sand: the colors of soil, stone and clay. Warm, grounded, organic and trustworthy.
cards.phrase: earth-tone palette: terracotta, ochre, olive, sand and warm brown

cards.name: Jewel tones
cards.desc: Deep, saturated colors named after gems: emerald, sapphire, ruby, amethyst, topaz. Luxurious, rich and a little theatrical.
cards.phrase: jewel-tone palette of emerald, sapphire, ruby and amethyst with gold accents

cards.name: Neon
cards.desc: Over-saturated, glowing colors, usually on near-black. Feels nocturnal, techy and energetic; they only glow if the background is dark.
cards.phrase: glowing neon accents in magenta, cyan and lime on a near-black background

cards.name: Bright primaries
cards.desc: Clean, fully saturated colors close to the primaries, usually on white. Confident, playful and loud.
cards.phrase: bold primary palette: saturated red, yellow and blue on clean white

cards.name: Black & white
cards.desc: No color at all, only light and dark. Timeless and graphic; pushes attention onto shape, texture and expression.
cards.phrase: black and white with deep blacks and bright highlights, rich midtone gradation

cards.name: Sepia & vintage
cards.desc: Warm browns and creams like an old photograph or yellowed paper. Nostalgic and archival.
cards.phrase: sepia-toned palette of warm browns and aged cream, like an old photograph

cards.name: Sun-bleached
cards.desc: Colors that look left out in the sun: pale, chalky and slightly warm, with no true blacks. Laid-back, dusty and nostalgic.
cards.phrase: sun-bleached palette: faded, chalky, warm-washed colors with no true blacks

cards.name: Dark & moody
cards.desc: Deep, low-key colors with a few rich mid-tones and almost no bright areas. Intimate, serious and cinematic.
cards.phrase: dark and moody palette: deep charcoals and forest greens, small pools of warm light

cards.name: Light & airy
cards.desc: Mostly whites and very pale neutrals with soft color only in small amounts. Fresh, open and calm.
cards.phrase: light and airy palette: whites and pale neutrals with soft touches of [blush]

cards.name: Tonal neutrals
cards.desc: Creams, taupes, oatmeal and stone in close steps. Expensive-feeling and calm; contrast comes from texture rather than color.
cards.phrase: tonal neutral palette of cream, oatmeal, taupe and stone, close in value

cards.name: Autumn
cards.desc: Rust, mustard, burgundy, burnt orange and olive. Cozy, nostalgic and warm.
cards.phrase: autumn palette: rust, mustard, burgundy, burnt orange and olive

cards.name: Winter
cards.desc: Icy blues, silver, slate and snow white, with a deep navy for night. Clean, quiet and crisp.
cards.phrase: cold winter palette: icy blue, silver gray, slate and snow white

cards.name: Spring
cards.desc: Fresh green, blossom pink, butter yellow and sky blue: light and saturated at once. Optimistic and new.
cards.phrase: spring palette: fresh leaf green, blossom pink, butter yellow and clear sky blue

cards.name: Summer
cards.desc: Turquoise, coral, sunshine yellow and sand under a big blue sky. Bright, carefree and saturated.
cards.phrase: summer palette: turquoise water, coral, sunshine yellow and warm sand

cards.name: Desert
cards.desc: Sand, terracotta, sage, dusty rose and a hot pale sky. Sun-baked and spacious.
cards.phrase: desert palette: sand, terracotta, sage, dusty rose under a pale hot sky

cards.name: Coastal
cards.desc: Navy, sea-glass green, sand and sail white, often with a touch of red. Breezy and clean.
cards.phrase: coastal palette: navy, sea-glass green, sand and crisp white with a small red accent

cards.name: Forest
cards.desc: Pine, moss, bark brown and fern green with a cool mist. Grounded, quiet and a little mysterious.
cards.phrase: forest palette: deep pine, moss, fern green, bark brown and misty gray

cards.name: Tropical
cards.desc: Lush deep greens with flashes of hibiscus pink, mango and parrot blue. Hot, humid and joyful.
cards.phrase: tropical palette: lush jungle greens with flashes of hibiscus pink, mango orange and parrot blue

cards.name: Sunset
cards.desc: A band of peach, coral, magenta and violet fading to indigo. Romantic and wistful; works as a gradient or as flat bands.
cards.phrase: sunset palette in bands: peach, coral, magenta, violet fading to indigo

cards.name: Night city
cards.desc: Deep blues and blacks with warm windows and a few colored lights. Lonely, cinematic and quiet.
cards.phrase: night palette: deep navy and black with warm yellow windows and a few colored lights

cards.name: Dusty Americana
cards.desc: Faded denim, rust, prairie gold, sagebrush and bone, as if everything has been on the road for a while. Folk-song nostalgia.
cards.phrase: dusty Americana palette: faded denim blue, rust, prairie gold, sagebrush and bone white

cards.name: Vaporwave
cards.aka: aesthetic, A E S T H E T I C
cards.desc: Pastel pink, mint, lavender and cyan, with marble busts, grids and early-web nostalgia. Dreamy, ironic and soft.
cards.phrase: vaporwave palette: pastel pink, mint, lavender and cyan with a soft retro-web feel

cards.name: Synthwave
cards.desc: Hot magenta and electric cyan on deep purple, a striped sunset sun and a glowing grid. Pure 80s night-drive energy.
cards.phrase: synthwave palette: hot magenta and cyan on deep purple-black, striped orange-to-pink sunset sun

cards.name: Cyberpunk
cards.desc: Acid yellow, toxic cyan and hot pink cutting through wet black streets. Harsher and grittier than synthwave.
cards.phrase: cyberpunk palette: acid yellow, cyan and hot pink neon against wet black and teal shadows

cards.name: Y2K
cards.desc: Chrome, icy blue, bubblegum pink, lime and translucent plastic. Glossy, optimistic and very 1999 to 2004.
cards.phrase: Y2K palette: chrome silver, icy blue, bubblegum pink and lime, glossy translucent plastic

cards.name: Memphis
cards.desc: Saturated primaries and pastels thrown together with black squiggles and confetti patterns. Cheerful, loud and anti-tasteful on purpose.
cards.phrase: Memphis design palette: mint, pink, yellow, cobalt and black, with squiggles and confetti

cards.name: 70s retro
cards.desc: Harvest gold, burnt orange, avocado green and chocolate brown, often as rounded stripes. Warm, mellow and nostalgic.
cards.phrase: 70s retro palette: harvest gold, burnt orange, avocado green and chocolate brown in rounded stripes

cards.name: Mid-century modern
cards.desc: Mustard, teal, orange and walnut brown on warm off-white. Optimistic, tidy and crafted.
cards.phrase: mid-century modern palette: mustard, teal, tangerine and walnut brown on warm off-white

cards.name: Art Deco
cards.desc: Black, gold and cream with deep emerald or navy. Glamorous, geometric and opulent.
cards.phrase: Art Deco palette: black, metallic gold and cream with deep emerald accents

cards.name: Bauhaus
cards.desc: Red, yellow, blue, black and off-white in hard geometric shapes. Rational, bold and teacherly.
cards.phrase: Bauhaus palette: primary red, yellow and blue with black on off-white, hard geometric shapes

cards.name: Swiss style
cards.desc: White, black and one signal red, nothing else. Clean, objective and confident.
cards.phrase: Swiss style palette: white, black and a single signal red

cards.name: Scandinavian
cards.desc: White, pale birch, soft gray and a muted sage or dusty blue. Bright, calm and practical.
cards.phrase: Scandinavian palette: white, pale birch wood, soft gray and muted sage

cards.name: Japandi
cards.desc: Warm stone, charcoal, natural oak, clay and muted olive. Earthier and darker than Scandinavian; restful and handmade.
cards.phrase: Japandi palette: warm stone, charcoal, natural oak, clay and muted olive

cards.name: Dark academia
cards.desc: Oxblood, forest green, tweed brown, parchment and ink black. Bookish, autumnal and a little gothic.
cards.phrase: dark academia palette: oxblood, forest green, tweed brown, parchment and ink black

cards.name: Cottagecore
cards.desc: Cream, sage, buttercup, faded rose and linen. Soft, rural and handmade, like a cottage garden.
cards.phrase: cottagecore palette: cream, sage, buttercup yellow, faded rose and linen

cards.name: Solarpunk
cards.desc: Leaf green, solar gold, sky blue and white with warm wood. Optimistic, sustainable and sunny.
cards.phrase: solarpunk palette: leaf green, solar gold, clear sky blue and white with warm wood

cards.name: Barbiecore
cards.desc: Every shade of saturated pink, from bubblegum to magenta, often head to toe. Playful, loud and unapologetic.
cards.phrase: Barbiecore palette: saturated hot pink, bubblegum and magenta, pink on pink

cards.name: Millennial pink
cards.desc: A muted, slightly orange pink paired with gray, cream and brass. Soft and knowing; a 2010s signature.
cards.phrase: millennial pink palette: muted salmon-pink with warm gray, cream and brass

cards.name: Acid graphics
cards.desc: Acid green, chrome, black and hot orange, with distorted type. Aggressive, club-flyer energy.
cards.phrase: acid graphics palette: acid green and hot orange on black, with chrome highlights

cards.name: Pop art
cards.desc: Flat primaries, hot pink and black outlines with Ben-Day dots. Bold, ironic and graphic.
cards.phrase: pop art palette: flat primary red, yellow, cyan and hot pink with thick black outlines and Ben-Day dots

cards.name: Ukiyo-e
cards.desc: Prussian blue, indigo, soft vermilion, pale ochre and paper cream. Flat, quiet and graphic.
cards.phrase: ukiyo-e palette: Prussian blue, indigo, soft vermilion and pale ochre on cream paper

cards.name: Risograph
cards.desc: A handful of bright translucent inks (fluorescent pink, blue, yellow, teal) that overlap into new colors, on off-white paper with grain.
cards.phrase: risograph palette: fluorescent pink and medium blue inks overprinting to purple, slight misregistration, grain

cards.name: Kodak Portra
cards.desc: Soft contrast, warm and flattering skin tones, gentle pastel greens and fine grain. Reads as tender, natural and timeless.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodak Portra 400: soft contrast, warm natural skin tones, gentle pastel color, fine grain

cards.name: Kodak Ektar
cards.desc: Very saturated, punchy color with super-fine grain, especially in blues and reds. Landscape film; unkind to skin.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodak Ektar 100: vivid saturated blues and reds, crisp, ultra-fine grain

cards.name: Fuji Velvia
cards.desc: Slide film with intense saturation, deep blacks and vivid greens and magentas. Dramatic nature photography.
cards.phrase: Fuji Velvia slide film look: intensely saturated greens and magentas, deep blacks, high contrast

cards.name: Fujifilm cool greens
cards.desc: Cooler than Kodak, with minty greens, cyan-leaning skies and clean whites. Fresh, airy and a little nostalgic.
cards.phrase: Fujifilm color: cool minty greens, cyan-leaning skies, clean whites, soft grain

cards.name: Kodachrome
cards.desc: Rich reds, deep blues, warm yellows and dense shadows, with an archival 50s to 80s feel. Saturated but never neon.
cards.phrase: Kodachrome look: rich reds, deep blues, warm yellows, dense shadows, mid-century archival feel

cards.name: CineStill 800T
cards.desc: Tungsten-balanced cinema film used at night: teal-blue shadows and red glowing halos around every light. The signature look of neon nights on film.
cards.phrase: CineStill 800T at night: cool teal shadows, red halation glow around every light source, visible grain

cards.name: Technicolor
cards.desc: Lush, saturated primaries with candy reds, deep blues and glowing skin. The look of 1930s to 50s Hollywood musicals.
cards.phrase: three-strip Technicolor look: lush saturated primaries, candy reds, glowing skin, painterly sets

cards.name: Two-strip color
cards.desc: Early color film that only had two dyes, so everything is orange-red and cyan-green with no true blue or yellow. Strange, antique and dreamy.
cards.phrase: two-strip color film look: only orange-red and cyan-green tones, no true blues or yellows

cards.name: Polaroid
cards.desc: Soft, slightly washed colors with odd shifts (cyan shadows, warm highlights), soft focus and a white border.
cards.phrase: Polaroid instant film look: soft, washed color, cyan-tinted shadows, warm highlights, white frame

cards.name: Bleach bypass
cards.desc: Skipping the bleach step keeps silver in the film: colors drop toward gray while contrast and grit go up. Harsh, metallic and war-movie bleak.
cards.phrase: bleach bypass look: desaturated, silvery, high contrast with gritty blacks

cards.name: Cross-processed
cards.desc: Slide film developed in negative chemicals (or the reverse): yellow-green highlights, blue or magenta shadows, blown contrast. Lo-fi and 90s.
cards.phrase: cross-processed look: yellow-green highlights, blue-magenta shadows, punchy contrast

cards.name: Cyanotype
cards.desc: An old iron-based print process that renders everything in Prussian blue and white. Botanical, archival and calm.
cards.phrase: cyanotype print: Prussian blue and white only, soft edges, paper texture

cards.name: Teal & orange
cards.desc: Skin and warm lights pushed toward orange, shadows and backgrounds pushed toward teal. The complementary split makes people pop; overused, it looks generic.
cards.phrase: teal and orange grade: warm orange skin and highlights, teal shadows and background

cards.name: Split toning
cards.aka: split tone, color in highlights and shadows
cards.desc: One color added to the highlights and a different one to the shadows, such as warm gold highlights with blue shadows. The quiet engine behind most cinematic grades.
cards.phrase: split toning: warm golden highlights and cool blue-green shadows

cards.name: Faded & lifted blacks
cards.aka: matte look, washed blacks, film fade
cards.desc: The darkest tones are raised to a soft charcoal so nothing is truly black. Gentle, nostalgic and dreamy; a big part of the “film” look on social media.
cards.phrase: faded matte look with lifted blacks, soft charcoal shadows, gentle contrast

cards.name: Crushed blacks
cards.desc: The dark tones are pushed all the way to pure black, hiding detail in the shadows. Bold, graphic and moody.
cards.phrase: crushed blacks: deep inky shadows with no detail, high contrast

cards.name: Desaturated
cards.aka: muted grade, washed color, low saturation
cards.desc: Color pulled close to gray across the whole image, keeping only a hint. Serious, bleak or documentary.
cards.phrase: heavily desaturated grade, just a hint of color remaining, cool and somber

cards.name: Selective color
cards.desc: The image is black and white except for one colored element. Instantly points at what matters; easy to overdo.
cards.phrase: black and white image with only the [red umbrella] in full color

cards.name: Green tint
cards.desc: The whole image washed with a cold green, like office fluorescent light or a computer screen. Uneasy, artificial and digital.
cards.phrase: cold green-tinted grade like fluorescent light, uneasy and artificial

cards.name: Yellow-green urban
cards.aka: Fincher look, sodium vapor, nicotine grade
cards.desc: Muddy yellow-greens and dim browns, like old cigarette smoke or sodium street lights. Grimy, tense and paranoid.
cards.phrase: grimy yellow-green grade, sodium-vapor light, desaturated browns, tense and paranoid

cards.name: Pastel symmetry grade
cards.desc: Soft pinks, mint, mustard and powder blue with low contrast and very even light. Storybook, deadpan and precise.
cards.phrase: Wes Anderson style grade: soft pinks, mint and mustard, low contrast, flat even light, centered symmetry

cards.name: Cyan & magenta night
cards.desc: Night scenes lit in saturated cyan and magenta, with skin glowing in both. Intimate, dreamy and modern.
cards.phrase: night portrait lit with saturated cyan from one side and magenta from the other, glowing skin

cards.name: Day for night
cards.desc: Shot in daylight, then graded deep blue and underexposed to look like moonlight. Theatrical, storybook night with sharp shadows.
cards.phrase: day-for-night grade: deep blue, underexposed daylight that reads as bright moonlight

cards.name: Monochrome tint
cards.aka: toned black and white, tinted mono
cards.desc: A black-and-white image tinted with one color, like sepia, cyan, or the red of a darkroom. Unified and graphic.
cards.phrase: monochrome image tinted entirely in [deep red], like a toned darkroom print

cards.name: Golden hour
cards.desc: The hour after sunrise or before sunset: low warm sunlight, long shadows, glowing edges and honeyed color. Nostalgic and kind.
cards.phrase: golden hour light: low warm sun, long shadows, glowing amber edges

cards.name: Blue hour
cards.desc: The short time after sunset when the sky goes deep blue and artificial lights start to glow warm. Calm, melancholy and cinematic.
cards.phrase: blue hour: deep blue twilight sky with warm glowing windows and street lights

cards.name: Overcast
cards.desc: Clouds act as a giant softbox: no hard shadows, low contrast, colors look true and slightly cool. Calm, honest and Nordic.
cards.phrase: overcast flat light: soft shadowless illumination, muted cool colors

cards.name: Harsh noon sun
cards.desc: Sun straight overhead: hard short shadows, bleached highlights and saturated color. Hot, honest, Mediterranean or desert.
cards.phrase: harsh midday sun: hard short shadows, bleached highlights, saturated hot color

cards.name: Candlelight & tungsten
cards.desc: Warm orange light from candles, lamps or bulbs falling off quickly into darkness. Cozy, intimate and old-world.
cards.phrase: lit only by warm candlelight: deep orange glow falling off into dark shadows

cards.name: Neon night
cards.desc: Night lit by colored signs: magenta, cyan and red light spilling over wet surfaces. Electric, lonely and urban.
cards.phrase: neon night lighting: magenta and cyan sign glow reflecting on wet pavement

cards.name: Backlit haze
cards.desc: The light source sits behind the subject, flooding the frame with glow and lifting the shadows into haze. Dreamy, hopeful and soft.
cards.phrase: backlit by a low sun, hazy glow lifting the shadows, soft flare, subject partly dissolved in light

cards.name: Fog & atmosphere
cards.desc: Each layer further away gets paler and bluer, as if seen through mist. Adds depth and quiet mystery with almost no effort.
cards.phrase: layers fading into mist: each distant layer paler and bluer (atmospheric perspective)

cards.name: Catppuccin Mocha
cards.desc: Soft pastel accents (mauve, peach, sky, green) on a deep blue-gray base. Cozy, friendly and very readable; one of the most-ported themes there is.
cards.phrase: Catppuccin Mocha color theme: background #1e1e2e, text #cdd6f4, accents #f38ba8, #a6e3a1, #f9e2af, #89b4fa, #cba6f7, #94e2d5

cards.name: Catppuccin Latte
cards.desc: The light flavor of Catppuccin: warm off-white base with saturated versions of the same accents. Pairs with Mocha for light and dark modes.
cards.phrase: Catppuccin Latte color theme: background #eff1f5, text #4c4f69, accents #d20f39, #40a02b, #df8e1d, #1e66f5, #8839ef, #179299

cards.name: Dracula
cards.desc: Bright candy accents (pink, purple, green, cyan) on a cool purple-gray. Punchy and playful for a dark theme.
cards.phrase: Dracula color theme: background #282a36, text #f8f8f2, accents #ff79c6, #50fa7b, #f1fa8c, #8be9fd, #bd93f9, #ffb86c

cards.name: Nord
cards.desc: Cool slate grays with frosty blues and muted aurora accents. Calm, clean and Scandinavian; it rarely looks garish.
cards.phrase: Nord color theme: background #2e3440, text #d8dee9, accents #bf616a, #a3be8c, #ebcb8b, #81a1c1, #b48ead, #88c0d0

cards.name: Solarized
cards.desc: A precisely engineered palette by Ethan Schoonover: 8 accents that work on both a deep teal-black and a cream background with the same contrast. Distinctive and low-glare.
cards.phrase: Solarized color theme: background #002b36, text #839496, accents #dc322f, #859900, #b58900, #268bd2, #6c71c4, #2aa198

cards.name: Gruvbox
cards.desc: Warm, earthy retro colors (mustard, rust, olive, faded aqua) on a brown-black. Feels like an old amber terminal with taste.
cards.phrase: Gruvbox color theme: background #282828, text #ebdbb2, accents #fb4934, #b8bb26, #fabd2f, #83a598, #d3869b, #8ec07c

cards.name: Tokyo Night
cards.desc: Deep indigo night with soft neon blue, violet and orange, like Tokyo's lights from a distance. Modern and moody.
cards.phrase: Tokyo Night color theme: background #1a1b26, text #c0caf5, accents #f7768e, #9ece6a, #e0af68, #7aa2f7, #bb9af7, #7dcfff

cards.name: Rosé Pine
cards.desc: Muted rose, gold, pine and foam on a dark violet. Romantic, soft and low-contrast; “all natural pine, faux fur and a bit of soho vibes”.
cards.phrase: Rosé Pine color theme: background #191724, text #e0def4, accents #eb6f92, #31748f, #f6c177, #9ccfd8, #c4a7e7, #ebbcba

cards.name: One Dark
cards.desc: Balanced mid-saturation accents on a cool gray, from the Atom editor. The neutral, can't-go-wrong dark theme.
cards.phrase: One Dark color theme: background #282c34, text #abb2bf, accents #e06c75, #98c379, #e5c07b, #61afef, #c678dd, #56b6c2

cards.name: Monokai
cards.desc: Hot pink, lime and orange on an olive-black. Loud and confident; the classic Sublime Text look.
cards.phrase: Monokai color theme: background #272822, text #f8f8f2, accents #f92672, #a6e22e, #e6db74, #66d9ef, #ae81ff, #fd971f

cards.name: Everforest
cards.desc: Soft greens, sand and muted pastels on a gray-green base. Like reading in a shaded forest; very easy on the eyes.
cards.phrase: Everforest color theme: background #2d353b, text #d3c6aa, accents #e67e80, #a7c080, #dbbc7f, #7fbbb3, #d699b6, #83c092

cards.name: Kanagawa
cards.desc: Colors from Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa: ink black, faded paper, wave blue, autumn red and spring green. Painterly and calm.
cards.phrase: Kanagawa color theme: background #1f1f28, text #dcd7ba, accents #c34043, #98bb6c, #e6c384, #7e9cd8, #957fb8, #7aa89f

cards.name: Grand Budapest
cards.desc: Rose, peach and pastry pink with a deep oxblood and burnt orange, from The Grand Budapest Hotel. Confectionery and deadpan.
cards.phrase: Grand Budapest Hotel palette: peach #f1bb7b, coral pink #fd6467, oxblood #5b1a18, burnt orange #d67236

cards.name: Darjeeling Limited
cards.desc: Pure red, teal, saffron, orange and sky blue from The Darjeeling Limited. Bold, sunny and travel-poster bright.
cards.phrase: Darjeeling Limited palette: red #ff0000, teal #00a08a, saffron #f2ad00, orange #f98400, sky blue #5bbcd6

cards.name: Moonrise Kingdom
cards.desc: Powder blue, ballet pink, khaki olive and sand yellow from Moonrise Kingdom. Scout-camp nostalgia.
cards.phrase: Moonrise Kingdom palette: powder blue #85d4e3, pink #f4b5bd, khaki olive #9c964a, sand #cdc08c, butter yellow #fad77b

cards.name: Game Boy
cards.desc: The original Game Boy screen: four shades of olive green, nothing else. Instant retro handheld nostalgia.
cards.phrase: original Game Boy palette, only four shades of green: #0f380f, #306230, #8bac0f, #9bbc0f

cards.name: PICO-8
cards.desc: The fixed 16-color palette of the PICO-8 fantasy console. Warm, cheerful and balanced; a favorite for pixel art and game jams.
cards.phrase: pixel art using only the PICO-8 16-color palette

cards.name: Pantone Color of the Year
cards.desc: Pantone's yearly pick, which then shows up everywhere from phones to sofas: Very Peri (2022), Viva Magenta (2023), Peach Fuzz (2024), Mocha Mousse (2025) and the soft white Cloud Dancer (2026). The hexes are Pantone's screen approximations.
cards.phrase: built around Pantone's [Mocha Mousse #a47864] as the hero color, with warm neutrals

cards.name: International Klein Blue
cards.desc: The ultramarine Yves Klein patented in 1960: so saturated it seems to vibrate and absorb you. Pure, spiritual and avant-garde.
cards.phrase: International Klein Blue (#002fa7) as a deep, vibrating field of color

cards.name: Tiffany Blue
cards.desc: The light robin-egg turquoise of Tiffany's boxes. Says gift, luxury and celebration.
cards.phrase: Tiffany Blue (#81d8d0)

cards.name: Hermès orange
cards.desc: The warm, slightly burnt orange of Hermès boxes. Luxurious without being cold.
cards.phrase: Hermès orange (#f37021)

cards.name: Rosso Corsa
cards.desc: Italy's national racing red. Speed, passion and engineering pride.
cards.phrase: Rosso Corsa (#d40000)

cards.name: British racing green
cards.desc: The deep green of British racing cars. Heritage, craft and old money.
cards.phrase: British racing green (#004225)

cards.name: Majorelle Blue
cards.desc: The intense violet-blue of Jacques Majorelle's garden villa in Marrakech, later Yves Saint Laurent's. Hot-climate, exotic, joyful.
cards.phrase: Majorelle Blue (#6050dc)

cards.name: Shocking pink
cards.desc: Elsa Schiaparelli's 1937 magenta-pink. Surreal, daring and fashion-forward.
cards.phrase: Shocking pink (#fc0fc0)

cards.name: Barbie pink
cards.desc: The bright magenta-pink of Barbie's branding. Playful, confident and unapologetically pink.
cards.phrase: Barbie pink (#e0218a)

cards.name: Safety orange
cards.desc: The fluorescent orange of traffic cones and hunting vests, chosen to be seen against any background. Urgent, utilitarian, industrial.
cards.phrase: Safety orange (#ff7900)

cards.name: Coca-Cola red
cards.desc: A warm, saturated red associated with Coca-Cola and, through its ads, with the modern Santa Claus. Festive and bold.
cards.phrase: Coca-Cola red (#f40009)

cards.name: Off-white
cards.desc: A warm white with a whisper of gray or yellow. Calmer and more expensive-looking than pure white, which can feel clinical.
cards.phrase: warm off-white (#f0eee9) instead of pure white

cards.name: Rich black
cards.desc: A deep black with a hint of color (blue, green or brown) instead of pure #000. Looks richer in print and gentler on screens.
cards.phrase: rich near-black (#14161a) instead of pure black

cards.name: Ultramarine
cards.desc: A deep, slightly violet blue once ground from lapis lazuli and worth more than gold. Renaissance painters saved it for the Virgin Mary's robes.
cards.phrase: Ultramarine (#120a8f)

cards.name: Prussian blue
cards.desc: A dark, inky blue-green discovered by accident in 1706. Cool, deep and ideal for shadows; the blue of Japanese woodblocks and blueprints.
cards.phrase: Prussian blue (#003153)

cards.name: Vermilion
cards.desc: A brilliant orange-red made from cinnabar. Lacquer, temple gates and seals.
cards.phrase: Vermilion (#e34234)

cards.name: Yellow ochre
cards.desc: An earthy, muted yellow-brown clay pigment, used since the first cave paintings. Warm, natural and humble.
cards.phrase: Yellow ochre (#cc7722)

cards.name: Burnt sienna
cards.desc: Sienna earth roasted to a warm reddish brown. Terracotta roofs, skin shadows and Tuscan walls.
cards.phrase: Burnt sienna (#e97451)

cards.name: Raw umber
cards.desc: A cool, greenish dark brown earth. The workhorse dark for underpaintings and old-master shadows.
cards.phrase: Raw umber (#826644)

cards.name: Viridian
cards.desc: A cool, transparent blue-green. Deep water, glass and conifers.
cards.phrase: Viridian (#40826d)

cards.name: Payne's gray
cards.desc: A dark blue-gray watercolor pigment that stands in for black. Stormy skies, rain and slate.
cards.phrase: Payne's gray (#536878)

cards.name: Naples yellow
cards.desc: A soft, creamy pale yellow. Sunlit skin, butter and old plaster.
cards.phrase: Naples yellow (#fada5e)

cards.name: Cadmium red
cards.desc: A fully saturated, warm, opaque red. The brightest red on a painter's palette.
cards.phrase: Cadmium red (#e30022)

cards.name: Alizarin crimson
cards.desc: A cool, transparent, slightly blue-red. Wine, roses and deep glazes.
cards.phrase: Alizarin crimson (#e32636)

cards.name: Tyrian purple
cards.desc: An ancient dye made from sea snails, so costly only emperors wore it. Regal, deep and wine-colored.
cards.phrase: Tyrian purple (#66023c)

cards.name: Verdigris
cards.desc: The blue-green crust that grows on old copper and bronze. Weathered, coastal and historic.
cards.phrase: Verdigris (#43b3ae)

cards.name: Celadon
cards.desc: A pale gray-green from Chinese and Korean ceramic glazes. Quiet, cool and refined.
cards.phrase: Celadon (#ace1af)

cards.name: Indigo
cards.desc: A dark, slightly violet blue plant dye. Denim, Japanese aizome and boro textiles.
cards.phrase: Indigo (#2a3a6b)

cards.name: Egyptian blue
cards.desc: The world's first synthetic pigment, a bright clean blue from ancient Egypt. Tomb paintings and faience.
cards.phrase: Egyptian blue (#1034a6)

cards.name: Linear gradient
cards.desc: Color blends in a straight line from one to another. Clean and simple; the in-between colors matter, so pick hues that don't go muddy in the middle.
cards.phrase: smooth linear gradient from [deep violet] to [warm coral], no muddy midpoint

cards.name: Radial gradient
cards.desc: Color spreads outward from a center point, like a glow or spotlight. Draws the eye to the middle.
cards.phrase: radial gradient glow from a bright center fading to dark edges

cards.name: Conic gradient
cards.desc: Color sweeps around a center point like a clock hand. Pie charts, color wheels and holographic sheens.
cards.phrase: conic gradient sweeping through the full hue circle

cards.name: Mesh gradient
cards.desc: Several colors blend in soft, organic patches rather than a line. Lush, modern and very 2020s web.
cards.phrase: soft mesh gradient of [peach, lilac and aqua] blending in organic patches

cards.name: Aurora gradient
cards.desc: Big, blurry, slowly drifting color shapes on a dark background, like the northern lights. Popular for AI and tech brands.
cards.phrase: aurora gradient: large blurred drifting color orbs of [teal, violet and magenta] on near-black

cards.name: Grainy gradient
cards.desc: A gradient with fine noise on top, which hides banding and makes digital color feel printed and tactile.
cards.phrase: grainy gradient from [orange] to [pink] with visible fine noise texture

cards.name: Gradient map
cards.desc: Every tone in an image is replaced by a color from a gradient: shadows become one color, highlights another. The engine behind duotones and stylized photo looks.
cards.phrase: gradient map the image: shadows to [deep indigo], midtones to [magenta], highlights to [peach]

cards.name: Duotone
cards.desc: An image reduced to two colors, one for darks and one for lights. Unifies mixed photos and feels graphic and branded.
cards.phrase: duotone treatment: every image in [deep navy] for darks and [hot pink] for lights

cards.name: Tritone
cards.desc: Like a duotone with a third color in the midtones. Richer, more painterly, still unified.
cards.phrase: tritone treatment: [black] shadows, [teal] midtones, [cream] highlights

cards.name: Posterized
cards.aka: banded tones, reduced colors, cel bands
cards.desc: Smooth tones broken into a few flat bands of color. Graphic, screen-printed or retro-digital.
cards.phrase: posterized into [4] flat tonal bands, no smooth gradients

cards.name: Color blocking
cards.desc: Large, hard-edged areas of flat solid color placed side by side. Bold, modern and fashion-led.
cards.phrase: color blocking: large hard-edged areas of solid [mustard], [cobalt] and [blush]

cards.name: Overprint
cards.desc: Translucent inks printed on top of each other, so where they overlap a third color appears. Handmade and luminous.
cards.phrase: overprinted translucent inks: [pink] and [blue] overlap to make [purple]

cards.name: Spot inks
cards.desc: The image is built from a few solid inks, each with a job, and shading comes from dots or grain rather than blending. Tight, controllable color.
cards.phrase: flat color separation in [5] spot inks: [ink] for [job], [ink] for [job]; no blended gradients

cards.name: CMYK halftone
cards.desc: Color built from tiny dots of cyan, magenta, yellow and black at different angles. Comic-book, newsprint, printed-matter texture.
cards.phrase: visible CMYK halftone dots, comic-print texture

cards.name: Iridescent
cards.desc: Color that shifts through pinks, golds, mints and blues as the angle changes, like a soap bubble or holographic foil. Futuristic and Y2K.
cards.phrase: iridescent holographic sheen shifting through pink, gold, mint and blue

cards.name: Chromatic aberration
cards.desc: Red, green and blue channels slightly misaligned so edges get colored fringes. Glitchy, lens-like or VHS.
cards.phrase: slight chromatic aberration: red and cyan fringes on high-contrast edges

cards.name: Glow & bloom
cards.aka: light bloom, soft glow, Orton effect
cards.desc: Bright areas bleed soft light into their surroundings. Dreamy, magical and warm; too much looks like a 2000s video game.
cards.phrase: soft bloom around highlights, light bleeding gently into the surroundings

cards.name: Color tokens
cards.desc: Colors named by job (surface, text-muted, accent, danger) rather than by value (blue-500). Swapping themes then changes values while the names stay put.
cards.phrase: define colors as semantic tokens (background, surface, text, text-muted, border, accent, danger) as CSS variables

cards.name: 50-900 color scale
cards.desc: Each hue built as a ladder of about ten steps from very light (50) to very dark (900 or 950). Gives you backgrounds, borders, text and hover states from one hue.
cards.phrase: build each color as a 50-950 scale; use 50-100 for backgrounds, 500-600 for accents, 800-900 for text

cards.name: OKLCH
cards.desc: A color space where equal steps of lightness actually look equal. Scales built in OKLCH don't get muddy, and every hue at the same L has the same contrast.
cards.phrase: build the palette in OKLCH so every hue at the same lightness has matching contrast

cards.name: Tinted neutrals
cards.aka: warm gray, cool gray, slate, stone
cards.desc: Grays with a hint of the brand hue mixed in: slate (blue), stone (warm), sage (green). They make an interface feel considered instead of default.
cards.phrase: use warm stone neutrals (grays tinted slightly toward [brown]) for surfaces and text

cards.name: Dark mode palette
cards.desc: Not just inverted: near-black blue or gray instead of pure black, off-white text instead of pure white, and accents lightened and desaturated so they don't glow.
cards.phrase: dark mode: #121417-ish background, off-white text, accents lightened and slightly desaturated, no pure black or white

cards.name: Surface elevation
cards.desc: In dark mode, higher layers (cards, menus, dialogs) get slightly lighter instead of casting shadows. Light mode uses shadows; dark mode uses tone.
cards.phrase: in dark mode, show elevation by lightening surfaces step by step (background, card, menu, dialog)

cards.name: Contrast ratio
cards.desc: How different text is from its background, measured as a ratio. WCAG AA asks for 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and icons. Light gray on white usually fails.
cards.phrase: all text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI icons)

cards.name: Don't rely on color alone
cards.desc: Pair every color meaning with a second cue (an icon, label, pattern or position) so people with color-vision deficiency, or a grayscale printout, still get it.
cards.phrase: never use color as the only signal; pair status colors with icons and text labels

cards.name: Semantic status colors
cards.desc: A fixed set of colors that always mean the same thing: green for success, amber for warning, red for danger, blue for info. Keep them apart from the brand palette.
cards.phrase: semantic status colors kept separate from the brand: success green, warning amber, danger red, info blue

cards.name: State layers
cards.desc: Each interactive color needs variations for hover, pressed, focused and disabled. Usually a step darker or a translucent overlay, plus a visible focus ring.
cards.phrase: include hover (one step darker), pressed (two steps), visible focus ring, and 40%-opacity disabled states

cards.name: Dynamic color
cards.desc: The whole theme is generated from one seed color, often pulled from the user's wallpaper, into tonal palettes for primary, secondary, tertiary and neutrals.
cards.phrase: generate a Material 3 dynamic color scheme from the seed color [#6750a4]

cards.name: Categorical palette
cards.desc: Distinct hues for things with no order (products, teams, regions). Keep it to about 6-8; beyond that, people can't tell them apart.
cards.phrase: categorical palette of 6 distinct, equally prominent hues for unordered series

cards.name: Sequential palette
cards.desc: One hue from light to dark for ordered values (low to high). Darker means more; readers get it without a legend.
cards.phrase: sequential single-hue palette from pale to dark [blue] for low-to-high values

cards.name: Diverging palette
cards.desc: Two hues meeting at a neutral middle, for data with a meaningful center (above or below average, gain or loss).
cards.phrase: diverging palette: [blue] for below zero, neutral gray at zero, [red] for above

cards.name: Highlight one series
cards.desc: Everything in gray except the one series the chart is about. The fastest way to make a chart say one thing.
cards.phrase: all series in light gray except [our product], highlighted in the accent color

cards.name: Okabe-Ito palette
cards.desc: Eight colors chosen to stay distinguishable for the common forms of color blindness. The default safe choice for scientific charts.
cards.phrase: use the color-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette (#e69f00, #56b4e9, #009e73, #f0e442, #0072b2, #d55e00, #cc79a7)

cards.name: Viridis
cards.desc: A purple-to-teal-to-yellow ramp designed so equal data steps look equal, it prints in grayscale and works for color-blind readers. Its siblings are magma, inferno and plasma.
cards.phrase: use the viridis colormap (purple to teal to yellow) for the continuous scale

cards.name: Avoid rainbow scales
cards.desc: Rainbow ramps create fake boundaries (the yellow band looks like a jump) and fail for color-blind readers. Ask for a perceptual ramp instead.
cards.phrase: no rainbow or jet colormaps; use a perceptually uniform ramp

cards.name: Old-style serif
cards.desc: The oldest roman type, from 1500s France and Venice. Gentle contrast between thick and thin, slanted stress like a broad pen, and small, warm letterforms. Reads as literary, calm and timeless.
cards.phrase: an old-style serif like Garamond or Caslon: low stroke contrast, diagonal stress, warm and bookish

cards.name: Transitional serif
cards.desc: The 1750s step between old-style and modern: sharper serifs, more contrast and an upright axis. Crisp, sturdy and trustworthy, it is the default voice of newspapers, law firms and universities.
cards.phrase: a transitional serif like Baskerville: moderate contrast, vertical stress, crisp bracketed serifs, authoritative and trustworthy

cards.name: Didone
cards.desc: Extreme contrast: hairline-thin serifs and horizontals against heavy verticals, perfectly upright. Glamorous and dramatic at large sizes, the look of fashion magazines and perfume bottles. Thin strokes vanish at small sizes.
cards.phrase: a Didone serif like Bodoni or Didot: extreme thick-thin contrast, hairline serifs, vertical stress, used large for a glamorous fashion-magazine feel

cards.name: Slab serif
cards.desc: Thick, block-shaped serifs and almost no contrast. Born on 1800s posters to shout from a distance; today it feels sturdy, mechanical and a little rugged.
cards.phrase: a slab serif like Rockwell or Clarendon: heavy rectangular serifs, low contrast, sturdy and mechanical

cards.name: Inscriptional serif
cards.desc: Capitals modeled on letters carved in stone in ancient Rome, often caps-only. Wide, stately and ceremonial; it is the classic epic movie poster.
cards.phrase: Roman inscriptional capitals like Trajan: all caps, wide stately proportions, chiseled serifs, ceremonial and epic

cards.name: Soft serif
cards.aka: Cooper-style, wonky serif, retro soft serif
cards.desc: Heavy serifs with rounded, melted-looking corners and big round bowls. Friendly, warm and very 1970s, and it has come back in food, wellness and indie brands.
cards.phrase: a soft, rounded serif in the spirit of Cooper Black: heavy weight, blobby rounded serifs, warm and retro 1970s

cards.name: Screen text serif
cards.desc: Modern serifs drawn for long reading on screens: large x-height, sturdy serifs and open shapes that hold up at 16px. The voice of good digital publications.
cards.phrase: a contemporary text serif made for screens, like Charter or Source Serif: large x-height, sturdy serifs, comfortable for long reading

cards.name: Condensed editorial serif
cards.desc: Tall, narrow serifs with sharp details, set big and light, often with an italic. The current look of design studios, magazines and premium startups.
cards.phrase: a condensed editorial display serif like Instrument Serif or Canela, set large and light with an italic for emphasis

cards.name: Fat face
cards.desc: A Didone pushed to its heaviest: huge black verticals with hairline joins. Made in the 1800s to be the loudest thing on the wall, now used for punchy editorial headlines.
cards.phrase: a fat face poster serif like Ultra Bodoni: ultra-heavy verticals with hairline thins, loud and theatrical

cards.name: Grotesque
cards.desc: The first sans serifs, from the 1800s and early 1900s. Slightly uneven and quirky, with some stroke contrast and a printed, workmanlike feel. Newspapers and posters still love them.
cards.phrase: a grotesque sans like Franklin Gothic or Akzidenz-Grotesk: slightly irregular, a little stroke contrast, industrial and workmanlike

cards.name: Neo-grotesque
cards.desc: The polished 1950s refinement: even strokes, closed shapes and a neutral, "no opinion" voice. The default for interfaces, signage and corporate design.
cards.phrase: a neutral neo-grotesque sans like Helvetica or Inter: even strokes, closed apertures, clean and unopinionated

cards.name: Geometric sans
cards.desc: Built from circles, triangles and straight lines: a perfectly round o, pointed A and M. Clean, modern and optimistic; it can feel cold or chic depending on the weight.
cards.phrase: a geometric sans like Futura: near-perfect circles, pointed apexes, modernist and optimistic

cards.name: Humanist sans
cards.desc: A sans with the bones of handwriting: open shapes, slight stroke variation and a true italic. Warm and very legible, which is why it is common on road signs and in interfaces.
cards.phrase: a humanist sans like Frutiger or Source Sans: open apertures, subtle calligraphic stroke, warm and highly legible

cards.name: Quirky grotesk
cards.desc: Today's startup and studio sans: a grotesque skeleton with a few odd details like ink traps, flat terminals or a strange G. Neutral enough for UI, with a wink.
cards.phrase: a contemporary grotesk with quirky details, like Space Grotesk or Söhne: neutral structure, idiosyncratic letterforms, tech-studio feel

cards.name: Rounded sans
cards.desc: Stroke ends and corners rounded off like a felt-tip marker. Approachable and playful: kids' products, games, wellness and friendly fintech.
cards.phrase: a rounded sans like VAG Rounded or Nunito: soft terminals, friendly and playful

cards.name: Condensed sans
cards.desc: Tall, narrow letters that fit big words in tight spaces. Urgent and loud in heavy weights, which is why sports, news tickers and movie posters lean on them.
cards.phrase: a heavy condensed sans like Bebas Neue or Druk: tall narrow all-caps letters, tight spacing, urgent and loud

cards.name: Extended sans
cards.desc: Letters stretched wide and set heavy. Feels expensive, futuristic or sporty depending on context: car brands, fashion, streetwear and tech launches.
cards.phrase: a wide extended sans like Monument Extended: stretched horizontal proportions, heavy weight, bold and futuristic

cards.name: Squared techno sans
cards.desc: Rounded-rectangle letters with flat sides, as if machined. Says space program, video game or 1970s science fiction.
cards.phrase: a squared techno sans like Eurostile or Microgramma: rounded-rectangle forms, flat sides, retro-futuristic sci-fi feel

cards.name: Monospace
cards.desc: Every character takes the same width, so columns line up. Essential for code and terminals, and a shorthand for "technical" when used for labels and numbers.
cards.phrase: a modern monospace like JetBrains Mono or IBM Plex Mono for code, data and small technical labels

cards.name: Typewriter
cards.desc: The look of a manual typewriter: monospaced slab letters, sometimes with uneven ink. Feels like a document, a screenplay, a dossier or a letter from someone.
cards.phrase: a typewriter face like Courier or American Typewriter, slightly uneven inked letters, like a typed document

cards.name: Formal script
cards.desc: Elegant joined letters from a pointed pen, with fine hairlines and swelling strokes. Weddings, invitations, certificates and old-world luxury.
cards.phrase: a formal copperplate script like Snell Roundhand: pointed-pen hairlines and swells, elegant and ceremonial

cards.name: Retro script
cards.aka: casual script, diner script, baseball script
cards.desc: A bouncy connected script with a mid-century feel, often with a swash underline. Diners, baseball jerseys, soda bottles and surf shops.
cards.phrase: a mid-century retro script like a 1950s diner sign or baseball jersey, connected and bouncy with a swash tail

cards.name: Brush script
cards.desc: Letters made with a loaded brush: fast, energetic strokes with uneven edges. Sporty, punchy and handmade.
cards.phrase: an energetic brush script with fast, slanted strokes and rough edges, handmade and punchy

cards.name: Handwriting
cards.desc: Fonts that look like everyday handwriting with a pen or marker. Personal, casual and honest; good for notes, annotations and asides, tiring for paragraphs.
cards.phrase: a casual handwritten font like Caveat for notes and annotations, as if jotted with a pen

cards.name: Blackletter
cards.aka: gothic script, Old English, Fraktur, textura
cards.desc: The dense, angular book hand of medieval Europe and Gutenberg's Bible. Reads as old, heavy and serious: newspaper mastheads, diplomas, metal bands and tattoo flash.
cards.phrase: a blackletter face like Fraktur or Old English: dense angular broken strokes, medieval and heavy

cards.name: Tuscan woodtype
cards.aka: Western type, circus type, saloon type
cards.desc: Decorative 1800s wood type with split, forked or bulging serifs. The instant signal of the Old West, circus posters and medicine-show playbills.
cards.phrase: Tuscan Western woodtype with forked, bulging serifs, like a 19th-century wanted poster or circus playbill

cards.name: Display face
cards.desc: A typeface designed only for big sizes, with a strong gimmick: layered, inline, shadowed or chunky. One word, once, at the top.
cards.phrase: one bold display face used only for the main title, paired with a plain text face for everything else

cards.name: Stencil
cards.desc: Letters with deliberate gaps where a stencil holds its middle pieces. Military, industrial, shipping crates and protest signs.
cards.phrase: a stencil typeface with bridged gaps in the letters, like spray-painted shipping crates or military gear

cards.name: Pixel / bitmap
cards.aka: 8-bit font, bitmap font, retro game font
cards.desc: Letters built from a visible square grid, like early computer screens and arcade machines. Instant nostalgia; set it at whole-pixel multiples so it stays crisp.
cards.phrase: a pixel bitmap font like Press Start 2P, crisp square pixels, 8-bit arcade style

cards.name: Variable font
cards.aka: variable axes, weight and width axes
cards.desc: One font file that slides continuously along axes like weight, width, optical size or slant, instead of shipping fixed styles. Lets you fine-tune and animate type.
cards.phrase: use a variable font and tune its axes (weight, width, optical size) instead of picking from fixed styles

cards.name: Garamond
cards.aka: Adobe Garamond, Garamond Premier, EB Garamond
cards.desc: Claude Garamond's 1500s roman, revived dozens of times. Graceful and slightly old-fashioned; the default book face of the twentieth century.
cards.phrase: Garamond (EB Garamond as the free version) for an elegant, literary book feel

cards.name: Baskerville
cards.desc: John Baskerville's 1757 face: crisp, high-contrast for its time, with a famous swashy italic Q and ampersand. Polite, trustworthy and very English.
cards.phrase: Baskerville (Libre Baskerville as the free version), crisp and trustworthy, with its italic ampersand used as an accent

cards.name: Bodoni and Didot
cards.desc: The two great Didones. Didot is the Vogue and Harper's Bazaar masthead; Bodoni is a little sturdier. Both say high fashion the instant they appear.
cards.phrase: Didot or Bodoni (Bodoni Moda as the free version) set large, like a Vogue cover

cards.name: Times New Roman
cards.desc: Made for The Times of London in 1932 to fit more words in a narrow column. Everywhere, which makes it feel default and official, sometimes in a good way.
cards.phrase: Times New Roman for a plain, official, newspaper-of-record feel

cards.name: Georgia
cards.desc: A serif drawn for low-resolution screens with a big x-height and sturdy serifs. Still one of the most readable serifs installed on nearly every computer.
cards.phrase: Georgia as a screen-friendly, universally installed body serif

cards.name: Clarendon
cards.desc: A heavy 1845 slab with soft, bracketed serifs and round ball terminals. Hearty and Americana: old Western posters, the Sony logo and the National Park Service signs.
cards.phrase: Clarendon-style bracketed slab serif (Roboto Slab Black as a free stand-in), hearty and Americana

cards.name: Trajan
cards.desc: Carol Twombly's 1989 face, traced from the inscription on Trajan's Column in Rome. So common on dramatic movie posters that it became a cliché.
cards.phrase: Trajan-style Roman capitals (Cinzel as the free version), widely letter-spaced, like an epic movie poster

cards.name: Cooper Black
cards.desc: Oswald Cooper's 1922 heavy soft serif. The sound of the 1970s: Pet Sounds, Garfield, Easy-Bake Oven and every lava-lamp-era ad.
cards.phrase: Cooper Black (Fraunces at its softest, heaviest setting as a free stand-in) for warm 1970s retro

cards.name: Playfair Display
cards.desc: A free, high-contrast transitional display serif with a lively italic. The most popular "elegant headline" font on the web, so it is safe but common.
cards.phrase: Playfair Display for elegant high-contrast headlines, with its italic for emphasis

cards.name: Helvetica
cards.desc: Swiss, 1957, and the most famous typeface in the world. Neutral, solid and corporate-cool: the New York subway, American Airlines, and decades of iOS.
cards.phrase: Helvetica (Inter as the free version), tightly tracked in bold for a confident Swiss modernist voice

cards.name: Futura
cards.desc: Paul Renner's 1927 geometric sans, went to the Moon on the Apollo 11 plaque. Modern, confident and stylish; Wes Anderson and Supreme both swear by it.
cards.phrase: Futura (Jost as the free version), geometric and confident, in bold caps

cards.name: Gill Sans
cards.desc: Eric Gill's 1928 humanist sans, "the Helvetica of England". Classic British: the BBC, Penguin Books and the old London railways.
cards.phrase: Gill Sans (or a humanist free alternative like Source Sans) for a classic British, slightly literary sans

cards.name: Frutiger
cards.desc: Adrian Frutiger's 1976 face, designed for signs at Charles de Gaulle airport so it reads at a glance from far away. Clear and friendly; healthcare and transit love it.
cards.phrase: Frutiger-style humanist sans (Source Sans as a free stand-in), clear and friendly like airport signage

cards.name: DIN
cards.desc: The German industrial standard font for road signs and engineering drawings. Rational, square-shouldered and technical; also great for numbers on dashboards.
cards.phrase: DIN (Barlow as a free stand-in), engineered and technical, especially for numbers

cards.name: Gotham
cards.desc: Inspired by New York building signs, made famous by the 2008 Obama campaign. All-American, confident and wide-shouldered.
cards.phrase: Gotham (Montserrat as the free version), wide, confident all-caps sans

cards.name: Franklin Gothic
cards.desc: Morris Fuller Benton's 1902 American grotesque. Heavy, newsy and no-nonsense: the face of headlines, comics covers and protest signs.
cards.phrase: Franklin Gothic (Libre Franklin as the free version), heavy and newsy

cards.name: Impact
cards.desc: An ultra-heavy condensed sans installed on every computer, famous as white text with a black outline on image macros. Loud, cheap and instantly internet.
cards.phrase: Impact-style meme text: ultra-heavy condensed white caps with a thick black outline, top and bottom of the image

cards.name: Comic Sans
cards.desc: Made in 1994 for a cartoon dog in Microsoft Bob. Mocked by designers, but genuinely approachable and helpful for some dyslexic readers. Use it on purpose or not at all.
cards.phrase: Comic Sans (or Comic Neue), deliberately casual and goofy

cards.name: Inter
cards.desc: Rasmus Andersson's free neo-grotesque tuned for screens: tall x-height, lots of OpenType features, a display cut for big sizes. The most common font in modern web apps.
cards.phrase: Inter for UI and body text, with Inter Display or tighter tracking for large headings, and tabular numbers in data

cards.name: San Francisco (SF Pro)
cards.aka: system-ui on Apple, SF Pro, SF Compact, New York
cards.desc: Apple's system font on every device since 2015, with automatic optical sizes. Using it makes an app feel native to iPhone and Mac.
cards.phrase: the system font (SF Pro via -apple-system / .body text styles) so it feels native on Apple platforms

cards.name: Roboto
cards.aka: Roboto Flex, Google Sans (Google's brand face)
cards.desc: Android's system font since 2011 and Material Design's default. Mechanical skeleton with open curves; reads as Google.
cards.phrase: Roboto (the Android/Material default) or the device system font on Android

cards.name: IBM Plex
cards.aka: Plex Sans, Plex Serif, Plex Mono
cards.desc: IBM's free open-source superfamily: sans, serif, mono and condensed that share one skeleton. Engineered, slightly quirky, and very good at technical writing.
cards.phrase: the IBM Plex superfamily: Plex Sans for UI and text, Plex Mono for code and labels, Plex Serif for long reading

cards.name: Verdana
cards.desc: Matthew Carter's 1996 screen sans: very wide, very open, generous spacing. Extremely legible at tiny sizes; it feels like the early 2000s web.
cards.phrase: Verdana for a wide, highly legible early-web feel

cards.name: System font stack
cards.desc: Not one font but an instruction: use whatever the reader's device uses (SF Pro on Apple, Segoe UI on Windows, Roboto on Android). Zero download and feels native everywhere.
cards.phrase: the native system font stack (system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif) so text loads instantly and feels native

cards.name: Serif headlines, sans body
cards.desc: A characterful serif for headlines over a plain sans for text. The serif brings personality, the sans keeps reading easy. The most common pairing on the web.
cards.phrase: pair a characterful serif for headlines with a clean, neutral sans for body text and UI

cards.name: Sans headlines, serif body
cards.desc: A bold, tight sans for headlines with a comfortable serif for long text. Feels modern on top and literary underneath.
cards.phrase: bold, tightly tracked sans headlines over a comfortable serif for long body text

cards.name: One superfamily
cards.desc: Use a family that ships matching sans, serif and mono versions. They share proportions, so they mix without clashing. The safest way to get variety.
cards.phrase: one superfamily throughout (e.g. IBM Plex Sans, Serif and Mono) for variety that never clashes

cards.name: One family, many weights
cards.desc: No pairing at all: one versatile family, with hierarchy from weight, size and color. Clean, cohesive and hard to get wrong.
cards.phrase: a single type family for everything, with hierarchy from weight (800 / 600 / 400), size and color only

cards.name: Mono accents
cards.desc: A sans or serif for reading, plus a monospace for small labels, numbers, dates and tags. Instantly says "technical" or "made by engineers".
cards.phrase: small uppercase monospace labels for metadata, dates and tags alongside a clean sans for headings and text

cards.name: Display face + workhorse
cards.aka: hero font with a plain partner
cards.desc: One loud, decorative face used only for the title, with a quiet, neutral face for everything else. The plain partner makes the display face look intentional.
cards.phrase: one expressive display face only for the main title, everything else in a quiet neutral sans so the display face stands out

cards.name: Script accent
cards.desc: A formal or casual script for one or two words, paired with spaced-out serif or sans capitals. Romantic and elegant when the script stays small in quantity.
cards.phrase: a script used for one or two accent words only, paired with widely tracked serif capitals for everything else

cards.name: Contrast, not near-misses
cards.desc: The rule behind every pairing: combine faces that are clearly different (serif with sans, heavy with light) but share proportions like x-height. Two similar sans serifs look like a mistake.
cards.phrase: pair faces with clear contrast (different classification and weight) but similar x-height and proportions; never two near-identical faces

cards.name: Fraunces + Inter
cards.desc: A soft, characterful old-style display serif over the most neutral UI sans. Friendly, crafted and modern at once.
cards.phrase: Fraunces (soft, optical size up) for headlines with Inter for body and UI

cards.name: Instrument Serif + Inter
cards.desc: A light condensed display serif at huge sizes, with Inter doing the work underneath. The look of design studios and premium startups right now.
cards.phrase: Instrument Serif at very large sizes (with italic accents) for headlines, Inter for everything else

cards.name: Garamond + Futura
cards.desc: A Renaissance serif with a 1920s geometric sans. Elegant and literate, with crisp modern labels. A favorite of book designers and museums.
cards.phrase: Garamond (EB Garamond) for text and headlines, Futura (Jost) in spaced capitals for labels and navigation

cards.name: Libre Baskerville + Libre Franklin
cards.desc: A trustworthy transitional serif with a sturdy American grotesque. Feels like a serious publication: clear, credible and unfussy.
cards.phrase: Libre Baskerville for headlines and body, Libre Franklin bold for kickers, bylines and UI

cards.name: Bodoni Moda + Work Sans
cards.desc: High-contrast Didone headlines and a light, wide-open grotesque in spaced caps. Luxurious and editorial.
cards.phrase: Bodoni Moda for large headlines, Work Sans light in tracked capitals for navigation and captions

cards.name: Bebas Neue + Inter
cards.desc: Tall condensed caps for punchy headlines, Inter for everything else. Energetic and direct; good for events, sports and fitness.
cards.phrase: Bebas Neue in big uppercase for headlines and numbers, Inter for body and UI

cards.name: Oswald + Newsreader
cards.desc: Condensed gothic headlines over a refined text serif. Has the urgency of a front page and the readability of a long feature.
cards.phrase: Oswald bold uppercase headlines with Newsreader for body text

cards.name: Cinzel + EB Garamond
cards.desc: Roman capitals for titles and a Renaissance text face for reading. Feels epic, historical or mythic: fantasy novels, games, wineries.
cards.phrase: Cinzel capitals for titles with EB Garamond for body text, epic and historical

cards.name: Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono
cards.desc: A quirky contemporary grotesk with a programmer's mono. Technical, a bit playful, very at home on developer product sites.
cards.phrase: Space Grotesk for headings and body, JetBrains Mono for code, labels and numbers

cards.name: Syne + Inter
cards.desc: An eccentric, wide, avant-garde display sans with a quiet partner. Arty and experimental without becoming unreadable.
cards.phrase: Syne extra-bold for headlines, Inter for text, an experimental art-gallery feel

cards.name: Rye + Courier Prime
cards.desc: Western woodtype for the title, typewriter for the details. Dusty, cinematic Americana: bands, barbecue joints, outdoor brands.
cards.phrase: Rye Western woodtype for the title, Courier Prime for details, dusty frontier Americana

cards.name: Shrikhand + Nunito
cards.desc: A fat, italic, 70s-flavored display face with a rounded sans. Cheerful and warm: cafés, ice cream, kids' brands.
cards.phrase: Shrikhand for headlines and Nunito for text, cheerful retro friendliness

cards.name: Modular type scale
cards.aka: type ramp, size scale, major third, perfect fourth
cards.desc: A fixed set of sizes where each step is the last one multiplied by a ratio (1.25 is a "major third", 1.333 a "perfect fourth"). Sizes stop being arbitrary and the page feels related.
cards.phrase: a modular type scale with a 1.25 ratio from a 16px base (13, 16, 20, 25, 31, 39, 49px), and only those sizes

cards.name: Type roles
cards.aka: text styles, display / headline / title / body / label
cards.desc: Name text by its job, not its size: display, headline, title, body, label and caption. Every piece of text gets one role, and each role has one fixed style.
cards.phrase: define named type roles (display, headline, title, body, label, caption), each with a fixed size, weight, line height and tracking, and use only those

cards.name: Eyebrow
cards.desc: A short, small label above a headline, often uppercase and letter-spaced or in an accent color. It says what section or topic you're in before the headline says what it's about.
cards.phrase: a small uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow label in the accent color above each section headline

cards.name: Deck
cards.desc: The one or two sentences between a headline and the article, set larger than body text. It sells the story and tells skimmers what they'll get.
cards.phrase: under each headline, a one-to-two sentence deck set about 1.3× body size in a lighter color

cards.name: Dramatic scale contrast
cards.desc: A huge headline next to small, quiet text, with little in between. Skipping the middle sizes makes the page feel confident and editorial.
cards.phrase: dramatic scale contrast: one very large headline (8–10× body size) and small body text, no middle sizes

cards.name: Hierarchy without size
cards.aka: weight and color hierarchy, dense UI type
cards.desc: In dense interfaces, keep sizes close together and use weight and color (dark, mid gray, light gray) to rank text. More fits on screen and it still scans.
cards.phrase: in dense UI, keep text within 2–3 sizes and create hierarchy with weight and three text colors (primary, secondary, tertiary)

cards.name: Big number
cards.desc: A single figure set huge, with a small label underneath. The number is the headline.
cards.phrase: key figures set as big numbers (display size, tight tracking, tabular figures) with a small label underneath

cards.name: Metadata line
cards.desc: Small, muted supporting facts (author, date, read time, category) on one line with separators like · or |. It sits close to the thing it describes.
cards.phrase: a single small, muted metadata line (author · date · read time) separated by middle dots, placed tight under the title

cards.name: Line length
cards.aka: measure, characters per line, max-width in ch
cards.desc: Comfortable lines hold about 45 to 75 characters. Longer lines make the eye lose its place; shorter ones chop the rhythm. On the web, cap the width with max-width: 65ch.
cards.phrase: body text limited to about 65 characters per line (max-width: 65ch), even on wide screens

cards.name: Line height
cards.desc: Space between lines. Body text wants about 1.4 to 1.6 times the font size; big headlines want much tighter, around 1.0 to 1.15, or they fall apart.
cards.phrase: line height 1.5–1.6 for body text, 1.05–1.15 for large headlines

cards.name: Letter-spacing
cards.desc: Uniform space added or removed between all letters. Tighten big headlines slightly; add space to small uppercase labels; leave body text alone.
cards.phrase: tighten large headings (about -0.02em to -0.04em), loosen small uppercase labels (+0.08em to +0.15em), leave body text at 0

cards.name: Ragged vs. justified
cards.aka: flush left, rag right, full justification, rivers
cards.desc: Flush-left text with a ragged right edge is the safe default on screens. Justified text looks formal in print, but without hyphenation it opens "rivers" of white space.
cards.phrase: flush-left, ragged-right body text; only justify with hyphenation turned on (hyphens: auto)

cards.name: Balanced headlines
cards.desc: Headlines broken into lines of similar length, instead of a full line and a lonely last word. Browsers now do it with one CSS line.
cards.phrase: balanced line breaks on headings (text-wrap: balance) so multi-line headlines have even lines

cards.name: No widows or orphans
cards.desc: A paragraph shouldn't end with one short word alone on its last line, and a heading shouldn't be stranded at the bottom of a column. Small fix, noticeably more polished.
cards.phrase: avoid single-word last lines in paragraphs (text-wrap: pretty or a non-breaking space) and never leave a heading at the bottom of a column

cards.name: Vertical rhythm
cards.desc: All line heights and spaces are multiples of one base unit (often 4 or 8px), so text in neighboring columns lines up and the page feels calm.
cards.phrase: a consistent vertical rhythm: line heights and margins all multiples of an 8px base unit

cards.name: Fluid type
cards.desc: Headline sizes that grow smoothly with the screen between a minimum and a maximum, instead of jumping at breakpoints. One line of CSS.
cards.phrase: fluid type for headings with CSS clamp() (e.g. clamp(2rem, 5vw + 1rem, 4.5rem)) so they scale smoothly from phone to desktop

cards.name: Paragraph spacing or indents
cards.desc: Separate paragraphs with a blank space (web convention) or a first-line indent (book convention), but never both.
cards.phrase: separate paragraphs with a first-line indent of 1.5em and no extra space, like a printed book

cards.name: Drop cap
cards.desc: An oversized first letter that drops down three or four lines into the opening paragraph. Signals "the story starts here" with old-book ceremony.
cards.phrase: open the article with a three-line drop cap in the display serif (CSS initial-letter: 3)

cards.name: Pull quote
cards.desc: A striking line lifted from the text and set big in the middle of the article to catch skimmers. Usually with large quotation marks or rules above and below.
cards.phrase: pull quotes set large in the italic display serif, with an oversized opening quotation mark and thin rules above and below

cards.name: Small-caps lead-in
cards.aka: run-in caps, opening words in caps
cards.desc: The first few words of an article or section set in small capitals, easing the reader from the headline into the text.
cards.phrase: start each section with its first three to five words in letter-spaced small caps

cards.name: Hanging punctuation
cards.desc: Opening quotation marks and bullets pushed into the margin so the letters, not the punctuation, line up with the text edge. Subtle, but the edge looks cleaner.
cards.phrase: hang opening quotation marks and bullets outside the text block so the letters align with the left edge

cards.name: Sidenotes
cards.desc: Notes in the margin beside the line they refer to, instead of footnotes at the bottom. Readers glance over without losing their place.
cards.phrase: sidenotes in the right margin aligned with their reference (Tufte style), collapsing to tap-to-expand notes on phones

cards.name: Captions & credits
cards.desc: Small text under an image that says what it shows, with the photographer credited in an even smaller or lighter style. Often in the sans of a serif page.
cards.phrase: image captions in a small sans, with a short bold lead-in and the credit in small caps or a lighter color

cards.name: Running heads & folios
cards.desc: Small repeated text at the top or bottom of each page: the book or chapter title and the page number. Makes a document feel like a real publication.
cards.phrase: running heads with the chapter title in small spaced caps at the top of each page, and folios (page numbers) at the outer bottom corner

cards.name: Section break
cards.desc: A small ornament between sections of text, like three spaced asterisks or a fleuron, marking a shift in time or scene.
cards.phrase: mark section breaks with a centered dinkus (three spaced asterisks) instead of a heading

cards.name: Readable body size
cards.desc: Body text at least 16px on the web and 17pt on iOS (the system default), larger for long reading. Small text is the most common reason a design feels hard to use.
cards.phrase: body text at least 16px (18–20px for long reading), nothing under 12px, and form inputs at 16px or more so mobile Safari doesn't zoom

cards.name: Text contrast
cards.desc: Text needs enough contrast against its background: 4.5 to 1 for body text, 3 to 1 for large text. Pale gray on white is the classic failure.
cards.phrase: all text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text), including placeholder and secondary text

cards.name: Caps and italics in small doses
cards.desc: All caps and italics are for a few words: labels, emphasis, titles. Whole paragraphs in either are slower to read and feel like shouting or whispering.
cards.phrase: use all caps only for short labels (with added letter-spacing) and italics only for emphasis and titles, never for whole paragraphs

cards.name: Respect text size settings
cards.aka: Dynamic Type, rem units, font scaling
cards.desc: People enlarge text in their device settings. Use rem units on the web, Dynamic Type on iOS and sp on Android so the layout grows with them instead of breaking.
cards.phrase: support user text scaling (rem on web, Dynamic Type on iOS, sp on Android) and make sure layouts reflow up to 200% text size

cards.name: Legibility-first fonts
cards.desc: Fonts designed so similar letters can't be confused: I l 1, O 0, rn and m. Helps low-vision readers and anyone reading codes, serial numbers or medication names.
cards.phrase: a legibility-first font like Atkinson Hyperlegible, with clearly distinct I/l/1 and O/0 shapes

cards.name: Fast font loading
cards.desc: Web fonts are downloads. Load as few files as possible, preload the main one, show fallback text immediately (font-display: swap), and tune the fallback so the page doesn't jump when the font arrives.
cards.phrase: load at most two font families as variable WOFF2 files, preload the body font, use font-display: swap, and size-adjust the fallback font to avoid layout shift

cards.name: Free vs. licensed fonts
cards.aka: OFL, Google Fonts, Adobe Fonts, font licensing
cards.desc: Famous fonts like Helvetica, Futura and Gotham need a paid license to use on a website or app. Fonts under the SIL Open Font License (everything on Google Fonts) are free for any use.
cards.phrase: use only free, open-licensed fonts (Google Fonts or Fontshare), and name the closest free alternative for any commercial typeface

cards.name: Baseline, x-height, cap height
cards.desc: Letters sit on the baseline. The x-height is the height of lowercase x; cap height is the height of capitals; ascenders (h, d) rise above and descenders (p, g) drop below.
cards.phrase: a typeface with a generous x-height and short descenders so it stays readable at small sizes

cards.name: Large vs. small x-height
cards.desc: At the same font size, a font with a large x-height looks bigger and reads better on screens; a small x-height looks more elegant and classical.
cards.phrase: choose a typeface with a large x-height for UI and small sizes

cards.name: Stroke contrast
cards.desc: How much a letter's strokes vary between thick and thin. Low contrast is sturdy and readable small; high contrast is dramatic and elegant large.
cards.phrase: high stroke contrast with hairline thins, only at display sizes

cards.name: Serif shapes
cards.desc: Serifs come in kinds: bracketed (curving into the stem), hairline (thin and unbracketed), slab (blocky), and wedge (triangular). Each sets a different tone.
cards.phrase: a serif with soft bracketed serifs (or: hairline / slab / wedge serifs)

cards.name: Open vs. closed apertures
cards.desc: The aperture is the opening in letters like c, e, a and s. Open apertures stay legible small and at a glance; closed ones look tight and uniform.
cards.phrase: a sans with open apertures for legibility at small sizes and at a distance

cards.name: Terminals
cards.aka: ball terminal, teardrop, flat terminal, ink trap
cards.desc: How a stroke ends without a serif: a round ball or teardrop (classic and lively), a flat cut (modern), or with ink traps, notches carved into joins.
cards.phrase: a serif with ball terminals on a, c, f, r and y for a lively classical feel

cards.name: True italic vs. oblique
cards.desc: A true italic has redrawn, cursive shapes (a single-story a, a curly f); an oblique is the upright letters simply slanted. Serifs usually have true italics; many sans use obliques.
cards.phrase: a typeface with a true cursive italic for emphasis, not a slanted roman

cards.name: Weight range
cards.desc: Font weights run from 100 (thin or hairline) through 400 (regular) and 700 (bold) to 900 (black). Name numbers, not "a bit bolder".
cards.phrase: headlines at weight 800, subheads at 600, body at 400, captions at 400 in a lighter color

cards.name: Width
cards.desc: Many families come in widths from compressed to extended. Narrow widths fit more; wide widths feel calm and luxurious or loud and sporty.
cards.phrase: the condensed width of the family for headlines so long titles fit on one line

cards.name: Optical size
cards.aka: opsz, display vs. text cuts, caption cuts
cards.desc: Versions of a face drawn for a specific size: text cuts are sturdier and looser for small sizes, display cuts are finer and tighter for big ones. Variable fonts can adjust automatically.
cards.phrase: use optical sizes: the display cut for headlines and the text cut for body (font-optical-sizing: auto with a variable font)

cards.name: Tabular figures
cards.desc: Digits that all share one width, so numbers line up in columns and don't jiggle when they change. Essential for tables, prices, timers and dashboards.
cards.phrase: tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) for every table, price, timer and changing number

cards.name: Old-style figures
cards.desc: Numbers with ascenders and descenders, like lowercase letters, so they blend into running text instead of shouting. Lining figures are cap-height and suit tables and all-caps.
cards.phrase: old-style figures in running text (oldstyle-nums), lining figures in tables and headings

cards.name: True small caps
cards.desc: Capitals drawn at lowercase height with matching stroke weight, for acronyms, labels and lead-ins. Faked small caps (shrunken capitals) look thin and spindly.
cards.phrase: true small caps (font-variant-caps: all-small-caps) for acronyms like NASA and HTML in running text

cards.name: Ligatures
cards.aka: liga, dlig, fi fl ffi, discretionary ligatures
cards.desc: Pairs of letters merged into one shape so they don't collide, like fi and fl. Discretionary ligatures (ct, st) are decorative and old-fashioned; coding fonts have their own for => and !=.
cards.phrase: standard ligatures on for body text; discretionary ligatures (ct, st) only in the display title for an antique touch

cards.name: Fractions & superscripts
cards.desc: Real fractions (½, 3⁄4), properly drawn superscripts for footnotes and ordinals (1st), and subscripts for chemistry, instead of tiny shrunken digits.
cards.phrase: true diagonal fractions (diagonal-fractions) in recipes and measurements, and real superscripts for footnotes and ordinals

cards.name: Slashed zero & clear glyphs
cards.desc: A zero with a slash or dot so it can't be read as O, plus distinct I, l and 1. Matters for codes, passwords, keys and anything people copy by hand.
cards.phrase: slashed zeros (slashed-zero) and clearly distinct I/l/1 in codes, API keys and reference numbers

cards.name: Stylistic alternates
cards.desc: Optional alternate letter shapes built into a font, like a single-story a, a straight-legged R or a simpler g. They change a font's personality without changing fonts.
cards.phrase: enable the font's stylistic alternates (e.g. single-story a and g) for a friendlier, more geometric look

cards.name: Kerning
cards.desc: Spacing adjustments for specific letter pairs, like A and V or T and o, that would otherwise look gappy. Always on for text; check it by eye on big logos and headlines.
cards.phrase: kerning on everywhere, and hand-check letter pairs in the logo and largest headlines

cards.name: Refined underlines
cards.desc: Link underlines set a little below the baseline, at a deliberate thickness, skipping descenders. A tiny detail that makes links feel designed.
cards.phrase: link underlines with text-underline-offset: 0.2em, 1px thickness in a muted color, thickening on hover, and skip-ink on

cards.name: Oversized hero type
cards.desc: A headline so large it spans the whole width of the page and replaces the hero image. Bold and confident; works best with few words.
cards.phrase: an oversized hero headline that spans the full viewport width (font-size around 12–18vw), tight tracking and leading, no hero image

cards.name: Stacked headline
cards.aka: tight stack, poster stack, negative leading
cards.desc: Short words stacked on separate lines in heavy condensed caps, with line height under 1 so the lines nearly touch. A dense block of type with poster energy.
cards.phrase: a stacked headline: one or two words per line in heavy condensed uppercase, line height about 0.85 so lines nearly touch

cards.name: Italic serif accent
cards.desc: A sans headline with one or two words swapped into an elegant italic serif. Adds warmth and a hint of luxury; one of the most recognizable looks of the 2020s.
cards.phrase: a sans-serif headline with one key word set in an italic serif (like Instrument Serif Italic) for emphasis

cards.name: Outlined type
cards.desc: Letters drawn as outlines with transparent insides, often alternated with solid lines. Lighter than solid bold type and very graphic.
cards.phrase: alternate solid and outlined lines in the headline (outlined using -webkit-text-stroke, transparent fill)

cards.name: Image-filled type
cards.aka: knockout text, clipping mask, background-clip: text
cards.desc: Huge, heavy letters filled with a photo or gradient, as if cut out of the picture. Works only with very bold faces and short words.
cards.phrase: a short, ultra-bold headline filled with a photo through the letterforms (background-clip: text)

cards.name: Gradient text
cards.desc: Text filled with a smooth color gradient instead of one color. Very common on tech and AI sites; keep it to a word or two and check contrast.
cards.phrase: one key phrase in the headline filled with a two- or three-color gradient (background-clip: text); the rest solid

cards.name: Highlighter marks
