cards.desc: A word underlined or highlighted as if by hand with a marker: a swash, circle or highlighter stripe behind the text. Friendly and conversational.
cards.phrase: emphasize one word in the headline with a hand-drawn marker highlight or a loose underline swash behind it

cards.name: Strikethrough correction
cards.desc: A word struck through and replaced with a better one, like an edit in progress. Witty and human when it makes a point.
cards.phrase: a headline that strikes through one word and replaces it with another, as a visible edit

cards.name: Vertical type
cards.desc: Text turned 90 degrees running up the side of a page or image, or stacked vertically. Adds an editorial, poster-like edge; keep it short.
cards.phrase: a short vertical label running up the left edge (writing-mode: vertical-rl, rotated 180°), in small tracked caps

cards.name: Text on a path
cards.aka: circular text, arched type, badge text
cards.desc: Text set along a curve: around a circle like a stamp or badge, or arching over an image. Classic for seals, logos and vintage labels.
cards.phrase: a circular badge with the name set around the edge on a circle path (SVG textPath) and a small mark in the center

cards.name: Type over image
cards.aka: layered type, text behind subject, overlap
cards.desc: A headline that overlaps a photo, or sits partly behind the subject (letters disappear behind a person's head). Creates depth and a magazine-cover feel.
cards.phrase: a magazine-cover layout where the masthead sits partly behind the subject, giving depth

cards.name: Wide-tracked capitals
cards.desc: Short words in capitals with very generous letter-spacing. Quiet, expensive and calm; the default for luxury logos and fashion navigation.
cards.phrase: the wordmark and navigation in widely letter-spaced capitals (letter-spacing about 0.3em), light weight

cards.name: Cropped giant letters
cards.aka: type as texture, bleed type, oversize crop
cards.desc: Letters blown up so large they bleed off the edges, becoming abstract shapes. Recognizable as type, used as pattern or backdrop.
cards.phrase: one or two giant letters cropped off the edges of the frame as a graphic backdrop behind smaller text

cards.name: Forced-justified block
cards.desc: Each line set at a different size so every line fills exactly the same width, making a solid rectangle of type. A classic woodtype and Swiss poster move.
cards.phrase: a headline block where each line is sized to fill the same width exactly, forming a solid rectangle

cards.name: Repeated echo
cards.desc: The same word repeated several times in a column, fading or outlining as it repeats. Rhythmic and hypnotic; common in music and event graphics.
cards.phrase: the title repeated five times in a column, the center line solid and the others fading out or outlined

cards.name: 3D extruded
cards.desc: Letters with solid depth behind them, made from many stacked shadows, like signs cut from thick wood or retro video game titles.
cards.phrase: chunky 3D extruded letters with a solid darker-color extrusion down and to the right (stacked text-shadows)

cards.name: Offset shadow
cards.aka: hard shadow, misregistered shadow, drop shadow line
cards.desc: A flat, crisp copy of the text offset behind it in a second color, with no blur. Retro and poster-printed; very common in 70s and Y2K styles.
cards.phrase: a hard offset shadow behind the headline: a flat second-color copy shifted down and right, no blur

cards.name: Neon glow
cards.desc: Text with a bright core and a soft colored glow around it, on a dark background, like it emits light. The glow is layered text-shadows.
cards.phrase: neon glow text: a near-white core with layered pink and magenta glows on a near-black background, a subtle flicker

cards.name: Chrome / metallic
cards.desc: Letters filled with a mirror-like gradient (sky blue to horizon line to dark ground), with highlights and a bevel. Pure 1980s heavy-metal, sci-fi and arcade.
cards.phrase: chrome metallic lettering: a mirror gradient from pale sky blue to a sharp horizon line to dark brown, with a thin bright outline and a lens-flare highlight

cards.name: Glitch / RGB split
cards.desc: Text split into offset red and cyan copies, sometimes sliced and jittered, as if a screen or video signal is breaking up. Tech, gaming, electronic music.
cards.phrase: a glitch effect on the title: offset red and cyan copies (RGB split) with occasional horizontal slice jitter

cards.name: Letterpress / debossed
cards.desc: Text that looks pressed into or raised out of the surface, using a light highlight on one edge and a shadow on the other. Tactile and crafted.
cards.phrase: debossed letterpress text pressed into thick cotton paper: a soft inner shadow above and a light highlight below

cards.name: Distressed texture
cards.desc: Letters with speckled, worn or broken edges, like old ink on paper or paint on wood. Adds age, grit and authenticity.
cards.phrase: distressed, worn-ink texture on the display type, with speckled gaps and rough edges like an old print

cards.name: Marquee ticker
cards.aka: scrolling text, ticker tape, infinite marquee
cards.desc: A line of large text scrolling sideways forever, like a stock ticker or a news crawl. Energetic, a bit retro; very common on fashion and event sites.
cards.phrase: an infinite horizontal marquee of large uppercase text separated by ✦ marks, scrolling slowly, paused for reduced-motion users

cards.name: Typewriter reveal
cards.desc: Text that appears one character at a time behind a blinking cursor, as if being typed. Good for a short hero line or a terminal demo.
cards.phrase: the hero line types itself out character by character with a blinking block cursor, once, then rests

cards.name: Variable weight motion
cards.aka: animated weight, hover morph, breathing type
cards.desc: A variable font animating its weight or width, so letters swell and slim as you hover, scroll or listen. Only possible with variable fonts.
cards.phrase: animate the headline's variable weight axis from thin to black on hover (or with scroll), smoothly, using a variable font

cards.name: Staggered reveal
cards.aka: line-by-line reveal, split text, mask reveal
cards.desc: Lines or words slide up into view one after another from behind an invisible mask as the page loads or scrolls. Polished, cinematic and very common.
cards.phrase: headline lines slide up from behind a mask one after another (80ms stagger, ease-out), once on load

cards.name: Rotating word
cards.aka: word swap, cycling headline, text loop
cards.desc: A headline where one word cycles through options ("Built for designers / engineers / founders"). Says a lot in one line.
cards.phrase: one word in the headline cycles through three alternatives every 2.5 seconds with a vertical slide

cards.name: Victorian playbill
cards.desc: Centered lines of many different wood typefaces at different sizes, with rules, stars and pointing hands, crammed onto one sheet. Loud, theatrical and handmade.
cards.phrase: a Victorian woodtype playbill: centered lines mixing many typefaces (Tuscan, fat face, slab, condensed gothic) at different sizes, ornamental rules and stars, on aged cream paper

cards.name: Art Deco
cards.desc: Tall, thin, geometric capitals with sharp contrasts, often gold on black, with fan and sunburst ornaments. Glamorous, symmetrical and machine-age.
cards.phrase: Art Deco typography: tall thin geometric capitals, wide tracking, gold on black, symmetrical layout with sunburst and stepped ornaments

cards.name: Bauhaus
cards.desc: Geometric sans, often all lowercase, with primary colors and circles, squares and triangles. Rational, experimental and bold.
cards.phrase: Bauhaus typography: geometric lowercase sans, primary red, yellow and blue with black, circles and bars on an asymmetric grid

cards.name: Constructivism
cards.desc: Heavy condensed sans on strong diagonals, red and black on cream, with photomontage and bold bars. Urgent, political and dynamic.
cards.phrase: Constructivist typography: heavy condensed sans on sharp diagonals, red and black on cream, thick bars and dynamic angles

cards.name: Swiss / International Style
cards.desc: A neo-grotesque (Helvetica, Akzidenz), flush-left text on a strict grid, lots of white space, asymmetric layout, often with one red element. Objective and timeless.
cards.phrase: Swiss International Style: a neo-grotesque like Helvetica, flush-left ragged-right on a strict modular grid, asymmetric layout, generous white space, black and white with one red accent

cards.name: 60s psychedelic
cards.aka: Fillmore poster, acid lettering, hippie type
cards.desc: Hand-drawn lettering that swells, warps and fills every gap, in vibrating complementary colors. Hard to read on purpose.
cards.phrase: 1960s psychedelic poster lettering: swelling, warped letterforms filling the space, vibrating complementary colors like orange on purple

cards.name: 70s groovy
cards.desc: Soft fat serifs (Cooper Black) and bubbly display faces in orange, mustard and brown, with rainbow stripes and curves. Warm, mellow and nostalgic.
cards.phrase: 1970s groovy typography: soft heavy Cooper Black-style serifs, orange-mustard-brown palette, rounded rainbow stripes

cards.name: 80s synthwave
cards.desc: Chrome or neon italic type over a magenta-to-orange sunset and a glowing grid floor. Nostalgic for an 80s that never quite existed.
cards.phrase: 80s synthwave typography: chrome italic headline with a neon script subtitle, over a striped magenta-orange sunset and a glowing perspective grid

cards.name: 90s grunge
cards.aka: Ray Gun style, David Carson, deconstructed type
cards.desc: Distressed typewriter and mismatched fonts, overlapping, rotated and cut off, legibility deliberately broken. Raw and anti-design.
cards.phrase: 90s grunge typography in the style of David Carson: distressed typewriter and mismatched faces, overlapping and rotated words, deliberately broken legibility

cards.name: Y2K
cards.desc: Wide futuristic sans, bubbly chrome, iridescent gradients, tiny pixel captions and sparkle stars. Optimistic, shiny late-90s tech futurism, now back in fashion.
cards.phrase: Y2K typography: wide extended sans with iridescent chrome fill, sparkle stars, small pixel-font captions, pastel holographic background

cards.name: Web brutalism
cards.aka: brutalist web design, raw HTML aesthetic
cards.desc: Default-looking fonts (Times, Arial, monospace) at clashing sizes, visible borders, blue underlined links and raw grids. Honest, confrontational and anti-polish.
cards.phrase: brutalist web typography: Times New Roman and monospace at clashing sizes, raw black borders, default blue underlined links, no rounded corners or shadows

cards.name: Punk zine / ransom note
cards.desc: Letters cut from different magazines and pasted crookedly, with photocopied grain, tape and marker. Rebellious, DIY and urgent.
cards.phrase: punk zine ransom-note lettering: each letter cut from a different magazine and pasted crookedly, black and white photocopy grain, tape and marker scrawl

cards.name: Luxury fashion editorial
cards.desc: Huge Didone headlines with tight letters, tiny widely-spaced sans captions, and lots of empty space. Restraint is the luxury.
cards.phrase: luxury fashion editorial typography: a very large high-contrast Didone headline, tiny widely tracked sans captions, extreme white space

cards.name: Newspaper broadsheet
cards.aka: front page, old newspaper, broadsheet layout
cards.desc: A blackletter or bold serif masthead, rules between narrow justified columns, stacked headlines and datelines. Instantly says news, history or record.
cards.phrase: old newspaper front-page typography: blackletter masthead, thin and thick rules, narrow justified serif columns, condensed bold headlines and a dateline

cards.name: Western frontier
cards.desc: Tuscan and slab woodtype, sepia paper, stars and rope borders, typewriter details. Dusty, cinematic Americana; the natural voice of folk, country and outdoor brands.
cards.phrase: Western frontier typography: Tuscan woodtype headline, slab serif and typewriter details, sepia aged paper, stars and a rope border

cards.name: Modern tech minimal
cards.desc: One neutral sans in two or three weights, tight tracking on large headings, generous space, small mono labels and a single accent color. Calm, competent and current.
cards.phrase: modern tech-minimal typography: one neutral sans (Inter or Geist), tight negative tracking on headings, generous white space, small mono labels, one accent color

cards.name: Japanese poster
cards.desc: Vertical Japanese text alongside small horizontal Latin type, bold color fields and precise grids. Calm and graphic, with a sense of order.
cards.phrase: Japanese poster typography: large vertical Japanese headline set top to bottom, small horizontal Latin captions, a flat color field and precise grid

cards.name: Hand-painted sign
cards.aka: sign painting, gold leaf window lettering, shop sign
cards.desc: Lettering painted by a sign painter: gold leaf with dark outlines on shop windows, or painted script and block letters on walls and trucks. Warm, crafted and nostalgic.
cards.phrase: hand-painted gold-leaf sign lettering on a shop window: a script word over block capitals, black outline and drop shadow, slight brush imperfection

cards.name: Hand lettering
cards.desc: A short phrase drawn by hand as one composition, mixing script, caps and flourishes, with words sized to fit together. Personal and illustrative.
cards.phrase: a hand-lettered composition: the phrase drawn as one interlocking unit mixing bouncy script and tall caps, with small flourishes and banners

cards.name: Calligraphy
cards.aka: pointed pen, copperplate, Spencerian, broad nib
cards.desc: Writing as an art: a pointed pen makes swelling copperplate strokes, a broad nib makes italic or blackletter. Flourishes and ink on textured paper.
cards.phrase: pointed-pen copperplate calligraphy in black ink on textured cotton paper, with hairline flourishes and swelling downstrokes

cards.name: Brush lettering
cards.aka: brush pen, sumi brush, dry brush
cards.desc: Letters painted fast with a brush or brush pen, with visible dry-brush texture at the stroke ends. Energetic and expressive.
cards.phrase: expressive dry-brush lettering in black ink, fast slanted strokes with frayed bristle texture at the ends

cards.name: Chalkboard
cards.desc: Hand-drawn chalk letters on a dark slate board, with dusty edges, borders and little drawings. Café menus and specials boards.
cards.phrase: chalkboard lettering: dusty white and pastel chalk on a dark green-black slate, mixed hand-drawn styles with simple borders and doodles

cards.name: Neon sign
cards.desc: Glass tubes bent into script or block letters, glowing against a dark brick wall, sometimes with a flickering letter. Nightlife, motels and diners.
cards.phrase: a real neon sign: glowing pink and blue glass tubes bent into script lettering, mounted on a dark brick wall, soft light spill and one flickering letter

cards.name: Screen-printed poster
cards.aka: gig poster, silkscreen, two-color print, overprint
cards.desc: Flat ink in two or three colors, slightly misregistered so colors overlap where they shouldn't, with grain and paper texture. The look of concert and gig posters.
cards.phrase: a screen-printed gig poster: two flat ink colors (rust and navy) slightly misregistered with multiply overprint, paper grain, bold condensed type

cards.name: Marquee lights
cards.aka: bulb letters, cinema marquee, carnival sign
cards.desc: Big letters outlined with round light bulbs, like a theater marquee, a carnival or Las Vegas. Celebratory and showbiz.
cards.phrase: marquee bulb lettering: large letters outlined with rows of warm glowing light bulbs, against a dark night sky

cards.name: Carved inscription
cards.aka: engraved stone, chiseled letters, monument lettering
cards.desc: Roman capitals cut into stone with V-shaped grooves, lit from the side. Permanent, solemn and classical.
cards.phrase: Roman capitals carved into pale limestone with V-cut grooves, raking side light, weathered surface

cards.name: Embroidered patch
cards.desc: Lettering made of thread: satin-stitched letters with a merrowed edge on a patch, or fuzzy chenille varsity letters. Workwear, scouting and college merch.
cards.phrase: an embroidered patch with satin-stitched lettering and a thick merrowed border, visible thread texture, on canvas

cards.name: Rubber stamp
cards.desc: Bold caps in a border, stamped in red or blue ink at an angle, with uneven ink coverage. Official, urgent or archival.
cards.phrase: a red rubber-stamp mark at a slight angle: bold condensed caps inside a double border, uneven ink and worn gaps

cards.name: Split-flap board
cards.aka: Solari board, departure board, flip display
cards.desc: Letters on hinged flaps in little black tiles, like old train station and airport departure boards. Mechanical, travel-flavored and satisfying.
cards.phrase: split-flap departure board lettering: white uppercase characters on individual black flap tiles with a center seam, yellow headings

cards.name: Typewritten page
cards.desc: A sheet from a manual typewriter: uneven ink, slightly misaligned letters, strikeovers and handwritten corrections. Intimate, archival and literary.
cards.phrase: a typewritten page on aged paper: uneven ribbon ink, slightly jumping letters, a few x-ed out words and pencil corrections

cards.name: Quote the exact words
cards.desc: Put the words you want rendered in quotation marks and spell them exactly, including capitalization. Models treat quoted text as text to draw, not as an idea to illustrate.
cards.phrase: the poster reads "TALL PINES" in large letters and "LIVE AT THE GRANGE" underneath, spelled exactly as written

cards.name: Keep it to a few words
cards.desc: Image models spell one to five words reliably; long sentences come out garbled. Put the title in the image and add longer text afterwards in a design tool.
cards.phrase: only short text in the image: the title (one to four words) and nothing else; no paragraphs or small print

cards.name: Describe the look, not the font
cards.desc: Image models know styles better than font names. "Tall condensed white capitals with a slight distressed texture" works; "set in Druk Wide" usually doesn't.
cards.phrase: lettering described by its look: tall condensed sans-serif capitals, off-white, slightly distressed, tightly spaced

cards.name: Text as part of the scene
cards.desc: Say what the words are physically made of and where they live: painted on a barn, glowing in a motel window, carved over a door. Text that belongs to the scene looks far more natural than text floating on top.
cards.phrase: the words "NIGHT RIVER" painted in faded white capitals on the side of a weathered red barn, lit by a low evening sun

cards.name: Say where the text goes
cards.aka: text placement, layout in the prompt
cards.desc: Name the position and size: "large across the top third", "small, bottom right corner", "centered on the sign". Without it, models guess and often crowd the subject.
cards.phrase: the title large and centered across the top third, the subtitle small along the bottom edge, nothing covering the subject's face

cards.name: Leave room for type
cards.aka: negative space, copy space, text-free area
cards.desc: Generate the artwork without text, with a clean empty area reserved for it, then set the type yourself with real fonts. The most reliable way to get exact lettering on album covers and posters.
cards.phrase: no text in the image; leave a clean, uncluttered area of open sky in the top third for a title to be added later

cards.name: Cover title block
cards.aka: album cover type, poster title lockup
cards.desc: The standard cover arrangement: the artist name small or large, the title in a contrasting style, and maybe one tiny line of detail, locked together as one unit.
cards.phrase: a cover title lockup: the artist name in small tracked capitals above the album title in a large italic serif, locked together, bottom left

cards.name: Extreme wide shot
cards.aka: EWS, establishing shot, extreme long shot
cards.desc: The person is a tiny figure and the place is the subject. It says "where are we" and, often, "how alone are they".
cards.phrase: extreme wide shot, a tiny lone figure in a vast landscape, the place dominating the frame

cards.name: Wide shot
cards.desc: The whole person, head to toe, with plenty of space around them. You see what they are doing and where they are doing it.
cards.phrase: wide shot, the full figure small in the frame with the surroundings clearly visible

cards.name: Full shot
cards.desc: Head to toe, with the person filling the frame top to bottom. The standard for showing an outfit, a pose or a stance.
cards.phrase: full shot, head to toe, the figure filling the frame height

cards.name: Cowboy shot
cards.aka: medium long shot, American shot, three-quarter shot
cards.desc: From mid-thigh up. It was named for westerns, where it kept the gun holster in frame, and it still reads as confident and ready.
cards.phrase: cowboy shot, framed from mid-thigh up

cards.name: Medium shot
cards.desc: From the waist up. Close enough to read a face, wide enough to see gestures. The default for conversation and interviews.
cards.phrase: medium shot, framed from the waist up

cards.name: Medium close-up
cards.aka: MCU, chest shot, head and shoulders
cards.desc: From mid-chest up. The face carries the image, but there is still some body language and a hint of clothing.
cards.phrase: medium close-up, framed from mid-chest up

cards.name: Close-up
cards.desc: The face fills the frame, often cutting off the top of the head. Every small expression becomes the story.
cards.phrase: close-up portrait, the face filling the frame, top of the head slightly cropped

cards.name: Extreme close-up
cards.desc: A single detail: the eyes, a mouth, a fingertip. Intense and intimate, and it hides the context on purpose.
cards.phrase: extreme close-up on the eyes, filling the frame edge to edge

cards.name: Insert shot
cards.desc: A close look at an object or a hand doing something: a key turning, a letter, steam off a cup. It tells you what matters.
cards.phrase: insert shot, a tight detail of hands holding a steaming coffee cup, no face visible

cards.name: Two-shot
cards.desc: Two people sharing the frame, usually from the waist or knees up. The space between them says something about the relationship.
cards.phrase: two-shot, two people facing each other, framed from the waist up

cards.name: Over-the-shoulder
cards.desc: Shot from behind one person's shoulder toward someone facing them. The blurred shoulder in front puts you inside the conversation.
cards.phrase: over-the-shoulder shot, the foreground shoulder dark and out of focus, the person facing camera in sharp focus

cards.name: POV shot
cards.desc: The camera is someone's eyes. Their own hands, feet or handlebars appear at the bottom of the frame, reaching into the scene.
cards.phrase: first-person POV shot, the viewer's own hands holding a paper map at the bottom of the frame, the road ahead beyond it

cards.name: Eye level
cards.desc: The camera at the subject's eye height, looking straight at them. It feels honest and equal, which is why it's the default.
cards.phrase: eye-level camera angle, straight-on and neutral

cards.name: Low angle
cards.desc: The camera below the subject, looking up. People and buildings look taller, stronger and a little threatening.
cards.phrase: low-angle shot looking up at the subject, sky behind, verticals converging upward, heroic and imposing

cards.name: High angle
cards.desc: The camera above the subject, looking down. The subject looks smaller, more vulnerable or overwhelmed.
cards.phrase: high-angle shot looking down on the subject, ground filling the background, the figure small and vulnerable

cards.name: Bird's-eye view
cards.aka: overhead shot, top-down, God's-eye view, plan view
cards.desc: The camera points straight down from directly above. Everything becomes a flat pattern of shapes and shadows.
cards.phrase: bird's-eye view shot straight down from directly above, flat graphic composition, long shadows on the ground

cards.name: Worm's-eye view
cards.desc: The camera on the ground looking almost straight up. Trees, towers or people loom and lean toward a point in the sky.
cards.phrase: worm's-eye view from ground level looking straight up, tall shapes converging toward the sky

cards.name: Dutch angle
cards.aka: Dutch tilt, canted angle, oblique angle
cards.desc: The camera is rolled sideways so the horizon slants. It signals that something is off: unease, madness, a world out of balance.
cards.phrase: Dutch angle, the camera tilted about 20 degrees so the horizon slants, uneasy and off-balance

cards.name: Aerial shot
cards.desc: Taken from a drone, plane or helicopter high above. The landscape becomes a map of textures, roads and coastlines.
cards.phrase: aerial drone photograph from high above, the landscape reduced to patterns of texture and color

cards.name: Flat lay
cards.aka: knolling, top-down still life, overhead product shot
cards.desc: Objects arranged on a surface and shot from straight above. Knolling is the strict version, where everything is lined up at right angles.
cards.phrase: flat lay, objects arranged neatly at right angles on a plain surface, shot straight down, soft even shadows

cards.name: Rule of thirds
cards.desc: Picture a tic-tac-toe grid over the frame and put the subject on one of the lines or crossings instead of the center. It feels natural and leaves room for the scene.
cards.phrase: rule-of-thirds composition, the subject on the left third line, horizon on the lower third

cards.name: Centered symmetry
cards.aka: symmetrical composition, central framing, one-point perspective
cards.desc: The subject dead center with the two halves of the frame mirroring each other. Formal, calm and a little uncanny.
cards.phrase: perfectly centered symmetrical composition, one-point perspective, the subject dead center

cards.name: Leading lines
cards.desc: Roads, rails, fences or shorelines that run from the edge of the frame toward the subject and pull the eye along with them.
cards.phrase: strong leading lines from the foreground converging on the subject

cards.name: Negative space
cards.desc: A small subject surrounded by a large empty area of sky, water, wall or snow. The emptiness becomes part of the meaning.
cards.phrase: minimalist composition with vast negative space, a small subject in the lower corner of an empty frame

cards.name: Frame within a frame
cards.desc: A doorway, window, arch or gap in the trees surrounds the subject inside the picture, adding depth and pointing straight at it.
cards.phrase: frame within a frame, the subject seen through a dark stone archway

cards.name: Foreground layering
cards.aka: depth layering, foreground interest, foreground / midground / background
cards.desc: Something close to the lens, the subject in the middle, and scenery behind. Three planes make a flat picture feel deep.
cards.phrase: layered depth: out-of-focus foreground grasses, the subject sharp in the midground, mountains fading in the background

cards.name: Lead room
cards.desc: Leave space in front of where the subject is looking or moving. Without it, they seem to bump into the edge of the frame.
cards.phrase: generous lead room, the subject on the left facing right into open space

cards.name: Low horizon
cards.desc: Where you put the horizon decides what the picture is about. Low horizon: the sky is the story. High horizon: the land, water or road is.
cards.phrase: very low horizon, a vast dramatic sky filling four fifths of the frame

cards.name: Mirror reflection
cards.desc: A still lake, puddle or window doubles the scene, usually with the horizon or waterline across the middle of the frame.
cards.phrase: mirror-still water reflecting the scene, the waterline across the center of the frame

cards.name: Ultra-wide (14–16mm)
cards.desc: An enormous field of view. Things near the lens look huge, things far away shrink to nothing, and lines bend toward the edges. Dramatic and a little distorted.
cards.phrase: shot on an ultra-wide 14mm lens, exaggerated perspective, the foreground looming and the background tiny

cards.name: Wide (24mm)
cards.desc: Wide enough to show a whole room or street around the subject, with some perspective stretch but less than an ultra-wide.
cards.phrase: shot on a 24mm wide-angle lens, the subject in context with lots of environment, deep perspective

cards.name: 35mm
cards.desc: Slightly wider than the human eye. It feels like you are standing right there, which is why street and documentary photographers love it.
cards.phrase: shot on a 35mm lens, natural documentary perspective

cards.name: 50mm (normal)
cards.aka: normal lens, nifty fifty, standard lens
cards.desc: Roughly matches how big things look to the eye. Honest and undistorted, the classic all-purpose lens.
cards.phrase: shot on a 50mm lens, natural undistorted perspective

cards.name: 85mm (portrait)
cards.desc: The classic portrait lens. Faces look flattering because features are not stretched, and the background starts to grow and blur.
cards.phrase: shot on an 85mm portrait lens, flattering facial proportions, background compressed and softly blurred

cards.name: Telephoto (200mm+)
cards.desc: A long lens from far away. Distance collapses: a sun or mountain behind the subject looks enormous, and layers stack up flat like stage scenery.
cards.phrase: shot from far away on a 400mm telephoto lens, extreme compression, an enormous sun directly behind the subject

cards.name: Macro
cards.desc: Focusing extremely close so something tiny fills the frame: an insect's eye, a dewdrop, the weave of a fabric. Depth of field becomes razor thin.
cards.phrase: macro photograph at 1:1 magnification, a dewdrop on a leaf filling the frame, razor-thin depth of field

cards.name: Fisheye
cards.desc: An extreme wide lens that bends every straight line into a curve, sometimes squeezing the whole scene into a circle.
cards.phrase: fisheye lens, strong barrel distortion, curved horizon, skate-video look

cards.name: Tilt-shift
cards.aka: miniature effect, fake miniature, tilt-shift lens
cards.desc: A tilted lens throws the top and bottom of the frame out of focus, so a real city seen from above looks like a toy model.
cards.phrase: tilt-shift miniature effect, a town seen from above with only a thin band in focus, saturated toy-like colors

cards.name: Anamorphic
cards.desc: Cinema lenses that squeeze a wide image onto the sensor. They leave a signature: oval out-of-focus lights, long horizontal blue flares and a very wide frame.
cards.phrase: shot on anamorphic lenses, 2.39:1 widescreen, oval bokeh and horizontal blue lens flares

cards.name: Shallow depth of field
cards.aka: wide aperture, f/1.4, f/1.8, background blur
cards.desc: Only a thin slice of the scene is sharp, so the subject pops against a creamy, blurred background. The lower the f-number, the stronger the effect.
cards.phrase: shallow depth of field, shot wide open at f/1.4, the subject tack-sharp against a creamy blurred background

cards.name: Deep focus
cards.aka: small aperture, f/11, f/16, everything sharp, hyperfocal
cards.desc: Everything from the nearest flower to the farthest mountain is sharp. Common in landscapes and in films that want you to look around the whole frame.
cards.phrase: deep focus at f/16, everything sharp from the foreground to the horizon

cards.name: Bokeh
cards.desc: The shape and quality of out-of-focus light. Pinpoints of light behind the subject turn into soft discs; their shape comes from the lens aperture.
cards.phrase: large round bokeh balls from string lights in the background

cards.name: Swirly bokeh
cards.aka: Petzval swirl, Helios 44 swirl, cat's-eye bokeh
cards.desc: Some vintage lenses stretch out-of-focus lights into ovals that circle around the center, so the background seems to spin around the subject.
cards.phrase: vintage Helios 44 swirly bokeh, the background spinning in a ring around the subject

cards.name: Split diopter
cards.aka: split-field diopter, two planes in focus
cards.desc: A half-lens filter that keeps something very close on one side and something far away on the other both in focus, with a soft seam between them.
cards.phrase: split-diopter shot: a face in the near foreground and a figure far in the background, both in sharp focus, with a soft seam between

cards.name: Long exposure
cards.aka: slow shutter, silky water, ND filter, time exposure
cards.desc: The shutter stays open for seconds or minutes. Moving water turns to mist, clouds streak and people vanish, while still things stay sharp.
cards.phrase: long exposure of 60 seconds, silky misty water and streaked clouds, the pier perfectly sharp

cards.name: Light trails
cards.aka: car light trails, streaks of light
cards.desc: A long exposure at night turns moving headlights and taillights into continuous ribbons of white and red light.
cards.phrase: long-exposure night shot, red and white car light trails streaking along the road

cards.name: Panning
cards.desc: A slowish shutter while the camera follows a moving subject. The subject stays fairly sharp and the background smears into horizontal streaks of speed.
cards.phrase: panning shot at 1/30s, the cyclist sharp and the background smeared into horizontal motion streaks

cards.name: Frozen motion
cards.desc: A very fast shutter or a flash stops action dead: a splash hangs in midair, a dancer floats, every droplet is a crystal.
cards.phrase: high-speed photograph at 1/8000s, the splash frozen in midair, every droplet crystal sharp

cards.name: Intentional camera movement
cards.desc: Moving the camera on purpose during the exposure, usually straight up or down through trees, to paint the scene into soft streaks like a watercolor.
cards.phrase: intentional camera movement, a vertical swipe through an autumn birch forest, painterly streaks of color

cards.name: Double exposure
cards.desc: Two images laid on top of each other in one frame. The classic version fills a dark silhouette, often a profile, with a landscape.
cards.phrase: double exposure, a person's profile silhouette filled with a misty pine forest and mountains, pale background

cards.name: Lens flare
cards.desc: Bright light bouncing inside the lens, leaving a chain of colored rings or hexagons across the frame and a hazy glow over everything.
cards.phrase: natural lens flare from the sun, a chain of soft hexagonal ghosts and a warm haze

cards.name: Vignette
cards.desc: The corners and edges fall off into darkness, pulling the eye to the center. Old lenses do it naturally; editors add it on purpose.
cards.phrase: strong natural vignette, corners falling off into darkness

cards.name: Chromatic aberration
cards.desc: A lens fails to focus all colors at the same point, leaving thin purple, green or red-cyan fringes along high-contrast edges.
cards.phrase: visible chromatic aberration, purple and green fringing on high-contrast edges

cards.name: Halation & bloom
cards.aka: Pro-Mist filter, diffusion filter, glow, Black Pro-Mist
cards.desc: Highlights bleed a soft glow into the area around them and the blacks lift slightly. A diffusion filter like Black Pro-Mist gives the cinematic version.
cards.phrase: Black Pro-Mist 1/4 diffusion filter, highlights blooming into soft halos, slightly lifted blacks

cards.name: Soft focus
cards.desc: A sharp image with a soft glowing layer over it, so skin and light seem to radiate. Classic Hollywood used it for close-ups of stars.
cards.phrase: soft-focus glow, a dreamy haze over the highlights, old Hollywood glamour

cards.name: Polarizing filter
cards.desc: A filter that cuts glare from water and glass and deepens blue skies. It makes colors look richer and lets you see into water.
cards.phrase: shot with a circular polarizer, deep blue sky, no glare on the water, rich saturated color

cards.name: Sunstar
cards.desc: At a small aperture like f/16, the sun or a streetlight turns into a crisp star with sharp rays. It works best when the sun peeks past an edge.
cards.phrase: sun peeking past the edge of a tree, a crisp sunstar with sharp rays at f/16

cards.name: Prism effect
cards.aka: prism photography, crystal ball, rainbow refraction
cards.desc: A glass prism or crystal held in front of the lens throws rainbows, ghost reflections and soft smears into the edges of the frame.
cards.phrase: shot through a glass prism, a soft rainbow refraction and a mirrored ghost along the left edge of the frame

cards.name: Shooting through
cards.aka: foreground blur framing, shoot-through, dirty frame
cards.desc: Shooting past leaves, glass, fabric or a doorway close to the lens, so soft blurs of color frame the subject. It makes the viewer feel hidden, like they are peeking.
cards.phrase: shot through out-of-focus foreground leaves, soft green blur framing the subject, voyeuristic

cards.name: Hard light
cards.aka: specular light, direct light, harsh light
cards.desc: A small or distant light source, like the noon sun or a bare bulb. It makes crisp shadows with sharp edges and strong contrast.
cards.phrase: hard direct light from a single small source, crisp sharp-edged shadows, high contrast

cards.name: Soft light
cards.aka: diffused light, wraparound light, flattering light
cards.desc: A large light source close to the subject, like a big window, an overcast sky or a softbox. Shadows fade gradually and skin looks smooth.
cards.phrase: soft diffused light from a large window, gentle gradual shadows wrapping around the subject

cards.name: Front light
cards.desc: Light from right behind the camera. Shadows fall behind the subject where you can't see them, so everything looks evenly lit and a bit flat.
cards.phrase: flat front lighting from directly behind the camera, minimal shadows

cards.name: Side light
cards.desc: Light from 90 degrees to one side. Half the subject is bright and half falls into shadow, which shows off shape and texture.
cards.phrase: strong side light from the left at 90 degrees, half the subject in shadow, revealing texture

cards.name: Backlight
cards.aka: rim light, contre-jour, kicker, edge light
cards.desc: Light from behind the subject, aimed toward the camera. It draws a bright outline around the edges and separates the subject from the background.
cards.phrase: strong backlight from behind the subject, a bright glowing rim outlining the edges, contre-jour

cards.name: Top light
cards.desc: Light from directly above. Eye sockets and the area under the nose and chin go dark. Moody and severe, sometimes unflattering on purpose.
cards.phrase: hard top light from directly overhead, deep shadows in the eye sockets, moody and severe

cards.name: Under light
cards.desc: Light from below, the opposite of how sun and lamps normally fall. Shadows run upward and faces look unnatural or sinister.
cards.phrase: eerie under-lighting from below, shadows climbing upward, unsettling

cards.name: Silhouette
cards.aka: shot against the light, blacked-out subject
cards.desc: The subject is completely dark against a bright background, so only its outline reads. Expose for the sky and let the subject go black.
cards.phrase: pure black silhouette against a bright sunset sky, no detail in the subject

cards.name: Rembrandt lighting
cards.desc: The key light about 45 degrees to the side and above eye level. The far cheek falls into shadow except for a small triangle of light under the eye.
cards.phrase: Rembrandt lighting: key light 45 degrees to the left and above, a small triangle of light on the shadowed cheek

cards.name: Loop lighting
cards.desc: The key light a little to the side and above, so the nose casts a small loop-shaped shadow down toward the corner of the mouth. Flattering on almost everyone.
cards.phrase: loop lighting: key light 30 degrees to the left and slightly above, a small nose shadow angled toward the mouth

cards.name: Butterfly lighting
cards.desc: The key light straight in front and high above the face. It casts a small butterfly-shaped shadow under the nose and sculpts the cheekbones.
cards.phrase: butterfly lighting: key light high and directly in front, a small symmetrical shadow under the nose, sculpted cheekbones

cards.name: Split lighting
cards.desc: The key light at 90 degrees, so exactly half the face is lit and half is in shadow. Dramatic, mysterious, a little villainous.
cards.phrase: split lighting: hard key light at 90 degrees to the left, exactly half the face in deep shadow

cards.name: Clamshell lighting
cards.desc: A soft key above the face and a reflector or second light below, like an open clamshell. Shadows nearly disappear and the eyes get two catchlights.
cards.phrase: clamshell beauty lighting: soft key above and a reflector below, almost shadowless skin, double catchlights

cards.name: Ring light
cards.desc: A circular light around the lens. Light falls evenly from the front, leaving ring-shaped catchlights and a soft shadow halo on the wall behind.
cards.phrase: ring light lighting, even shadowless front light, ring-shaped catchlights in the eyes

cards.name: Rim light
cards.desc: A light behind and to one side that traces a bright edge along the hair, cheek and shoulder. It pulls a dark subject off a dark background.
cards.phrase: strong rim light from behind, a thin bright edge tracing the hair, jaw and shoulders against a dark background

cards.name: Catchlights
cards.aka: eye lights, specular highlights in the eyes
cards.desc: The reflection of the light source in the eyes. It makes eyes look alive, and its shape tells you what the light was: a window, a softbox, a ring.
cards.phrase: clear window-shaped catchlights in both eyes at the 10 o'clock position

cards.name: Three-point lighting
cards.desc: The textbook setup: a key light for shape, a softer fill on the other side to open the shadows, and a back light to separate the subject from the background.
cards.phrase: classic three-point lighting: soft key from the left, gentle fill from the right, back light rimming the hair

cards.name: High-key
cards.desc: Bright, low-contrast lighting with a white or very light background and almost no dark tones. Clean, optimistic and commercial.
cards.phrase: high-key lighting, bright white background, soft even light, minimal shadows, airy and clean

cards.name: Low-key
cards.desc: Mostly shadow, with one controlled light picking out a few areas. A black background and deep contrast make it dramatic and secretive.
cards.phrase: low-key lighting, a single soft light from the side, deep black background, most of the subject falling into shadow

cards.name: Chiaroscuro
cards.aka: tenebrism, Caravaggio lighting, Dutch still-life light
cards.desc: Italian for "light-dark". A single warm light carves objects out of near-black darkness, as in Baroque painting. Rich, sculptural and timeless.
cards.phrase: chiaroscuro lighting like a Dutch Golden Age still life, one warm window light carving objects out of deep darkness

cards.name: Practical lights
cards.desc: Lamps, candles, screens and signs that are visible in the shot and seem to light the scene. The light looks like it belongs to the world, not to a film crew.
cards.phrase: lit only by practical lights in the scene: a warm table lamp casting a pool of light, the rest of the room in dusky shadow

cards.name: Colored gels
cards.aka: dual-color lighting, split-color gels, RGB lighting
cards.desc: Colored filters over the lights, often two contrasting colors from opposite sides such as magenta and cyan or red and blue. Bold, electric and nightlife-like.
cards.phrase: dual-color gel lighting, hot magenta from the left and electric cyan from the right, dark background

cards.name: Neon light
cards.desc: Neon signs as the main light: saturated pink, red, blue and green glowing on wet streets and faces at night.
cards.phrase: neon-lit night street, pink and cyan neon signs reflecting in rain-soaked pavement, deep blue shadows

cards.name: Window-blind shadows
cards.aka: gobo, cookie, venetian blinds, noir stripes
cards.desc: Light cut into stripes or patterns by blinds, a window frame or a cut-out placed in front of the lamp. Instantly reads as film noir.
cards.phrase: hard light through venetian blinds casting diagonal striped shadows across the face and wall, film noir

cards.name: Direct flash
cards.aka: on-camera flash, paparazzi flash, point-and-shoot flash
cards.desc: A flash fired straight from the camera. Faces are bright and flat, backgrounds drop into darkness, and a hard shadow outline sits just behind the subject.
cards.phrase: harsh direct on-camera flash, bright flat-lit face, hard shadow behind on the wall, dark falloff, candid party snapshot

cards.name: Dragging the shutter
cards.aka: slow-sync flash, rear-curtain sync, flash with motion blur
cards.desc: A flash freezes the subject while a slow shutter records the ambient light, so a sharp person is wrapped in streaks and ghosts of colored light.
cards.phrase: slow-sync flash, dragging the shutter: the subject frozen by flash with streaks of colored ambient light swirling around them

cards.name: Light painting
cards.desc: Moving a light through a long exposure to draw shapes in the air. Spinning burning steel wool throws a circle of sparks around a dark figure.
cards.phrase: long-exposure light painting, a ring of spinning steel-wool sparks around a dark silhouette at night

cards.name: Candlelight
cards.aka: firelight, warm low light, Barry Lyndon lighting
cards.desc: A tiny warm flame as the only light: deep orange tones, fast falloff into darkness, and a soft flicker of light from below.
cards.phrase: lit only by candlelight from below and in front, warm amber glow, darkness falling off quickly

cards.name: Golden hour
cards.aka: magic hour, the hour after sunrise or before sunset
cards.desc: When the sun is low, its light turns warm and soft, shadows stretch long and everything gets a glowing edge. The most flattering natural light there is.
cards.phrase: golden hour, low warm sun skimming across the scene, long soft shadows, glowing rim light

cards.name: Blue hour
cards.desc: The short window just after sunset or before sunrise when the sky turns deep, even blue and artificial lights start to glow warm against it.
cards.phrase: blue hour, deep cobalt twilight sky, warm glowing windows contrasting with the cool blue

cards.name: Midday sun
cards.aka: high noon, harsh sunlight, hard daylight
cards.desc: The sun high overhead gives hard, short shadows straight down, deep blue skies and bright, saturated color. Usually avoided for portraits, loved for graphic summer looks.
cards.phrase: harsh midday sun overhead, short hard shadows directly beneath, saturated summer color

cards.name: Alpenglow
cards.desc: Just after the sun sets, mountain peaks and clouds keep glowing pink and rose while the land below has already gone into blue shadow.
cards.phrase: alpenglow just after sunset, the mountain peaks glowing rose pink above cool blue valleys

cards.name: Moonlight
cards.desc: Cool, silvery light from a bright moon with stars overhead. Blacks are deep, highlights are blue-white, and shapes read mostly as silhouettes.
cards.phrase: moonlit night, cool silver-blue light, a glittering moon path on the water, stars overhead

cards.name: Milky Way night sky
cards.desc: A long exposure under a dark sky that shows the band of the Milky Way and thousands of stars above a silhouetted landscape.
cards.phrase: astrophotography of the Milky Way arching over a silhouetted landscape, thousands of stars, 20-second exposure

cards.name: Overcast
cards.desc: A sky full of clouds turns the whole sky into one giant softbox. No hard shadows, gentle contrast, colors muted but true.
cards.phrase: soft overcast daylight, an even white sky, shadowless and gentle, muted natural color

cards.name: Fog & mist
cards.desc: Fog swallows distance. Each layer of trees or hills gets paler as it recedes, colors drain away and the scene turns quiet and mysterious.
cards.phrase: thick morning fog, layers of pine trees fading into white mist with distance, quiet and mysterious

cards.name: God rays
cards.aka: crepuscular rays, volumetric light, light shafts
cards.desc: Beams of light made visible by dust, mist or smoke as they pour through gaps in trees, clouds or windows.
cards.phrase: volumetric god rays streaming through the forest canopy, visible shafts of light in misty air

cards.name: Dappled light
cards.desc: Sunlight broken up by leaves into scattered spots of light and shadow on the ground, a wall or a face. Komorebi is the Japanese word for it.
cards.phrase: dappled sunlight filtering through leaves, soft spots of light scattered across the subject and ground

cards.name: Rain & wet streets
cards.aka: rain-soaked, after the rain, wet pavement
cards.desc: Rain makes every surface a mirror. At night especially, lights double themselves in puddles and streaks of rain catch the backlight.
cards.phrase: rainy night, wet pavement mirroring the streetlights, visible rain streaks backlit by the lamps

cards.name: Snowfall
cards.desc: Snow softens and quiets everything: a pale, low-contrast world with blue shadows and flakes that blur in the foreground.
cards.phrase: gentle snowfall, a pale white landscape with soft blue shadows, out-of-focus snowflakes in the foreground

cards.name: Storm light
cards.aka: dramatic light, breaking storm, sunlight after rain
cards.desc: Dark storm clouds with sunlight breaking through underneath, so a bright, saturated landscape sits against a nearly black sky.
cards.phrase: dramatic storm light, sunlight breaking through under dark slate-grey clouds onto a vivid green landscape, a faint rainbow

cards.name: Window light
cards.aka: north light, Vermeer light, natural side light
cards.desc: Soft daylight from a single window to one side. It falls off gently across the room and models faces beautifully. The light Vermeer painted again and again.
cards.phrase: soft window light from the left, gentle falloff across the room, quiet Vermeer-like interior

cards.name: Mixed lighting
cards.aka: tungsten and daylight, warm and cool, color contrast
cards.desc: Two light sources with different color temperatures in one scene: blue dusk through a window and orange lamplight inside. The clash reads as cinematic.
cards.phrase: mixed lighting, cool blue twilight from the window on one side and warm tungsten lamplight on the other

cards.name: Sodium streetlight
cards.aka: sodium vapor, orange streetlight, high-pressure sodium
cards.desc: The old orange streetlights that turn a whole night street a single amber color, with murky green-brown shadows. Increasingly rare, instantly nostalgic.
cards.phrase: night street under sodium-vapor streetlights, everything washed in monochrome amber orange, murky shadows

cards.name: Fluorescent light
cards.aka: office light, tube light, green cast
cards.desc: Overhead tube lights with a flat, slightly green tint. It feels institutional and a bit sickly, perfect for offices, hospitals and late-night convenience stores.
cards.phrase: flat overhead fluorescent tube lighting, slightly green cast, sterile and institutional

cards.name: Screen glow
cards.aka: laptop light, phone light, monitor glow
cards.desc: A face lit only by the cool blue-white glow of a screen in a dark room. It feels late-night, private and modern.
cards.phrase: face lit only by the cool blue glow of a laptop screen in a dark room, late at night

cards.name: Kodak Portra 400
cards.desc: The most loved color negative film today. Soft contrast, warm and natural skin, gentle pastel colors and fine grain. It forgives everything.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodak Portra 400 film, soft natural contrast, warm skin tones, gentle pastel color, fine grain

cards.name: Kodak Ektar 100
cards.desc: Kodak's finest-grain, most saturated color negative film. Punchy blues and reds, crisp detail, made for landscapes and travel.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodak Ektar 100, vivid saturated color, deep blue sky, ultra-fine grain

cards.name: Kodak Gold 200
cards.desc: Cheap consumer film from the family photo albums of the 80s and 90s. Warm, yellow-golden cast, visible grain, a sunny-nostalgic feeling.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodak Gold 200, warm golden-yellow cast, nostalgic 90s snapshot color, visible grain

cards.name: Kodachrome
cards.desc: The legendary slide film, discontinued in 2009. Rich reds and yellows, deep blue-cyan skies, dense shadows and high contrast that feels mid-century.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodachrome 64 slide film, rich reds and yellows, deep cyan-blue sky, high contrast, mid-century color

cards.name: Fujichrome Velvia 50
cards.desc: Fuji's famously over-saturated slide film. Greens and blues are almost electric and contrast is steep. The landscape photographer's film of the 90s.
cards.phrase: shot on Fujichrome Velvia 50, hyper-saturated greens and blues, punchy contrast, landscape slide film

cards.name: Fujicolor Superia
cards.aka: Fuji Superia 400, Fuji Pro 400H, Fuji greens
cards.desc: Fuji's consumer negative film with its famous greens and cool, slightly minty cast. Skies lean cyan and shadows lean green.
cards.phrase: shot on Fujicolor Superia 400, cool cyan-green cast, fresh greens, soft grain

cards.name: CineStill 800T
cards.desc: Motion-picture film adapted for still cameras and made for tungsten light. At night lights glow with a red halo (halation) and the shadows go teal.
cards.phrase: shot on CineStill 800T, night scene, red halation halos glowing around the lights, cool teal shadows, grain

cards.name: Kodak Aerochrome
cards.desc: A discontinued infrared film made for aerial surveys. Living plants reflect infrared, so green foliage turns hot pink and red while skies stay blue.
cards.phrase: Kodak Aerochrome infrared film, foliage turned vivid pink and red, surreal false color

cards.name: LomoChrome Purple
cards.desc: A modern experimental film that swaps colors: greens turn purple and violet, blues turn green, and skin stays roughly natural.
cards.phrase: shot on LomoChrome Purple, greens turned lavender and violet, blues shifted to teal, dreamy color-shifted film

cards.name: Kodak Tri-X 400
cards.aka: Tri-X, Ilford HP5, pushed black and white
cards.desc: The classic black-and-white film of photojournalism. Gritty grain, deep blacks and punchy contrast, especially when pushed in development.
cards.phrase: shot on Kodak Tri-X 400 pushed to 1600, gritty high-contrast black and white, coarse grain, deep blacks

cards.name: Fine-grain black & white
cards.aka: Ilford Pan F 50, Fuji Acros, smooth monochrome
cards.desc: Slow, fine-grained black-and-white film with long, silky grey tones and almost no visible grain. Elegant and classical.
cards.phrase: fine-grain black and white on Ilford Pan F 50, smooth silky tonality, rich mid-greys, crisp detail

cards.name: Black & white infrared
cards.aka: IR photography, Wood effect, infrared monochrome
cards.desc: Infrared-sensitive film (or a converted camera) turns leaves and grass glowing white and blue skies nearly black. Dreamlike and otherworldly.
cards.phrase: black-and-white infrared photograph, foliage glowing white, near-black sky, dreamlike halation

cards.name: Polaroid
cards.desc: Instant prints with the thick white border at the bottom. Soft focus, faded and slightly shifted colors, and a dreamy, imperfect look.
cards.phrase: vintage Polaroid SX-70 instant photo, faded dreamy colors, soft focus, white border with a thick bottom edge

cards.name: Disposable camera
cards.aka: single-use camera, point-and-shoot film, date stamp
cards.desc: A cheap plastic camera with a built-in flash. Harsh flash on faces, dark backgrounds, soft corners, warm film color and that orange date in the corner.
cards.phrase: disposable camera snapshot, harsh on-camera flash, dark background, warm grainy film, orange date stamp in the corner

cards.name: Toy camera
cards.desc: Cheap plastic cameras with plastic lenses. Heavy dark corners, soft blurry edges, unpredictable color and the occasional light leak.
cards.phrase: Holga toy camera photo, square frame, heavy vignette, soft blurry edges, shifted saturated color

cards.name: Light leaks
cards.aka: light leak, film burn, edge fogging
cards.desc: Stray light sneaking into the camera body fogs part of the film with glowing streaks of red, orange and yellow, usually from one edge.
cards.phrase: warm red and orange light leaks bleeding in from the right edge of the frame, film burn

cards.name: Expired film
cards.aka: expired stock, degraded film, fogged film
cards.desc: Film used years past its date. Colors drift (often magenta or green), blacks turn muddy, grain gets heavy and nothing is quite predictable.
cards.phrase: shot on expired film, faded magenta color shift, lifted muddy blacks, heavy grain, unpredictable color

cards.name: Cross-processing
cards.aka: xpro, C-41 in E-6, cross-processed slide film
cards.desc: Developing film in the wrong chemistry. Contrast shoots up, highlights go yellow-green and shadows go blue: the club-flyer look of the late 90s.
cards.phrase: cross-processed slide film, harsh contrast, acid yellow-green highlights and blue shadows, late-90s magazine look

cards.name: Wet plate collodion
cards.desc: A 19th-century process on metal or glass plates. Silvery, warm-grey tones, fierce detail, glowing skin, and swirly chemical marks at the edges.
cards.phrase: wet plate collodion tintype portrait, silvery warm-grey tones, dark ragged edges with chemical pour marks, 1860s look

cards.name: Cyanotype
cards.desc: An 1840s iron-based printing process that produces Prussian-blue prints. Often made by laying leaves or objects directly on the paper in the sun.
cards.phrase: cyanotype print, white fern and leaf silhouettes on deep Prussian blue paper, brushy hand-coated edges

cards.name: Super 8
cards.aka: 8mm home movie, film still, Super 8 frame
cards.desc: The home-movie film of the 60s to 80s. Tiny frames mean huge grain, soft focus, warm faded color and rounded frame corners.
cards.phrase: Super 8 film still, heavy grain, warm faded home-movie color, soft focus, rounded frame corners

cards.name: VHS camcorder
cards.aka: camcorder footage, analog video, VHS tape
cards.desc: Home video from the 80s and 90s. Low resolution, color bleeding sideways, scan lines, a tracking glitch and the white on-screen date and PLAY text.
cards.phrase: VHS camcorder footage, smeared bleeding colors, scan lines, a tracking glitch band, white on-screen date overlay

cards.name: Early digital camera
cards.desc: The small digital cameras of the early 2000s. Cool white balance, blown-out flash, crisp but slightly cheap detail, and a timestamp.
cards.phrase: early-2000s digital point-and-shoot photo, harsh flash, cool white balance, clipped highlights, CCD sensor look, date stamp

cards.name: Medium format
cards.desc: Film four times the size of 35mm. Smoother tones, finer detail and a gentler, three-dimensional falloff of focus. Often square.
cards.phrase: shot on medium format film with a Hasselblad 500C/M, square 6x6 frame, smooth tonality, gentle shallow focus

cards.name: Teal and orange
cards.desc: Shadows and backgrounds pushed toward teal, skin and highlights toward orange. Because the two colors are opposites, people pop off the background.
cards.phrase: teal and orange color grade, teal shadows and warm orange skin tones, blockbuster look

cards.name: Bleach bypass
cards.aka: skip bleach, silver retention, desaturated high contrast
cards.desc: A lab trick that keeps silver in the film, giving low saturation, high contrast and a gritty, metallic, washed look.
cards.phrase: bleach bypass grade, desaturated silvery color, harsh contrast, gritty war-film look

cards.name: Faded matte
cards.aka: lifted blacks, matte look, film fade
cards.desc: The darkest tones are lifted to a soft grey so nothing is truly black. Gentle, nostalgic, a little hazy. Huge on Instagram in the 2010s.
cards.phrase: faded matte grade, lifted milky blacks, soft low contrast, slightly desaturated

cards.name: Split toning
cards.aka: split tone, warm highlights cool shadows
cards.desc: Highlights tinted one color and shadows another, usually warm highlights and cool shadows. It adds mood without changing the colors of the scene too much.
cards.phrase: split-toned grade, warm cream highlights and cool blue shadows, muted overall

cards.name: Sepia
cards.aka: sepia tone, antique toning, brown tone
cards.desc: A monochrome image in warm brown tones, originally from toning prints with cuttlefish ink. It instantly reads as old.
cards.phrase: sepia-toned monochrome photograph, warm brown and cream tones, antique feel

cards.name: Pastel grade
cards.aka: soft pastel, candy color, Wes Anderson palette
cards.desc: Every color softened toward a light, chalky pastel: pinks, mint greens, butter yellows and powder blues, with gentle contrast.
cards.phrase: soft pastel color grade, pink, mint and powder-blue tones, gentle low contrast

cards.name: Vivid saturated
cards.aka: high saturation, punchy color, hyperreal color
cards.desc: Color pushed hard, so reds, blues and yellows are almost cartoonishly strong. Used for joy, kitsch and summer.
cards.phrase: vivid hyper-saturated color, punchy reds, yellows and blues, glossy and bright

cards.name: Editorial portrait
cards.desc: A styled, art-directed portrait made for a magazine: a strong pose, bold color or a clean seamless backdrop, deliberate lighting and attitude.
cards.phrase: editorial magazine portrait, bold orange seamless backdrop, crisp studio lighting, confident direct gaze

cards.name: Street photography
cards.desc: Unposed moments of strangers in public places, caught in passing. Strong light and shadow, layered people, and a sense of the city's rhythm.
cards.phrase: candid street photography, a lone pedestrian stepping into a shaft of hard sunlight between deep shadows, 35mm

cards.name: Documentary
cards.desc: Real people and real events photographed honestly, often in black and white, with available light, grain and slightly imperfect framing that says "this happened".
cards.phrase: documentary photojournalism, candid and unstaged, available light, grainy black and white, Magnum style

cards.name: Product photography
cards.aka: packshot, hero product shot, commercial still life
cards.desc: An object made to look its best: a clean seamless or gradient background, controlled reflections, crisp edges and soft shadows.
cards.phrase: premium product photography, the bottle centered on a soft gradient seamless, strip-light rim highlights, subtle reflection below

cards.name: Food photography
cards.aka: food styling, dark and moody food, overhead food
cards.desc: Dishes styled to look delicious: natural side light, a textured surface, a few scattered ingredients and props. Shot either overhead or at a low 45 degrees.
cards.phrase: dark and moody food photography from overhead, a bowl of ramen on slate, side window light, scattered herbs and chopsticks

cards.name: Architectural photography
cards.aka: architecture shot, corrected verticals, building portrait
cards.desc: Buildings photographed so their lines stay perfectly straight (often with a tilt-shift lens), usually on clear days with strong sun and shadow sculpting the form.
cards.phrase: architectural photography with perfectly corrected verticals, a brutalist concrete facade, hard sun carving deep geometric shadows, clean blue sky

cards.name: Interior photography
cards.desc: Rooms shot with a wide lens from a corner or straight on, at chest height, with straight verticals and balanced window and lamp light. Calm and aspirational.
cards.phrase: interior design photography, wide 24mm view straight on, perfectly vertical lines, soft daylight from tall windows, calm minimal styling

cards.name: Wildlife photography
cards.desc: Animals in their habitat, shot from far away with long lenses. The background melts into soft color, the eye is tack sharp, and the moment is everything.
cards.phrase: wildlife photography with a 600mm lens, a grey heron standing in shallow water, tack-sharp eye, background melted into smooth green blur

cards.name: Cinematic film still
cards.aka: movie still, film frame, cinematic photography
cards.desc: A photo that looks like a frame from a movie: widescreen letterbox, motivated light, a deliberate color grade and a sense that a story is mid-scene.
cards.phrase: cinematic film still, 2.39:1 letterbox, a lone figure on a rain-slicked street under a streetlight, teal and orange grade, anamorphic

cards.name: Fine-art conceptual
cards.aka: surreal photography, conceptual photography, staged fine art
cards.desc: A staged, often surreal image built around an idea rather than a moment: an impossible object, a symbolic prop, a dreamlike landscape.
cards.phrase: surreal fine-art conceptual photograph, a lone wooden door standing open in a misty field, warm light pouring through it

cards.name: Ansel Adams
cards.aka: Zone System, f/64, Yosemite black and white
cards.desc: Majestic black-and-white American landscapes with the full range of tones from deep black to bright white, dramatic skies and razor detail.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Ansel Adams: majestic black-and-white mountain landscape, full tonal range from deep black to bright white, dramatic clouds, large-format detail

cards.name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
cards.desc: Black-and-white street photography built on "the decisive moment": the split second when movement, geometry and gesture line up perfectly.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Henri Cartier-Bresson: a decisive-moment black-and-white street photograph, a man leaping over a puddle, his reflection mirrored in the water, 50mm

cards.name: Saul Leiter
cards.aka: painterly color street, New York in the rain
cards.desc: Quiet, painterly color photographs of New York, often shot through steamy or rain-streaked windows, with big blocks of dark and tiny spots of red.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Saul Leiter: painterly color street photograph through a rain-streaked window, large dark shapes filling the frame, a small red umbrella in falling snow, muted tones

cards.name: Fan Ho
cards.desc: Black-and-white Hong Kong in the 1950s and 60s: shafts of light cutting through alleys and smoke, tiny figures dwarfed by geometry and shadow.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Fan Ho: black-and-white Hong Kong alley, a single diagonal shaft of light through smoky air, a tiny lone figure in the beam, deep geometric shadows

cards.name: William Eggleston
cards.desc: The photographer who made color serious art. Ordinary American scenes (a ceiling, a tricycle, a diner) in saturated, almost lurid dye-transfer color.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of William Eggleston: an everyday American interior in saturated dye-transfer color, a blood-red ceiling with a bare bulb and white wires

cards.name: Martin Parr
cards.desc: Funny, garish color photos of tourists, beaches and consumer life, lit with a ring flash in bright daylight so colors scream.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Martin Parr: saturated daylight-flash close-up of a dripping ice cream cone at a crowded seaside, garish color, humorous documentary

cards.name: Gregory Crewdson
cards.desc: Huge, staged photographs of small-town America at twilight, lit like a film set, where something quietly strange is happening.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Gregory Crewdson: cinematic suburban street at blue hour, every window glowing, a lone figure standing motionless on the lawn, faint mist, eerie stillness, staged like a film set

cards.name: Todd Hido
cards.aka: houses at night, fogged windshield landscapes
cards.desc: Lonely suburban houses at night with one lit window, and blurry landscapes seen through a wet or foggy car windshield. Moody, cinematic, quietly sad.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Todd Hido: a lone house at night with a single glowing window, murky foggy air under a sodium streetlight, seen through a misted car windshield

cards.name: Hiroshi Sugimoto
cards.desc: Black-and-white seascapes where the horizon cuts the frame exactly in half: sea below, sky above, nothing else, rendered in endless soft greys.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Hiroshi Sugimoto: minimalist black-and-white seascape, the horizon exactly centered, silky long-exposure sea and empty sky in soft greys

cards.name: Roger Deakins
cards.desc: The cinematographer of Blade Runner 2049, Skyfall and 1917. Bold single sources, silhouettes against walls of colored haze, and perfectly simple compositions.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Roger Deakins: a lone silhouetted figure walking through dense orange haze, single-source light, minimal composition, monumental scale

cards.name: Wong Kar-wai & Christopher Doyle
cards.aka: step-printing, neon smear, In the Mood for Love
cards.desc: Hong Kong romance in saturated greens and reds, smeared step-printed motion, neon through dirty glass and figures framed in narrow corridors.
cards.phrase: in the spirit of Wong Kar-wai and Christopher Doyle: step-printed motion smear, a figure blurred in a narrow neon-lit Hong Kong corridor, saturated green and red, shot through dirty glass

cards.name: Wes Anderson
cards.desc: Symmetrical, centered compositions in candy pastel palettes, flat frontal staging and dollhouse-like sets. The style is so recognizable it has its own Instagram account.
cards.phrase: in the style of a Wes Anderson film: a perfectly symmetrical pastel pink hotel facade, centered, flat frontal composition, candy-colored palette

cards.name: Cave painting
cards.aka: Paleolithic rock art, prehistoric cave art
cards.desc: Animals painted with ochre, charcoal and blown pigment straight onto cave rock, often using the bumps of the stone as muscles. It feels alive, raw and very old.
cards.phrase: prehistoric cave painting, red ochre and charcoal animals in side view on rough limestone, blown-pigment hand stencils, flickering torchlit rock texture, no background scene

cards.name: Egyptian wall painting
cards.desc: Figures shown in "composite view": head and legs in profile but eye and shoulders facing you, so every part is shown at its most recognizable. Scenes are stacked in horizontal bands (registers) with flat, unshaded color and hieroglyphs filling the gaps.
cards.phrase: ancient Egyptian tomb wall painting, composite profile figures with frontal eyes and shoulders, flat unshaded ochre, red, blue and green, horizontal registers, hieroglyph columns on plaster

cards.name: Greek vase painting
cards.desc: Scenes painted on pots in two colors only: black-figure paints black silhouettes on orange clay and scratches details in, red-figure flips it so the figures stay clay-colored on a glossy black ground. Bands of key pattern frame the scene.
cards.phrase: ancient Greek red-figure vase painting, terracotta figures with fine black contour lines on glossy black ground, meander key border, profile figures on a single ground line

cards.name: Byzantine mosaic & icon
cards.desc: Holy figures made of thousands of glass and gold tiles (tesserae) or painted on wood, standing flat and frontal against a shimmering gold ground. They are meant to feel eternal and otherworldly, not lifelike.
cards.phrase: Byzantine gold-ground mosaic, frontal saint with large almond eyes and halo, visible glass tesserae, flat deep blue and purple robes, shimmering gold leaf background, solemn and timeless

cards.name: Illuminated manuscript
cards.desc: Handwritten books decorated with gold leaf and bright pigment: huge ornamented first letters, vine borders and tiny jewel-like scenes. "Illuminated" means the gold literally catches the light.
cards.phrase: medieval illuminated manuscript page, ornate gilded initial on ultramarine, vine and ivy border with gold dots, vermilion accents, parchment, tiny jewel-like painted miniature

cards.name: Medieval tapestry
cards.desc: Pictures woven in wool and silk to hang on castle walls, often packed with flat figures and animals floating on a ground of countless tiny flowers ("millefleurs", a thousand flowers). Colors are earthy reds, deep greens and indigo, with a soft woven texture.
cards.phrase: medieval millefleurs tapestry, flat white unicorn on a deep green ground scattered with tiny flowers, woven wool texture, madder red border, no perspective, muted vegetable dyes

cards.name: Gothic stained glass
cards.desc: Pictures built from pieces of colored glass held together by black lead strips, set in tall pointed windows and round rose windows. Sunlight through it gives a glowing, jewel-like color you cannot get with paint.
cards.phrase: Gothic stained glass window, jewel-toned ruby, cobalt and emerald glass pieces separated by thick black lead lines, pointed lancet arches and rose window, glowing backlit light

cards.name: Chinese shan shui
cards.desc: Landscapes in ink on silk or paper ("shan shui" means mountain-water): towering peaks, drifting mist and tiny people, usually on a tall hanging scroll. Empty space is part of the picture and stands for mist, water or air.
cards.phrase: Chinese shan shui ink landscape on silk hanging scroll, towering misty mountains, layered gray ink washes and texture strokes, tiny pavilion and traveler, pines, generous empty space, red seal

cards.name: Persian miniature
cards.desc: Small, jewel-bright book paintings where the world is seen from high above, so floors, gardens and carpets tilt up like a map. Every surface carries pattern, from tiles to robes, under a gold or lapis sky.
cards.phrase: Persian miniature painting, high bird's-eye view, tilted-up garden and pavilion with patterned turquoise tiles, lapis lazuli and gold leaf, slender turbaned figures, flowering trees, fine detail

cards.name: Early Renaissance
cards.desc: Painters rediscover depth: Giotto gives figures weight, and by the 1400s linear perspective makes floors and buildings recede to a single point. The colors are chalky and clear, the mood calm and devout.
cards.phrase: Early Renaissance fresco, one-point linear perspective, tiled floor and slender arches, pale chalky egg tempera colors, ultramarine and rose, gold halos, calm solid figures

cards.name: High Renaissance
cards.desc: The peak of balance and ideal beauty: figures arranged in stable triangles, softly modeled with sfumato (edges melting into smoky shadow) before a hazy blue landscape. Everything feels harmonious and serene.
cards.phrase: High Renaissance oil painting, in the manner of Leonardo and Raphael: pyramidal composition, soft sfumato modeling, idealized serene faces, hazy blue atmospheric landscape behind

cards.name: Northern Renaissance
cards.desc: Oil paint built up in thin transparent glazes lets painters render every thread, jewel and reflection with almost microscopic precision. Everyday objects often hide religious symbols.
cards.phrase: Northern Renaissance oil painting, in the manner of Jan van Eyck: microscopic detail, luminous oil glazes, domestic interior with convex mirror and bullseye windows, rich brocade, symbolic objects

cards.name: Mannerism
cards.desc: A deliberate break from Renaissance balance: bodies stretch and twist into S-curves, space feels crowded or unstable, and colors turn acid. Elegant and slightly uneasy.
cards.phrase: Mannerist painting, in the manner of El Greco and Pontormo: elongated twisting figures with small heads, acid pink, lime and cold blue, stormy flickering sky, unstable crowded space

cards.name: Baroque
cards.desc: Drama and motion: figures lit by a single strong light burst out of deep shadow (chiaroscuro), often frozen at the most intense moment. Compositions run on bold diagonals.
cards.phrase: Baroque oil painting, dramatic chiaroscuro, figures emerging from deep shadow, single raking light, rich warm darks, crimson and gold drapery, theatrical diagonal composition

cards.name: Dutch Golden Age still life
cards.desc: Arrangements of glasses, fruit, pewter and flowers painted so precisely they look touchable, glowing against a dark background. Many are "vanitas" pictures: a skull, a peeled lemon or a guttered candle reminds you life is short.
cards.phrase: Dutch Golden Age still life oil painting, dark ground, glass roemer, pewter plate and half-peeled lemon on a table edge, glowing highlights, vanitas skull, muted tonal browns and greens

cards.name: Rococo
cards.desc: Light, playful and pretty: aristocrats flirt in feathery gardens painted in pastel pinks, blues and creams. Frames and rooms swirl with gilded shell-and-scroll ornament (rocaille).
cards.phrase: Rococo painting, in the manner of Fragonard and Boucher: pastel pink and powder blue, frothy silk gowns, feathery garden trees, rose garlands, playful lighthearted mood, gilded rocaille frame

cards.name: Neoclassicism
cards.desc: A sober reaction to Rococo, inspired by ancient Greece and Rome: crisp outlines, smooth invisible brushwork and figures posed like a carved frieze. Calm, noble and serious.
cards.phrase: Neoclassical oil painting, in the manner of Jacques-Louis David: crisp contours, smooth finish, figures in a frieze-like row before Doric columns and arches, togas, restrained red and stone gray

cards.name: Romanticism
cards.desc: Feeling over reason: tiny people face vast, wild nature (fog, storms, moonlit ruins) to evoke the "sublime", awe mixed with fear. A favorite device is the Rückenfigur, a figure seen from behind so you look out through their eyes.
cards.phrase: Romantic landscape painting, in the manner of Caspar David Friedrich: lone figure seen from behind on a dark crag above a sea of fog, distant peaks, pale moon, sublime melancholy

cards.name: Hudson River School & Luminism
cards.desc: Huge, detailed American landscapes celebrating untouched wilderness, often bathed in golden sunset light. Luminism is its quiet branch: glassy still water, hidden brushstrokes and a hushed, glowing calm.
cards.phrase: Hudson River School landscape, Luminist light: vast panoramic valley, golden glowing haze, mirror-still lake, distant blue mountains, tiny figures, dark framing tree, smooth invisible brushwork

cards.name: Pre-Raphaelite
cards.desc: Victorian painters who wanted the honesty of art "before Raphael": every leaf and flower painted in sharp, jewel-bright detail, usually around a melancholy medieval or literary heroine.
cards.phrase: Pre-Raphaelite oil painting, in the manner of Rossetti and Waterhouse: jewel-bright detail, woman with long flowing copper hair in medieval green gown, dense flowers and foliage, dreamy melancholy

cards.name: Realism
cards.desc: Paintings of ordinary working people, shown honestly and at full dignity instead of gods, kings or pretty myths. The mood is quiet, heavy and earthbound.
cards.phrase: Realism oil painting, 19th-century French peasants at work in a wide field, earthy ochre and umber palette, soft overcast light, low horizon, honest unidealized figures

cards.name: Post-Impressionism
cards.desc: Painters who kept Impressionism's bright color but added structure: Cézanne built landscapes from blocks of parallel strokes, Gauguin used flat areas of bold color with dark outlines. It feels solid, deliberate and a little stylized.
cards.phrase: Post-Impressionist oil painting, Cézanne-like landscape built from patches of parallel brushstrokes, blocky ochre houses, blue-violet mountain, flat color zones with dark outlines

cards.name: Symbolism
cards.desc: Paintings of dreams, myths, death and the soul, more interested in mood and hidden meaning than in the real world. Scenes glow softly out of dusky darkness, like a vision half remembered.
