cards.phrase: Symbolist painting, dreamlike mystical scene in dusky twilight, soft inner glow, dark cypresses and still water, lone pale figure, muted violet and gold, hushed mood

cards.name: Vienna Secession
cards.desc: A group of Viennese artists who broke from the official academy to treat posters, furniture and buildings as art. Their look is flat, square, gilded and ornamental, with stark black-and-white grids beside shimmering gold.
cards.phrase: Vienna Secession poster design, square format, flat gold leaf ornament, grids of small squares and spirals, black-and-white checker border, stylized elegant figure, geometric lettering

cards.name: Fauvism
cards.desc: The "wild beasts": painters who used color for feeling, not accuracy, so trees turn red, skies orange and faces green. Pure paint straight from the tube, laid on in loose energetic strokes.
cards.phrase: Fauvist painting, harbor scene in wildly unnatural pure colors, red tree trunks, pink and turquoise water, orange sky, loose bold brushstrokes, patches of bare canvas

cards.name: German Expressionism
cards.aka: Die Brücke, Der Blaue Reiter, Expressionist painting
cards.desc: Art that bends and distorts the world to show inner feeling, usually anxiety, alienation or spiritual yearning. Forms are jagged and stretched, colors harsh and clashing, outlines rough like a woodcut.
cards.phrase: German Expressionist painting, jagged elongated figures on a tilted city street, harsh acid green and hot pink against black, rough woodcut-like outlines, anxious mood

cards.name: Futurism
cards.desc: An Italian movement in love with speed, machines and the modern city, which tried to paint motion itself. Objects repeat like stacked film frames and are sliced by sharp lines of force.
cards.phrase: Futurist painting, speeding automobile shown as overlapping repeated forms, sharp wedge-shaped lines of force, fractured planes, energetic diagonals, steel gray, red and electric blue

cards.name: Orphism
cards.desc: An offshoot of Cubism that turned to pure color and rhythm, like visual music. Bright concentric discs and arcs overlap and pulse against each other.
cards.phrase: Orphism abstract painting, overlapping concentric color discs split into quarters, bright complementary colors side by side, rhythmic circular motion, flat paint, like visual music

cards.name: Metaphysical painting
cards.desc: Eerie, silent city squares painted with a too-clear afternoon light, where nobody lives and something seems about to happen. It is the direct ancestor of Surrealism, but calmer and more architectural.
cards.phrase: Metaphysical painting, empty Italian piazza with dark arcades, long raking late-afternoon shadows, deep green sky, lone statue, distant train, eerie silent stillness, smooth flat paint

cards.name: Suprematism
cards.desc: Pure abstraction built from the simplest shapes (squares, bars, circles, crosses) floating on white space, meant to express pure feeling rather than any object. It looks weightless, like shapes drifting in outer space.
cards.phrase: Suprematist abstract painting, flat black, red and yellow rectangles, bars and a circle floating diagonally on off-white ground, weightless composition, lots of empty space, crisp edges

cards.name: Dada
cards.desc: An anti-art protest born from the madness of World War I, using nonsense, chance and insult to mock respectable culture. Visually it is cut-up photos, machine parts and shouting typography slammed together on purpose to make no sense.
cards.phrase: Dada photomontage, absurd cut-out photo fragments of heads, eyes and machine gears, chaotic mixed typography at odd angles, newsprint scraps, black and red ink, deliberately nonsensical

cards.name: New Objectivity
cards.desc: A cold, sharp-focus realism that came after Expressionism, showing Weimar Germany's war cripples, profiteers and nightclub sophisticates without warmth. Everything is smooth, crisply outlined and slightly too clear, often with biting satire.
cards.phrase: New Objectivity oil portrait, cold sharp-focus realism, smooth enamel paint, hard outlines, pale sallow skin, unflattering stare, cool greenish-gray background, satirical Weimar-era mood

cards.name: Precisionism
cards.desc: American painters who celebrated factories, grain silos and skyscrapers as the new cathedrals, painting them with razor-clean edges and almost no people. It feels calm, orderly and machine-made.
cards.phrase: Precisionist painting, clean industrial landscape of factories, smokestacks and grain silos, crisp hard-edged geometry, smooth flat planes, clear pale blue sky, transparent diagonal light beams, no people

cards.name: Harlem Renaissance
cards.aka: New Negro Movement art, Aaron Douglas style
cards.desc: A flowering of Black American art, music and writing centered in Harlem, which told African American history and hope in a new modern visual language. Aaron Douglas's murals mixed flat silhouettes, Art Deco geometry and African sculpture into glowing purple-gold scenes.
cards.phrase: Harlem Renaissance mural in the manner of Aaron Douglas: flat silhouetted figure in profile, concentric rings of light, translucent overlapping bands, purple, violet and gold palette, Art Deco geometry

cards.name: Mexican muralism
cards.desc: After the Mexican Revolution, the government paid artists to paint huge public walls telling the nation's history and the struggles of workers and Indigenous people. Figures are heavy, rounded and monumental, packed into crowded story-telling scenes.
cards.phrase: Mexican muralism fresco, monumental rounded figures of workers and farmers, simplified heavy volumes, earthy terracotta, ochre and deep green, crowded narrative scene, flat matte fresco texture, social themes

cards.name: American Regionalism
cards.desc: Painters who turned away from European modernism to paint the rural Midwest: farms, small towns and the people who worked them. Grant Wood's landscapes swell into toy-like rolling hills with lollipop trees and neatly combed fields.
cards.phrase: American Regionalism painting, rolling stylized Midwest farmland with pillowy hills, curving crop rows, round lollipop trees in neat lines, small red barn and white farmhouse, smooth forms, warm clear light

cards.name: WPA poster
cards.aka: Federal Art Project poster, New Deal silkscreen poster
cards.desc: Posters made by artists employed by the New Deal's Federal Art Project, hand-printed by silkscreen to promote national parks, public health, libraries and safety. Simple flat shapes in a few muted inks, with bold, plain sans-serif lettering in a block at the bottom.
cards.phrase: WPA poster, 1930s Federal Art Project silkscreen, flat layered national park landscape in five muted inks, no gradients, bold condensed sans-serif lettering band at bottom, small credit line

cards.name: Socialist Realism
cards.desc: The official art style of the Soviet Union, which showed workers and farmers as idealized heroes building a glorious future. It is realistic in technique but always optimistic and staged, with strong bodies, red banners and faces lifted toward the horizon.
cards.phrase: Socialist Realism painting, heroic worker and farm woman seen from a low angle, upward hopeful gaze, red banner, factories and wheat fields, warm sunrise light, idealized confident realism

cards.name: Art Brut / Outsider art
cards.aka: outsider art, raw art, self-taught art
cards.desc: Art made by people outside the art world (self-taught makers, hospital patients, loners) that Jean Dubuffet called "raw art". It feels urgent and private, with crude figures and every inch of the surface filled.
cards.phrase: Art Brut outsider art drawing, crude untrained figures with staring eyes, thick black outlines, obsessive repeated patterns filling every space, crayon and ink on brown paper, flat with no perspective

cards.name: Color field
cards.desc: Paintings made of big, calm areas of color meant to swallow you when you stand close. Unlike the splashy side of Abstract Expressionism, there are almost no visible gestures, just soft glowing fields.
cards.phrase: Color field painting, large soft-edged rectangles of glowing color stacked on a deep ground, feathered blurry edges, thin translucent stained paint, meditative, no brushwork, canvas texture

cards.name: Hard-edge painting
cards.desc: Abstract painting made of flat shapes with perfectly crisp borders, as if cut from colored card. It feels clean, confident and sunny, the opposite of the dripping postwar style.
cards.phrase: Hard-edge painting, flat saturated color shapes with razor-sharp borders, one bold curve against straight panels, no brushwork or texture, clean geometric abstraction, sunny California palette

cards.name: Psychedelic poster
cards.aka: San Francisco rock poster, 60s concert poster
cards.desc: Concert posters for the Fillmore and Avalon ballrooms, designed to be decoded slowly, with lettering that melts and swells to fill a shape. Clashing complementary colors make the edges seem to vibrate.
cards.phrase: Psychedelic 1960s concert poster, melting swollen hand-drawn lettering filling the shape, vibrating complementary colors red on green, wavy concentric bands, flat ink, Art Nouveau curves

cards.name: Photorealism
cards.desc: Paintings copied from photographs so precisely that they look like photos, often of ordinary things: diners, storefronts, cars, giant faces. The thrill is in the cool, impossible detail of reflections.
cards.phrase: Photorealist painting, city storefront with plate-glass windows reflecting buildings, gleaming chrome car bumper, crisp highlights, everything in sharp focus, cool even daylight, no visible brushstrokes

cards.name: Neo-expressionism
cards.desc: A loud return to painting by hand after years of cool, conceptual art: big canvases, rough figures and raw emotion. It feels like graffiti, a child's drawing and a history lesson colliding.
cards.phrase: Neo-expressionist painting, raw scrawled black lines over rough patches of bright color, masklike head with gritted teeth, crossed-out words, drips and scratches, crude energetic figures, large canvas

cards.name: Graffiti & street art
cards.desc: Art painted on walls and trains, from fast name tags to giant murals. Graffiti writers prize style in letters; street artists add stencils, paste-ups and murals that speak to passers-by.
cards.phrase: Graffiti street art on a brick wall, fat bubble-letter throw-up with black outline and white highlights, paint drips, fuzzy sprayed halo, crisp stencil figure, scribbled tags, bold saturated colors

cards.name: Lowbrow / Pop surrealism
cards.desc: Gallery painting that grew out of hot-rod "kustom kulture", underground comics and tattoo flash, made with old-master polish. Expect sweet, eerie dreamlike scenes: cute on the surface, unsettling underneath.
cards.phrase: Pop surrealism lowbrow painting, porcelain-skinned girl with huge glossy eyes, candy pastel palette, smooth old-master oil finish, ornate gilded frame, cute yet eerie dreamlike details

cards.name: Superflat
cards.desc: Takashi Murakami's name for art that merges anime, manga, kawaii character design and old Japanese painting into one flat, glossy surface. It is cheerful and dense, with an edge of critique about consumer culture.
cards.phrase: Superflat art, dense all-over pattern of smiling cartoon flowers with rainbow petals, perfectly flat color, crisp black outlines, no shading, anime kawaii style, glossy white ground

cards.name: Afrofuturism
cards.desc: Art, music and fiction that imagine Black futures by mixing space-age technology with African history and myth. The look is cosmic and regal: stars, chrome and planets meeting textile patterns and adornment; prompts should borrow its palette and pattern language rather than copy specific sacred or ceremonial designs.
cards.phrase: Afrofuturist art, regal figure with a gleaming chrome and gold headdress against a deep purple starfield, glowing sun disk, ringed planet, bold woven textile stripes, cosmic and majestic

cards.name: Glitch art
cards.desc: Art made by breaking digital images on purpose: corrupting files, misreading video or sorting pixels so the image tears apart. It feels like a broken screen, beautiful and unstable.
cards.phrase: Glitch art, digital image torn into horizontal slices shifted sideways, RGB channel split with red and cyan ghosting, pixel-sorted streaks, blocky compression artifacts, scanlines, neon error colors

cards.name: Generative art
cards.aka: algorithmic art, code art, plotter art
cards.desc: Art made by writing rules or code that then draws the picture, often with randomness built in. The result looks precise but organic, like thousands of lines combed by an invisible wind.
cards.phrase: Generative plotter art, thousands of thin black ink lines flowing along an invisible flow field, uniform pen weight, slight jitter, off-white paper, a few red accent lines, precise yet organic

cards.name: New Contemporary figurative
cards.desc: A popular strand of recent painting with simplified, flat figures who have tiny heads and huge, heavy limbs, posed calmly in rooms with plants. It feels warm, quiet and graphic, like a mid-century illustration slowed down.
cards.phrase: Contemporary flat figurative painting, seated figure with a tiny head and oversized rounded limbs, flat matte color, terracotta arch, sage and cream palette, potted monstera, calm simple interior

cards.name: Maximalism
cards.desc: The reaction to minimalism: more color, more pattern, more objects, all at once. It feels joyful and personal, as if someone collected everything they love into one room.
cards.phrase: Maximalist interior illustration, clashing patterns everywhere, floral wallpaper on emerald walls, leopard print armchair, striped rug, ornate gold mirror, lush plants, jewel tones, no empty space

cards.name: Golden Age illustration
cards.aka: Golden Age of Illustration, Edwardian gift-book illustration
cards.desc: The era when lavish illustrated books and magazines made illustrators famous: fine ink line drawing laid under soft, muted watercolor. Think fairy tales, twisted old trees and slightly eerie, enchanted woods.
cards.phrase: Golden Age storybook illustration, fine sepia ink line with muted watercolor washes, gnarled twisting tree, enchanted forest, faded earthy palette, aged paper, 1910s gift book plate

cards.name: Classic picture book
cards.aka: Storybook ink and wash, nursery illustration
cards.desc: Gentle children's book art: a delicate pen line, light washes of color and lots of empty white page around a small scene. Animals often wear little jackets and act like people.
cards.phrase: classic children's picture book illustration, delicate pen and ink with soft watercolor wash, small vignette on white paper, rabbit in a blue jacket, gentle, lots of white space

cards.name: Botanical & naturalist
cards.desc: Drawing made to identify a species: one specimen shown clearly on a plain page, with details like seeds or cross-sections beside it. Precise and calm, it reads as scientific and quietly beautiful.
cards.phrase: vintage botanical illustration plate, single specimen from root to flower on cream paper, precise fine linework and delicate watercolor, labelled detail studies, scientific accuracy

cards.name: Fashion illustration
cards.desc: Drawings made to sell clothes before photography took over: impossibly tall, elegant figures caught in a few quick strokes. The garment gets bold attention and everything else is barely suggested.
cards.phrase: mid-century fashion illustration, elongated elegant figure, bold sweeping black brushstrokes, loose watercolor wash, minimal detail, a single red accent, lots of blank paper

cards.name: Wartime propaganda poster
cards.aka: WWI and WWII poster, home-front poster
cards.desc: Posters made to recruit, ration and rally: one heroic figure seen from below, flat bold color, and a band left clear for a big slogan. Urgent, proud and very direct.
cards.phrase: vintage wartime propaganda poster, heroic figure from a low angle pointing forward, flat bold red navy and cream, sunburst rays, bold outlines, empty slogan band, lithograph texture

cards.name: Pulp cover art
cards.aka: Pulp magazine cover, golden-age sci-fi cover
cards.desc: Painted covers for cheap fiction magazines, designed to grab you from a newsstand: lurid colors, danger and wonder all at once. Rocket ships, monsters, ray guns and a hero in trouble.
cards.phrase: vintage pulp magazine cover art, lurid saturated oil paint, sleek finned rocket ship, ringed planet in a purple and orange sky, monster rising, hero in peril, dramatic

cards.name: Pin-up
cards.desc: Glossy painted calendar and ad art of cheerful, glamorous women: smooth skin, bright lipstick, a wink and a playful pose. For a tasteful result, ask for the polish and the charm (a wink, a sailor top, polka dots) rather than the cheesecake.
cards.phrase: 1950s pin-up illustration, glossy painted portrait, cheerful winking woman with victory-roll hair and red lipstick, sailor top, red polka dot background, smooth vintage calendar art

cards.name: Mid-century illustration
cards.aka: Mid-century commercial illustration, Golden Books style
cards.desc: Postwar illustration that flattened everything into lively, slightly wonky shapes in a few printed colors. Linework floats loosely off the color, and dry-brush textures make it feel hand printed.
cards.phrase: mid-century illustration, flat stylized shapes, limited palette of mustard teal coral and black, loose offset linework, dry brush textures, whimsical 1950s Golden Books feel

cards.name: Conceptual editorial
cards.desc: Illustration that carries an article's argument as one clever idea, usually a visual pun or metaphor. Very few elements and colors, so the idea lands instantly.
cards.phrase: conceptual editorial illustration, single clever visual metaphor, minimal flat shapes, limited palette of navy cream and red, lots of negative space, witty and simple

cards.name: Rubber hose
cards.desc: The look of the earliest sound cartoons: characters with bendy, boneless limbs that bounce to the music. Black and white, round and endlessly cheerful (or slightly creepy).
cards.phrase: 1930s rubber hose cartoon, black and white, bouncy character with noodle limbs and white gloves, pie-cut eyes, big grin, smiling sun, film grain and vignette

cards.name: UPA cartoon modern
cards.desc: A modernist rebellion against round Disney cartoons: angular, flat characters and backgrounds made of loose abstract color blocks. Color shapes and lines are drawn separately, so they do not quite line up.
cards.phrase: 1950s UPA cartoon modern style, angular flat stylized character, abstract color block background, thin line furniture drawn off the color, mustard coral and teal palette

cards.name: Ligne claire
cards.desc: Comics drawn with one even, clean outline around everything and flat bright color inside, with no hatching or heavy shadow. Every object reads crisply, from the car to the window frames.
cards.phrase: ligne claire comic illustration, uniform clean black outlines, flat bright colors, no hatching or shading, detailed European street with vintage car, clear daylight

cards.name: Silver Age superhero comic
cards.aka: Silver Age comics, Kirby style, four-color comics
cards.desc: Bold, energetic comic books printed in cheap four-color: heroes punch straight out of the page while cosmic energy crackles around them. Everything is louder, closer and more dramatic.
cards.phrase: Silver Age comic book art, dynamic foreshortened hero punching toward viewer, thick black inks, Ben-Day dots, Kirby crackle energy, four-color print, primary colors, starburst

cards.name: Underground comix
cards.desc: Self-published, rule-breaking comics of the counterculture, drawn in dense black and white pen. Rubbery, lumpy characters strut through scenes buried in obsessive crosshatching.
cards.phrase: underground comix style, black and white pen and ink, dense crosshatching, rubbery cartoon figure strutting with huge feet, wobbly hand-inked lines, 1960s counterculture

cards.name: Manga
cards.aka: Japanese comics, black and white manga
cards.desc: Japanese comics, mostly black and white, where gray comes from printed dot screens called screentone. Big expressive eyes, speed lines and dramatic panel shapes carry the emotion and the action.
cards.phrase: black and white manga page, angled panels, screentone shading, radiating speed lines, close-up of a large glossy expressive eye with highlights, crisp ink lines

cards.name: Kawaii & chibi
cards.desc: Japanese cute culture: round, soft characters with oversized heads, tiny bodies and minimal faces. Chibi means drawing any character this way, about two heads tall.
cards.phrase: kawaii chibi illustration, round character with oversized head and tiny body, simple dot eyes, pink blush cheeks, pastel colors, soft rounded outlines, little hearts and stars

cards.name: European sci-fi comics
cards.aka: Métal hurlant style, bande dessinée sci-fi
cards.desc: Adult French science fiction comics with vast, dreamlike alien landscapes drawn in delicate line and pale, strange color. Tiny travelers cross enormous deserts under giant planets.
cards.phrase: European 1970s sci-fi comic art, vast alien desert, tiny rider on a strange creature, giant pale planet, fine clean pen line, pastel peach turquoise and lilac color

cards.name: American traditional tattoo
cards.aka: Old school tattoo, Sailor Jerry flash
cards.desc: Classic tattoo designs drawn as "flash" sheets for customers to pick from: bold, simple and built to last on skin. Thick black outlines hold a few strong colors.
cards.phrase: American traditional tattoo flash, bold black outlines, solid red green yellow and navy, swallow, rose pierced by a dagger, stars, vintage parchment background

cards.name: Concept art & matte painting
cards.aka: Pre-production art, environment concept, speed painting
cards.desc: Paintings made to imagine a film or game world before it is built: huge scale, moody light and atmosphere over detail. Quick broad brushwork sets the mood, and a tiny figure gives the size.
cards.phrase: cinematic concept art, atmospheric speed painting, colossal towers fading into haze, tiny silhouette figure on a cliff, god rays, broad textured brushstrokes, moody desaturated palette

cards.name: Madhubani
cards.desc: Painting from the Mithila region of Bihar, made for generations by women on the mud walls of their homes for weddings and festivals, and on paper since the 1960s. Every figure gets a double outline and every gap is filled with pattern, so the picture feels dense, joyful and ceremonial.
cards.phrase: Madhubani (Mithila) painting style: double black ink outlines, every gap filled with hatching and tiny flowers, stylized fish and peacock, flat red, turmeric yellow, indigo and green, triangle border

cards.name: Gond art
cards.desc: Painting by the Pardhan Gond community of central India, carried from house walls onto paper and canvas by Jangarh Singh Shyam in the 1980s. Animals and trees are drawn as bold flat silhouettes and then filled with rhythmic dots, dashes and lines, so they seem to hum with life.
cards.phrase: Gond art style: flat silhouettes of a deer and a tree, filled with rhythmic dots, dashes and fine lines, bright orange, green, yellow and blue on cream, no shading

cards.name: Tenango embroidery
cards.desc: Hand embroidery from the Otomí villages of the Sierra Otomí-Tepehua, where deer, birds, rabbits and flowering plants are stitched in dense satin stitch on white cotton, in a single bold color or a rainbow. The designs are a community heritage, so borrow the look (flat stitched silhouettes, symmetry, color) rather than copying a real piece.
cards.phrase: Tenango Otomí embroidery style: flat satin-stitched silhouettes of deer, birds and flowers on white cotton, visible thread direction, rainbow of solid colors, mirrored folk layout, no outlines

cards.name: Calavera print
cards.desc: Cheap satirical broadsheet prints by José Guadalupe Posada showing skeletons dressed as fine ladies, dandies and politicians, a cheerful reminder that death comes for everyone. His elegant skeleton lady, La Catrina, became the face of Día de Muertos.
cards.phrase: In the manner of José Guadalupe Posada: calavera relief print, grinning skeleton lady in a wide feathered hat, black ink on off-white newsprint, bold cut lines and hatching

cards.name: Papel picado
cards.desc: Mexican banners of colored tissue paper with lace-like designs chiseled through stacks of sheets, strung across streets, churches and altars for fiestas and Día de Muertos. The light shines through the holes, so the effect is bright, fluttering and festive.
cards.phrase: Papel picado style: strings of bright tissue paper banners in hot pink, orange, green and purple, intricate symmetrical cut-out flowers, skulls and lattices, scalloped edges, blue sky showing through

cards.name: Wycinanki
cards.desc: Polish folk paper-cutting, first done with sheep shears to brighten cottage walls and beams for Easter. Łowicz cuts stack layer upon layer of glossy colored paper into mirror-symmetric roosters, birds and flower trees, while Kurpie cuts are single-color silhouettes.
cards.phrase: Polish wycinanki paper-cut style: mirror-symmetric roosters facing a flower tree, stacked layers of glossy red, yellow, blue, green and magenta paper on a dark base, crisp scissor-cut edges, white background

cards.name: Chinese paper-cut
cards.desc: Designs cut from a single sheet of red paper, often folded so the pattern repeats in perfect symmetry, and pasted on windows and doors for Spring Festival and weddings. Lucky subjects such as fish, peonies, zodiac animals and characters like 福 (good fortune) are held together by a lace of crescent and sawtooth cuts.
cards.phrase: Chinese jianzhi paper-cut style: round red window flower cut from a single sheet, radial symmetry, crescent and sawtooth lace cuts, leaf motifs, crisp edges, soft shadow on cream

cards.name: Rosemaling
cards.desc: Decorative folk painting on wooden bowls, trunks, cupboards and church walls in rural Norway, adapted from Baroque and Rococo acanthus ornament. Big C and S scrolls sweep around stylized flowers in confident single brushstrokes, finished with fine pale liner work.
cards.phrase: Norwegian rosemaling style: sweeping C and S scrolls, acanthus leaves and a stylized rose, tapered single brushstrokes, cream liner work, ochre, red and blue on deep teal painted wood

cards.name: Pennsylvania Dutch fraktur & hex signs
cards.aka: Pennsylvania German folk art, barn stars, distelfink
cards.desc: Folk art of German-speaking settlers in Pennsylvania: brightly painted, hand-lettered birth and marriage certificates (fraktur) and, later, big round star paintings on barns (hex signs). Both share one cheerful vocabulary of distelfink birds, tulips, hearts and compass stars.
cards.phrase: Pennsylvania Dutch folk art style: round hex sign with an eight-point compass rosette and scalloped border, distelfink birds and tulips, flat red, yellow, green and blue on red barn boards

cards.name: Northwest Coast formline
cards.aka: formline design, Haida, Tlingit, Tsimshian, Kwakwaka’wakw art
cards.desc: The design system of the Haida, Tlingit, Tsimshian, Kwakwaka’wakw and neighboring Nations, used on poles, bentwood boxes, masks and Chilkat blankets: black lines that swell and taper to form ovoids and U-shapes, with red secondary lines. Crests and specific designs belong to families and clans, so borrow only the visual grammar (ovoids, U-forms, black and red), never a particular crest or artwork.
cards.phrase: Northwest Coast formline-inspired design: interlocking ovoids and U-forms in bold black lines that swell and taper, red secondary shapes, small blue-green accents, flat on natural cream, tight symmetrical panel

cards.name: Aboriginal dot painting
cards.aka: Western Desert painting, Papunya Tula style
cards.desc: Acrylic painting that began at Papunya in 1971, when Western Desert artists moved designs from ground drawings, body paint and ceremony onto boards and canvas, often using dots to veil restricted sacred details. Many designs belong to particular people, Country and Dreaming stories, so prompts should borrow only the technique and palette (dotting, concentric circles, earth colors), never the stories or symbols.
cards.phrase: Western Desert-inspired dot painting technique: dense fields of small round dots, concentric dotted circles linked by dotted paths, red ochre, yellow ochre, white and black on dark brown, aerial view

cards.name: Alebrijes
cards.desc: Fantastical hybrid creatures first made in papier-mâché by Pedro Linares in Mexico City, from a fever dream, and later carved from copal wood in Oaxacan villages like San Antonio Arrazola and San Martín Tilcajete. They are painted in electric colors and covered edge to edge in tiny dots, stripes and zigzags.
cards.phrase: Alebrije folk art style: fantastical winged horned creature with a curly tail, hand-painted in hot pink, turquoise, orange and yellow, every surface covered in tiny dots, stripes and zigzags

cards.name: Islamic geometric pattern
cards.desc: Pattern built with compass and straightedge from repeating stars and polygons, used across the mosques, palaces and manuscripts of the Islamic world in tile, carved plaster and wood. Bands seem to weave over and under each other without end, suggesting infinite order without showing any figures.
cards.phrase: Islamic geometric pattern style: interlocking eight-point stars and crosses, white strapwork interlace, zellige tile mosaic in cobalt, green, ochre and black, framed by a pointed arch in carved plaster

cards.name: Celtic knotwork
cards.desc: Endless interlaced bands from the illuminated Gospel books and carved stone crosses of early medieval Ireland and Britain. Each strand passes alternately over and under the next with no loose ends, so the eye keeps travelling round in loops.
cards.phrase: Celtic knotwork style: ribbons strictly alternating over and under, no loose ends, gold strands with black outlines on dark green, framed panel with red dot border, illuminated manuscript

cards.name: Arts & Crafts pattern
cards.desc: Wallpaper and textile design from the Arts and Crafts movement, which championed handcraft over cheap factory goods. William Morris drew dense, flat, medieval-inspired repeats of twisting vines, leaves, flowers and birds that fill the whole surface with a calm rhythm.
cards.phrase: In the manner of William Morris: dense seamless repeat of twisting vines, leaves, flowers, berries and thrushes, flat woodblock-printed indigo, sage green, madder red and cream

cards.name: Batik
cards.desc: Indonesian cloth decorated by drawing hot wax onto cotton with a small copper pen (canting) or stamp, dyeing it, and repeating, so the waxed lines stay pale. Classic court batik of Yogyakarta and Solo uses indigo and sogan brown with motifs like the diagonal parang blade and the four-oval kawung, and fine crackle lines appear where the wax cracks in the dye.
cards.phrase: Javanese batik style: wax-resist cotton with diagonal parang bands and a kawung border, cream wax lines on sogan brown and indigo, fine crackle veins, soft dye-bled edges, flat textile pattern

cards.name: Blue-and-white tile
cards.desc: Cobalt blue painted on white glaze, perfected on Chinese porcelain under the Yuan and Ming dynasties and then imitated in Dutch Delftware and Portuguese azulejo tiles. The brush leaves pooled darks and pale washes, giving a cool, crisp, hand-painted look.
cards.phrase: Blue-and-white tile style: hand-painted cobalt blue on glossy white tin glaze, brushy pale-to-dark washes, repeating floral azulejo tiles whose corner motifs join into circles across thin grout lines

cards.name: Kente cloth
cards.desc: Hand-woven cloth of the Asante and Ewe peoples of Ghana, made on narrow looms as long strips that are sewn edge to edge so blocks of pattern form a checkerboard. Each pattern has a name and every color carries meaning (gold for wealth, green for growth, red for sacrifice and struggle), so treat it as meaningful cloth and borrow the woven structure and palette rather than presenting a named pattern as generic decoration.
cards.phrase: Kente-inspired hand-woven textile: narrow strips sewn side by side, offset checkerboard of warp stripes and geometric weft blocks, gold, green, red and black, visible thread texture

cards.name: Wagara patterns
cards.aka: Japanese traditional patterns, seigaiha, asanoha, shippo
cards.desc: Named repeating motifs on Japanese kimono, furoshiki, ceramics and paper, each carrying a wish: seigaiha waves for calm and good fortune, asanoha hemp leaf for healthy growth, shippo interlocking circles for harmony. They are crisp, geometric and endlessly repeatable.
cards.phrase: Japanese wagara pattern style: patchwork panels of seigaiha wave scales in indigo, asanoha hemp-leaf star lattice on vermilion, shippo interlocking circles in gold on cream, crisp fine lines

cards.name: Mandala & rangoli
cards.desc: Radially symmetric designs drawn on floors and doorsteps across South Asia in colored powder, rice flour or flower petals, especially for Diwali, Pongal and weddings, as a welcome and blessing for the home. Some mandalas, such as Tibetan Buddhist sand mandalas, are sacred diagrams, so borrow the radial symmetry, petals and color rather than reproducing a ritual design.
cards.phrase: Rangoli style: radially symmetric floor design with rings of petals and dots in magenta, saffron, yellow, green and blue powder, white rice-flour outlines, soft grainy edges, small clay oil lamps

cards.name: Woodcut
cards.desc: A picture carved into a plank of wood along the grain, then inked and pressed onto paper, so every white is a cut and every black is wood left standing. It feels bold, rough and urgent; unlike linocut, the wood fights back, leaving grain streaks and splintery edges.
cards.phrase: Woodcut print, plank wood grain visible in the solid blacks, splintery gouged white lines, chunky black shapes, rough edges, black ink on cream paper, stark expressive carving

cards.name: Wood engraving
cards.desc: Cut into the hard end grain of boxwood with fine engraving tools, so the artist draws in thin white lines out of a black block. The result is tiny, crisp and silvery, with skies made of hundreds of fine parallel lines.
cards.phrase: Wood engraving, fine white lines cut from a black block, tightly ruled parallel-line sky, crisp miniature detail, small oval vignette with broken edges, black ink on white paper

cards.name: Etching
cards.desc: The artist scratches through a wax coating on a copper plate and lets acid bite the lines, so they flow as freely as a pen sketch. Prints carry a faint film of plate tone and a pressed rectangle (the plate mark) around the image.
cards.phrase: Etching on cream paper, delicate wandering acid-bitten lines, loose scribbled hatching, soft plate tone, visible plate mark border, warm brown-black ink, airy open composition

cards.name: Engraving
cards.aka: line engraving, burin engraving, banknote engraving
cards.desc: Lines are pushed into a metal plate with a sharp burin, so each one starts thin, swells and tapers like a ribbon. Engravers model form with orderly parallel lines that curve around a face, which is why it still says money, stamps and official portraits.
cards.phrase: Line engraving, crisp burin lines that swell and taper, parallel curved hatching following the form, guilloche oval frame, banknote portrait style, single dark green ink on pale paper

cards.name: Mezzotint
cards.desc: The whole plate is roughened so it would print solid velvety black, then the artist scrapes and burnishes it smooth where light should be. It works from dark to light, giving soft glowing forms floating out of deep shadow.
cards.phrase: Mezzotint print, deep velvety black ground, forms scraped up into soft glowing light, no outlines, smooth tonal gradations, fine grainy texture, quiet still life

cards.name: Lithograph poster
cards.desc: Drawn with greasy crayon and ink on a flat stone, so prints keep the grainy crayon texture alongside big flat color areas. Belle Époque poster artists added "crachis", a spatter flicked from a toothbrush, for speckled tones.
cards.phrase: Belle Époque color lithograph poster, flat bold areas of ochre, olive and red, grainy crayon texture, spatter crachis speckles, cropped black silhouette in the foreground, hand-drawn lettering

cards.name: Letterpress
cards.aka: wood type, relief printing, hand-set type
cards.desc: Raised metal or wood letters are inked and pressed hard into thick paper, so the type bites in and leaves a slight dent. The ink is never perfectly even: you get a darker rim where it squeezes out and tiny speckles where it skipped.
cards.phrase: Letterpress print, chunky wood type, deep impression in thick cotton paper, ink squeeze at the letter edges, slightly uneven speckled coverage, red and black ink, ornamental rules

cards.name: Pochoir & stencil
cards.desc: Color is dabbed by hand through a series of cut stencils, one per color, over a printed black outline. It gives crisp flat jewel-like color with soft mottled dabbing inside and a little pooling of pigment at the stencil edges.
cards.phrase: Pochoir stencil print, flat saturated jewel colors, hand-dabbed mottled color with darker pooled edges, thin black key line slightly out of register, 1920s fashion plate, cream paper

cards.name: Monotype
cards.desc: The artist paints or rolls ink onto a smooth plate, wipes some away with rags, fingers or brushes, then presses a single sheet onto it. Only one strong print is possible, and it looks like a ghostly, soft-edged painting.
cards.phrase: Monotype print, dark ink plate with light wiped out by rag and fingers, soft ghostly blurred edges, brush drag marks, mottled pressed texture, touches of muted color, moody landscape

cards.name: Etching with aquatint
cards.desc: Powdered resin is melted onto the plate so the acid bites around each grain, giving grainy tones like a wash instead of lines. Mixed with etched lines it creates dramatic pools of shadow and light, perfect for dark, dreamlike scenes.
cards.phrase: Etching with aquatint, grainy tonal washes in sepia stepping from light to deep shadow, crisp etched outlines, dramatic night sky, pool of light, moody satirical scene

cards.name: Fresco
cards.desc: Pigment painted into wet lime plaster so it dries as part of the wall. Colors come out chalky, matte and soft, and old frescoes show cracks, faded patches and bare plaster where pieces have fallen away.
cards.phrase: Ancient fresco on lime plaster, chalky matte colors, Pompeian red panel with ochre borders, floating figure, hairline cracks, flaked areas of bare plaster, softly faded

cards.name: Egg tempera
cards.desc: Pigment mixed with egg yolk dries in seconds, so painters build forms from countless tiny hatched strokes instead of blending. It gives pale, luminous, slightly flat color, often against a background of gold leaf.
cards.phrase: Egg tempera on gold-ground panel, fine hatched brushstrokes building the face, green underpaint in the shadows, pale luminous color, crisp contours, ultramarine robe, medieval Italian icon feeling

cards.name: Encaustic
cards.desc: Pigment mixed into melted beeswax and brushed on hot, so each stroke sets in a rich translucent layer. It looks waxy and luminous, with soft thick strokes that catch the light like the Fayum mummy portraits.
cards.phrase: Encaustic painting on wood panel, translucent layers of pigmented beeswax, soft thick rounded strokes, waxy sheen, luminous skin, large dark eyes, Fayum portrait feeling

cards.name: Mosaic
cards.desc: Pictures built from small cut cubes of stone or glass (tesserae) set in mortar. The direction the rows flow (the andamento) traces each shape, like contour lines echoing around a figure.
cards.phrase: Roman floor mosaic, small square stone tesserae with grey grout, rows of tiles flowing around the figure, cream background with halo rows, terracotta and slate blue, patterned border

cards.name: Gold leaf & gilding
cards.desc: Gold beaten thinner than tissue is laid over a red clay (bole), burnished to a mirror shine, then pressed with punches and incised lines. Where it wears, the warm red shows through.
cards.phrase: Gilded panel, burnished gold leaf over red bole, halo tooled with punched dot rings and rosettes, incised rays, worn edges showing red, ultramarine mantle, medieval altarpiece

cards.name: Paper marbling
cards.desc: Colors are floated on a bath of thickened water, combed or pulled into patterns, and lifted off with a sheet of paper. Every sheet is one of a kind, full of swirling bands, feathered combing and round "stones".
cards.phrase: Marbled paper, ebru, colors floating in swirling combed bands, feathered and zigzag pulls, round dropped stones, navy, crimson, ochre and cream, antique book endpaper

cards.name: Embroidery & cross-stitch
cards.desc: Pictures stitched in thread on cloth. Satin stitch lays glossy parallel threads across a shape, while cross-stitch builds pixel-like images from little X stitches on a grid.
cards.phrase: Hand embroidery on natural linen, glossy satin-stitch petals, stem stitch and French knots, a cross-stitch heart on a grid, visible thread texture, wooden hoop, soft daylight

cards.name: Scratchboard
cards.desc: A board coated with white clay and black ink: the artist scratches away the black with a blade, so the image is made of fine white lines on black. It is brilliant for fur, feathers and crisp, high-contrast detail.
cards.phrase: Scratchboard illustration, fine white lines scratched from solid black, fur and feathers rendered with short crisp strokes, radiating line patterns, stark high contrast

cards.name: Silverpoint
cards.desc: Drawing with a thin silver wire on paper coated with a tinted ground: the lines are always faint, fine and silvery grey and cannot be erased. Renaissance masters used it for delicate studies of heads and hands.
cards.phrase: Silverpoint drawing on blue-grey prepared paper, faint fine silvery lines, delicate parallel hatching, white heightening on the highlights, Renaissance profile study, visible corrected lines

cards.name: Enamel & cloisonné
cards.desc: Thin gold or brass wires are bent into cells on a metal object, filled with powdered colored glass and fired until glossy. Every color sits in its own wire-edged cell, like a stained-glass window you can hold.
cards.phrase: Cloisonné enamel vase, thin gold wire outlines around every cell, glossy vitreous enamel in turquoise, coral and cobalt, lotus motif, scrolling wire clouds, bright specular highlights

cards.name: Patchwork quilt
cards.aka: pieced quilt, log cabin, improv quilting
cards.desc: Fabric scraps sewn into repeating blocks, then layered and stitched through with small running stitches. Patterns range from orderly log cabin squares to the bold improvised strips of the Gee's Bend quilters of Alabama.
cards.phrase: Patchwork quilt, pieced cotton fabrics in small prints and solids, log cabin blocks with light and dark halves, one improvised housetop block, visible hand quilting stitches, warm faded colors

cards.name: Silhouette cut
cards.desc: Shapes cut from black paper with scissors and set against a light ground, from tiny profile portraits to whole fairy-tale scenes. Lotte Reiniger animated such cut-outs in the 1920s, adding lacy trees and curling vines.
cards.phrase: Black paper silhouette cut, crisp scissor-cut profile portrait, lacy cut-out collar, curling vine and bird, solid black shapes against a warm amber gradient, fairy-tale shadow theatre

cards.name: Chiaroscuro
cards.desc: Strong light and shadow used to make forms look round and solid, with one clear light source falling across the subject. Italian for "light-dark", it gives a picture weight, warmth and drama.
cards.phrase: chiaroscuro oil painting, single warm light from upper left, forms modelled from bright highlight into deep shadow, rich brown darks, strong cast shadows

cards.name: Tenebrism
cards.desc: The extreme form of chiaroscuro: most of the picture drops into pure black, and a spotlight or candle picks out only faces and hands. It feels theatrical, secret and intense.
cards.phrase: tenebrist painting, figure emerging from pitch-black darkness, lit only by a single candle, hard falloff to black, glowing faces and hands, warm amber light

cards.name: Sfumato
cards.desc: Tones melt into one another like smoke, with no hard outlines anywhere, so faces seem to breathe and edges dissolve into haze. Leonardo used it to make expressions feel ambiguous and alive.
cards.phrase: sfumato oil portrait, smoky soft transitions with no hard edges or outlines, veiled shadows around eyes and mouth, hazy blue-green landscape behind, muted warm palette

cards.name: Grisaille
cards.desc: A painting made entirely in shades of grey, often to imitate carved stone statues in niches. Painters also used it as a first layer to work out light and shadow before adding color.
cards.phrase: grisaille painting, entirely in shades of grey, figures rendered like carved stone statues standing in painted niches, crisp sculptural lighting, no color

cards.name: Glazing
cards.desc: Thin, transparent layers of color are laid one over another on top of a monochrome underpainting, so light passes through and bounces back like stained glass. It gives jewel-like depth and glow that a single coat of paint cannot.
cards.phrase: oil painting built with transparent glazes, luminous jewel-like color glowing from within, smooth enamel surface without visible brushstrokes, deep layered crimson and ultramarine

cards.name: Alla prima
cards.desc: Painting finished in one sitting, wet paint into wet paint, with each stroke put down confidently and left alone. The result is fresh, loose and lively, with the brushwork on show.
cards.phrase: alla prima oil painting, wet-into-wet, bold confident visible brushstrokes, loose fresh handling, crisp highlights flicked on top, painted in a single sitting

cards.name: Scumbling
cards.desc: A thin, broken layer of light opaque paint is dragged over a darker dry layer so the color below peeks through. It makes hazy veils of mist, smoke, dusty light and soft skies.
cards.phrase: oil painting with scumbled veils, thin broken layers of pale opaque paint dragged over dark underpainting, hazy misty light, glowing sunset haze, soft atmospheric texture

cards.name: Dry brush
cards.desc: A brush with very little paint is dragged across textured paper so the color catches only on the peaks, leaving scratchy, broken strokes. It is perfect for dry grass, weathered wood and hair.
cards.phrase: dry brush painting, scratchy broken strokes dragged over textured paper, fine detailed dry grass and weathered wood, muted ochre and grey palette, quiet rural mood

cards.name: Palette knife
cards.desc: Paint is spread with a flat metal knife instead of a brush, leaving thick, flat slabs of color with sharp ridges at their edges. The surface looks chunky, sculptural and bold.
cards.phrase: palette knife painting, thick flat slabs of paint with sharp ridged edges, bold unblended color, chunky sculptural texture, angular planes catching the light

cards.name: Trompe-l'oeil
cards.desc: French for "deceive the eye": painting so realistic, life-size and shallow that it seems to be a real object. Typical tricks are a fly on the frame, papers pinned to a wooden board or something poking out of the picture.
cards.phrase: trompe-l'oeil painting, hyperreal life-size objects in very shallow space, papers pinned to a wooden board with curling corners, crisp cast shadows, a fly resting on the frame

cards.name: Visible underdrawing
cards.desc: A painting left partly unfinished, so the pencil or charcoal sketch, grid lines and raw canvas edges are still showing beside the painted parts. It reveals the process and feels honest and immediate.
cards.phrase: unfinished oil painting, half painted and half visible pencil underdrawing, construction lines and grid showing, raw canvas edges, process visible

cards.name: Tonalism
cards.desc: Landscapes painted in one narrow, muted color family, wrapped in haze at dusk, night or fog, so everything feels soft, quiet and dreamy. Whistler called his night pictures "nocturnes", like pieces of music.
cards.phrase: tonalist nocturne painting, muted unified blue-green haze, low contrast soft silhouettes at twilight, a few tiny glowing lights reflected in still water, quiet dreamy mood

cards.name: Gesture drawing
cards.desc: Very fast drawings, often 30 seconds to two minutes, that catch the movement and energy of a pose rather than its details. A single sweeping "line of action" sets the curve of the whole body.
cards.phrase: gesture drawing, fast flowing charcoal lines capturing movement, strong curved line of action through each figure, simple oval heads, no detail, several dynamic poses on cream paper

cards.name: Blind contour
cards.desc: A drawing made with one slow line while looking only at the subject, never at the paper. The parts drift out of place, giving a wobbly, charming, oddly truthful result.
cards.phrase: blind contour drawing, single wobbly continuous ink line, features slightly misaligned and drifting, no shading, naive charming distortion on white paper

cards.name: Continuous line
cards.desc: The whole picture is one unbroken line, pen never lifted, but unlike blind contour it is controlled and graceful. It is popular for minimal portraits, tattoos and logos.
cards.phrase: continuous line drawing, one smooth unbroken black line forming a minimal face profile, elegant looping strokes, lots of negative space, single soft color accent

cards.name: Line and wash
cards.desc: A loose pen drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid in quickly, the color not quite matching the lines. It feels like an on-the-spot travel sketch.
cards.phrase: line and wash urban sketch, loose fine ink pen lines, transparent watercolor washes spilling past the outlines, white paper showing, lively street scene

cards.name: Sanguine
cards.desc: Drawing in reddish-brown chalk on cream paper, the favorite medium for Renaissance figure and head studies. The warm color makes skin look alive with very little effort.
cards.phrase: sanguine red chalk drawing on cream paper, Renaissance study of a head, warm rust-colored lines, diagonal parallel hatching for shadows, soft paper texture

cards.name: Trois crayons
cards.desc: Black, red and white chalk together on toned paper: black for line and dark, red for warmth in cheeks and lips, and white for highlights. The mid-tone paper does the rest, so three sticks give a full, lifelike effect.
cards.phrase: trois crayons drawing, black, red and white chalk on toned tan paper, delicate head study, red warming cheeks and lips, white chalk highlights, paper as mid-tone

cards.name: Value study
cards.desc: A quick painting or drawing that reduces a scene to three to five flat shades of grey, with no detail. It checks whether a composition reads from light and dark alone before color is added.
cards.phrase: value study, landscape simplified into four flat grey tones, big simple shapes, no detail or texture, clear light, mid and dark separation

cards.name: Notan
cards.desc: A Japanese design idea about the balance of dark and light: the picture is designed using just two flat values, so the shapes of the black and the white must both be beautiful. Arthur Wesley Dow taught it to American artists.
cards.phrase: notan design, two flat values only, pure black and cream shapes interlocking, pine branch and full moon silhouette, balanced asymmetric composition, no gradients

cards.name: Academic figure drawing
cards.desc: The slow, careful drawing taught in art academies: copying plaster casts and models under steady light, measuring with plumb lines, and rendering every tone smoothly. It looks calm, precise and highly finished.
cards.phrase: academic cast drawing, plaster sphere, cube and cone under one steady light, smooth graphite tonal rendering, core shadows and reflected light, faint plumb line and measuring marks

cards.name: Ballpoint pen
cards.desc: Drawing in an ordinary blue ballpoint, building darks by layering fine hatching and scribbles. It ranges from loose notebook doodles to surprisingly detailed renderings.
cards.phrase: blue ballpoint pen drawing on lined notebook paper, layered fine crosshatching building dark tones, scribbled shading, casual sketchbook doodle feel

cards.name: Thumbnail sketches
cards.desc: Tiny, rough boxes drawn side by side to try out different compositions in seconds before committing to a final picture. Only the big shapes and placement matter.
cards.phrase: page of thumbnail sketches, grid of tiny rough boxed compositions in grey marker, blocky simple shapes, one favorite circled in red pencil, planning stage

cards.name: Hieronymus Bosch
cards.desc: Wide, pale landscapes swarming with tiny naked people, hybrid creatures and giant fruit, painted as busy moral allegories. It feels like a dream told by a preacher with a wicked sense of humor.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Hieronymus Bosch: Netherlandish oil on panel, pale green high-horizon landscape, swarms of tiny pale figures, hybrid creatures, giant fruit, eggshell houses, crisp detail

cards.name: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
cards.desc: Busy village scenes seen from a high viewpoint, full of peasants working, feasting and playing, set in a sweeping landscape. It feels earthy, humorous and alive, like a whole community on one panel.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Pieter Bruegel the Elder: Flemish oil on panel, high bird's-eye village view, crowds of stocky peasants in red and white, earthy browns, blue-green distance

cards.name: Johannes Vermeer
cards.desc: A single person absorbed in a quiet task in a room lit by a window on the left. The light is soft and pearly, and everything feels still, clean and intimate.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Johannes Vermeer: Dutch Golden Age oil, quiet interior, pearly daylight from a left window, lone figure in lemon yellow and ultramarine, checkered floor, still

cards.name: Rembrandt
cards.aka: golden light out of deep brown shadow
cards.desc: Faces and hands glow with warm golden light while everything else sinks into deep brown darkness. The paint is thick where the light falls, which makes the people feel tender, aged and real.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Rembrandt: Dutch Baroque oil portrait, warm golden light on face and hands, deep brown shadow, thick impasto highlights, loose soft edges, tender aged character

cards.name: J. M. W. Turner
cards.desc: Seas, storms and sunsets painted as swirling veils of light and mist, where boats and buildings almost melt away. It feels sublime: the weather is the real subject.
cards.phrase: in the manner of J. M. W. Turner: Romantic oil, swirling vortex of golden light and mist, sea and sky dissolving, dark ship fading into haze, luminous yellow on grey-blue

cards.name: Vincent van Gogh
cards.desc: Everything, even the sky, is built from thick, short, directional brushstrokes in intense blues and yellows. The marks swirl and flicker, so the scene feels charged with emotion and movement.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Vincent van Gogh: Post-Impressionist oil, thick short directional impasto strokes, swirling sky, cobalt blue and chrome yellow, twisting trees, glowing halo sun, vivid and restless

cards.name: Gustav Klimt
cards.desc: Pale, dreamy faces and hands float inside robes and backgrounds made of real gold leaf and mosaic-like ornament. It feels sensual, decorative and precious, like an icon crossed with a jewel box.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Gustav Klimt: Vienna Secession painting, gold leaf, flat mosaic ornament of spirals, eyes and rectangles, softly modeled pale face with closed eyes, scattered flower meadow

cards.name: Henri Matisse (cut-outs)
cards.desc: In his last years Matisse cut shapes straight out of paper he had painted in pure color, then pinned them up: seaweed fronds, stars, dancers. The result is joyful, flat and bold, with the slightly wobbly edge of scissors.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Henri Matisse's late paper cut-outs: flat painted-paper shapes with wobbly scissor edges, seaweed fronds and stars, saturated ultramarine, magenta, orange and green on white

cards.name: Hilma af Klint
cards.desc: Huge, symmetrical abstract paintings made as spiritual diagrams: spirals, petals, split circles and soft curls in pinks, oranges, lavenders and blues. They feel botanical, mystical and calm, years before abstraction had a name.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Hilma af Klint: early abstract tempera, symmetrical diagram of petals, snail spirals and split yellow-blue circles, flat pastel peach, pink and lavender, mystical and botanical

cards.name: Wassily Kandinsky
cards.desc: Pure abstract compositions built like music: circles, triangles, crossing lines and checkerboards in vivid color on a soft ground. It feels playful and rhythmic, as if shapes were notes.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Wassily Kandinsky: geometric abstract painting, circles with soft halos, concentric rings, crisp crossing black lines, triangles and checkerboards, primary colors on warm cream, musical rhythm

cards.name: Edward Hopper
cards.desc: Plain American rooms, diners and streets, with one or two people sitting still in hard slabs of sunlight or electric light. It feels quiet, lonely and cinematic, like a paused film.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Edward Hopper: American realist oil, solitary figure in a plain room, hard slabs of window sunlight, muted green, ochre and brick red, cinematic loneliness

cards.name: René Magritte
cards.desc: Ordinary things (apples, bowler hats, clouds, doors) painted flatly and politely, then put in impossible situations or at impossible sizes. Calm and clear on the surface, quietly unsettling underneath.
cards.phrase: in the manner of René Magritte: deadpan Surrealist oil, smooth flat paint, ordinary objects at impossible scale, clear blue sky with puffy clouds, bowler-hatted man, crisp clean edges, quietly uncanny

cards.name: Georgia O'Keeffe
cards.desc: Flowers painted so close up that they fill the whole canvas, plus sun-bleached bones and smooth New Mexico hills. The paint is silky and the forms are simplified into soft, flowing curves.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Georgia O'Keeffe: American modernist oil, extreme close-up flower filling the frame, silky smooth gradients, simplified flowing petals, soft pink and white into a deep center

cards.name: Frida Kahlo
cards.desc: Frontal, steady-eyed portraits framed by lush leaves, flowers and animals, painted in the flat, bright, symbolic style of Mexican folk retablos. They feel personal, proud and emblematic.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Frida Kahlo: Mexican folk-influenced oil, frontal portrait with steady gaze, flower crown and braids, embroidered blouse, parrot, dense tropical leaves, flat bright symbolic color

cards.name: M. C. Escher
cards.desc: Precise black-and-white prints of interlocking shapes that tile the plane and slowly turn into birds or fish, and of buildings whose stairs loop impossibly. They feel like mathematical puzzles you can look at.
cards.phrase: in the manner of M. C. Escher: black-and-white lithograph, interlocking tessellation that gradually morphs from checkerboard into birds, crisp exact lines, mathematical and impossible

cards.name: Arthur Rackham
cards.desc: Fairy-tale illustrations drawn in fine, nervous pen line and tinted with muted sepia, grey-green and rust washes. Trees have faces and twisting roots, and goblins and fairies lurk in the misty half-light.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Arthur Rackham: Edwardian fairy-tale illustration, fine brown pen line, muted sepia, grey-green and rust washes, gnarled trees with faces, spindly branches, misty and eerie

cards.name: Beatrix Potter
cards.desc: Small, accurately observed animals wearing a jacket or apron, painted in delicate watercolor over light pencil. The pictures are small and fade softly into white paper, so they feel cozy, quiet and true to nature.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Beatrix Potter: delicate Edwardian watercolor over light pencil, realistic small animal wearing a little jacket, soft garden setting, vignette fading into white paper

cards.name: Tove Jansson
cards.aka: inky Nordic islands and soft round creatures
cards.desc: Confident black pen line with dense hatching for storms and night, plus flat muted color for sea and rock. Her worlds are rocky Finnish islands with lighthouses and round, soft little beings, both cozy and melancholy.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Tove Jansson: Nordic pen-and-ink illustration, confident black line, dense hatching for stormy sky, flat muted blue sea and grey rocks, lighthouse, pine trees, cozy and melancholy

cards.name: Mary Blair
cards.desc: Flat, childlike shapes in daring color combinations (hot pink skies, teal hills, orange houses). Everything is simplified and a little tilted, so it feels joyful, naive and musical.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Mary Blair: mid-century gouache concept art, flat childlike shapes, hot pink sky, teal and purple hills, tilted stacked houses, lollipop trees, flower sun, joyful

cards.name: Charley Harper
cards.desc: Birds and animals reduced to circles, triangles and flat color, with no outlines and no texture. He called it minimal realism: you count the wings, not the feathers, and it feels clever and serene.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Charley Harper: minimal-realism wildlife print, bird built from circles and triangles, flat even colors, no outlines, crisp geometric branch, pattern of dots, serene and witty

cards.name: Saul Bass
cards.desc: Bold, symbolic graphics made from a few rough cut-paper shapes in two or three colors, usually black and white on a strong red or orange. One striking silhouette tells the whole story.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Saul Bass: mid-century film poster, rough hand-cut paper shapes, black silhouette of a running figure, tilted white strips, flat red-orange ground, bold symbolic minimal

cards.name: Edward Gorey
cards.desc: Tiny, meticulous pen drawings of Edwardian people in long fur coats, standing in hatched rooms beside urns and gloomy wallpaper. Deadpan and darkly funny, as if a Victorian picture book went wrong.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Edward Gorey: black pen-and-ink vignette, dense fine parallel hatching, Edwardian figure in long fur coat and top hat, stone urn, striped wallpaper, deadpan gothic humor

cards.name: Maurice Sendak
cards.desc: Soft watercolor scenes laced with fine crosshatching, often at night in a forest, where chubby children meet big shaggy creatures. Tender and a little wild, like a dream you are not quite scared of.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Maurice Sendak: picture-book pen crosshatching over soft watercolor, moonlit forest night, big shaggy creature with round yellow eyes, small child in pajamas, tender and wild

cards.name: Establishing shot
cards.desc: The shot that tells you where and when before the scene starts: the outside of the building, the city at night, the house on the hill. A screenplay writes it as a slugline.
cards.phrase: establishing shot, the exterior of a roadside diner at night, warm windows glowing, a neon sign on the roof, small figures visible inside

cards.name: Master shot
cards.desc: One wide take of the whole scene from start to finish, with everyone in frame. Editors cut back to it to remind you where people are, and it saves the scene if nothing else works.
cards.phrase: wide master shot of the whole scene, both people at the booth in frame, the room around them visible

cards.name: Single
cards.desc: One person alone in the frame, usually from the chest up, looking just off the lens at someone we can't see. Most dialogue is cut from singles.
cards.phrase: clean single, medium close-up of one person alone in the frame, looking just off camera at someone unseen

cards.name: Over-the-shoulder
cards.desc: A single with a slice of the other person in the foreground: the back of a head and a shoulder, soft and dark. It ties the two people together while favoring one.
cards.phrase: over-the-shoulder shot, the back of one person's head soft and dark in the foreground, the other person facing camera in sharp focus

cards.name: 50/50 shot
cards.desc: Two people in profile facing each other, each taking half the frame. It feels balanced and theatrical, and the gap between them becomes part of the story.
cards.phrase: 50/50 profile two-shot, two people facing each other in profile across a table, each taking half the frame

cards.name: Shot / reverse shot
cards.desc: The back-and-forth that carries most film dialogue: a shot of one person, then the matching shot from the opposite side on the other. Each angle mirrors the other in size and height.
cards.phrase: shot / reverse shot coverage, matching over-the-shoulder angles on each person, same lens and height

cards.name: Reaction shot
cards.desc: A cut to someone who is not talking, to show how the words land. Often the strongest shot in a scene, because the audience reads the listener's face.
cards.phrase: reaction shot, a silent close-up of the listener's face as the news lands, eyebrows lifting, lips parted

cards.name: Insert
cards.desc: A close shot of an object or a hand in the middle of the scene: the note, the key, the gun in the drawer. It tells the audience exactly what to notice.
cards.phrase: insert shot, a hand sliding a folded note and a brass key across a diner table, no faces

cards.name: Cutaway
cards.desc: A cut to something outside the main action (a clock, the rain, a passer-by), then back. It shows time passing or tension rising, and it lets the editor hide a cut.
cards.phrase: cutaway to the wall clock above the counter, its second hand ticking, between shots of the conversation

cards.name: POV shot
cards.desc: A character looks, then we cut to what they see, framed from their position. The audience shares their eyes and, for a moment, their feelings.
cards.phrase: point-of-view shot from her seat in the booth, looking at the diner door as a dark figure in a hat steps in

cards.name: Italian shot
cards.aka: extreme close-up on the eyes, Leone close-up
cards.desc: A wide frame filled by nothing but a pair of eyes. Sergio Leone made it famous in the stand-offs of his westerns, cutting faster and closer until only eyes are left.
cards.phrase: extreme close-up "Italian shot" of a gunslinger's squinting eyes filling a 2.39:1 frame, sweat and stubble, harsh sun

cards.name: 180-degree rule
cards.aka: the axis of action, the line
cards.desc: Draw an imaginary line through the two people talking. As long as every camera stays on one side of it, A is always on the left looking right and B on the right looking left.
cards.phrase: coverage that respects the 180-degree rule: every angle on the same side of the line between the two people, so their screen positions never flip

cards.name: Crossing the line
cards.desc: Cutting to a camera on the other side of the line flips the screen: suddenly both people seem to look the same way. Done by accident it confuses; done on purpose it unsettles.
cards.phrase: deliberately cross the 180-degree line between shots so the two people suddenly face the same direction on screen, creating unease

cards.name: 30-degree rule
cards.desc: If you cut between two shots of the same person, move the camera at least 30 degrees (or change the shot size a lot). Anything less looks like a mistake: a jump cut.
cards.phrase: cut between angles at least 30 degrees apart, or change the shot size, so cuts between shots of the same subject never look like a jump

cards.name: Screen direction
cards.aka: direction of travel, continuity of movement
cards.desc: If someone leaves one shot walking left to right, they should keep going left to right in the next, or the audience thinks they turned around. Long journeys often run one way the whole film.
cards.phrase: keep screen direction consistent: the traveler moves left to right in every shot of the journey

cards.name: Eyeline match
cards.desc: When two shots are cut together, the eyelines have to agree: if she looks down to the right, he should look up to the left. Get it wrong and they seem to be looking at different people.
cards.phrase: matched eyelines across the cut: she looks down and to the right from the balcony, he looks up and to the left from the street

cards.name: Look room
cards.desc: Leave empty space in the direction a person is looking or moving. With room ahead the frame feels comfortable; with none, the person seems boxed in or about to be surprised.
cards.phrase: framed with generous look room: the face on the left third of the frame, gazing right into open space

cards.name: Cut on action
cards.desc: Cut in the middle of a movement (a door opening, a punch, a coat coming off) and finish it in the next shot. The motion carries the eye across the cut so it disappears.
cards.phrase: cut on action: a wide shot of her pushing the diner door, cut mid-movement to a close-up of her hand on the handle

cards.name: Cheating
cards.aka: cheat the angle, cheat a look
cards.desc: Turning an actor, a prop or a look slightly toward the camera so it reads on screen, even though it would be wrong in the room. The audience never notices; the shot just works.
cards.phrase: cheat both actors' angles toward camera so their faces read clearly while they still seem to face each other

cards.name: Deep staging
cards.aka: staging in depth, deep focus staging
cards.desc: Action on several planes at once, all sharp: a face in the foreground, someone in the middle of the room, a third person far behind. The audience chooses where to look, and the layers comment on each other.
cards.phrase: deep staging with deep focus: a face in the near foreground, a figure in the middle of the room, a child visible through the far window, all sharp

cards.name: Doorway frame
cards.aka: frame within a frame, the Searchers shot
cards.desc: A dark doorway, window or arch around a brighter world outside. It isolates the person, adds depth and often says something: inside and outside, home and wilderness.
cards.phrase: framed through a dark doorway, a lone figure silhouetted against a bright desert landscape outside

cards.name: Planimetric staging
cards.desc: The camera faces the back wall straight on and the actors line up across the frame like figures in a painting or a police line-up. Everything is flat, frontal and deliberate.
cards.phrase: planimetric staging: camera square to the back wall, three people standing side by side facing the lens, flat frontal composition, centered

cards.name: One-point perspective
cards.desc: Every line in the set runs to a single vanishing point in the middle of the frame. It pulls the eye down a corridor or a road and feels both perfect and oppressive.
cards.phrase: one-point perspective down a long symmetrical hotel corridor, all lines converging to the center, a small figure at the far end

cards.name: Walk and talk
cards.desc: Two or more people deliver a scene while walking, with the camera backing up in front of them. It turns exposition into momentum and shows off the set.
cards.phrase: walk-and-talk: two colleagues stride toward the camera down a busy office corridor mid-conversation, the camera backing up ahead of them on a Steadicam

cards.name: Split diopter
cards.desc: A half-lens over one side of the camera so a face very close and a person far away are both sharp, with a soft seam between them. It looks slightly wrong, which is why thrillers love it.
cards.phrase: split diopter shot: a face in extreme foreground on the left and a figure far in the background on the right, both in sharp focus, a faint soft seam between them

cards.name: Mirror shot
cards.desc: A character seen in a mirror, often with their real self in the frame too. It suggests a split, a lie, or someone sizing themselves up.
cards.phrase: mirror shot: a man stares into a bathroom mirror, his reflection sharp and lit, the real back of his head dark and soft in the foreground

cards.name: Shadow play
cards.desc: The threat shows up as a shadow on the wall before the person does: huge, distorted and moving. Lit by one hard light from low down, it is one of the oldest tricks in horror.
cards.phrase: expressionist shadow play: the elongated shadow of a clawed figure climbing a staircase wall, one hard low light, no person visible

cards.name: Top shot
cards.desc: The camera looks straight down from the ceiling. People become shapes on a pattern, which makes a scene feel planned, fated or clinical.
cards.phrase: top shot looking straight down at four people around a round card table, tops of heads, scattered chips and cards, hard overhead lamp

cards.name: Triangle staging
cards.desc: Three people placed at the corners of a triangle so every one of them can see, and threaten, the other two. Any one shot holds the whole tension.
cards.phrase: triangle staging, a three-way standoff in a dusty circular plaza, two figures in the near corners, one far in the middle, all facing inward

cards.name: Trunk shot
cards.desc: A low angle from inside a car trunk as people open it and look down at whatever (or whoever) is inside. The sky behind them, the trunk lid framing the top.
cards.phrase: trunk shot: extreme low angle from inside a car trunk, two men in suits looking down into the lens, bright sky behind them, the dark trunk lid framing the top

cards.name: The Spielberg face
cards.desc: A slow push-in on a face lit by something just off screen, eyes wide, mouth slightly open, before you see what they're looking at. It tells you to feel wonder first.
cards.phrase: the Spielberg face: slow push-in on a child's upturned face, eyes wide, mouth slightly open in awe, lit by a warm glow from something off screen

cards.name: The Kubrick stare
cards.desc: Chin lowered, eyes rolled up toward the lens from under the brow, often with a faint smile. It signals that something in the character has broken.
cards.phrase: the Kubrick stare: a man tilts his head down and glares up into the lens from under his brow, a faint unsettling smile, symmetrical framing

cards.name: Double dolly
cards.desc: The actor stands on the same dolly as the camera, so they glide through the world without walking. The street slides past and they seem to float toward their fate.
cards.phrase: Spike Lee double-dolly shot: a man glides forward without walking, standing still on the moving dolly, the night street sliding past behind him

cards.name: Low-angle hero 360
cards.desc: The camera circles low around one or more heroes as they rise to their feet or turn to face the enemy, the sun flaring behind them. Pure swagger.
cards.phrase: low-angle hero 360: the camera circles low around a team of heroes rising to their feet, sun flaring behind them, slow motion

cards.name: Pillow shot
cards.desc: A still, empty shot between scenes: laundry on a line, a hallway, smokestacks, a vase. It rests the eye and lets time pass, like a pause in a poem.
cards.phrase: Ozu-style pillow shot: an empty tatami room at low height, a teapot on a low table, paper screens glowing with afternoon light, no people

cards.name: SnorriCam
cards.desc: A camera strapped to the actor's body, pointing back at their face. The face stays locked in the middle while the world lurches around it, like being drunk, high or panicking.
cards.phrase: SnorriCam shot: the camera rigged to his chest facing his sweating, panicked face, which stays locked in frame while the street lurches and tilts behind him

cards.name: Overhead insert
cards.desc: A neat top-down shot of hands and objects arranged on a colored surface: a suitcase being packed, a letter, a record player. It reads like a diorama.
cards.phrase: overhead insert shot, straight down on a mustard-yellow suitcase being packed with neatly arranged books, binoculars and a portable record player, two small hands, symmetrical

cards.name: Monumental scale
cards.desc: A minuscule human against an enormous structure or landscape, often in haze. It makes the world feel ancient, alien or indifferent.
cards.phrase: monumental scale: a tiny lone figure at the foot of a colossal brutalist monolith rising into thick orange haze, minimal composition

cards.name: Hand through the grass
cards.desc: A hand drifting over a field of tall grass or wheat at magic hour, the sun flaring low behind it. Paired with whispered voice-over, it stands for memory and grace.
cards.phrase: a hand brushing the tops of tall wheat at magic hour, the low sun flaring directly behind it, golden backlight, floating handheld camera

cards.name: Cross-cutting
cards.desc: Cutting back and forth between two things happening at the same time in different places, usually racing toward each other. Each cut makes the shots shorter and the stakes higher.
cards.phrase: cross-cut between the hero sprinting through the rain and the train bearing down, alternating shots that get shorter and closer

cards.name: Parallel editing
cards.desc: Alternating between two storylines that are not happening at the same moment (a father and a son decades apart, or two strangers in different cities) so each comments on the other.
cards.phrase: parallel editing between a young father in 1917 in sepia and his grown son in the present day in color, the scenes echoing each other

cards.name: Kuleshov effect
cards.desc: The same blank face reads as hunger, grief or tenderness depending on the shot cut next to it. The audience supplies the emotion; the cut does the acting.
cards.phrase: Kuleshov-style edit: hold on a neutral, unreadable face, then cut to the thing he sees, letting the cut supply the emotion

cards.name: Axial cut
cards.desc: Jumping straight closer (or farther) along the line of the lens, in one or more abrupt steps. It hits like a gasp; Kurosawa used two or three in a row.
cards.phrase: axial cut: two abrupt cut-ins straight down the lens axis, from a wide shot of a man in a field to a medium shot to a close-up

cards.name: Elliptical edit
cards.desc: Leaving out the boring middle of an action: she leaves the house, and the next shot she is already at the sea. The audience fills the gap without noticing.
cards.phrase: elliptical edit: she shuts her front door, then cut straight to her arriving at the empty beach, skipping the journey

cards.name: Long take
cards.desc: A whole scene, or a whole film, in one unbroken shot with no cuts. The camera moves through rooms and crowds, and the tension builds because nothing lets you look away.
cards.phrase: one continuous long take with no cuts: the camera follows them in through the kitchen, along the corridor and out into the crowded club

cards.name: Split screen
cards.desc: Two or more shots side by side in one frame, so the audience watches both at once. Good for phone calls, simultaneous action and stylized, comic-book energy.
cards.phrase: split screen: the left half shows her on the phone in a pink bedroom, the right half shows him on the phone in a blue office, the two halves divided by a clean line

cards.name: Freeze frame
cards.desc: The action stops dead on one frame, often at the end of a film or the moment a character is introduced. It turns a moment into a memory, a verdict or a joke.
cards.phrase: freeze frame on the boy's face as he turns to look straight into the camera on the beach, the image stops, grainy black and white

cards.name: Montage sequence
cards.desc: A run of short shots, usually over a song, that squeezes a long process (training, falling in love, building a house) into a minute or two.
