cards.phrase: a rack focus from the foreground grass to the distant mountains, shallow depth of field

cards.name: Aerial flyover
cards.desc: A high camera gliding forward over the landscape, smooth and godlike. The signature of travel films, opening titles and epic establishing shots.
cards.phrase: a smooth aerial drone flyover gliding forward and slightly down over the landscape at golden hour

cards.name: FPV drone
cards.aka: first-person drone, FPV dive, racing drone
cards.desc: A fast, agile drone that dives, banks and threads through gaps. Rollercoaster energy; feels like flying.
cards.phrase: a fast FPV drone shot diving toward the figure and banking hard around them

cards.name: Handheld
cards.desc: The camera is held by hand and drifts and jitters slightly. Feels immediate, documentary and real; heavy shake reads as chaos or panic.
cards.phrase: a handheld camera with gentle, natural micro-shake, documentary style

cards.name: Steadicam float
cards.desc: A stabilized camera that glides as if floating, smooth but alive, with a gentle drift no dolly track can make. Dreamy and immersive.
cards.phrase: a smooth floating Steadicam glide with gentle drift, no shake

cards.name: POV shot
cards.desc: The camera becomes the character's eyes, bobbing gently with each step. Puts the viewer inside the scene, for horror, games or intimacy.
cards.phrase: a first-person POV shot walking forward, with a gentle head bob on each step

cards.name: Bullet time
cards.desc: Time freezes or crawls while the camera keeps orbiting around the subject. Made famous by The Matrix; now an easy effect with image-to-video.
cards.phrase: bullet time: the moment freezes mid-action while the camera orbits around the figure

cards.name: Slow motion
cards.desc: Filmed at a high frame rate and played back at normal speed, so time stretches. Makes moments feel weighty, beautiful or dreamlike, and shows details the eye misses.
cards.phrase: in slow motion, like 120 frames per second played back at 24, every droplet and strand of hair visible

cards.name: Timelapse
cards.desc: Frames taken minutes apart and played quickly, so hours pass in seconds: clouds race, shadows swing and the sun crosses the sky. Shows the passing of time.
cards.phrase: a timelapse: clouds race across the sky and the light shifts from afternoon to dusk in seconds

cards.name: Hyperlapse
cards.desc: A timelapse where the camera also travels a long distance, so you rocket through a city or landscape. Energetic and slightly surreal.
cards.phrase: a hyperlapse rushing forward through the landscape, the light shifting fast

cards.name: Speed ramp
cards.desc: The playback speed changes within one shot: fast, then dramatically slow at the key moment, then fast again. A staple of action scenes, sports edits and trailers.
cards.phrase: a speed ramp: real speed, then ramping down to slow motion at the peak of the jump, then snapping back to speed

cards.name: Freeze frame
cards.desc: The action stops dead on one frame, often with a title or narration over it. Punctuates a moment: an introduction, a joke or a final image.
cards.phrase: the action freezes on a single frame mid-jump, slightly desaturated, while the music cuts out

cards.name: Reverse motion
cards.desc: Footage played backward, so water leaps up into a glass and shards fly together. Uncanny and magical; also a trick for impossible-looking stunts.
cards.phrase: reverse motion: scattered fragments fly back together into the whole object

cards.name: Stop motion
cards.desc: Physical objects moved a little and photographed one frame at a time. The slight choppiness and the hand-made jitter between frames are the charm.
cards.phrase: stop-motion animation at 12 frames per second with slight frame-to-frame jitter, tactile handmade materials

cards.name: Cinemagraph
cards.desc: A still photograph where one small part moves in a seamless loop, like steam from a cup or water in a river, while everything else stays frozen. Hypnotic and elegant.
cards.phrase: a cinemagraph: the scene is a frozen photo except the river, which flows in a seamless loop

cards.name: Seamless loop
cards.aka: perfect loop, infinite loop, GIF loop
cards.desc: A clip whose last frame flows invisibly into its first, so it can repeat forever with no jump. Essential for backgrounds, social posts and living album covers.
cards.phrase: a seamless loop where the final frame matches the first exactly, so it repeats with no visible cut

cards.name: Boomerang
cards.desc: A short burst of action played forward then backward, over and over. Instantly recognizable from social media; a cheap way to loop anything.
cards.phrase: a boomerang loop: a one-second action plays forward and then backward, repeating

cards.name: Shutter feel
cards.desc: A normal film shutter gives soft motion blur that reads as cinematic. A very fast shutter freezes each frame crisply, giving a jittery, staccato feel used for battle scenes and adrenaline.
cards.phrase: a narrow shutter for crisp, staccato motion with no motion blur, like the beach landing in Saving Private Ryan

cards.name: One motion per shot
cards.desc: Ask for one clear subject action and at most one camera move per clip. Models handle "she turns her head toward the sun" well and "she turns, walks, waves and the camera orbits" badly.
cards.phrase: one clear action per shot: the figure slowly turns toward the sun; nothing else changes

cards.name: Camera and subject, separately
cards.desc: Describe what the camera does and what the subject does in separate phrases. Otherwise the model guesses whether "moving toward" means the person walks or the camera pushes.
cards.phrase: Camera: slow push-in. Subject: the figure stands still, coat moving in the wind.

cards.name: Ambient motion
cards.aka: subtle motion, environmental motion, living still
cards.desc: Small natural movement in the environment (drifting dust, swaying grass, moving clouds, flickering light) brings a still to life without risking the subject. The most reliable request there is.
cards.phrase: subtle ambient motion only: drifting dust in the light, grass swaying gently, slow-moving clouds

cards.name: Say what stays still
cards.desc: Name the things that must not move or change, like the face, the text or the horizon. Models tend to animate everything; anchors keep the composition intact.
cards.phrase: the figure, the horizon and the mountains stay completely still; only the sky and light change

cards.name: Speed and duration words
cards.desc: Words like "slowly", "gradually", "gently" and a duration ("over 5 seconds") strongly change the result. Without them, models default to brisk, often too-fast motion.
cards.phrase: the camera moves very slowly and steadily over the full 8 seconds

cards.name: Start and end frames
cards.aka: first and last frame, keyframe video, interpolation
cards.desc: Give the model a first image and a last image and let it invent the motion between. The most control you can get over where a shot ends up.
cards.phrase: use this image as the first frame and that one as the last; move smoothly between them with no extra action

cards.name: Physical forces
cards.desc: Describe the forces acting on things instead of the motion itself: "a strong wind from the left", "heavy rain", "the coat is heavy wool". The model works out the movement and it looks more physical.
cards.phrase: a steady warm wind blows from the left, pushing the grass and the figure's coat to the right

cards.name: Keep identity
cards.desc: Ask explicitly that faces, hands, logos and text stay the same throughout. Video models drift and morph details over time, especially in longer or faster shots.
cards.phrase: keep the figure's face, clothing and proportions exactly consistent throughout; no morphing

cards.name: Beat-by-beat timing
cards.desc: For longer clips, break the prompt into timed beats: "0 to 3 seconds: ..., 3 to 6 seconds: ...". Some models follow timestamps; others still benefit from the clear order.
cards.phrase: 0–3s: static wide shot, dust drifting. 3–6s: slow push-in toward the figure. 6–8s: the figure turns toward the sun.

cards.name: Motion strength
cards.desc: Many tools have a motion-strength setting, and words like "subtle", "moderate" and "dynamic" act the same way. Low strength protects the image; high strength invites warping.
cards.phrase: low motion strength: subtle, gentle movement that preserves the original image

cards.name: Kinetic typography
cards.aka: animated type, lyric video, type in motion
cards.desc: Words that move, scale, slam and rearrange in time with speech or music, so the type itself performs. Great for lyric videos, title sequences and bold social posts.
cards.phrase: kinetic typography: each word slams in on the beat, scaling and stacking in bold condensed type

cards.name: Flat motion design
cards.desc: Simple flat shapes and icons that pop, bounce and morph with tight easing and bright colors. The look of startup explainer videos and app onboarding.
cards.phrase: flat 2D motion design: simple geometric shapes pop in with overshoot, morph and slide with snappy easing on a solid background

cards.name: Line draw-on
cards.aka: stroke reveal, self-drawing line art, write-on
cards.desc: An illustration or signature draws itself stroke by stroke, as if by an invisible pen. Elegant and calm; great for maps, logos and diagrams.
cards.phrase: line art that draws itself on, stroke by stroke, as if by an invisible pen

cards.name: Liquid and blobs
cards.desc: Soft blobs that merge, stretch and split like liquid. Organic and playful; a gooey filter makes separate shapes melt into one another.
cards.phrase: gooey liquid blobs that merge and split organically, soft and colorful

cards.name: 2.5D parallax photo
cards.aka: Ken Burns 3D, camera-mapped still, depth photo
cards.desc: A still photo cut into layers (foreground, subject, background) with a gentle virtual camera move, so it gains depth. The documentary and image-to-video staple for bringing old photos to life.
cards.phrase: a 2.5D parallax effect: the still photo split into foreground, subject and background layers with a slow drifting camera

cards.name: Isometric
cards.desc: Objects drawn at a fixed 30-degree angle with no perspective, building up like toy blocks. Clean, technical and charming; popular in tech and infrastructure explainers.
cards.phrase: isometric motion graphics: blocks rise and assemble on a 30-degree grid with no perspective

cards.name: Particles
cards.desc: Many tiny points (dust, sparks, embers, snow, fireflies) drifting under simple forces. Adds atmosphere and magic to almost any shot.
cards.phrase: warm floating dust particles drifting slowly upward through the golden light

cards.name: Data animation
cards.desc: Charts that build in front of you: bars grow, lines draw left to right, numbers count up. Animation reveals the story in the data one step at a time.
cards.phrase: animated data: bars grow from the baseline with a stagger while the trend line draws left to right

cards.name: Logo sting
cards.desc: A two-to-five-second animation where pieces assemble into a logo, often with a sound hit. Opens or closes videos and gives a brand a signature move.
cards.phrase: a three-second logo sting: shapes fly in and lock together into the mark on a sound hit, then the wordmark fades up

cards.name: VHS and analog
cards.desc: Scan lines, color bleed, tracking wobble and a timestamp, as if recorded on 1980s tape. Instant nostalgia for home-video memories and retro music videos.
cards.phrase: a VHS look: scan lines, chroma bleed, occasional tracking wobble and a camcorder date stamp

cards.name: Hand-drawn 2D
cards.aka: cel animation, traditional animation, line boil
cards.desc: Drawn frame by frame, with lines that wobble slightly from drawing to drawing (line boil) and flat colors. Warm and human.
cards.phrase: hand-drawn 2D cel animation on twos, flat colors with a gentle line boil

cards.name: Rubber hose
cards.desc: Bendy noodle limbs with no elbows, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, and everything bouncing to the beat. Black-and-white jazz-age charm.
cards.phrase: 1930s rubber-hose cartoon style: noodle limbs, pie-cut eyes, everything bouncing in rhythm, black and white film grain

cards.name: Anime
cards.desc: Limited animation with sharp, held poses punctuated by explosive bursts of fluid motion (sakuga), speed lines, dramatic lighting and painted backgrounds.
cards.phrase: anime style: held dramatic poses, radial speed lines on the burst of action, painterly sky background

cards.name: Rotoscope
cards.desc: Animation traced over filmed footage, so movement is eerily realistic while the image is drawn. Dreamlike and uncanny.
cards.phrase: rotoscoped animation: realistic human motion traced over film, with flat color and drawn outlines

cards.name: Claymation
cards.desc: Clay figures moved by hand between frames, with visible fingerprints and slight wobble. Cozy, funny and tactile.
cards.phrase: claymation: plasticine characters with visible fingerprints and slight frame-to-frame wobble, at 12 frames per second

cards.name: Paper cut-out
cards.desc: Flat paper shapes with torn or cut edges and hard shadows, moved in jerky steps. Handmade and storybook-like; Monty Python's collage version is wilder.
cards.phrase: paper cut-out animation: flat textured paper shapes with soft drop shadows, moving in small jerky steps

cards.name: Pixel art animation
cards.desc: Low-resolution characters on a visible pixel grid, animated in a handful of frames. Reads as retro games, though modern pixel art can be rich and subtle.
cards.phrase: 16-bit pixel art animation: a small sprite with a 4-frame walk cycle on a crisp pixel grid, no smoothing

cards.name: 3D animated feature
cards.desc: Soft, rounded 3D characters with subsurface glow, big expressive eyes and squash-and-stretch performance. Polished and family-friendly.
cards.phrase: Pixar-style 3D animation: soft rounded forms, warm subsurface lighting and expressive squash-and-stretch

cards.name: Comic-book painterly
cards.desc: CG animation that looks printed: halftone dots, offset color registration, hand-drawn ink lines and characters on twos against smooth cameras. Graphic, kinetic and loud.
cards.phrase: comic-book painterly animation like Spider-Verse: halftone shading, offset print colors, ink lines and characters animated on twos

cards.name: White oak
cards.aka: rift-sawn oak, quarter-sawn oak, European oak
cards.desc: A pale, honey-to-straw wood with long, straight grain. Rift-sawn boards show tight parallel lines; quarter-sawn ones add silvery ray flecks. The default of modern Scandinavian and Japandi interiors.
cards.phrase: rift-sawn white oak with tight straight grain, pale natural finish

cards.name: Walnut
cards.desc: A rich chocolate wood with purple-grey undertones and gently wavy grain. It reads as warm, expensive and mid-century.
cards.phrase: American black walnut with flowing grain and a warm oiled finish

cards.name: Burl wood
cards.desc: Wood cut from a knotty growth on the trunk, so the grain swirls in every direction and is dotted with small dark eyes. Almost always used as a thin veneer, polished to a high gloss.
cards.phrase: highly figured burl wood veneer with swirling grain and dark knot eyes, high-gloss finish

cards.name: End grain
cards.aka: butcher block, end-grain block, parquet de bout
cards.desc: Wood cut across the trunk so you see growth rings instead of long grain, usually glued up as a checkerboard of small blocks. It reads as craft, kitchens and workshops.
cards.phrase: end-grain butcher block of alternating maple and walnut squares, growth rings visible on each block

cards.name: Plywood edge
cards.aka: birch ply, Baltic birch, exposed ply
cards.desc: Thin sheets of wood glued in layers, with the striped edge left on show. It says honest, affordable, maker-built: studios, shop fittings and flat-pack furniture.
cards.phrase: Baltic birch plywood with the layered striped edge exposed, clear matte finish

cards.name: Reclaimed barn wood
cards.aka: weathered wood, driftwood grey, salvaged timber
cards.desc: Old boards silvered by sun and rain, with open cracks, nail holes and saw marks. It reads as rustic, coastal or farmhouse, and it signals a story.
cards.phrase: reclaimed weathered barn wood planks, silver-grey and brown, raised grain, nail holes and cracks

cards.name: Bamboo
cards.desc: Hollow grass stalks with swollen rings, called nodes, every so often. As poles it reads as tropical or Japanese; pressed into boards it reads as eco-friendly.
cards.phrase: natural bamboo poles in honey and green tones, with pronounced nodes

cards.name: Cork
cards.desc: The bark of the cork oak, ground into granules and pressed. Warm, soft, speckled and a little retro. It reads as sustainable, quiet and tactile.
cards.phrase: agglomerated cork with coarse speckled granules in warm tan and brown

cards.name: Rattan cane webbing
cards.desc: Thin strips of rattan woven into an open eight-sided mesh, stretched over a frame. It reads as 1970s, Riviera and breezy.
cards.phrase: woven rattan cane webbing in honey tones, open octagonal mesh

cards.name: Carrara marble
cards.desc: White to pale grey Italian marble with soft, feathery grey veining spread evenly across the slab. Classic, clean and widely used, so it reads as nice rather than flashy.
cards.phrase: Carrara marble with soft feathery grey veining on a cool white ground

cards.name: Calacatta marble
cards.desc: A brighter white marble with thick, dramatic veins in grey and gold. Rarer than Carrara and much more expensive, so it signals luxury.
cards.phrase: Calacatta gold marble, bright white with bold dramatic grey and gold veining, polished

cards.name: Nero Marquina
cards.desc: A deep black Spanish marble with sharp white veins. It reads as moody, dramatic and Art Deco.
cards.phrase: Nero Marquina black marble with crisp white veining, polished to a mirror sheen

cards.name: Travertine
cards.desc: A warm beige limestone layered in soft bands and full of small holes from trapped gas. Filled and honed it looks soft and creamy; unfilled it looks ancient.
cards.phrase: honed travertine in warm cream and beige, horizontal banding with small natural pits

cards.name: Terrazzo
cards.desc: Chips of marble, glass or stone set in cement or resin and ground smooth. Small grey chips feel civic and 1960s; big bright chips feel playful and current.
cards.phrase: terrazzo with large angular chips of terracotta, sage, black and white on a cream ground, polished

cards.name: Granite
cards.desc: A hard, crystalline stone with an even speckle of black, white, grey and sometimes pink grains. It reads as durable, civic and a little 1990s kitchen.
cards.phrase: polished salt-and-pepper granite with dense black, white and grey crystals

cards.name: Slate
cards.desc: A dark blue-grey stone that splits into thin sheets with a rippled, layered face. It reads as slate roofs, Welsh quarries and serious restaurants.
cards.phrase: riven blue-grey slate with a natural cleft surface and matte finish

cards.name: Backlit onyx
cards.desc: A banded, semi-translucent stone that glows when lit from behind. It is the move for showpiece bars and walls where the stone itself is the lamp.
cards.phrase: backlit honey onyx glowing amber, translucent wavy bands

cards.name: Sandstone & rammed earth
cards.desc: Stone or packed earth laid down in visible horizontal layers of ochre, rust and sand. It reads as desert, geological time and slow architecture.
cards.phrase: rammed earth wall with horizontal strata in ochre, rust and sand tones

cards.name: Linen
cards.desc: A crisp, slightly irregular plain weave from flax, with visible slubs and soft rumples. It reads as natural, summery and relaxed.
cards.phrase: stonewashed natural linen in oatmeal, visible slubby weave and soft creases

cards.name: Raw denim
cards.desc: A sturdy cotton twill dyed indigo, with diagonal ribs and a slightly mottled color that fades with wear. It reads as workwear, Americana and Japanese heritage brands.
cards.phrase: raw indigo selvedge denim with a visible diagonal twill and slight fading

cards.name: Wool felt
cards.desc: Wool fibers matted together without weaving, so the surface is soft, fuzzy and even, with no grain at all. It reads as cozy, crafty and acoustic.
cards.phrase: thick mustard merino wool felt with a soft fuzzy matte surface

cards.name: Bouclé
cards.desc: Fabric woven from looped yarn, so the surface is a mass of tiny nubbly curls. Cream bouclé is the signature of current soft-modern furniture.
cards.phrase: cream wool bouclé upholstery with a dense nubbly looped texture

cards.name: Velvet
cards.desc: A dense, short pile that soaks up light and then catches it at the edges and folds. Deep jewel colors make it read as plush, theatrical and a little decadent.
cards.phrase: deep emerald cotton velvet with a soft pile sheen catching light at the folds

cards.name: Full-grain leather
cards.desc: Hide with its natural surface left on: fine pores, small creases and color that deepens with use. Contrast stitching makes it read as handmade goods.
cards.phrase: vegetable-tanned cognac full-grain leather with visible pores, faint creases and cream saddle stitching

cards.name: Suede
cards.desc: Leather sanded to a soft nap, so it looks velvety and matte and shows finger marks where the nap is brushed the other way.
cards.phrase: sand-colored suede with a soft brushed nap and gentle tonal shifts

cards.name: Cotton canvas
cards.aka: duck canvas, waxed canvas, natural canvas
cards.desc: A heavy plain weave with a coarse, even grid of threads. Natural canvas reads as tote bags and artist stretchers; waxed canvas reads as outdoor heritage.
cards.phrase: heavyweight natural cotton duck canvas with a coarse even weave

cards.name: Chunky knit
cards.aka: cable knit, Aran knit, hand knit
cards.desc: Thick yarn looped into rows of V-shaped stitches, sometimes twisted into rope-like cables. It reads as winter, comfort and handmade.
cards.phrase: chunky cream wool cable knit with plump V stitches and soft fuzz

cards.name: Herringbone tweed
cards.desc: A wool twill woven in zigzag columns, often flecked with other colors. It reads as British country, academia and tailoring.
cards.phrase: grey-brown herringbone wool tweed with colorful flecks

cards.name: Board-formed concrete
cards.aka: board-marked concrete, béton brut, raw concrete
cards.desc: Concrete poured against timber planks, so the wood grain and board seams are printed into the wall. It is the signature of Brutalism and of architects who want concrete to look made by hand.
cards.phrase: board-formed raw concrete wall with visible timber grain imprints, plank seams and small air pockets

cards.name: Polished concrete
cards.desc: A concrete slab ground and sealed until it is smooth and softly reflective, often with small stones of aggregate showing through. It reads as galleries, lofts and calm retail.
cards.phrase: polished concrete floor, mottled grey with exposed fine aggregate and soft blurred reflections

cards.name: Tadelakt
cards.aka: Moroccan lime plaster, polished plaster, Venetian plaster
cards.desc: Lime plaster troweled, burnished with a stone and sealed with soap until it is smooth and water-resistant, with soft cloudy tones and a waxy glow. It reads as hammams, spas and quiet luxury.
cards.phrase: burnished tadelakt lime plaster in warm clay pink, seamless, soft cloudy tones and a waxy sheen

cards.name: Limewash
cards.aka: lime paint, mineral paint, chalky wash
cards.desc: A thin mineral paint brushed on in overlapping strokes, so it dries into a soft, chalky cloud of lighter and darker patches. It makes plain walls look old, soft and sun-warmed.
cards.phrase: limewashed wall in warm stone white, chalky matte, soft mottled crisscross brush strokes

cards.name: Stucco
cards.desc: A thick cement or lime render applied with a rough, blotchy texture. White stucco reads as Mediterranean and Spanish Colonial; sand-colored stucco reads as the American Southwest.
cards.phrase: rough white knockdown stucco wall, raking sunlight picking out the texture

cards.name: Terracotta tile
cards.desc: Unglazed fired clay in warm orange and rust, each tile a slightly different shade. It reads as Tuscan farmhouses, Mexican haciendas and sunny kitchens.
cards.phrase: unglazed terracotta floor tiles in mixed rust and orange tones, matte, with pale grout

cards.name: Zellige
cards.desc: Small handmade Moroccan tiles with a thick, glassy glaze that pools unevenly, so every tile is a slightly different shade and catches the light differently. It reads as warm, crafted and current.
cards.phrase: handmade green zellige tiles with uneven glossy glaze, tile-to-tile color variation and wavy edges

cards.name: Crackle glaze
cards.desc: A ceramic glaze that has cracked into a fine web of lines as it cooled, often darkened with ink or smoke so the web shows. It reads as Song dynasty celadon, raku pottery and handmade tableware.
cards.phrase: pale celadon crackle glaze with a fine web of dark crazing lines, glossy

cards.name: Brick
cards.aka: red brick, exposed brick, running bond
cards.desc: Fired clay blocks laid in staggered rows with mortar between. Old red brick reads as warehouses, London and Brooklyn; painted or pale brick reads as Scandinavian or Dutch.
cards.phrase: exposed reclaimed red brick wall in running bond, mixed tones, recessed lime mortar

cards.name: Brushed steel
cards.aka: brushed stainless, brushed aluminum, satin metal
cards.desc: Metal sanded in one direction so it has fine parallel lines and a soft, streaky shine instead of a mirror. It reads as appliances, tools and precise engineering.
cards.phrase: brushed stainless steel with fine linear grain and soft streaked highlights

cards.name: Polished chrome
cards.aka: mirror chrome, chrome plating, mirror-polished steel
cards.desc: A mirror-bright plated finish that reflects everything around it, with hard edges between light and dark. It reads as 1950s cars, faucets, motorcycles and Y2K.
cards.phrase: mirror-polished chrome with crisp, high-contrast reflections of sky and horizon

cards.name: Brass
cards.aka: polished brass, unlacquered brass, satin brass
cards.desc: A warm yellow metal. Polished it reads as hotel lobbies and old ships; unlacquered it darkens and softens with handling, which is why designers love it.
cards.phrase: polished brass with warm golden reflections

cards.name: Copper
cards.aka: polished copper, raw copper, rose metal
cards.desc: A pinkish orange metal that glows warm when polished and darkens to brown, then green, with age. It reads as kitchens, distilleries and warm industrial.
cards.phrase: polished copper with rosy orange reflections and slight warm tarnish

cards.name: Blackened steel
cards.aka: hot-rolled steel, mill scale, waxed steel
cards.desc: Steel left dark and mottled from the mill or darkened with chemicals, then waxed. It has blue-grey and brown clouds in it and reads as workshops, restaurants and moody modern design.
cards.phrase: waxed blackened hot-rolled steel, dark charcoal with blue-grey mill scale mottling and a low sheen

cards.name: Corten steel
cards.aka: weathering steel, COR-TEN, rusted steel panel
cards.desc: A steel made to rust on purpose: the rust layer protects the metal underneath and turns a rich, even orange-brown. It reads as landscape architecture, wineries and serious sculpture.
cards.phrase: Corten weathering steel panels with a deep, even orange-brown rust patina

cards.name: Hammered metal
cards.desc: Metal shaped by hand with a hammer, leaving a surface of small overlapping dents that each catch their own highlight. It reads as handmade, artisanal and a little rustic.
cards.phrase: hand-hammered copper with overlapping dimpled facets catching small highlights

cards.name: Anodized aluminum
cards.desc: Aluminum given a hard, dyed surface layer, so it keeps a metallic shimmer in saturated color. It reads as carabiners, bike parts, iPods and tech accessories.
cards.phrase: satin anodized aluminum in cobalt blue with a fine metallic sheen

cards.name: Galvanized steel
cards.desc: Steel dipped in molten zinc, which cools into a pattern of crystal patches called spangle. It reads as farm buckets, ducting, garden planters and utility.
cards.phrase: hot-dip galvanized steel with a crystalline zinc spangle pattern

cards.name: Clear glass
cards.desc: Transparent and smooth, so you see it mostly through what it does to the world behind it: bent, flipped and edged with dark rims and bright glints.
cards.phrase: clear optical glass with sharp refraction, dark edges and crisp specular highlights

cards.name: Frosted glass
cards.aka: acid-etched glass, sandblasted glass, satin glass
cards.desc: Glass etched or sandblasted to a fine matte surface, so light comes through but shapes behind it melt into soft blurs. It reads as privacy, calm and clean modern design.
cards.phrase: frosted acid-etched glass panel, objects behind it softened into blurred glowing shapes

cards.name: Reeded glass
cards.aka: fluted glass, ribbed glass, cathedral reeded
cards.desc: Glass with a row of vertical ribs, so whatever is behind it splits into narrow repeating slices. It is everywhere in current interiors, from cabinet doors to shower screens.
cards.phrase: reeded fluted glass with vertical ribs fragmenting the colors behind it into slivers

cards.name: Dichroic glass
cards.aka: color-shift glass, rainbow film, iridescent acrylic
cards.desc: Glass or acrylic coated with thin metal layers, so it reflects one color and lets another through, shifting as you move. It reads as futuristic, festival and luxury retail.
cards.phrase: dichroic glass panels shifting from cyan to magenta to gold, casting colored light

cards.name: Colored acrylic
cards.desc: Clear plastic sheet in transparent candy colors. Where pieces overlap the colors mix, and the cut edges glow brighter than the faces. It reads as playful, 1970s and design-fair.
cards.phrase: transparent colored acrylic sheets overlapping, glowing cut edges and colored shadows

cards.name: Glossy plastic
cards.desc: Hard, smooth, evenly colored plastic with a bright, wet-looking highlight. It reads as toys, consumer electronics and Pop design.
cards.phrase: glossy injection-molded ABS plastic in tomato red, smooth with a crisp highlight

cards.name: Recycled plastic
cards.aka: speckled recycled plastic, Smile Plastics, marbled HDPE
cards.desc: Sheets pressed from shredded plastic waste, so the surface is a confetti of colored flecks and smears. It reads as sustainable, playful and current.
cards.phrase: recycled plastic sheet with colorful speckled and swirled flecks, satin finish

cards.name: Rubber
cards.aka: studded rubber flooring, silicone, matte rubber
cards.desc: A soft, matte, slightly dusty surface that soaks up light. Studded rubber flooring reads as gyms, transit and industrial; smooth silicone reads as kitchen tools and tech.
cards.phrase: matte black studded rubber flooring with raised round dots

cards.name: Carbon fiber
cards.desc: Woven carbon cloth set in glossy resin, so you see a checkerboard of tiny weave blocks that flicker light and dark as you tilt it. It reads as supercars, racing bikes and high-end tech.
cards.phrase: glossy 2x2 twill carbon fiber weave under a deep clear coat

cards.name: Matte
cards.desc: A surface that scatters light evenly and shows no shine at all. It reads as calm, soft and modern, and it hides small dents and fingerprints.
cards.phrase: dead-flat matte finish with no reflections, soft even shading

cards.name: Eggshell
cards.desc: Just a hint of sheen, like the shell of an egg. It is the default finish for walls because it wipes clean without looking shiny.
cards.phrase: eggshell finish with a faint soft sheen

cards.name: Satin
cards.desc: A soft, pearly sheen halfway between matte and gloss. It reads as quality without flash, and it is common on woodwork, appliances and furniture.
cards.phrase: satin finish with a soft, blurred highlight

cards.name: High gloss
cards.desc: A hard, shiny surface that shows crisp highlights and blurry reflections of the room. It reads as bold, wipe-clean and a little pop.
cards.phrase: high-gloss finish with crisp highlights and clear reflections

cards.name: Piano lacquer
cards.desc: Many coats of lacquer sanded and polished until the surface is a perfect mirror. In black it reads as grand pianos, luxury cars and Japanese urushi ware.
cards.phrase: piano-black mirror lacquer with deep, razor-sharp reflections

cards.name: Soft-touch
cards.aka: rubberized coating, velvet touch, peach skin
cards.desc: A rubbery coating that looks matte and a little velvety and feels warm in the hand. It reads as tech accessories and premium packaging.
cards.phrase: soft-touch rubberized matte coating with a velvety, powdery sheen

cards.name: Pearlescent
cards.desc: A white or pale surface that shifts toward pink, green and violet as it turns. It reads as cosmetics, wedding stationery and special-edition cars.
cards.phrase: pearlescent white finish with soft pink and green iridescent shifts

cards.name: Metallic flake
cards.desc: Paint with tiny aluminium flakes suspended under a clear coat, so it sparkles in the light and glows deeper in shadow. It reads as cars, guitars and custom bikes.
cards.phrase: candy-apple red metallic flake paint under a glossy clear coat, fine sparkles

cards.name: Sandblasted
cards.desc: A surface hit with fine grit until it turns an even, satin-grey frost. On metal it reads as precision hardware; on glass it makes a frosted logo.
cards.phrase: bead-blasted aluminium with a fine, even satin-grey frost

cards.name: Powder coat
cards.desc: Colored powder baked onto metal into a tough, slightly textured skin. It reads as outdoor furniture, bikes and industrial design, often in bold RAL colors.
cards.phrase: satin powder-coated steel in signal orange with a faint orange-peel texture

cards.name: Vitreous enamel
cards.desc: Powdered glass fused onto steel at high heat, giving a hard, glossy coat that chips rather than scratches. It reads as railway signs, camping mugs and old bathtubs.
cards.phrase: vitreous enamel sign in cobalt blue and white, glossy with small black chips at the edges

cards.name: Shou sugi ban
cards.aka: yakisugi, charred timber, burnt wood cladding
cards.desc: A Japanese method of charring cedar boards to preserve them. The surface cracks into a black, scaly crust with a silvery sheen, and it reads as Japanese and architectural.
cards.phrase: shou sugi ban charred cedar with a black alligator-scale crust and silvery sheen

cards.name: Oiled wood
cards.aka: hardwax oil, Danish oil, oil finish
cards.desc: Wood rubbed with oil that soaks in and darkens the grain without forming a film. It reads as warm, natural and repairable, and feels like wood rather than plastic.
cards.phrase: oiled walnut with a hand-rubbed hardwax oil finish, rich grain and a soft low sheen

cards.name: Gold leaf
cards.desc: Gold beaten thinner than paper and laid down in small squares. You can see the seams between leaves and the red clay underneath where it wears through. It reads as frames, icons and old signage.
cards.phrase: hand-laid 23-carat gold leaf with visible square seams and small breaks showing red bole

cards.name: Flocked
cards.desc: Short fibers glued onto a pattern so it stands up like velvet against a flat ground. It reads as Victorian parlors, curry houses, and lately, maximalist interiors.
cards.phrase: deep red velvet flock damask pattern on a cream wallpaper ground

cards.name: Knurled
cards.desc: A fine diamond pattern pressed into round metal so fingers can grip it. It reads as precision tools, camera lenses, audio dials and barbells.
cards.phrase: precision diamond-knurled stainless steel grip next to polished bands

cards.name: Patina
cards.aka: aged brass, living finish, bronze patina
cards.desc: The soft darkening brass and bronze get with age, polished back to bright gold wherever hands touch it most. It reads as old, loved and expensive.
cards.phrase: unlacquered brass with a warm, uneven patina, rubbed bright where hands touch it

cards.name: Verdigris
cards.desc: The blue-green crust copper grows outdoors over years. It reads as old rooftops, harbour towns and the Statue of Liberty.
cards.phrase: weathered copper covered in chalky blue-green verdigris, with streaks running down

cards.name: Rust
cards.desc: Iron and steel turning orange-brown and flaking as they oxidize. It reads as abandonment, shipyards, and industrial grit.
cards.phrase: heavily rusted steel with orange and brown blooms, pitting and flaking scale

cards.name: Peeling paint
cards.aka: flaking paint, chipped paint, shabby chic
cards.desc: Old paint lifting and curling away to show the wood or plaster underneath. It reads as neglect, coastal houses and old shutters.
cards.phrase: flaking pale blue paint peeling off weathered grey wood, crisp curled edges

cards.name: Sun-faded
cards.desc: Color washed out by years of sunlight, often with a brighter ghost where something used to cover it. It reads as summers past, old shopfronts and vintage fabric.
cards.phrase: sun-faded red and cream stripes, bleached pale, with a vivid unfaded rectangle where a frame once hung

cards.name: Crackle
cards.desc: A fine web of cracks across old paint, varnish or glaze, from the surface shrinking at a different rate from what is under it. It reads as old masters, antique china and age.
cards.phrase: antique craquelure, a fine web of dark hairline cracks across aged cream glaze

cards.name: Edge wear
cards.desc: Paint rubbed away on the corners and edges first, showing bare metal or wood underneath. It is the detail 3D artists add to make a prop look used.
cards.phrase: olive-green painted steel with worn edges and corners chipped back to bright bare metal

cards.name: Kintsugi
cards.desc: The Japanese craft of mending broken pottery with lacquer and gold, so the cracks become the most beautiful part. It reads as wabi-sabi, resilience and care.
cards.phrase: kintsugi repaired stoneware bowl, dark glaze crossed by branching seams of bright gold

cards.name: Risograph
cards.desc: A Japanese office duplicator adopted by artists. It prints one flat soy ink at a time, often fluorescent pink, blue and yellow, so colors overlap into new ones and never line up perfectly.
cards.phrase: two-color risograph print in fluorescent pink and blue on cream paper, grainy ink coverage, overlapping colors and slight misregistration

cards.name: Letterpress
cards.aka: relief printing, debossed letterpress, wood type
cards.desc: Metal or wood type and plates pressed hard into thick soft paper, so the letters sit in a shallow dent you can feel. Today it signals wedding invitations, fine stationery and craft.
cards.phrase: letterpress printed in navy ink on thick white cotton paper, deep debossed impression you can see in the raking light

cards.name: Screen print
cards.desc: Thick, opaque ink pushed through a fine mesh stencil, one color at a time. The colors are flat and punchy and can sit light on top of dark.
cards.phrase: three-color screen print poster, flat opaque inks in mustard, brick red and navy, crisp edges with slight overlaps

cards.name: Offset lithography
cards.desc: The press behind almost every magazine, book and box. It builds color from tiny dots of cyan, magenta, yellow and black at different angles, which form rosettes under a loupe.
cards.phrase: offset-printed four-color CMYK image, visible halftone rosettes up close

cards.name: Newsprint halftone
cards.aka: coarse halftone, Ben-Day dots, newspaper print
cards.desc: A photo turned into a grid of black dots of different sizes, printed coarse on cheap paper. It reads as newspapers, tabloids and pop art.
cards.phrase: coarse black newsprint halftone photo with large visible dots on grey newsprint paper

cards.name: Photocopy
cards.desc: Pages run through an office copier, often several times, so greys collapse to harsh black and white and the toner leaves specks and streaks. It reads as punk, DIY and underground.
cards.phrase: photocopied zine page, harsh high-contrast black and white, toner speckle and copier streaks, collaged and taped

cards.name: Duotone
cards.desc: A photo printed in two inks, usually one dark and one bright, so the shadows and highlights each take a color. It reads as album covers, festival posters and editorial design.
cards.phrase: duotone image in deep navy and warm orange, shadows in navy and highlights in orange

cards.name: Linocut
cards.desc: An image carved into a sheet of linoleum, then inked and printed. Everything not carved away prints solid, so the picture is built from bold black shapes and white gouge strokes.
cards.phrase: black linocut print on cream paper, bold carved shapes and tapered white gouge marks, slightly uneven ink

cards.name: Woodcut
cards.desc: An image cut into a plank of wood along the grain. Lines are more angular than linocut and the grain often prints into the solid areas. Japanese woodblocks add flat colors from separate blocks.
cards.phrase: woodcut print in black with a flat red second block, angular carved lines, wood grain showing in the solid ink

cards.name: Etching
cards.desc: Lines bitten into a metal plate with acid, inked into the grooves and pressed onto damp paper. Tone comes from hatching and cross-hatching, and the plate leaves a pressed rectangle around the image.
cards.phrase: fine-line etching in warm black ink, cross-hatched shading, soft plate tone and a visible plate mark on heavy cream paper

cards.name: Engraving
cards.desc: Lines cut directly into metal with a burin, so they are very fine, regular and swell and taper. Paired with spirograph-like guilloche patterns it is the look of money and certificates.
cards.phrase: banknote-style line engraving in dark green, fine parallel shading lines and intricate guilloche rosettes

cards.name: Stone lithograph
cards.desc: An image drawn with greasy crayon on a slab of limestone, then printed. The grain of the stone breaks the crayon into soft speckled tones, often with flat colors added. It is the look of 1890s Paris posters.
cards.phrase: stone lithograph with grainy crayon shading and flat areas of mustard and red, on warm aged paper

cards.name: Cyanotype
cards.desc: Paper brushed with iron salts and exposed to sunlight with objects laid on top. The paper turns a deep Prussian blue and the shapes stay white, often with brushy edges where the coating stops.
cards.phrase: cyanotype sun print, deep Prussian blue with white fern and leaf silhouettes, brushed edges on watercolor paper

cards.name: Stencil spray
cards.desc: Spray paint through a cut stencil onto a wall or board. Edges are soft with a fine overspray mist, letters have little bridges holding them together, and paint sometimes drips.
cards.phrase: spray paint stencil on a concrete wall, soft overspray edges, stencil bridges in the letters and a few drips

cards.name: Hand block print
cards.desc: A carved wooden block stamped by hand over and over across cloth, one block per color. Each repeat is a little different: ink weight varies and the colors drift out of line.
cards.phrase: hand block-printed cotton with a small repeating floral motif in madder red and black, slightly uneven ink and registration

cards.name: Foil stamping
cards.aka: hot foil, gold foil, foil blocking
cards.desc: A heated die presses a thin metallic film onto the paper, leaving shiny gold, silver or copper that catches the light. It is pressed in, so it sits in a slight dent.
cards.phrase: gold hot-foil stamped lettering and border on deep navy uncoated card, metallic sheen catching the light

cards.name: Blind embossing
cards.desc: Paper pressed between two shaped dies so a logo or pattern rises out of the sheet. With no ink, you see it only in the shadows and highlights.
cards.phrase: blind embossed crest raised from thick white cotton card, no ink, revealed by soft raking light

cards.name: Debossing
cards.desc: The opposite of embossing: the design is pressed down into the board, leaving a sunken shape. It is often used on thick board, leather and book covers.
cards.phrase: debossed lettering pressed into thick kraft board, no ink, crisp sunken edges

cards.name: Spot UV
cards.aka: spot gloss, spot varnish, raised UV
cards.desc: A clear glossy varnish printed only on chosen areas, usually over a matte background, so a logo or pattern shines when you tilt it. It reads as premium print and packaging.
cards.phrase: matte black card with a glossy spot UV pattern and logo, visible only where the light reflects

cards.name: Die cut
cards.desc: A shaped steel blade punches holes or custom outlines through the sheet. A die-cut window lets you see the layer behind, and a cut outline gives a card or sticker its own shape.
cards.phrase: die-cut cover with a round window and arch cut-outs revealing a patterned inner page, crisp cut edges with soft shadow

cards.name: Thermography
cards.desc: Wet ink dusted with resin powder and heated so it swells into glossy raised lettering. It looks like engraving at a fraction of the price and is common on business cards.
cards.phrase: thermographed business card with glossy raised black ink lettering on bright white stock

cards.name: Edge painting
cards.aka: painted edges, gilded edges, colored edges
cards.desc: Color painted or foiled onto the cut edges of thick cards or a book block, so a stack shows a bright stripe. It reads as boutique stationery and special editions.
cards.phrase: stack of thick cotton business cards with hot pink painted edges

cards.name: Newsprint
cards.desc: Cheap, thin, slightly grey paper made from wood pulp. Ink soaks in and looks a little soft and grey, and the sheet yellows within months. It reads as news, zines and urgency.
cards.phrase: printed on grey-cream newsprint with soft absorbent ink and faint show-through

cards.name: Kraft paper
cards.aka: brown paper, kraft board, butcher paper
cards.desc: Unbleached brown paper with long, visible fibers. Printed on in black or white, it reads as natural, honest, shipping and farmers-market packaging.
cards.phrase: printed in black ink on unbleached brown kraft paper with visible fibers

cards.name: Cotton rag paper
cards.aka: cold-press paper, watercolor paper, mould-made cotton
cards.desc: Thick paper made from cotton fiber with a soft, toothy surface. It takes ink and paint beautifully and feels expensive in the hand. It is the paper of fine-art prints and letterpress invitations.
cards.phrase: thick cold-press cotton rag paper with a pronounced soft tooth, warm white

cards.name: Deckle edge
cards.aka: torn edge, feathered edge, handmade paper
cards.desc: The rough, feathered edge left on handmade paper where the pulp thinned out in the mould. It says handmade, artisanal and slow.
cards.phrase: handmade paper with soft feathered deckle edges

cards.name: Washi
cards.aka: Japanese paper, kozo, mulberry paper, unryu
cards.desc: Japanese paper made from long mulberry fibers, light and strong, often translucent with fibers floating in it. It reads as delicate, natural and quietly crafted.
cards.phrase: translucent kozo washi paper with long visible mulberry fibers, softly backlit

cards.name: Vellum
cards.desc: A smooth, frosted, translucent paper laid over something so it shows through softly. It reads as refined: invitation wraps, book fly-leaves and architects' drawings.
cards.phrase: a translucent frosted vellum overlay softly veiling the print beneath

cards.name: Gloss coated paper
cards.aka: glossy art paper, magazine stock, silk coated
cards.desc: Paper with a smooth clay coating so ink sits on top, sharp and saturated, with a shine that catches the light. It reads as magazines, catalogs and commercial print.
cards.phrase: printed on glossy coated magazine paper, saturated color and a soft glare across the page

cards.name: Corrugated cardboard
cards.desc: Two sheets of kraft with a wavy fluted layer glued between them. Torn or cut, the flutes show. It reads as shipping, DIY, protest signs and rough-and-ready packaging.
cards.phrase: corrugated cardboard with a torn top layer revealing the wavy brown flutes

cards.name: Marbled paper
cards.desc: Paper laid on a bath of floating inks that have been combed and swirled, so it picks up flowing, feathered patterns. It reads as antique books, Italian stationery and Turkish craft.
cards.phrase: hand-marbled endpaper with combed swirls of indigo, rust and gold on cream

cards.name: Misregistration
cards.desc: When each ink color is printed in a separate pass and the passes do not line up, colors slip off their outlines, leaving slivers of paper or overlap. Loved in riso and screen printing.
cards.phrase: slight misregistration between the ink layers, colors shifted a few millimeters off their outlines

cards.name: Ink bleed
cards.desc: Ink wicking into absorbent paper so edges go soft and furry and fine details fill in. It reads as cheap stock, rubber stamps and wet ink on cotton.
cards.phrase: soft ink bleed into absorbent paper, edges slightly feathered and swollen

cards.name: Moiré
cards.desc: A shimmering ripple pattern that appears when two fine grids, like halftone screens or fabric weaves, overlap at slightly different angles. A defect in print, now used on purpose for a glitchy, op-art feel.
cards.phrase: a visible moiré interference pattern from two overlapping fine line screens

cards.name: Uneven ink coverage
cards.aka: patchy solids, ink starvation, roller marks
cards.desc: Large areas of solid color that come out mottled, streaky or lighter in places because the press could not lay down an even film. It is the signature of riso and hand-pulled prints.
cards.phrase: uneven, mottled ink coverage in the solid areas, with speckles of paper showing through

cards.name: Fold lines & creases
cards.desc: Creases from a print folded to post or pocket, with the ink cracked along the fold and soft light and shadow across the panels. It says this was handed out, carried and kept.
cards.phrase: creased from being folded in quarters, the ink cracked and worn white along the fold lines

cards.name: Foxing & age stains
cards.aka: yellowed paper, age spots, coffee ring
cards.desc: Brown speckles and blotches that appear on old paper, with yellowed edges and the odd ring from a cup. It reads as archives, old letters and found ephemera.
cards.phrase: aged paper with brown foxing spots, yellowed edges and a faint coffee ring stain

cards.name: Overprint
cards.desc: Transparent inks printed on top of each other so they mix where they overlap, making a third color: blue over yellow goes green, pink over yellow goes orange. Riso and screen artists design with it.
cards.phrase: transparent overprinting inks, fluorescent pink, yellow and blue mixing into new colors where they overlap

cards.name: Torn paper collage
cards.desc: Pieces of printed paper torn by hand and layered, with white fibrous edges where the tear went through the paper and the odd bit of tape. It reads as punk, scrapbooks and handmade.
cards.phrase: layered torn paper collage, rough white fibrous tear edges and strips of masking tape

cards.name: Roughness
cards.desc: How blurry a surface's reflections are. Low roughness gives sharp, mirror-like highlights; high roughness spreads them into a soft glow. It is the single most useful dial for realism.
cards.phrase: low roughness, crisp sharp reflections

cards.name: Metalness
cards.desc: Whether a surface behaves like metal. Plastic and paint show the color with a white highlight on top; metal has no color of its own beneath and tints its reflections instead.
cards.phrase: fully metallic gold surface with tinted, mirror-like reflections

cards.name: Subsurface scattering
cards.desc: Light that enters a material, bounces around inside and comes out somewhere else. It is why skin, wax, marble, jade and milk glow softly instead of looking like painted plastic.
cards.phrase: subsurface scattering, soft waxy translucency with warm light glowing through the edges

cards.name: Anisotropic
cards.desc: Reflections stretched in one direction because the surface has fine grooves, as on brushed or spun metal. It is what makes a pan bottom or a watch dial show a bow-tie of light.
cards.phrase: spun brushed aluminium with anisotropic reflections forming a bow-tie highlight

cards.name: Clearcoat
cards.aka: coat layer, clear lacquer layer, car paint shader
cards.desc: A thin clear varnish layer over a base material, so you see two highlights at once: a soft one from the color underneath and a sharp one from the gloss on top.
cards.phrase: deep red car paint with a glossy clearcoat, sharp top reflections over a soft colored glow

cards.name: Thin-film iridescence
cards.desc: Rainbow colors that swirl and shift with the viewing angle, caused by light bouncing inside a very thin layer. It reads as soap bubbles, oil on water, beetle shells and futuristic packaging.
cards.phrase: thin-film iridescence like a soap bubble, swirling magenta, green and gold bands

cards.name: Transmission & refraction
cards.desc: Light passing through a clear solid and bending as it goes, so what is behind it appears flipped and squeezed. The index of refraction, or IOR, sets how strongly it bends.
cards.phrase: solid clear glass sphere refracting the background upside down, IOR 1.5, bright caustic on the floor

cards.name: Displacement
cards.aka: displacement map, height map, vs bump map
cards.desc: Texture that actually moves the geometry, so bumps change the silhouette and cast real shadows. A bump or normal map only fakes the shading and leaves the outline smooth.
cards.phrase: true displacement mapping, deep bumpy surface relief that breaks the silhouette

cards.name: Claymation
cards.desc: Everything sculpted from soft modelling clay, with rounded forms, saturated colors and tiny fingerprints. It reads as handmade, funny and warm.
cards.phrase: claymation style, soft plasticine with visible fingerprints and slightly lumpy hand-sculpted forms

cards.name: Felt craft
cards.desc: Flat shapes cut from wool felt and stitched or glued together, with fuzzy edges and visible stitching. It reads as cozy, childlike and handmade.
cards.phrase: felt craft style, fuzzy wool felt cut-outs with visible blanket stitching

cards.name: Layered paper cut
cards.desc: A scene built from stacked layers of cut colored paper, each casting a soft shadow on the one behind. It reads as crafted, calm and storybook.
cards.phrase: layered paper-cut diorama, stacked colored paper with crisp edges and soft shadows between layers

cards.name: Glassmorphism
cards.aka: frosted glass UI, acrylic material, backdrop blur
cards.desc: Translucent frosted panels floating over bright blurred color, with a thin light border. It is a UI style from Apple and Microsoft design systems.
cards.phrase: glassmorphism, a frosted translucent glass card with a thin white border over vivid blurred color blobs

cards.name: Liquid chrome
cards.desc: Molten, mirror-bright metal in blobby organic shapes, reflecting a stretched sky and horizon. It is the signature of Y2K and acid graphics.
cards.phrase: liquid chrome blob, molten mirror-polished metal with flowing sharp reflections

cards.name: Holographic foil
cards.desc: A thin film that splits light into pastel rainbows that slide as it moves. It reads as Y2K, trading cards, festival fashion and beauty packaging.
cards.phrase: holographic iridescent foil with pastel rainbow gradients and a crinkled metallic sheen

cards.name: Inflatable
cards.desc: Shapes and letters that look pumped full of air, with soft rounded edges, glossy highlights and pinched seams. It reads as playful, pop and current motion design.
cards.phrase: inflatable puffy 3D shapes, glossy balloon-like vinyl with soft rounded seams

cards.name: Vinyl toy
cards.aka: designer toy, art toy, soft vinyl
cards.desc: Smooth, chunky collectible figures in glossy molded vinyl with simplified faces. It reads as street-culture collectibles and cute 3D characters.
cards.phrase: designer vinyl toy figure, glossy smooth molded plastic, big head and simple face

cards.name: Ancient Egyptian temple
cards.desc: Massive sandstone temples entered through a pylon, a pair of sloping towers flanking a gate, leading into a hypostyle hall (a forest of fat columns holding up a flat stone roof). Everything is heavy, symmetrical and carved with painted reliefs and hieroglyphs.
cards.phrase: ancient Egyptian temple, twin sloping sandstone pylon towers flanking a tall gateway, carved hieroglyph reliefs, obelisk and sphinx avenue in front, harsh golden desert sunlight, deep blue shadows

cards.name: Mesopotamian ziggurat
cards.desc: A man-made mountain of mud brick, built as stacked terraces that shrink as they rise, with long ramped stairways meeting at a small shrine on top. Solid rather than hollow, it feels monumental and earthy.
cards.phrase: Mesopotamian ziggurat, three stacked mud-brick terraces with grooved buttressed walls, long converging stairways rising to a small shrine on top, warm dusk light, date palms on a flat plain

cards.name: Persian Achaemenid
cards.desc: Royal halls set on a raised stone platform, filled with very tall, slender fluted columns topped by double-bull capitals (two kneeling bull foreparts back to back, which held the roof beams). Staircases carry long relief bands of marching tribute-bearers.
cards.phrase: Achaemenid Persian palace ruins, very tall slender fluted stone columns crowned with double bull capitals, raised terrace with relief bands of marching figures, pale limestone, mountain backdrop, clear dry light

cards.name: Mesoamerican stepped pyramid
cards.desc: Steep stone pyramids built in stacked tiers, with one very steep central stair climbing to a small temple at the top. Maya temples often carry a roof comb, a pierced stone crest that makes them taller still; many rise out of jungle.
cards.phrase: Maya stepped pyramid, steep tiers of pale limestone, single steep central staircase up to a small temple with a pierced roof comb, rising above dense green rainforest, soft humid light

cards.name: Byzantine domed church
cards.aka: dome on pendentives, Hagia Sophia style
cards.desc: Churches built around a huge central dome, held up on pendentives (curved triangles that let a round dome sit on a square base), with half-domes cascading down on each side. Outside: banded brick and stone; inside: gold mosaics and light falling from a ring of windows.
cards.phrase: Byzantine domed church, broad shallow lead-grey dome on a drum ringed with small arched windows, cascading half-domes, walls banded in red brick and cream stone, warm late afternoon light

cards.name: Romanesque
cards.desc: Solid, fortress-like churches and abbeys with very thick walls, small windows and round arches everywhere. Doorways are set deep in layers of stepped arches, and square towers stand guard; the mood is calm, heavy and earthbound.
cards.phrase: Romanesque stone church, thick rough-cut walls, round-arched portal set deep in stepped arches, small narrow windows, square bell tower with paired arched openings, overcast soft light, green meadow

cards.name: Islamic / Moorish
cards.desc: Inward-looking palaces and mosques built around courtyards with long reflecting pools. Horseshoe arches (arches that curve back in at the bottom) sit on slim marble columns, walls are lace-carved stucco and tile, and ceilings drip with muqarnas, honeycomb-like vaulting.
cards.phrase: Moorish palace courtyard, arcade of horseshoe arches on slender marble columns, lace-carved stucco walls, geometric tile dado, long still reflecting pool lined with clipped myrtle, bright sun and cool shade

cards.name: Dravidian Hindu temple
cards.desc: Temple complexes entered through gopurams, towering gateways that taper in many tiers and are crowded with painted sculpted figures, topped by a barrel-vaulted crown with gold finials. Borrow the forms and color; do not try to recreate a specific living temple.
cards.phrase: South Indian Dravidian temple gateway, a tall tapering gopuram of many tiers crowded with brightly painted sculpted figures, barrel-vaulted crown with gold finials, red and white striped walls, palms, warm sun

cards.name: Khmer temple
cards.desc: Temple mountains of grey sandstone with clusters of towers shaped like lotus buds, arranged in fives around a tall central tower and wrapped in long galleries carved with reliefs. Often seen at dawn across a moat that mirrors the towers.
cards.phrase: Khmer temple at dawn, five lotus-bud sandstone towers rising over long carved galleries, mirrored in a still moat, weathered grey-brown stone, palm silhouettes, pink and apricot sky

cards.name: Chinese imperial hall
cards.desc: Timber halls raised on white marble terraces, with rows of red lacquered columns and huge double-eaved hipped roofs whose corners sweep upward. Glazed yellow roof tiles were reserved for the emperor; brackets under the eaves are painted blue and green.
cards.phrase: Chinese imperial palace hall, sweeping double-eaved hipped roof of yellow glazed tiles with upturned corners, rows of red lacquered columns, blue and green painted brackets, white marble terrace, clear blue sky

cards.name: Sahelian mud architecture
cards.desc: Sculpted buildings of sun-dried mud brick and plaster, with tapering towers and buttresses topped by cone pinnacles. Toron, bundles of palm wood sticking out of the walls, act as permanent scaffolding for the yearly replastering festival.
cards.phrase: Sahelian mud-brick mosque facade, smooth hand-plastered ochre walls, tapering towers and cone pinnacles, rows of wooden beams bristling from the walls, egg finials, harsh noon sun, sandy square

cards.name: Italian Renaissance palazzo
cards.desc: A city palace shaped like a calm stone box: rough rusticated blocks at street level (stones left bold and deeply jointed), smoother walls above, rows of round-arched windows, and a huge overhanging cornice. Order, symmetry and proportion are the point.
cards.phrase: Italian Renaissance palazzo facade, rusticated stone ground floor, rows of round-arched windows with alternating pediments, massive overhanging cornice, warm honey sandstone, symmetrical, soft Florentine light

cards.name: Baroque
cards.desc: Theatrical architecture built to stir emotion: curving facades that swell in and out, stacked columns, big scroll-shaped volutes, broken pediments (triangles with their tops split open) and statues against the sky. Inside, gilding and painted ceilings open to fake heavens.
cards.phrase: Baroque church facade, curving two-storey front with paired columns, giant scroll volutes, broken pediment and oval window, rooftop statues, dome behind, warm stone raking in dramatic sunlight

cards.name: Palladian villa
cards.desc: A country house dressed as a temple: a symmetrical block fronted by a columned portico and triangular pediment, often with a low dome and matching wings. Based on Andrea Palladio's villas, it became the polite look of English and American estates.
cards.phrase: Palladian villa, perfectly symmetrical pale stucco house with a six-column temple portico and pediment, low central dome, matching wings, broad stone steps, lawns and cypresses, calm summer light

cards.name: Russian Orthodox onion domes
cards.desc: White-walled churches crowned by clusters of bulbous onion domes, each on its own drum and topped by a cross, sometimes gilded, sometimes painted in spirals and stripes. Kokoshniks, rows of rounded decorative gables, step up toward the domes.
cards.phrase: Russian Orthodox church with a cluster of onion domes, some gilded and some painted in spiral stripes of red, green and blue, white walls with rounded kokoshnik gables, gold crosses, crisp winter sky

cards.name: Georgian townhouse
cards.desc: Restrained brick houses in long terraces, all proportion and rhythm: rows of tall sash windows (sliding windows divided into small panes) that shrink on the upper floors, a panelled front door under a fanlight, and black iron railings to the street.
cards.phrase: Georgian brick townhouse terrace, flat red brick facade, rows of white six-over-six sash windows, black panelled front door under a semicircular fanlight, iron railings, grey overcast London light

cards.name: Spanish colonial mission
cards.desc: Thick adobe churches washed in white plaster, with a curving bell gable (an espadaña, a wall pierced with arched openings for bells), red clay tile roofs and long shady arcades along a courtyard. Simple, sunbaked and solid.
cards.phrase: Spanish colonial mission church, thick whitewashed adobe walls, curved bell gable with bronze bells in arched openings, red clay tile roof, shaded arcade, heavy wooden door, palms, bright desert sun

cards.name: Greek Revival
cards.desc: Houses, banks and courthouses dressed as Greek temples: a full-height portico of white columns holding a wide triangular pediment. In America it meant white-painted wood, green shutters and a stately front facing a lawn.
cards.phrase: Greek Revival house, white painted temple front with six tall columns under a wide triangular pediment, green shutters, door with sidelights, broad lawn and old shade trees, bright summer afternoon

cards.name: Gothic Revival / Victorian Gothic
cards.desc: Nineteenth-century buildings that brought back medieval pointed arches, steep gables and spires, often in polychrome brick (bands of different colored brick) and slate. Seen in churches, parliaments, universities and train stations.
cards.phrase: Victorian Gothic building, red brick banded with cream and black, steep slate gables, pointed lancet windows with striped arches and tracery, tall spired clock tower, moody overcast sky

cards.name: Second Empire
cards.desc: Grand houses and civic buildings capped with a mansard roof, a steep, almost vertical roof wrapped around the top floor and punched with dormer windows. Patterned slate, iron cresting along the top and tall windows under curved hoods give a stately, slightly spooky look.
cards.phrase: Second Empire mansion, steep mansard roof in patterned grey slate with arched dormers and iron cresting, taller central pavilion, tall windows under curved hoods, pale walls, late afternoon light

cards.name: Beaux-Arts
cards.desc: Lavish public buildings trained in the Paris École des Beaux-Arts: perfectly symmetrical, with grand arched entrances, paired columns, sculpture groups on the skyline and wide ceremonial stairs. Pale stone, festive and civic.
cards.phrase: Beaux-Arts public building, symmetrical pale limestone facade, huge central arched entrance flanked by paired columns, sculpture group on the roofline, rusticated base, wide ceremonial steps, ornate lamps

cards.name: Queen Anne Victorian
cards.desc: Playfully asymmetrical houses with a round corner turret, a wraparound porch trimmed with spindles, patterned shingles in the gables and a mix of colors and textures. Every side looks different.
cards.phrase: Queen Anne Victorian house, asymmetrical with a round corner turret and conical roof, wraparound porch with spindles, patterned fish-scale shingles, sage green with cream and maroon trim, picket fence

cards.name: Chicago School skyscraper
cards.desc: The first tall office buildings, made possible by steel frames and elevators. They read in three parts like a column (heavy stone base, repeating middle, decorated top) and are full of wide windows to pull daylight deep inside.
cards.phrase: Chicago School skyscraper, 1890s steel-frame office tower clad in warm terracotta, heavy stone base with arched entries, rows of wide three-part windows, ornate cornice, sooty city street, overcast daylight

cards.name: Art Nouveau architecture
cards.desc: A style that tried to grow buildings like plants. Iron, glass and stone bend into stems, tendrils and "whiplash" curves (a long S-shaped line that snaps back on itself), from Brussels townhouses to the famous green Paris metro entrances.
cards.phrase: Art Nouveau metro entrance, sea-green cast-iron stems curling into whiplash arches and plant-like lamps with glowing amber glass, enamel sign panel, cream limestone facade behind, Paris street in soft daylight

cards.name: Catalan Modernisme
cards.desc: Catalonia's own exuberant take on Art Nouveau, tied to regional pride. Facades ripple like waves, balconies look like masks or bones, and roofs and towers glitter with trencadís (mosaic made of broken tile and glass shards).
cards.phrase: Catalan Modernisme facade, wavy sandstone roofline shimmering with broken-tile mosaic in turquoise, cobalt and gold, bone-like columns, mask-shaped iron balconies, slender organic tower with ceramic finial, bright Mediterranean light

cards.name: Prairie School
cards.desc: Houses that hug the ground like the flat prairie around them. Everything stretches sideways: low hipped roofs with huge overhangs, bands of windows and long walls, all anchored by a big central chimney.
cards.phrase: Prairie School house, long low brick home with wide flat hipped roofs and deep shadowed eaves, ribbons of geometric art-glass windows, broad central chimney, stone planter urns, midwestern lawn, late afternoon sun

cards.name: Craftsman bungalow
cards.desc: The friendly one-and-a-half storey American home of the Arts & Crafts movement, which prized honest handwork and natural materials. Low gables, a deep front porch and visible wooden joinery make it feel cozy and built by hand.
cards.phrase: Craftsman bungalow, low gabled house with sage-green shingle siding, deep front porch on tapered columns over river-stone piers, exposed rafter tails and knee braces, cream trim, oak door, leafy street

cards.name: Amsterdam School
cards.desc: Dutch housing blocks sculpted entirely in brick. Walls swell into rounded corners, bulge, step and taper into towers, so that ordinary social housing looks like a ship or a fortress made by a craftsman.
cards.phrase: Amsterdam School building, sculpted red-brown brick block with a rounded corner tower and pointed crown, horizontal brick bands, clusters of small white-framed windows, steep tile roof, reflected in a calm canal

cards.name: Expressionist architecture
cards.desc: Buildings shaped by emotion and imagination rather than rules. Some are smooth and organic as if poured or carved; others are jagged and crystalline, inspired by mountains and faceted glass.
cards.phrase: Expressionist architecture, smooth cream-rendered observatory tower that looks sculpted from clay, rounded flowing base, deep curved window slots, small dome on top, set among dark trees, soft daylight

cards.name: Pueblo Revival
cards.desc: A 20th-century style that borrows the look of Indigenous pueblo villages and Spanish mission adobe. Thick earth-colored walls with softly rounded edges step back in layers, with log beam ends poking out.
cards.phrase: Pueblo Revival building, terraced adobe-tan stucco blocks with soft rounded edges, rows of projecting log beam ends, small deep windows with turquoise frames, wooden ladder, strong desert sun, deep blue sky

cards.name: Spanish Colonial Revival
cards.aka: Spanish Revival, Mission Revival, Mediterranean Revival
cards.desc: A romantic sunny style drawing on Spanish and Mexican colonial buildings. White plaster walls, red clay tile roofs, arched arcades and wrought-iron details, often with a bell tower and a courtyard full of flowers.
cards.phrase: Spanish Colonial Revival villa, white stucco walls and red clay tile roofs, round-arched arcade, small bell tower, black wrought-iron balcony, pink bougainvillea, tall palms, warm California sun

cards.name: Streamline Moderne
cards.desc: A late, sleeker cousin of Art Deco inspired by trains, ocean liners and aircraft. Buildings get rounded corners, long horizontal bands and porthole windows, as if designed to move fast.
cards.phrase: Streamline Moderne building, smooth white stucco with a sweeping rounded corner, ribbon windows and triple horizontal speed-line bands in teal, porthole window, glass-block entrance, vertical fin, pastel sunset sky

cards.name: Googie
cards.desc: The playful roadside architecture of the car and space age: diners, motels and gas stations designed to catch a driver's eye. Roofs swoop up like boomerangs, signs explode into starbursts, and everything glows with neon.
cards.phrase: Googie diner, upswept boomerang roof in white and turquoise, wall of glass glowing warm inside, tall neon pylon sign with a starburst and atomic orbits, vintage car fins, purple and orange dusk sky

cards.name: Desert modernism
cards.desc: Mid-century houses tuned to the desert: razor-thin flat roofs throwing deep shade, walls of glass opening to the pool, and stone and decorative block walls framing views of bare mountains.
cards.phrase: Desert modernist house, razor-thin white flat roof over floor-to-ceiling glass, patterned breeze-block wall, stone accent wall, turquoise pool, palms and agave on pale gravel, bare brown mountains, clear desert light

cards.name: Tropical modernism
cards.desc: Modernism adapted to heat and monsoon rain. Buildings open up to the breeze with deep shading roofs, louvres and brise-soleil (fixed sun-shading fins), and the line between inside, garden and jungle almost disappears.
cards.phrase: Tropical modernist house, white concrete frame with deep overhanging roof, vertical sun fins and dark timber louvres, open shaded ground floor, plants tumbling from ledges, lotus pond, dense jungle, humid diffused light

cards.name: Metabolism
cards.desc: A Japanese postwar movement that imagined cities as living organisms. Fixed concrete cores carry plug-in capsules or modules that could, in theory, be swapped out and replaced as needs changed.
cards.phrase: Metabolist capsule tower, two raw concrete cores studded with stacked white box capsules, each with one round porthole window, irregular plug-in arrangement, gray Tokyo sky, 1970s futurism

cards.name: High-tech architecture
cards.desc: Buildings that show off how they work. Steel frames, cross-bracing, pipes, ducts and escalators are put on the outside, often color-coded, so the building looks like a precise machine.
cards.phrase: High-tech building, glass box wrapped in an exposed white steel frame with X cross-bracing, bright blue, red, green and yellow service pipes running up the facade, glass escalator tube climbing diagonally, crisp daylight

cards.name: Critical regionalism
cards.desc: Modern architecture that refuses to look the same everywhere. It keeps clean modern lines but answers the local place: its stone, timber, slope, climate and light, so the building feels like it belongs to that one landscape.
cards.phrase: Contemporary house rooted in its landscape, dry-stone base wall stepping down the hillside, white rendered volume with timber slat screen, mono-pitch metal roof following the slope, olive trees, soft afternoon light

cards.name: Minimalist concrete
cards.desc: Calm, silent spaces made of almost nothing: perfectly smooth concrete, a single slot of daylight, a sheet of still water. The emptiness makes you notice light, shadow and your own footsteps.
cards.phrase: Minimalist concrete interior, smooth gray walls with a neat grid of tie holes, a single tall slit of daylight cutting through the wall, beam of light across a still reflecting pool, lone figure, silent and spare

cards.name: Blobitecture
cards.desc: Buildings shaped like soft bulging organisms, made possible by computer design. There are no straight walls or right angles: just a swelling, rounded skin, often covered in shiny discs, panels or glass bubbles.
cards.phrase: Blobitecture department store, huge bulging amorphous building with no corners, deep blue skin covered in thousands of polished aluminium discs, glossy highlights, curved glass entrance, ordinary boxy city blocks around it

cards.name: Neo-futurism
cards.desc: Architecture of soaring optimism: dazzling white structures that sweep, arch and wing outward like birds, skeletons or spaceships, often mirrored in reflecting pools. Engineering becomes spectacle.
cards.phrase: Neo-futurist building, enormous sweeping white ribbed shell curving up like a bird's wing, glass beneath the arc, slender white ribs repeating, mirrored in a turquoise reflecting pool, cloudless blue sky

cards.name: Biophilic / vertical forest
cards.aka: green architecture, vertical garden tower, biophilic design
cards.desc: Buildings that bring nature back into the city by planting it on them. Staggered balconies carry real trees and shrubs, walls are covered in living plants, and the tower looks like a forest stood on end.
cards.phrase: Vertical forest residential tower, white concrete balconies staggered on every floor, each overflowing with real trees and shrubs, layers of green climbing the facade, glass behind, bright city sky, lush and alive

cards.name: Modern Nordic
cards.aka: Scandinavian modern house, new Nordic, black barn house
cards.desc: Simple archetypal house shapes stripped to their essence: a steep pitched roof with no overhang, walls and roof wrapped in the same black-stained timber or metal, and huge windows opening a pale, warm wooden interior to the landscape.
cards.phrase: Modern Nordic house, simple steep-gabled black timber barn with no eaves, huge gable window glowing with pale wood interior, light timber deck, white birch trees, wild grass meadow, soft overcast light

cards.name: Mass-timber architecture
cards.desc: Large modern buildings built from engineered wood instead of concrete and steel. Cross-laminated timber (CLT: thick panels of wood glued in crossing layers) and glulam (glued laminated beams) are left exposed, so the inside feels warm and the structure stores carbon.
cards.phrase: Mass-timber office building, glass facade revealing exposed honey-colored glulam columns and cross-laminated timber floors on every level, larch fin cladding, warm interior glow, stack of CLT panels on the plaza

cards.name: Adobe pueblo
cards.aka: Pueblo style, adobe house, terraced pueblo
cards.desc: Stacked, flat-roofed rooms made of sun-dried mud brick (adobe) and plaster, stepping back like a terraced hillside. The walls are thick and rounded at the edges, so the whole thing looks hand-shaped and warm.
cards.phrase: terraced adobe pueblo with stacked flat-roofed rooms, smooth rounded tan mud-plaster walls, protruding wooden roof beams, wooden ladders, small blue-trimmed windows, high desert sun and sharp shadows

cards.name: Log cabin
cards.aka: log house, frontier cabin, chalet log home
cards.desc: A simple house built from whole tree trunks stacked horizontally and notched together at the corners. It reads instantly as woods, wilderness and wood smoke.
cards.phrase: rustic log cabin of stacked honey-brown round logs with notched corner ends, fieldstone chimney with drifting smoke, small glowing windows, dark pine forest and dusky mountain sky

cards.name: A-frame cabin
cards.desc: A house that is basically one big triangle: two steep roof planes run straight down to the ground, with a wall of glass filling the gable end. It became the classic mid-century ski and lake getaway.
cards.phrase: mid-century A-frame cabin, steep dark roof sloping to the snowy ground, full triangular glass gable glowing amber at twilight, timber deck, tall snowy pines and blue mountain dusk

cards.name: Thatched cottage
cards.aka: English country cottage, cottage with thatched roof
cards.desc: A small whitewashed or stone cottage under a thick, rounded roof of straw or reed. The roof dominates: it bulges over little windows like eyebrows and makes the house look soft and storybook.
