cards.phrase: storybook thatched cottage with a thick rounded golden straw roof and eyebrow dormer, whitewashed walls, low green door, small paned windows, pink climbing roses and a white picket fence, soft morning light

cards.name: Tudor half-timbered house
cards.aka: half-timbered, black-and-white house, Tudor Revival, Fachwerk
cards.desc: A house whose wooden structural frame is left visible on the outside, dark timbers with pale plaster between them. Upper floors often jut out over the lower ones (jetties), under steep gables and tall chimneys.
cards.phrase: Tudor half-timbered house, dark oak beams in crosses and diagonals over cream plaster, jettied upper floor, steep gable, diamond-paned leaded windows, tall red brick chimney, soft English daylight

cards.name: Cape Cod cottage
cards.aka: Cape Cod house, New England cape
cards.desc: A low, wide, symmetrical one-and-a-half-storey house with a steep roof, a central door and a big chimney. Weathered gray cedar shingles and white trim give it a calm seaside look.
cards.phrase: classic Cape Cod cottage with weathered silver-gray cedar shingles, crisp white trim, steep dark roof with two dormers, central red door, navy shutters, blue hydrangeas and dune grass, clear coastal light

cards.name: Scandinavian red cottage
cards.aka: falu red cottage, Swedish stuga, rödfärg house
cards.desc: A wooden country cottage painted a deep rusty red (falu red, a paint made from copper-mine pigment) with white trim at the corners and windows. It sits in meadows and birch woods like part of the landscape.
cards.phrase: Swedish falu red wooden cottage with white window frames and corner boards, dark tiled roof, birch trees and a wildflower meadow sloping to a blue lake, soft long summer evening light

cards.name: Cycladic whitewashed house
cards.aka: Greek island house, Santorini style, Mykonos house
cards.desc: Cube-shaped houses coated in brilliant white lime, tumbling down a rocky island slope toward the sea. Doors, shutters and the occasional chapel dome are painted strong blue; borrow the forms rather than recreating a specific church.
cards.phrase: Cycladic island village of whitewashed cube houses with rounded edges, cobalt blue doors and a blue dome, white steps, magenta bougainvillea, deep blue sea below, dazzling midday sun

cards.name: Japanese machiya townhouse
cards.desc: A narrow, deep wooden townhouse that once held a shop at the front and the family behind. The street face is a calm screen of fine wooden slats, with a low tiled eave between the two floors.
cards.phrase: traditional Kyoto machiya townhouse, dark wood facade with fine vertical lattice screens, gray tiled eave, cream plaster upper floor with slatted windows, indigo noren curtain, paper lantern, quiet stone lane

cards.name: Moroccan riad
cards.desc: A house turned inward: plain walls to the street, and inside, a garden courtyard open to the sky with a fountain and trees. Arcades, carved plaster, painted wood and mosaic tile wrap around it.
cards.phrase: inside a Moroccan riad courtyard, rose plaster walls with horseshoe arches, zellige mosaic tile in green and blue, central tiled fountain, potted orange trees, carved cedar gallery above, dappled sun from the open sky

cards.name: Yurt (ger)
cards.desc: A round, portable home of felt stretched over a wooden lattice wall and roof poles, with a ring (crown) at the top to let in light and let out smoke. It sits alone in vast grassland.
cards.phrase: Mongolian ger with white felt walls and shallow cone roof, red rope bands, ornate orange painted door, thin stovepipe smoke, lone rider nearby, endless golden steppe and snow-tipped mountains under a vast blue sky

cards.name: Stilt house
cards.aka: pile dwelling, palafito, kampong air, bahay kubo
cards.desc: A house raised on wooden posts above water or flood-prone ground, so it stays dry and catches the breeze. Walls are often woven bamboo or timber, roofs thatched with leaves.
cards.phrase: tropical stilt house of woven bamboo raised on timber posts over calm green water, steep palm-thatch roof, wooden ladder and dugout canoe, coconut palm, warm hazy sunset reflected in the water

cards.name: Creole shotgun house
cards.aka: shotgun house, New Orleans shotgun, camelback
cards.desc: A narrow, one-room-wide house with rooms in a line from front to back, its gable end facing the street. In New Orleans they are painted bright colors and dressed in lacy wooden trim on the front porch.
cards.phrase: New Orleans shotgun house painted teal with white gingerbread trim, front-facing gable, full-height louvered shutters, raised porch on brick piers, pastel neighbors close on each side, humid golden light

cards.name: Hacienda
cards.aka: Spanish colonial ranch house, estancia, casa grande
cards.desc: A large ranch house of thick stucco walls under red clay tile roofs, laid out low and long around courtyards. Shady arcades (portales) run along the front.
cards.phrase: sprawling Spanish colonial hacienda, whitewashed stucco walls under red barrel-tile roofs, long shaded arcade of round arches, carved wooden doors, magenta bougainvillea, agave and terracotta pots, warm dry afternoon

cards.name: Boathouse on a lake
cards.aka: lake boathouse, boat shed, Muskoka boathouse
cards.desc: A wooden shed built over the water with a big door at water level so a boat can glide in, often with a little loft above. It sits on the shoreline of a still lake, doubled by its reflection.
cards.phrase: red wooden boathouse standing in a glassy lake, wide arched boat door at the waterline with a varnished boat inside, white trim, small dock, dark pine shoreline, perfect mirror reflection in calm morning light

cards.name: Haussmann boulevard
cards.desc: The long, uniform avenues of 19th-century Paris, lined with cream stone apartment buildings of equal height. Iron balconies run along two floors and steep gray zinc roofs with little windows sit on top.
cards.phrase: Parisian Haussmann boulevard, uniform cream limestone apartment facades with long wrought-iron balconies, tall French windows, gray zinc mansard roofs, chestnut trees, café awnings, soft overcast light

cards.name: Brownstone row houses
cards.desc: Attached city houses faced in chocolate-brown sandstone, each with a tall stoop (front steps) rising to a parlor-floor door. Bay windows, heavy cornices and iron railings repeat down a tree-lined block.
cards.phrase: row of New York brownstone townhouses, chocolate sandstone facades, tall stoops with black iron railings, bay windows, ornate cornices, leafy trees dappling the sidewalk, late afternoon sun

cards.name: Painted Ladies
cards.aka: Victorian row houses, San Francisco Victorians
cards.desc: Rows of wooden Victorian houses painted in three or more bright colors to show off their trim. Steep gables, bay windows and fancy carved details line up on a sloping street.
cards.phrase: row of Victorian Painted Ladies, wooden houses in mint, pink, lavender and butter yellow with contrasting trim, steep gables and bay windows, green park slope in front, hazy city skyline behind, crisp sunny day

cards.name: Amsterdam canal houses
cards.desc: Tall, narrow brick houses packed shoulder to shoulder along a canal, each topped with a decorative gable (stepped, bell-shaped or neck-shaped). Many lean slightly forward and have a hoisting beam at the top for lifting furniture.
cards.phrase: Amsterdam canal houses, tall narrow dark brick facades with stepped and bell gables, white window frames, hoisting beams, bicycles along the railing, reflections in the still green canal, soft gray light

cards.name: Mediterranean hill town
cards.desc: A village of stone and stucco houses heaped up a hilltop, roofs overlapping like scales, with a church tower or castle at the crown. From a distance it looks like one sculpted object.
cards.phrase: Mediterranean hill town of ochre and cream stone houses stacked up a hill under overlapping terracotta roofs, bell tower at the top, dark cypress trees on the slopes, warm golden evening light

cards.name: Medina alleyways
cards.aka: souk lanes, old city alleys, kasbah streets
cards.desc: The narrow, winding lanes of an old North African or Middle Eastern walled city, often only an arm’s span wide. Tall earthen walls, arches and hanging goods squeeze the light into bright shafts.
cards.phrase: narrow medina alleyway between tall sun-baked ochre walls, pointed arch ahead, carved blue door, hanging rugs and a brass lantern, a dusty shaft of sunlight cutting through deep shade

cards.name: Beijing hutong
cards.desc: Narrow alleys of old Beijing lined with the gray brick walls of courtyard houses (siheyuan). The walls are plain, but the gates are red with painted beams, guarded by lanterns and old trees.
cards.phrase: quiet Beijing hutong lane, gray brick walls and curved gray tile roofs, red lacquered courtyard gate with brass studs and painted beams, red lanterns, a parked bicycle, scholar tree shade

cards.name: Hong Kong tower blocks
cards.aka: Hong Kong high-rises, dense residential towers
cards.desc: Thin residential towers packed so tightly they become a wall of windows, with green mountains rising right behind. Air conditioners, laundry poles and patched paint cover every face.
cards.phrase: dense wall of Hong Kong residential towers, faded pastel facades with endless tiny windows, air conditioners and colorful laundry, steep green mountain behind, humid hazy daylight

cards.name: Soviet panel blocks
cards.desc: Mass-produced apartment buildings assembled from identical factory-made concrete panels, repeated across whole districts. The grid of seams, windows and glazed-in balconies is endlessly regular.
cards.phrase: Soviet-era prefab panel apartment block, gray-beige concrete panels with visible seams, identical windows and mismatched glazed balconies, birch trees and a rusty playground, flat overcast light

cards.name: Favela hillside
cards.desc: A self-built neighborhood of brick and concrete houses stacked up a steep hill, added to room by room. Some are bare orange brick, others painted bright colors, all crowned with blue water tanks and tangled wires.
cards.phrase: dense favela hillside of stacked bare orange brick and brightly painted concrete houses, blue rooftop water tanks, tangled wires, steep jungle-green mountain above, bright tropical sunlight

cards.name: Small-town Main Street
cards.desc: A short, friendly downtown of two- and three-storey brick shop buildings with apartments above. Striped awnings, painted signs and lampposts line a wide street with angled parking.
cards.phrase: small-town American Main Street, two-storey red and tan brick storefronts with ornate cornices, striped awnings and painted signs, lampposts and a flag, a vintage car at the curb, warm afternoon sun

cards.name: Tokyo backstreet
cards.desc: A narrow lane behind the big avenues, crowded with tiny bars and eateries (izakaya). Red paper lanterns glow under a tangle of power lines and concrete poles, with a vending machine shining on the corner.
cards.phrase: narrow Tokyo backstreet at dusk, glowing red paper lanterns and noren curtains, vertical shop signs, tangle of overhead power lines on concrete poles, lit vending machine, wet asphalt reflecting warm light

cards.name: Venetian canal
cards.desc: A narrow green canal walled in by old palaces (palazzi) whose doors open straight onto the water. Pointed Gothic windows, faded plaster and striped mooring poles make it unmistakable.
cards.phrase: Venetian canal lined with faded pink and ochre palazzi, white Gothic arched windows, striped mooring poles, a black gondola gliding on jade-green water, rippling reflections, soft hazy light

cards.name: Suburban cul-de-sac
cards.desc: A dead-end street ending in a round turnaround, ringed by similar single-family houses with driveways, front lawns and young trees. From above it looks like a keyhole or a lollipop.
cards.phrase: aerial view of a suburban cul-de-sac, round gray asphalt turnaround ringed by similar houses with hipped roofs, driveways and bright green lawns, young trees casting short shadows, midday sun

cards.name: Board-formed concrete
cards.desc: Concrete poured into forms made of rough timber planks, so each board leaves its grain and seam printed in the grey surface. Raw, heavy and surprisingly warm.
cards.phrase: board-formed concrete wall, cool grey surface printed with horizontal timber plank grain and seams, neat rows of round tie holes, low raking sunlight revealing the texture

cards.name: Exposed brick
cards.aka: face brick, Flemish bond, English bond, running bond
cards.desc: Brick left bare instead of plastered. The bond, the pattern the bricks are laid in, changes the character: Flemish bond alternates long sides (stretchers) and short ends (headers) in every row, English bond alternates whole rows of each, and running bond is all stretchers, offset by half.
cards.phrase: exposed red brick wall in Flemish bond, alternating long stretchers and darker short headers, varied clay tones, pale lime mortar, warm low sunlight raking across the surface

cards.name: Rammed earth
cards.desc: Damp soil packed hard, layer by layer, inside a temporary form, so the finished wall shows horizontal stripes like a cut through a cliff. Thick, quiet and earthy.
cards.phrase: rammed earth wall with horizontal striped layers of ochre, tan and rust soil, gritty pebbly texture, thick monolithic mass, warm desert light grazing the surface

cards.name: Ashlar stone
cards.desc: Stone cut into crisp, squared blocks and laid in level courses (rows) with very thin joints. It reads as permanent, formal and carefully made.
cards.phrase: ashlar masonry wall of large squared honey-colored limestone blocks in level courses, hairline joints, subtle tone variation between stones, soft afternoon light

cards.name: Fieldstone / rubble wall
cards.desc: Stones used roughly as found, round or irregular, fitted together with deep mortar joints or none at all. Rustic, handmade and rooted in the landscape.
cards.phrase: fieldstone wall of irregular rounded stones in mixed grey, brown and ochre, deep shadowed mortar joints, rustic handmade texture, low sun raking across the stones

cards.name: Heavy timber frame
cards.aka: post and beam, timber framing, mass timber
cards.desc: A structure of big squared wooden posts and beams, joined with pegs and braced with short angled knee braces, left visible inside. Warm, sturdy and barn-like.
cards.phrase: interior of a heavy timber frame building, thick dark oak posts and beams joined with wooden pegs, diagonal knee braces, white plaster walls, warm window light on wide plank floor

cards.name: Shou sugi ban (charred timber)
cards.desc: A Japanese technique of scorching wooden boards until the surface turns to a layer of charcoal, which protects the wood. The result is deep black with a cracked, scaly sheen.
cards.phrase: shou sugi ban cladding, vertical charred black timber boards with a cracked alligator-skin texture, silvery sheen where low light catches the scales, crisp board gaps

cards.name: Corten (weathering) steel
cards.desc: A steel that rusts on the surface into a stable, protective orange-brown skin, so it is left bare. It looks industrial, sculptural and earthy at once.
cards.phrase: tall Corten weathering steel wall, mottled rust orange and deep brown plates with darker drip streaks, thin crisp seams, rust stains on the pale gravel below, soft daylight

cards.name: Glass curtain wall
cards.desc: A skin of glass panels hung on a thin metal grid in front of the structure, so the façade carries no weight. It reflects sky, clouds and neighbors more than it shows what is inside.
cards.phrase: glass curtain wall office tower façade, grid of slim dark aluminum mullions, panes mirroring blue sky, clouds and a warped neighboring tower, crisp diagonal glare

cards.name: Glass block
cards.desc: Thick, hollow glass bricks laid in mortar like masonry. They let light through but blur what is behind, giving a soft watery glow.
cards.phrase: glass block wall, grid of thick square translucent blocks with rippled inner pattern, pale aqua tint, thin grey mortar joints, warm light glowing through, blurred plant beyond

cards.name: Terracotta cladding
cards.aka: terracotta baguettes, rainscreen tiles, architectural terracotta
cards.desc: Fired clay used as a façade skin: today often slim horizontal rods (baguettes) or tiles hung in front of the wall, in the past richly molded blocks. Warm, matte and gently rhythmic.
cards.phrase: façade of horizontal terracotta baguettes, rows of slim rounded orange-red fired clay rods with soft shadow gaps, slender vertical fins, warm glazing glowing behind

cards.name: Stucco / lime render
cards.desc: A thin coat of lime or cement plaster troweled over a wall, often painted or tinted, giving a soft, slightly uneven skin. Typical of Mediterranean, Mexican and Spanish Colonial houses.
cards.phrase: sunlit lime-rendered stucco wall in warm off-white, gently uneven troweled texture, deep-set arched window, crisp shadows, terracotta pot with a plant, Mediterranean light

cards.name: Copper with verdigris
cards.desc: Copper roofing or cladding starts shiny brown and over years weathers to a chalky blue-green patina called verdigris, often streaky with traces of the brown still showing.
cards.phrase: copper dome weathered to chalky blue-green verdigris, standing seams converging to a finial, streaks of brown copper showing through, pale sky behind

cards.name: Cedar shingles
cards.desc: Small overlapping cedar shingles in staggered rows, starting honey-colored and weathering to silver grey. Cozy, coastal and textured.
cards.phrase: weathered cedar shingle wall, overlapping staggered rows in mixed silver grey and honey tones, shadow line under each course, crisp white-trimmed window, coastal light

cards.name: Terrazzo
cards.desc: Chips of marble, glass or stone set in cement or resin and polished flat, giving a speckled, confetti-like surface. Playful at large chip sizes, refined at small ones.
cards.phrase: polished terrazzo floor, pale cream base scattered with angular chips of charcoal, terracotta, ochre and sage, thin brass divider strip, soft reflected window light

cards.name: Marble with veining
cards.desc: Polished stone with flowing veins. Calacatta has a bright white ground with bold grey and gold veins, Carrara is greyer with softer, finer veining. Slabs are often book-matched, opened like a book so the veins mirror.
cards.phrase: book-matched Calacatta marble wall, bright white polished stone with bold flowing grey and gold veins mirrored at the center seam, soft glossy reflections

cards.name: Travertine
cards.desc: A warm beige limestone full of small natural holes and fine horizontal bands, formed by mineral springs. Used for floors, walls and chunky furniture, it feels sun-baked and Roman.
cards.phrase: honed travertine wall, warm beige stone with fine horizontal banding and small elongated pits, large tiles with thin joints, soft raking sunlight

cards.name: Zellige tile
cards.desc: Small handmade Moroccan clay tiles with a thick glaze that pools unevenly, so each square differs in tone and catches light at slightly different angles.
cards.phrase: handmade zellige tile wall, small glossy squares in deep emerald with uneven surfaces and edges, rich tone variation, light glinting off pooled glaze, thin cream grout

cards.name: Encaustic cement tile
cards.aka: cement tile, mosaico hidráulico, Victorian floor tile
cards.desc: Thick cement tiles where the pattern is made of colored cement poured in, not painted on, so it wears with the tile. Bold geometric or floral motifs repeat into larger patterns across a floor.
cards.phrase: encaustic cement tile floor, bold repeating star and circle motif in navy, terracotta, ochre and cream, matte chalky surface with gentle wear, patterns joining across tiles

cards.name: Subway tile
cards.desc: Glossy white rectangular ceramic tiles, usually twice as wide as tall, laid in a staggered brick pattern. Clean, classic and a little utilitarian.
cards.phrase: white glossy subway tile wall in a staggered brick pattern, slightly beveled edges, thin grey grout, soft highlights, wooden shelf and countertop, calm daylight

cards.name: Limewash paint
cards.aka: lime paint, mineral paint, chalky wash
cards.desc: A paint made from lime that soaks into the wall and dries uneven, giving a soft, cloudy, chalky surface with visible brush movement. Earthy and calm.
cards.phrase: limewash wall in soft clay pink, cloudy mottled color with visible crisscross brush strokes, chalky matte surface, low plinth with a dark ceramic vase and a branch shadow

cards.name: Tadelakt / Venetian plaster
cards.aka: tadelakt, marmorino, stucco veneziano, polished plaster
cards.desc: Lime plaster polished by hand with stones or steel trowels until it is smooth, softly glossy and water-resistant. Tadelakt is Moroccan and used in baths; Venetian plaster is the Italian cousin, often with a marble-like depth.
cards.phrase: tadelakt bathroom, seamless polished lime plaster in warm terracotta with a soft satin sheen and cloudy burnish marks, rounded arched niche, curved edges, no grout lines

cards.name: Microcement
cards.aka: microtopping, polished concrete finish, seamless cement
cards.desc: A thin cement coating troweled over floors, walls and built-in furniture so everything flows together in one seamless skin. Minimal, soft grey and cloudy.
cards.phrase: minimal room in seamless microcement, warm grey floor, walls and built-in bench flowing as one surface, soft cloudy trowel marks, satin finish, diffuse window light

cards.name: Herringbone parquet
cards.desc: Wooden floor made of short planks laid in a zigzag where each plank end meets the side of the next. Chevron is the cousin where ends are cut at an angle to meet in a point.
cards.phrase: herringbone oak parquet floor, short honey-toned planks in a zigzag, varied grain from plank to plank, satin oiled finish, a stripe of sunlight across the boards

cards.name: Wainscoting & paneling
cards.desc: Wooden panels or moldings covering the lower part of a wall, capped by a chair rail (a horizontal ledge). Raised panels feel traditional, beadboard cottagey, picture-frame molding Parisian.
cards.phrase: room with sage-green painted wainscoting, framed raised panels with beveled moldings, chair rail and tall baseboard, warm cream plaster above, brass sconce glowing

cards.name: Rattan & cane
cards.desc: Rattan is a climbing palm whose stems are bent into furniture frames; cane is its thin outer skin, woven into an open mesh with little octagonal holes. Light, airy and summery.
cards.phrase: rattan chair back with woven cane webbing, honey-colored mesh with octagonal holes, rounded bentwood frame, wrapped legs, soft patterned shadow on a cream wall

cards.name: Bouclé upholstery
cards.desc: A fabric woven from yarn full of tiny loops, so it looks nubby and cloud-like. Usually creamy white on soft, rounded furniture.
cards.phrase: curvy armchair upholstered in cream bouclé, nubby looped wool texture, rounded sculptural silhouette, soft matte shading, warm taupe wall behind

cards.name: Velvet
cards.desc: A fabric with a short dense pile, so it shimmers between deep shadow and bright sheen as it curves. Rich, luxurious and glamorous.
cards.phrase: channel-tufted emerald velvet sofa, plush pile shimmering bright on each rounded channel and near-black in the folds, soft crush marks, dusty pink wall

cards.name: Brass & bronze fittings
cards.desc: Taps, handles, lamps and trims in warm gold-toned brass or darker brown bronze. Polished brass gleams, unlacquered brass dulls to a soft patina over time.
cards.phrase: unlacquered brass gooseneck faucet and cross handles on a white marble counter, brass bar pulls on deep green cabinets, bright warm highlights

cards.name: High-gloss lacquer
cards.desc: Many coats of paint or lacquer polished to a mirror shine, so walls or cabinets reflect the room like dark glass. Bold, jewel-box and glamorous.
cards.phrase: high-gloss oxblood lacquered cabinetry, mirror-like surface reflecting a window and a warm lamp, sharp highlight edges, thin brass pulls, dark glossy floor

cards.name: Rococo salon
cards.desc: A light, playful French drawing room: pale pastel walls framed in carved white and gold panels, curling shell-like ornament (rocaille) and furniture on slender curved legs. It feels like frosting and candlelight.
cards.phrase: Rococo salon interior, pale mint walls with carved white and gilt boiserie panels, ornate gold scroll mirror over a marble fireplace, pink silk bergère chairs on curved legs, crystal chandelier, parquet floor, soft daylight

cards.name: French Provincial
cards.desc: The countryside cousin of grand Parisian style: the same curvy furniture shapes, but in painted or waxed wood, with rough limewashed walls, terracotta floors and homely fabrics. Warm, sunny and lived-in.
cards.phrase: French Provincial farmhouse kitchen, limewashed plaster walls and dark beams, hexagonal terracotta tile floor, carved sage-painted armoire, rush-seat chair, blue gingham tablecloth, lavender by a shuttered window, warm sun

cards.name: Chinoiserie
cards.desc: An 18th century European fantasy of East Asia: hand-painted wallpapers of branches and birds, red or black lacquered cabinets and blue and white porcelain. It is a Western decorative style, so treat it as a historical look rather than an accurate picture of China.
cards.phrase: Chinoiserie drawing room, hand-painted celadon wallpaper with flowering branches and birds, red lacquer cabinet with brass fittings, blue and white ginger jars, black fretwork chair, navy rug, soft lamplight

cards.name: Shaker
cards.desc: The rooms of a 19th century American religious community that prized order and honest craft. Plain white walls, a wooden peg rail circling the room, and slender, beautifully made furniture with no decoration at all.
cards.phrase: Shaker room, plain white plaster walls with a wooden peg rail, chair hung upside down on a peg, ladderback chair with blue woven seat, maple trestle table with stacked oval boxes, muted blue-green trim, quiet daylight

cards.name: Victorian parlor
cards.desc: The crowded, cozy best room of a 19th century house. Dark patterned wallpaper, heavy fringed curtains, buttoned velvet furniture, gilt-framed portraits and potted ferns everywhere: more is more.
cards.phrase: Victorian parlor, deep burgundy damask wallpaper and dark wood paneling, plum velvet button-tufted sofa, heavy green drapes with gold tassels, fringed table lamp, gilt-framed portraits, potted fern, Persian rug, dim lamplight

cards.name: English country house
cards.desc: The relaxed, slightly faded comfort of a big old English house: floral chintz sofas, piles of books, oil landscapes, a dog bed by the fire. It should look inherited and used, never brand new.
cards.phrase: English country house sitting room, warm yellow walls and cream paneling, faded chintz sofa with mismatched cushions, skirted table with pleated lamp, oil landscapes, worn rug, dog bed, sash window onto a garden

cards.name: Art Deco interior
cards.desc: Jazz Age glamour: bold geometry, glossy black lacquer, gold, chrome and mirror, with stepped and fanned shapes everywhere. Rooms feel sleek, symmetrical and a little theatrical.
cards.phrase: Art Deco living room, cream fluted walls, black lacquer stepped fireplace with a gold sunburst mirror, curved burgundy velvet club chairs, chrome and glass side table, black and white floor, warm uplighting

cards.name: Hollywood Regency
cards.desc: Old movie star glamour at home: saturated lacquered walls, black and white floors, mirrored furniture, gold everywhere and bold pink or emerald upholstery. Polished, witty and made to be photographed.
cards.phrase: Hollywood Regency living room, glossy emerald lacquered walls, black and white checkerboard floor, hot pink tufted settee on gold legs, gilt sunburst mirror over a mirrored console, white ginger jar lamps, potted palm

cards.name: Mid-century modern interior
cards.desc: Optimistic post-war living: open plans, walls of glass to the garden, warm teak and walnut, and low furniture on slim tapered legs in mustard, teal and orange. Clean but friendly.
cards.phrase: Mid-century modern living room, glass wall onto trees, walnut slat wall, low mustard sofa on tapered legs, molded lounge chair, teak credenza with ceramics, arc floor lamp, sunburst clock, warm afternoon light

cards.name: 1970s conversation pit
cards.desc: A living room floor stepped down into a sunken square lined with built-in cushions, made for lounging and talking. Wrapped in shag carpet and wood paneling in orange, brown and harvest gold.
cards.phrase: 1970s sunken conversation pit, built-in burnt orange cushions around a sunken well, brown shag carpet, wood-paneled walls, round low coffee table, amber globe pendants, macramé plant hanger, golden sunset through a ribbon window

cards.name: Scandinavian
cards.desc: Bright, calm and practical rooms made for long dark winters: white walls, pale wood, soft greys and lots of daylight, warmed with textiles, candles and plants.
cards.phrase: Scandinavian living room, white walls and pale oak floor, light grey sofa with sheepskin throw, round birch coffee table, white pendant lamp, wishbone chair, fiddle leaf fig, soft northern daylight

cards.name: Japandi
cards.desc: A blend of Japanese and Scandinavian calm: low wooden furniture, warm neutrals, natural textures and a few handmade objects, with charcoal accents for contrast. Uncluttered but warm.
cards.phrase: Japandi living room, warm beige walls, low oak platform sofa with oatmeal linen cushions, slatted wood screen, paper lantern floor lamp, low dark coffee table with handmade ceramics, single branch, jute rug, soft diffused light

cards.name: Wabi-sabi
cards.desc: Built on a Japanese idea of beauty in imperfection and age. Rooms are earthy and quiet, with hand-troweled walls, raw wood, lumpy pottery and nothing too polished or symmetrical.
cards.phrase: wabi-sabi interior, hand-troweled clay plaster walls, rough timber bench, uneven handmade stoneware, dried branches in a rough vase, rumpled linen, worn concrete floor, deep plaster niche, soft low shadowy light

cards.name: Industrial loft
cards.desc: A converted factory or warehouse that keeps its bones on show: bare brick, steel-framed windows, concrete floors, exposed ducts and pipes, furnished with worn leather and reclaimed wood.
cards.phrase: industrial loft, exposed red brick wall, tall black steel factory windows, polished concrete floor, exposed silver ductwork, bare Edison bulb pendants, cognac leather sofa, reclaimed wood and steel coffee table

cards.name: Bohemian
cards.desc: A free-spirited, collected look: layered patterned rugs, rattan, floor cushions, macramé and plants in every corner, all in warm earthy colors. It should look gathered from travels and markets.
cards.phrase: bohemian living room, layered kilim rugs, rattan peacock chair, floor cushions and pouf, macramé wall hanging, hanging trailing plants, warm string lights, terracotta and rust tones, arched window

cards.name: Coastal
cards.desc: A breezy beach-house look: white and sand tones with ocean blues, slipcovered sofas, rattan and driftwood, and big windows letting in sea light. Relaxed and easy to clean.
cards.phrase: coastal living room, white shiplap walls, washed oak floor, white slipcovered sofa with navy striped pillows, rattan armchair, jute rug, driftwood coffee table, sheer linen curtains, big window onto the sea

cards.name: Modern farmhouse
cards.desc: Rustic country charm made crisp and new: white board walls, black-framed windows and black metal lights, reclaimed wood beams and a sliding barn door. Bright, homey and tidy.
cards.phrase: modern farmhouse dining room, white shiplap walls, reclaimed wood beams, sliding barn door on a black rail, black-framed windows, black metal dome pendant over a chunky wood table, cross-back chairs

cards.name: Minimalist
cards.desc: Rooms stripped to the essentials: a few well-chosen pieces, lots of empty floor and wall, and a tight palette of white, grey and one material. The calm comes from what is left out.
cards.phrase: minimalist living room, bare white walls, pale concrete floor, one long low sofa, a single small artwork, one black stool with a vase, huge frameless window, soft even daylight, almost empty

cards.name: Dark academia
cards.desc: A moody, bookish look borrowed from old universities: deep green and brown walls, floor-to-ceiling books, worn leather, brass lamps and candlelight. Rainy-day, romantic and a little gloomy.
cards.phrase: dark academia study, deep green walls, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, worn leather wingback chair with tartan throw, dark wood desk with green banker's lamp, antique globe, candle, rainy arched window

cards.name: Cottagecore
cards.desc: A romantic dream of country cottage life: small-sprig floral wallpaper, gingham, wildflowers in jugs, painted dressers of plates, quilts and baskets. Soft, sunny and handmade.
cards.phrase: cottagecore kitchen, small floral wallpaper, low wooden beams, gingham tablecloth with wildflowers in a jug, painted sage dresser with plates, patchwork cushion, wicker basket, sunny cottage window onto a flower garden

cards.name: Grandmillennial
cards.desc: Traditional grandmother style made fresh and fun: chintz, ruffles, pleated lampshades, blue and white china and wicker, used with a young, bright confidence.
cards.phrase: grandmillennial living room, blue trellis wallpaper, chintz camelback sofa with ruffled pink skirt, pleated scalloped lampshade on a skirted table, blue and white plates on the wall, wicker chair with needlepoint pillow

cards.name: Quiet luxury
cards.desc: Expensive without showing off: soft greige and taupe, rich textures like bouclé, cashmere, oak and travertine, curved sculptural furniture and gentle hidden lighting. Nothing shouts, everything feels heavy and good to touch.
cards.phrase: quiet luxury living room, greige oak paneled walls washed in soft light, curved cream bouclé sofa, travertine coffee table with a single dark vase, cashmere throw, large stone floor tiles, calm muted palette

cards.name: Moroccan-inspired
cards.desc: Rooms borrowing the forms of North African houses: keyhole arches, glazed zellige tile, pierced brass lanterns, low cushioned banquettes and woven rugs in rich spice colors. Borrow the forms, rather than recreating a specific sacred or historic site.
cards.phrase: Moroccan-inspired lounge, terracotta plaster walls, teal zellige tile dado, keyhole arch onto a sunny courtyard, low banquettes with patterned cushions, pierced brass lanterns, brass tray table with tea glasses

cards.name: Eclectic maximalist
cards.desc: Bold, personal rooms that layer color, pattern and collected objects with confidence: dark jewel walls, a packed gallery wall, clashing prints and velvet. It works when one color thread ties everything together.
cards.phrase: eclectic maximalist living room, deep teal walls with a dense gallery wall of mixed frames, raspberry velvet sofa piled with patterned pillows, black and cream striped armchair, leopard rug, colorful lamp, palms

cards.name: Great hall
cards.desc: One huge, tall room at the heart of a castle or manor, built for feasts and gatherings. It feels communal, smoky and a little theatrical.
cards.phrase: a medieval great hall, soaring dark oak hammerbeam roof, rough stone walls, tall lancet windows, roaring fireplace, long candlelit trestle table, heraldic banners, worn flagstone floor

cards.name: Library (double-height with ladders)
cards.desc: A library tall enough for two levels of books, with a walkway (gallery) running around the upper shelves and rolling ladders to reach the top. Hushed, warm and a little magical.
cards.phrase: a double-height wooden library, books from floor to ceiling, an upper gallery with a carved railing, a rolling brass ladder, tall arched window, warm lamplight, a worn Persian rug

cards.name: Conservatory / orangery
cards.desc: A room made mostly of glass held in a slender iron or timber frame, built to grow plants (orangeries were for citrus trees). Bright, humid and green.
cards.phrase: a Victorian glass conservatory, white wrought-iron frame and curved glass roof, potted orange trees and tall palms, terracotta pots, humid green light, sun dappling a tiled floor

cards.name: Atrium
cards.desc: A tall open space in the middle of a building, rising through several floors to a glass roof, with balconies looking down into it. It pulls daylight deep inside.
cards.phrase: a bright multi-storey atrium, white balconies with glass railings stacked around an open void, a gridded glass roof above, a tall tree on the ground floor, soft daylight pouring down

cards.name: Reading nook (window seat)
cards.desc: A small built-in seat tucked into a window bay or alcove, often with shelves around it. The coziest spot in the house: soft cushions, daylight, a book.
cards.phrase: a cozy window seat reading nook, deep cushioned bench in an alcove, built-in bookshelves on both sides, plump pillows, soft daylight through small-paned windows, a knitted blanket

cards.name: Enfilade (aligned doorways)
cards.desc: A row of rooms whose doorways line up exactly, so you can see through all of them in one long view. Common in palaces; it feels grand and slightly dreamlike.
cards.phrase: a palace enfilade, a long line of aligned doorways receding into the distance, gilded frames and open double doors, polished parquet, pastel walls, a bright window at the far end

cards.name: Attic room under the eaves
cards.desc: A room tucked into the roof, so the ceiling slopes down on both sides. Exposed beams, a small window or skylight, and a snug, hideaway feeling.
cards.phrase: a cozy attic bedroom under the eaves, steep sloping white ceilings with dark exposed rafters, a small round window, a skylight beam, wide pine floorboards, a quilted bed

cards.name: Vaulted cellar
cards.desc: An underground room roofed with a curved brick or stone vault (a ceiling built as a continuous arch). Cool, dim and enclosed, with sound that hangs in the air.
cards.phrase: a barrel-vaulted brick cellar, curved arches repeating into darkness, oak wine barrels along the walls, one warm hanging lantern, cool damp air, worn stone floor

cards.name: Thermal baths / bathhouse
cards.aka: Roman baths, hammam, onsen hall, spa
cards.desc: A grand room built around a pool of warm water, from Roman baths to Turkish hammams and modern spas. Steamy, echoing and calm.
cards.phrase: a grand thermal bathhouse, turquoise pool under tall stone arches, columns and mosaic bands, steam drifting in warm light, calm reflections, honey-colored stone

cards.name: Sunroom
cards.aka: sun porch, garden room, Florida room
cards.desc: A room with windows on almost every side, built to soak up daylight and look out at a garden. Airy and relaxed, usually with light furniture and plants.
cards.phrase: a bright sunroom with white-framed windows on three sides, rattan armchairs, potted ferns, sunlight patches on a honey wood floor, a green garden all around

cards.name: Cloister
cards.desc: A covered walkway with arches running around all four sides of a garden, traditionally in a monastery. Quiet, rhythmic and contemplative.
cards.phrase: looking out from a shaded stone cloister, round arches framing a square garden, a small fountain where paths cross, terracotta roof beyond, quiet golden afternoon light

cards.name: Interior courtyard
cards.desc: An open-air space in the middle of a building, with rooms and galleries all around and the sky as the ceiling. Private, shady and often cooled by water and trees.
cards.phrase: a sunlit interior courtyard open to the sky, arched two-storey galleries, a tiled fountain at the center, orange trees, patterned floor tiles, cool shade and bright blue sky

cards.name: Rotunda
cards.desc: A circular room crowned by a dome, often ringed with columns. It feels ceremonial and centered, as if everything points to the middle.
cards.phrase: a grand marble rotunda, a ring of pale columns under a coffered dome, sunlight falling from a round opening onto a patterned circular floor, hushed and symmetrical

cards.name: Grand staircase hall
cards.desc: An entrance hall built around a ceremonial staircase, often one flight that splits into two. Made for making an entrance.
cards.phrase: a grand imperial staircase hall, a wide marble stair splitting into two curving flights, a red carpet runner, carved balustrades, an arched upper gallery, a glowing crystal chandelier

cards.name: Double-height ceiling
cards.desc: A room that rises through two floors with no ceiling in between, often beside a part of the house that does have two levels. It feels open, airy and dramatic.
cards.phrase: a double-height living room, ceiling two storeys up, very tall windows, an upper landing looking down into the space, a long pendant light, warm afternoon light

cards.name: Clerestory windows
cards.desc: A band of windows set high on a wall, above eye level, often just under the roof. They let light pour in from above while keeping the walls private and free for furniture.
cards.phrase: a calm room lit by a continuous band of clerestory windows just under the ceiling, sunbeams slanting down across a plain plaster wall, solid lower walls

cards.name: Oculus / skylight
cards.desc: A round opening at the top of a dome or roof (oculus means "eye"), or more broadly a window in the roof. It throws a single shaft or disc of light onto the floor.
cards.phrase: a dark domed interior with a round oculus at the top, a single shaft of sunlight falling through the air, a bright disc of light on the stone floor

cards.name: Colonnade
cards.desc: A row of columns, usually carrying a beam or roof, running along a building or around a square. It sets up a strong rhythm of light and shadow.
cards.phrase: a long classical colonnade of pale stone columns receding into the distance, strong diagonal shadows striping the walkway, bright sun, deep blue sky

cards.name: Arcade
cards.aka: arcaded walkway, loggia, portico of arches
cards.desc: A row of arches carried on columns or piers, often forming a covered walkway along a street or courtyard. Like a colonnade, but with arches instead of a straight beam.
cards.phrase: a sunlit stone arcade, a row of round arches on slender piers, deep shade behind, warm ochre walls, arch-shaped pools of light on the pavement

cards.name: Cantilever
cards.desc: A part of a building that sticks far out into the air, supported only at one end. It looks daring and weightless, as if it is floating.
cards.phrase: a modern house with a long cantilevered volume jutting out over a cliff edge, nothing supporting it below, warm glowing windows, a deep shadow underneath, wide sky

cards.name: Spiral staircase
cards.desc: A staircase that winds round and round a central post, each step a wedge. It saves space and looks sculptural, especially from below or above.
cards.phrase: a sculptural spiral staircase of warm oak treads curling around a slim brass pole, a continuous curved handrail, light from above, dark concrete walls

cards.name: Mezzanine
cards.aka: mezzanine floor, gallery level, loft deck
cards.desc: A partial floor halfway up a tall room, open to the space below on one side. Often used as a study or bedroom above a living area.
cards.phrase: a loft apartment with a warm timber mezzanine over half the room, a slim railing, an open stair leading up, tall windows lighting the double-height space beside it

cards.name: Coffered / vaulted ceiling
cards.aka: coffers, caissons, barrel vault, groin vault
cards.desc: A coffered ceiling is divided into a grid of sunken panels; a vaulted ceiling is curved like an arch. Both make a room feel crafted and important.
cards.phrase: looking up at a deep coffered ceiling, a grid of recessed square panels with gilded edges and warm shadows, receding toward the far wall, classical and rich

cards.name: Bay window
cards.aka: oriel (if on an upper floor), box bay
cards.desc: A window that pushes out from the wall in three angled panes, making a little bump of room with views in three directions. Charming and bright.
cards.phrase: a Victorian house with a three-sided bay window projecting from a brick facade, white painted frames, warm lamplight glowing inside, a small slate roof above

cards.name: Moon gate
cards.desc: A perfectly circular opening in a garden wall, a classic of Chinese gardens. It frames the garden beyond like a painting and invites you to step through.
cards.phrase: a circular moon gate in a whitewashed garden wall with dark tile coping, framing bamboo, a red maple and a winding stone path beyond, soft misty light

cards.name: Pilotis
cards.desc: Pilotis are thin columns that lift a building off the ground, leaving open space underneath. A signature of modernism: the house seems to hover above the lawn.
cards.phrase: a white modernist house raised on slender pilotis, thin round columns lifting the box above a green lawn, deep cool shadow beneath, long ribbon windows, clear sky

cards.name: Brise-soleil
cards.desc: A grid of fixed fins or louvers on the outside of a building that blocks harsh sun (the name means "sun-breaker" in French). It makes facades deep, rhythmic and full of shadow.
cards.phrase: a concrete facade covered in a deep brise-soleil grid, crisp horizontal and vertical fins casting sharp geometric shadows over recessed dark windows, hot bright sun

cards.name: Mashrabiya screen
cards.aka: mashrabiya, jali (South Asian stone version), lattice screen
cards.desc: A carved or turned-wood lattice screen over a window, from Middle Eastern and North African architecture. It lets in breeze and filtered light while keeping the inside private.
cards.phrase: a dark room with a carved wooden mashrabiya lattice screen over the window, warm sunlight glowing through the delicate pattern, dappled light spilling across the floor

cards.name: Floor-to-ceiling glazing
cards.aka: window wall, curtain wall, glass wall
cards.desc: A whole wall of glass running from the floor right up to the ceiling. The view outside becomes part of the room.
cards.phrase: a minimalist living room with floor-to-ceiling glazing, slim black frames, a wide view of mountains and a lake, soft reflections on the glass, pale light on concrete

cards.name: Dormer windows
cards.desc: Small windows that poke out of a sloping roof, each with its own little roof. They bring light and headroom into the attic and give a house a storybook look.
cards.phrase: a pitched slate roof with three white gabled dormer windows glowing warmly, neat trim, a brick chimney, soft evening sky behind

cards.name: French formal parterre
cards.aka: jardin à la française, broderie parterre
cards.desc: A grand, flat, perfectly symmetrical garden laid out like a carpet in front of a palace. Low clipped box hedges trace swirling patterns over colored gravel, and long straight axes run to the horizon.
cards.phrase: French formal parterre seen from a palace terrace, low clipped box hedges in swirling scroll patterns, raked pale gravel, cone topiaries, round stone fountain basin, perfect symmetry to the horizon

cards.name: English landscape garden
cards.desc: An idealized, painterly countryside made on purpose: rolling lawns that run right up to the house, a curving lake, clumps of big trees and a little classical temple placed as a view-stopper. It looks natural but every curve was designed.
cards.phrase: English landscape garden, rolling green lawn sloping to a curving serpentine lake, clumps of ancient oaks and beeches, small domed classical temple on the far bank, soft hazy afternoon light

cards.name: Japanese dry garden (karesansui)
cards.desc: A walled rectangle of raked white gravel with a few carefully placed rocks and moss. The gravel stands for water and the rocks for islands or mountains; it is made to be looked at quietly from a veranda, not walked through.
cards.phrase: Japanese dry rock garden, raked white gravel in fine parallel lines rippling around mossy weathered stones, low ochre clay wall with grey tile coping, pine branch above, still overcast light

cards.name: Japanese stroll and moss garden
cards.desc: A garden you walk around a pond, with views that change at every turn: a curved bridge, a stone lantern, stepping stones across thick moss and maples that flare red in autumn. It feels intimate, green and hushed.
cards.phrase: Japanese stroll garden around a still pond, thick velvet moss, irregular stepping stones, granite lantern, red arched drum bridge, flaming red maple leaves, soft dappled light

cards.name: Chinese scholar's garden
cards.desc: A walled, intimate garden made to feel like a whole landscape in miniature. White walls frame views through moon gates and lattice windows, pierced limestone rocks stand like mountains, and pavilions with upswept roofs sit beside lotus ponds.
cards.phrase: Chinese scholar's garden, white plaster wall with a round moon gate framing bamboo, pierced grey limestone rock, pavilion with upswept dark tile roof and red columns over a lotus pond

cards.name: Mughal charbagh
cards.desc: A walled garden split into four equal parts by two crossing water channels, with a pool or fountain at the center. It reads as a calm, ordered paradise: shaded, symmetrical and full of the sound of running water.
cards.phrase: Mughal charbagh garden, long narrow water channels crossing at a square pool, small fountain jets, raised red sandstone walks, lines of dark cypress, white marble domed pavilion beyond, warm haze

cards.name: Italian Renaissance terraced garden
cards.desc: A hillside garden cut into level terraces, linked by grand stairs and held up by stone walls with balustrades. Fountains, statues, cypresses and clipped hedges line a strong central axis climbing to the villa.
cards.phrase: Italian Renaissance terraced garden on a hillside, stone balustrades and wide stairs climbing to an ochre villa, rows of slim dark cypress, umbrella pines, stone fountain, golden Tuscan light

cards.name: English cottage garden
cards.desc: A small, overflowing garden around a modest house, where flowers, herbs and roses crowd together with no bare soil showing. It feels romantic, cheerful and a little untidy on purpose.
cards.phrase: English cottage garden overflowing with foxgloves, hollyhocks and delphiniums, roses climbing a limewashed cottage with thatched roof, narrow brick path, white picket fence, soft summer light

cards.name: Mediterranean courtyard garden
cards.desc: An outdoor room enclosed by sun-bleached white walls, cooled by a small tiled fountain and shade. Terracotta pots, citrus trees and a spill of bougainvillea bring color against the white.
cards.phrase: sunlit Mediterranean courtyard, whitewashed walls, terracotta tile floor, small fountain clad in blue and yellow tiles, potted lemon tree and red geraniums, bougainvillea spilling over, blue arched door

cards.name: Desert xeriscape
cards.desc: A garden designed to need almost no watering, made of gravel, boulders and sculptural desert plants. It looks spare and graphic, with strong shadows and sculptural silhouettes against warm stone.
cards.phrase: desert xeriscape garden, tan gravel and flagstone path, blue-grey agaves, golden barrel cacti, spindly ocotillo, rust-colored boulders, crisp shadows under a clear sky, distant mesa

cards.name: New Perennial meadow planting
cards.desc: Big, loose drifts of grasses and long-lived flowers planted to look like a wild meadow, but chosen for structure all year. Seedheads are left standing, so it looks good in autumn and winter too.
cards.phrase: naturalistic meadow planting, drifts of feathery ornamental grasses, purple salvia spikes and pink coneflowers, dark seedheads, low golden evening backlight glowing through the grass

cards.name: Topiary & hedge maze
cards.desc: Evergreen hedges clipped into crisp walls, spirals, balls and cones. A maze uses tall hedges to make corridors you can get lost in; topiary turns shrubs into green sculpture.
cards.phrase: hedge maze seen from above at an angle, tall clipped dark green yew walls with crisp flat tops, narrow pale gravel corridors, spiral topiaries at the corners, long late-day shadows

cards.name: Picturesque ruin & folly
cards.desc: A deliberately ruined-looking building, often a gothic arch or broken tower, placed in a park as a romantic eye-catcher. It is about mood: melancholy, age and nature reclaiming stone.
cards.phrase: romantic garden folly, roofless gothic stone ruin with pointed window arches and ivy, fallen blocks in long grass, reflected in a still lake, brooding grey-gold sky

cards.name: Kitchen potager
cards.desc: A vegetable garden laid out as handsomely as a flower garden, with neat geometric beds, edging, paths and climbing frames. Cabbages, lettuces and beans become patterns of color and texture.
cards.phrase: ornamental kitchen potager, geometric beds edged in clipped box, rows of blue-green cabbages and red lettuces, bean teepees, worn brick paths, glass cloche, espaliered pears on a warm brick wall

cards.name: Piazza
cards.desc: An open paved square at the heart of a town, ringed by buildings with shaded arcades, often with a fountain and a bell tower. It is a place to linger, meet and people-watch.
cards.phrase: sunlit Italian piazza, fan-patterned brick paving, ochre and terracotta facades with a shaded ground-floor arcade, stone fountain at the center, brick bell tower, strolling people

cards.name: Waterfront promenade / boardwalk
cards.desc: A long walkway along the sea or a lake, made for strolling, with railings, lamp posts and benches facing the water. It feels breezy, open and holiday-like.
cards.phrase: seaside boardwalk promenade, weathered timber planks receding along white railings, ornate double lamp posts, benches facing a bright blue sea, sailboat on the horizon, breezy midday light

cards.name: Covered market hall
cards.desc: A big shed of iron columns and glass roof covering rows of food stalls, with a bright gable end letting light pour in. It is busy, colorful and full of produce.
cards.phrase: bustling covered market hall, green cast-iron columns and trusses under a glass roof, fan-shaped gable window, rows of stalls with red and white striped awnings piled with fruit

cards.name: Glass-roofed shopping arcade (galleria)
cards.desc: A grand indoor street lined with shopfronts and covered by an arched glass and iron roof. Ornate stone facades, mosaic floors and soft daylight make it feel like a palace for walking.
cards.phrase: grand nineteenth-century shopping galleria, arched glass and iron barrel-vault roof, ornate cream stone facades with glowing shopfronts, polished mosaic floor, soft daylight from above

cards.name: Railway station concourse
cards.desc: The vast arched hall of a big railway terminus, where iron ribs span the platforms and a huge glazed end screen lets light flood in. It feels busy, echoing and full of anticipation.
cards.phrase: vast railway station concourse, arched iron ribs and glass roof, radiating glazed end wall, hanging station clock, train at the platform, shafts of light through haze, hurrying travelers

cards.name: Victorian palm house
cards.desc: A large curving glasshouse of white-painted iron, built to keep tropical palms warm. From outside it glows like a bubble; inside it is humid, green and dappled.
cards.phrase: Victorian palm house, curving white iron and glass dome with lower wings, tall palms glimpsed through misty glass, formal bedding and lawn in front, soft overcast daylight

cards.name: Lighthouse & keeper's cottage
cards.desc: A tall white tower with a glass lantern on top, standing on a rocky point beside a small whitewashed house. It is lonely, sturdy and weather-beaten.
cards.phrase: white lighthouse with red bands and glass lantern on a rocky headland, small whitewashed keeper’s cottage with slate roof, waves breaking on dark rocks, gulls, soft dusk light

cards.name: Lakeside dock & pier
cards.desc: A simple timber jetty running out over calm water, with a painted boathouse and a rowboat tied up. It sets a quiet, summery cabin-at-the-lake mood.
cards.phrase: timber lakeside pier running into still water, wooden rowboat tied alongside, red boathouse on the shore, dark pine forest and snow-dusted mountains, mirror reflections, calm morning light

cards.name: Stone arch bridge
cards.desc: A bridge of cut stone spanning a river on round arches, whose reflections close into full circles in still water. It feels old, solid and timeless.
cards.phrase: old stone arch bridge over a calm river, three round arches with wedge-shaped voussoirs reflected into circles, low parapet with walkers, leafy riverbanks, warm afternoon light

cards.name: Suspension bridge
cards.desc: A long road deck hung from huge cables that swoop between tall towers. It feels heroic and elegant, especially in fog or at sunset.
cards.phrase: long suspension bridge at sunset, two tall rust-red towers, main cables sweeping in deep curves with fine vertical hangers, slim deck with tiny headlights, glowing water below

cards.name: Amphitheater
cards.desc: Curved tiers of stone seats stepping up around a stage, often cut into a hillside with a view behind. It is built so everyone can see and hear, and it frames a performance against the landscape.
cards.phrase: ancient open-air amphitheater, semicircular tiers of pale weathered stone seats with radial stair aisles, round orchestra and low stage, cypress trees and blue sea beyond, raking sunlight

cards.name: Rooftop garden terrace
cards.desc: A garden on a city roof: timber decking, planters of grasses and shrubs, a pergola and string lights, with the skyline all around. It feels like a secret green retreat above the streets.
cards.phrase: city rooftop garden terrace at dusk, warm timber deck, dark planters of ornamental grasses, pergola with climbing vines, glowing string lights, lounge chairs, skyline with lit windows

cards.name: Lido / outdoor pool
cards.desc: A public outdoor pool with a crisp white pavilion, often Art Deco, surrounded by sunbathing terraces. It is bright, cheerful and summery, all turquoise water and white walls.
cards.phrase: Art Deco lido, long turquoise outdoor pool with rippling light and lane lines, crisp white streamlined pavilion with blue and coral stripes, diving board, striped umbrellas, bright summer sun

cards.name: Forced perspective
cards.desc: A set built smaller and steeper toward the back, so a short street or hallway looks long and deep. Doors and windows shrink faster than they would in life, which makes anyone standing at the back look oddly huge.
cards.phrase: forced perspective film set, a short street of facades that shrink sharply toward a vanishing point, raked floor, tiny doors at the far end, an actor at the back looking giant

cards.name: Painted backdrop & flats
cards.aka: scenic backdrop, wing and drop, cut-out flats
cards.desc: The classic theatre way to build a world: a big painted canvas at the back and flat cut-out pieces (trees, houses, hedges) standing in layers in front. From the audience it reads as depth; from the wings you see plywood and braces.
cards.phrase: theatre stage of painted backdrop and layered cut-out flats, hand-painted sky and rolling hills on canvas, flat wooden tree and cottage cut-outs, visible braces, warm stage light

cards.name: Proscenium stage set
cards.desc: A room built on a stage behind a big decorative frame (the proscenium arch), with the fourth wall missing so the audience looks in. Red curtains, footlights and a gilded frame make everything feel like a performance.
cards.phrase: view from the audience of a proscenium stage, gilded arch and red velvet curtains framing a three-walled drawing room set, warm footlights, dark silhouettes of heads in the stalls

cards.name: Dollhouse cutaway set
cards.aka: cross-section set, open-front set, cutaway house
cards.desc: A building sliced open so every room faces the camera at once, like a dollhouse. Each room gets its own wallpaper and life, and the camera can track sideways from room to room.
cards.phrase: dollhouse cutaway set, a whole house sliced open to the camera, rooms side by side and stacked, each with different pastel wallpaper and furniture, small figures going about their day, flat frontal view

cards.name: Miniature model set
cards.desc: A whole town, ship or landscape built small on a tabletop and filmed up close. Real materials and real light give it a tactile charm that digital worlds struggle to match.
cards.phrase: handmade miniature model set on a workbench, tiny painted houses and lollipop trees on a grassy base, tweezers placing a tree, shallow depth of field, warm workshop lamp

cards.name: Period set dressing
cards.desc: Furnishing a set so every object belongs to one moment in history: the wallpaper, the lamps, the clock on the mantel. It works when nothing modern sneaks into the frame.
cards.phrase: Victorian parlour period set, dark green damask wallpaper, marble fireplace with gilded mirror, oil lamp glow, wingback armchair, oriental rug, candlesticks on the mantel, warm low light

cards.name: Lived-in production design
cards.aka: naturalistic set, worn set, used-universe look
cards.desc: Rooms dressed to look like someone really lives there: dishes in the sink, notes on the fridge, scuffs and stains. The mess tells you about the people before they say a word.
cards.phrase: lived-in kitchen production design, cluttered open shelves of mismatched jars, notes on the fridge, dishes stacked in the sink, worn linoleum, jacket over a chair, warm pendant light

cards.name: Liminal space
cards.aka: backrooms, empty in-between space, transitional space
cards.desc: An empty, in-between place built for passing through (corridors, waiting rooms, closed malls) shown with nobody there. The flat light and sameness make it feel like a dream or a place you half remember.
cards.phrase: liminal space, an empty office corridor receding into the distance, buzzing fluorescent ceiling panels, yellowed beige walls and mustard carpet, identical closed doors, no people, flat greenish light

cards.name: Abandoned interior
cards.desc: A room left behind for years: paint curling off the walls, plaster fallen, plants creeping in through broken windows. Light shafts through the dust make decay look beautiful.
cards.phrase: abandoned interior, faded green walls with peeling paint and exposed brick, broken arched window, a dusty shaft of light across warped floorboards, vines and ferns growing inside, an overturned chair

cards.name: Infinity cove / cyclorama studio
cards.aka: cyc wall, infinity wall, seamless studio
cards.desc: A studio where the floor curves smoothly up into the wall, so there is no corner and no horizon. Whatever you place there seems to float in a pure, endless space.
cards.phrase: infinity cove studio, seamless white floor curving into the wall with no horizon, a single orange chair in the middle casting a soft shadow, even diffuse light

cards.name: German Expressionist film set
cards.desc: Silent-film sets where walls lean, windows are jagged triangles and light and shadow are painted straight onto the scenery. The whole world looks twisted, as if seen through a troubled mind.
cards.phrase: German Expressionist film set, crooked leaning buildings with jagged triangular windows, zigzag street, light and shadow painted directly on the scenery, stark black and cream, grainy silent film look

cards.name: Symmetrical tableau set
cards.aka: centred composition, storybook symmetry, diorama framing
cards.desc: A set designed to be filmed dead-on from the front, perfectly mirrored left to right, often in a soft candy palette. It feels like a diorama or a page from a picture book.
cards.phrase: perfectly symmetrical tableau set, flat frontal view of a pastel pink hotel facade, mirrored windows, topiary trees and lamps, a single bellboy in red standing dead centre, soft even light

cards.name: Cyberpunk megacity
cards.aka: neon noir city, high tech low life
cards.desc: A crowded, rain-soaked city of towering blocks covered in glowing signs, where advanced tech sits on top of grime. Night, neon and reflections are the whole mood.
cards.phrase: cyberpunk megacity at night, dense dark towers covered in magenta and cyan neon signs, heavy rain, glowing pink haze, wet street reflections, a flying car between buildings

cards.name: Solarpunk city
cards.desc: A hopeful future city where buildings are covered in gardens and powered by sun and wind. Bright, clean and leafy, it pairs high tech with plants and craft.
cards.phrase: solarpunk city, white rounded towers overflowing with garden terraces, solar panel arrays and slim wind turbines, a canal lined with trees, a clean tram, bright sunny sky

cards.name: Space Age retrofuturism
cards.desc: The future as imagined in the 1950s and 60s: flying-saucer towers, boomerang roofs, starbursts and monorails. Optimistic, shiny and full of swooping angles.
cards.phrase: Space Age retrofuturist town, a flying-saucer observation tower on slender legs, a boomerang-roof diner with glass walls, starburst sign, monorail, teal and orange sunset sky

cards.name: Steampunk
cards.desc: A Victorian world where steam power ran wild: brass machinery, riveted copper halls, clock towers and airships. Everything is mechanical, ornate and a little smoky.
cards.phrase: steampunk city, riveted copper halls with glowing portholes, a clock tower, giant brass gears and pipes, an airship overhead, smokestacks puffing into a sepia sky

cards.name: Dieselpunk
cards.desc: A gritty, oil-powered version of the 1920s to 1940s: Art Deco towers, zeppelins, searchlights and heavy industry. Bold, dark and dramatic, like a propaganda poster come to life.
cards.phrase: dieselpunk city at smoggy dusk, stepped Art Deco skyscrapers with brass spires, searchlight beams crossing the sky, a zeppelin, smokestacks and an elevated train

cards.name: Fairy-tale castle
cards.desc: The castle from picture books: white walls, many round towers with pointed blue roofs, flags fluttering on a green hill. It looks more like a dream than a fortress.
cards.phrase: fairy-tale castle on a green hill, white walls and clustered round towers with tall pointed blue roofs, red pennants, arched gate, winding path, soft white clouds

cards.name: Elven / organic fantasy
cards.desc: Graceful buildings that grow out of the forest: slender pale columns curving like branches, leaf-shaped arches, bridges between giant trees. Everything flows and nothing has a hard corner.
cards.phrase: elven fantasy architecture, a pale stone pavilion of slender curving columns and leaf-shaped arches under a seed-pod dome, bridges to giant trees, waterfall mist, golden-green forest light

cards.name: Storybook cottage
cards.aka: storybook style, hobbit-like cottage, fairytale cottage
cards.desc: A small, crooked, cosy house that looks hand-made for a fairy tale: swooping thatched roof, round door, leaning chimney. Nothing is quite straight, and that is the charm.
cards.phrase: storybook cottage, thick swooping thatched roof with rolled eaves, crooked stone chimney puffing smoke, round green door, diamond-pane windows with flower boxes, wildflowers and a picket fence

cards.name: Gothic horror mansion
cards.desc: A tall, dark house on a hill with steep roofs, a pointed tower and iron spikes, one window glowing. Moonlight, bare trees and fog do the rest.
cards.phrase: Gothic horror mansion at night, steep mansard roof and pointed tower silhouetted against a huge full moon, one window glowing yellow, bare twisted tree, iron fence, low fog

cards.name: Post-apocalyptic ruin
cards.desc: A city after the end: broken towers with jagged tops, rubble and rusted cars, plants taking back the streets. Dust or orange haze hangs over everything.
cards.phrase: post-apocalyptic ruined city, jagged broken skyscrapers with empty windows, collapsed bridge, rubble and a rusted car, weeds reclaiming the street, thick orange dust haze, pale sun

cards.name: Arcology / megastructure
cards.desc: An entire city packed into one colossal building, rising in terraces with homes, farms and streets inside. Its sheer size is the point, so show something tiny beside it.
cards.phrase: arcology megastructure, an enormous stepped pyramid city rising from the desert, endless rows of windows and planted terraces, atmospheric haze at its base, tiny houses for scale

cards.name: Floating sky city
cards.desc: A city built on a chunk of land floating in the sky, with roots and waterfalls hanging off the bottom and clouds below. Domes and spires on top make it feel heavenly.
cards.phrase: floating sky city on a rocky island above a sea of clouds, white towers with golden domes and spires, hanging roots and a waterfall spilling off the edge, small airships

cards.name: Underwater habitat
cards.desc: Glass domes on the sea floor linked by tubes, glowing warm against the deep blue. Light rays from above, fish drifting past and kelp swaying make it feel calm and remote.
cards.phrase: underwater habitat, ribbed glass domes on the sea floor linked by tubes, warm glowing windows inside, deep blue water with light rays from above, kelp and fish, rising bubbles

cards.name: Sci-fi desert settlement
cards.desc: A sun-baked outpost on an alien desert: low domed adobe homes, slender machinery towers and sand everywhere, sometimes under two suns. Simple shapes and heat haze sell it.
cards.phrase: sci-fi desert settlement, smooth domed adobe dwellings around a sunken courtyard, slim metal moisture towers, rolling sand dunes, twin suns in a pale hot sky, a small hover vehicle

cards.name: Giovanni Battista Piranesi
cards.desc: An etcher who drew impossible interiors: vast vaulted dungeons with stairs and bridges going everywhere, and Roman ruins blown up to a superhuman scale. Everything is dark, crosshatched and dizzying, with tiny people lost in the gloom.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Giovanni Battista Piranesi: an imaginary vaulted underground hall, colossal stone arches, crisscrossing stairways and wooden bridges, hanging chains, deep crosshatched shadows, beams of light, tiny figures, sepia etching

cards.name: Étienne-Louis Boullée
cards.desc: A French architect famous for buildings that were mostly never built: gigantic spheres, cones and pyramids rendered with solemn, theatrical light. He wanted architecture to feel sublime, like standing before a mountain or the night sky.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Étienne-Louis Boullée: a new visionary monument, a colossal smooth stone sphere on a stepped circular plinth, ringed by dark cypresses, tiny human figures, solemn raking light, pale misty sky

cards.name: Antoni Gaudí
cards.desc: Buildings that seem grown rather than built: walls ripple, columns lean like tree trunks or bones, and roofs shimmer with broken-tile mosaic. Almost nothing is a straight line, and color and nature are everywhere.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Antoni Gaudí: a new apartment building with a rippling sandstone facade studded with blue and green broken-tile mosaic, bone-like columns, mask-shaped balconies, a scaly glazed roof and twisted mosaic chimneys

cards.name: Charles Rennie Mackintosh
cards.desc: Scottish architect and designer who mixed sturdy Scottish castle shapes with a delicate, elegant interior world: white rooms, tall ladder-backed chairs, and stylized pink roses. Outside, plain white walls; inside, light and lyrical.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Charles Rennie Mackintosh: a new white roughcast house with a steep slate roof, a round stair tower, tall narrow small-paned windows, black lattice gates and stylized pink and purple rose motifs

cards.name: Edwin Lutyens
cards.desc: The great English country house architect: big sheltering roofs, warm brick and stone, tall chimneys, and gardens laid out as outdoor rooms. Later he did grand, clean classical work, but always with a sense of craft and wit.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Edwin Lutyens: a new English country house with a vast sweeping clay-tile roof, tall brick chimneys, warm red brick with pale stone dressings, small-paned windows, terraces, yew hedges and a stone rill

cards.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
cards.desc: American architect whose houses hug the ground: long low lines, roofs that reach far out past the walls, and rooms that flow around a big central fireplace. Materials are earthy and the building feels tied to its landscape.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Frank Lloyd Wright: a new long low house hugging a lawn, deep cantilevered eaves, bands of geometric art-glass windows, thin tan Roman brick, a central chimney mass, stone planters, warm earthy palette

cards.name: Eileen Gray
cards.aka: early modernism, lacquer and furniture design
cards.desc: Irish designer and architect who made modernism feel human: a crisp white villa by the sea, but with canvas awnings, folding screens and clever furniture that makes it pleasant to live in. Light, airy and personal.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Eileen Gray: a new small white seaside villa raised on slim pilotis above rocks, strip windows, a terrace with tubular railings, a striped canvas sail awning, deep blue Mediterranean sea

cards.name: Le Corbusier
cards.aka: Charles-Édouard Jeanneret, béton brut, International Style
cards.desc: The most influential modernist: first pure white villas on stilts, then massive raw-concrete blocks with deep sunshades and bright painted panels. Bold, sculptural and built around his rules for modern living.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Le Corbusier: a new raw board-marked concrete housing slab on chunky tapered pilotis, a deep egg-crate grid of sunshades, some balconies painted red, yellow and blue, sculptural rooftop forms

cards.name: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
cards.desc: Calm, precise boxes of steel and glass where every joint is perfect and nothing extra is added. Walls become freestanding planes of marble, the roof floats on a few thin columns, and space flows from inside to out.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Ludwig Mies van der Rohe: a new glass pavilion on a travertine plinth, a thin floating white roof slab, slender chrome columns, a freestanding green marble wall, a still black reflecting pool

cards.name: Hugh Ferriss
cards.desc: An architectural illustrator rather than a builder: his moody charcoal drawings of stepped skyscrapers looming in fog and searchlight beams defined how the 1920s imagined the future city (and later inspired Gotham).
cards.phrase: in the manner of Hugh Ferriss: a new colossal stepped setback skyscraper at night, rendered in soft charcoal, searchlight beams rising from the fog, deep black shadows, glowing mist at street level, monochrome

cards.name: Alvar Aalto
cards.desc: Finnish architect who made modernism warm: waving wood ceilings, bentwood furniture, white walls with red brick, and soft daylight from round skylights. His buildings feel calm, natural and kind to people.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Alvar Aalto: a new bright Nordic reading room with an undulating pine slat ceiling, round skylights, white walls, bent birch plywood chairs, a big window onto birches and a lake

cards.name: Luis Barragán
cards.desc: Mexican architect of silence and color: big plain walls painted hot pink, yellow and purple, still pools, a thin stream of water, and sky. Very few elements, arranged to feel peaceful and almost spiritual.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Luis Barragán: a new quiet courtyard of tall plain stucco walls in hot pink, saffron yellow and violet, a long still water trough fed by a single spout, crisp shadows, deep blue sky

cards.name: Oscar Niemeyer
cards.desc: Brazilian architect of the curve: brilliant white concrete shaped into saucers, domes, waves and sweeping ramps, set beside water and tropical sky. Light, sensual and optimistic.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Oscar Niemeyer: a new white concrete pavilion shaped like a shallow bowl on a slender stem, a sweeping curved ramp, rows of parabolic arches, reflecting pool, bright tropical blue sky

cards.name: Eero Saarinen
cards.desc: Finnish-American architect and designer of swooping forms: concrete shells shaped like wings, soaring arches and pedestal furniture. Every project looks different, but all feel like the optimistic jet age.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Eero Saarinen: a new jet-age terminal with a vast swooping white concrete shell roof like spread wings, Y-shaped piers, a sweeping glass wall, warm sunset light

cards.name: Louis Kahn
cards.desc: American architect of massive, silent buildings in brick and concrete, cut with giant circles, triangles and slots that bring in light. Ancient in feeling, like modern ruins, with water and sky treated as materials.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Louis Kahn: a new monumental red brick building with giant circular and triangular openings, concrete bands, deep shadowed voids, a travertine plaza with a narrow water channel

cards.name: Carlo Scarpa
cards.desc: Venetian architect who treated concrete like jewelry: stepped edges, interlocking circles, water channels, brass and gold mosaic inserted with a craftsman's care. Every joint and threshold is a small event.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Carlo Scarpa: a new garden wall of grey concrete with stepped ziggurat edges, a pair of interlocking circular openings rimmed in gold mosaic and teal, a shallow water pool, brass details, dark cypresses

cards.name: John Lautner
cards.desc: Los Angeles architect of dramatic hillside houses: great curving concrete roofs, walls of glass and cantilevers flying over the city. They feel like spaceships and caves at the same time.
cards.phrase: in the manner of John Lautner: a new hillside house with a vast curved concrete roof cantilevering on one pedestal, a wraparound glass wall glowing warm, city lights spread below at dusk

cards.name: Geoffrey Bawa
cards.desc: Sri Lankan architect who blended modern simplicity with local roofs, courtyards and gardens. Buildings dissolve into the jungle: deep verandas, big clay-tile roofs and water that runs into lakes.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Geoffrey Bawa: a new low tropical house with a big clay-tile roof on slender white columns, a deep open veranda, a pool merging into a lake, frangipani and palms, soft humid light

cards.name: Lina Bo Bardi
cards.desc: Italian-Brazilian architect who mixed rough concrete with folk warmth: towers punched with irregular cloud-shaped windows, concrete walkways flying between buildings, and lots of plants and everyday life.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Lina Bo Bardi: a new community center of raw board-marked concrete towers with irregular cloud-shaped windows in red lattice, concrete bridges between towers, plants on top, an old brick hall

cards.name: Ricardo Bofill
cards.desc: Catalan architect whose early housing looks like a vivid, maze-like citadel of stacked towers and stairs, and whose later work turned prefab concrete into giant classical palaces. Theatrical and photogenic.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Ricardo Bofill: a new hillside housing citadel of interlocking stucco towers in red and pink, courtyards painted blue and violet, zigzag stairways, cross-shaped parapets, bright Mediterranean sun

cards.name: Friedensreich Hundertwasser
cards.desc: Austrian painter turned architect who hated straight lines: patchwork facades, wobbly floors, every window different, gold onion domes and trees growing out of windows and roofs. Joyful, childlike and green.
