cards.phrase: in the manner of Friedensreich Hundertwasser: a new apartment block with a patchwork facade of bright colors, wavy floor lines, mismatched windows, trees growing from windows, a grassy roof and a golden onion dome

cards.name: Zaha Hadid
cards.desc: Iraqi-British architect of motion: buildings that look like they are flowing, stretching or about to take off, with sharp tips, long streamlined curves and no right angles. Bold, futuristic and sculptural.
cards.phrase: in the manner of Zaha Hadid: a new cultural center of flowing white surfaces sweeping into a sharp cantilevered tip, dark glass bands following the curves, a plaza of converging lines, no right angles

cards.name: Wordmark
cards.desc: The full name set in a specific, often customized, typeface, with no symbol. The name is the logo, so it has to be short enough and distinctive enough to carry the brand alone.
cards.phrase: a wordmark logo: the full brand name in one carefully drawn typeface, no symbol, with one small custom detail in the letterforms

cards.name: Lettermark
cards.desc: Initials or an acronym set as the logo, usually for a name too long to say. It works once people already know what the letters stand for.
cards.phrase: a lettermark logo built from the brand's initials, bold and tightly spaced, readable as a single shape

cards.name: Monogram
cards.desc: Two or three letters woven, overlapped or joined into one ornamental figure. Older and more decorative than a lettermark; it reads as a seal of ownership.
cards.phrase: a monogram: two initials interlocked into one balanced figure, elegant high-contrast serif letters with a shared stroke

cards.name: Pictorial mark
cards.aka: brand mark, logo symbol, iconic mark
cards.desc: A recognizable picture of a real thing (an animal, a tree, a tool) simplified into a symbol. The picture can be literal or a step removed from what the company does.
cards.phrase: a pictorial mark: one recognizable object simplified to a few flat shapes, readable as a silhouette

cards.name: Abstract mark
cards.desc: A non-representational shape that stands for the brand through meaning the company assigns to it. It can say "motion" or "connection" without picturing anything literal.
cards.phrase: an abstract mark: a simple geometric shape that suggests the brand's idea without depicting anything literal, bold and memorable at small sizes

cards.name: Combination mark
cards.desc: A symbol and a wordmark designed to sit together, side by side or stacked. The two can also be used apart once the symbol is known.
cards.phrase: a combination mark: a simple symbol paired with a wordmark, drawn with matching stroke weight and proportions so they read as one unit

cards.name: Emblem
cards.desc: The name sits inside a shape (a circle, shield or badge) and can't be separated from it. Feels official, traditional or crafted.
cards.phrase: an emblem logo: the name set inside a circular badge with a double border, a small central illustration and a founding year

cards.name: Mascot
cards.desc: An illustrated character that represents the brand and can act, pose and talk. It gives the brand a face and a personality people get attached to.
cards.phrase: a mascot logo: a friendly, simple cartoon character with a clear silhouette, big readable features and two or three flat colors

cards.name: Dynamic identity
cards.aka: flexible logo, generative identity, variable mark
cards.desc: A logo that changes on purpose, by color, content or shape, while a fixed frame keeps it recognizable. The rules for change are the brand.
cards.phrase: a dynamic identity: one fixed frame and typeface with contents that change for each use (color, pattern or image), designed as a system of variations

cards.name: Crest
cards.aka: coat of arms, heraldic logo, shield
cards.desc: A shield with heraldic parts (a chevron, a beast, a motto ribbon) borrowed from coats of arms. Signals lineage, rank and permanence.
cards.phrase: a crest logo: a simplified heraldic shield with one charge and a chevron, a motto ribbon underneath, in two flat colors

cards.name: Signature mark
cards.desc: The logo is a name written by hand, as if signed. Personal and intimate; it promises a real person behind the work.
cards.phrase: a signature-style logo: the name written as a confident handwritten signature, smooth connected strokes, legible, with a single underline flourish

cards.name: Letter in a shape
cards.desc: A single letter set inside a solid container such as a circle, square or rounded tile. Compact and easy to use as an app icon or avatar.
cards.phrase: a single custom letter set inside a solid circle, the letter knocked out in the background color, simple enough for an app icon

cards.name: Symbol inside the type
cards.desc: A picture or shape is built into one letter of the wordmark, replacing a counter or a stroke. One logo does the work of a combination mark.
cards.phrase: a wordmark with a small symbol built into one letter, replacing its counter or dot, so the picture is discovered rather than added

cards.name: Horizontal lockup
cards.desc: Symbol on the left, name on the right, aligned to a shared center line or cap height. The default for headers, signs and anything wide.
cards.phrase: a horizontal lockup: symbol on the left and the name on the right, vertically centered, with a fixed gap equal to half the symbol width

cards.name: Stacked lockup
cards.desc: Symbol centered above the name. Taller and more formal; fits square and portrait spaces where a wide logo would shrink too far.
cards.phrase: a stacked lockup: symbol centered above the brand name, the name about as wide as the symbol is tall

cards.name: Responsive logo
cards.aka: logo system by size, adaptive logo
cards.desc: A set of versions that drop detail as space shrinks: full lockup with tagline, then name and symbol, then a short form, then the symbol alone.
cards.phrase: a responsive logo system in four sizes: full lockup with tagline, horizontal lockup, compact symbol with initials, symbol only

cards.name: Clear space
cards.aka: exclusion zone, safe area, breathing room
cards.desc: The minimum empty margin around the logo, measured in a unit taken from the logo itself (often the height of one letter). Nothing else may enter it.
cards.phrase: show the logo with its clear-space rule: a margin on all sides equal to the cap height of the wordmark, marked x

cards.name: Minimum size
cards.desc: The smallest the logo may appear, given in pixels for screens and millimeters for print. Below it, a simpler version takes over.
cards.phrase: specify a minimum size for the logo (for example 24px wide on screen, 12mm in print) and a simplified version for anything smaller

cards.name: Reversed logo
cards.desc: The logo in the background color on a solid dark or brand-colored field. Every mark needs a reversed and a one-color version as well as the full-color one.
cards.phrase: provide positive, reversed (knocked out of a solid dark field) and single-color versions of the logo

cards.name: Tagline lockup
cards.desc: The logo with a short line of text (a tagline or a descriptor) fixed in position and size. It is drawn once and never retyped.
cards.phrase: a lockup of the logo with a short tagline set in small tracked capitals beneath the name, aligned to its left edge

cards.name: App icon
cards.desc: The symbol redrawn to fill a rounded square tile at a fixed grid, with a background color. The platform crops the corners.
cards.phrase: an app icon: the symbol centered on a rounded-square tile in the brand color, simple flat shapes, readable at 29px

cards.name: Favicon
cards.desc: The tiny icon in a browser tab, often only 16 by 16 pixels. Usually a simplified symbol or a single letter, drawn for pixels.
cards.phrase: a favicon: the symbol simplified for a 16×16 pixel grid, solid shapes, high contrast against light and dark tabs

cards.name: Social avatar
cards.desc: The symbol placed for a circular crop on social profiles and chat apps, with padding so nothing touches the edge.
cards.phrase: a social avatar: the symbol centered in a circle with generous padding, solid brand-color background, nothing near the edge

cards.name: Co-brand lockup
cards.desc: Two logos shown together for a partnership, separated by a thin rule or an ×, sized to look equal in weight rather than equal in width.
cards.phrase: a co-brand lockup: two logos side by side separated by a thin vertical rule, optically balanced in size, sharing one baseline

cards.name: Animated logo
cards.aka: logo animation, motion mark, logo sting
cards.desc: A short sequence (one to three seconds) where the mark builds, morphs or reveals itself. Used at the start or end of videos and on app launch.
cards.phrase: an animated logo sting under two seconds: the symbol builds from simple shapes in three beats, ending on the static logo

cards.name: Geometric mark
cards.desc: Built from a few pure shapes: circles, squares, triangles and the arcs between them. Nothing is drawn freehand, so the mark looks deliberate and stays crisp from favicon to building sign.
cards.phrase: a geometric mark built only from circles, squares and quarter-circle arcs, flat fills, no freehand curves

cards.name: Circle-constructed
cards.aka: golden ratio logo, construction grid, Fibonacci circles
cards.desc: Every curve in the mark is a slice of a guide circle, often sized by the golden ratio. The construction drawing is shown in the guidelines as proof the curves were planned.
cards.phrase: a mark constructed from overlapping guide circles, every curve an arc of one circle, with the construction grid shown

cards.name: Monoline
cards.desc: Drawn with one stroke weight throughout, usually with rounded ends. It reads as friendly and modern, and pairs naturally with icon sets drawn the same way.
cards.phrase: a monoline mark drawn with a single consistent stroke weight and rounded line ends, no fills

cards.name: Negative space
cards.desc: A second image hides in the gap between shapes, so the background becomes part of the drawing. When it works people remember it because they discovered it themselves.
cards.phrase: a negative space mark where the gap between solid shapes forms a second image

cards.name: Overlapping shapes
cards.desc: Translucent shapes cross over each other and create new colors where they meet. It suggests collaboration, blending or many parts making one whole.
cards.phrase: a mark of translucent overlapping shapes that create new tints where they intersect, with a one-color fallback

cards.name: Modular grid
cards.desc: Assembled from one repeated module, such as a square and a quarter circle, placed on a strict grid. The same kit can spell other letters or patterns, so the mark grows into a system.
cards.phrase: a modular mark built from a repeating kit of squares and quarter circles on a strict grid

cards.name: Isometric
cards.desc: Flat faces drawn on a 30-degree grid so the mark reads as a solid object without any shading tricks. Cubes, stacked blocks and folded boxes are the usual subjects.
cards.phrase: an isometric mark drawn on a 30-degree grid, three flat faces in three tones, no gradients

cards.name: Dot matrix
cards.aka: pixel mark, LED grid, bitmap logo
cards.desc: Letters or shapes spelled in a grid of dots or square pixels, like a departure board or an old printer. It feels technical and a little nostalgic.
cards.phrase: a dot-matrix mark with the letter formed by filled dots on a visible grid of empty dots

cards.name: Ribbon & fold
cards.aka: continuous band, impossible figure, woven loop
cards.desc: A single band loops, folds or weaves over itself, sometimes into a shape that could not exist in three dimensions. It implies flow, connection and an unbroken process.
cards.phrase: a ribbon mark: one continuous band that loops and weaves over itself, with clear over-under crossings

cards.name: Fine line art
cards.desc: A small, detailed drawing in hairline strokes, often botanical, inside a circle or frame. It looks handmade and premium without being rustic.
cards.phrase: a fine line-art mark: a small botanical drawing in thin even strokes inside a circle

cards.name: Hand-drawn
cards.desc: Lettering and shapes that keep the wobble of a pen. It signals a person behind the business rather than a corporation, and it is hard to fake well.
cards.phrase: a hand-drawn mark with natural pen wobble, hand-lettered name inside a loose doodled circle

cards.name: Brush script
cards.desc: A single loaded brushstroke or brush-written name, fast and energetic. The dry edges and pressure changes carry the feeling of motion.
cards.phrase: a brush-script mark: one energetic painted stroke with dry edges, the name brush-lettered over it

cards.name: Heritage badge
cards.aka: vintage badge, est. mark, Americana seal
cards.desc: A round or shield badge with the name around the edge, a founding year and a small emblem in the middle. It borrows the authority of old labels and patches.
cards.phrase: a heritage badge: name arched around a circular border, an est. date and a small emblem in the center, two-color

cards.name: Art Deco
cards.desc: Sunbursts, stepped forms, fans and tall geometric capitals, usually in gold and black. It says glamour, travel and the machine age.
cards.phrase: an Art Deco mark: sunburst rays and stepped geometric forms, tall geometric capitals, gold on black

cards.name: Stencil
cards.aka: military stencil, crate type, spray stencil
cards.desc: Letters broken by the bridges a cut stencil needs to hold together. It reads as utilitarian, industrial or street, depending on how clean the cut is.
cards.phrase: a stencil wordmark with visible bridges breaking each letter, as if spray-painted through a cut template

cards.name: Woodcut & linocut
cards.aka: block print, relief print, carved mark
cards.desc: Shapes carved out of a solid block, with gouge lines left in the sky or water. It feels handmade, folky and a little rough at the edges.
cards.phrase: a woodcut-style mark: bold carved shapes in black with parallel gouge lines as texture, rough edges

cards.name: Seventies
cards.desc: Stacked rainbow stripes, rounded chunky type, warm oranges and browns. It feels sunny, nostalgic and relaxed.
cards.phrase: a 1970s retro mark: stacked rainbow stripes in warm oranges and golds, chunky rounded soft-serif type

cards.name: Engraved
cards.desc: Fine parallel lines and crosshatching build tone, the way currency and old stock certificates were printed. It signals trust, money and permanence.
cards.phrase: an engraved mark with fine crosshatched line shading like a banknote, inside an oval frame, serif capitals

cards.name: Die-cut sticker
cards.desc: A punchy shape with a thick white border, as if it had been cut out and stuck on. It feels playful, collectible and made for laptops and water bottles.
cards.phrase: a die-cut sticker mark: bold flat shape with a thick white border and a slight drop shadow, as if peeled and stuck

cards.name: Folk art
cards.aka: hex sign, folk motif, Scandinavian folk, Pennsylvania Dutch
cards.desc: Symmetrical rosettes, hearts, birds and tulips in flat bright colors, from barn hex signs, embroidery and painted furniture. Warm, rural and rooted in a place.
cards.phrase: a folk-art mark: symmetrical rosette of petals and tulips in flat bright red and green, like a painted hex sign

cards.name: Flat
cards.aka: flat design, solid color, no effects
cards.desc: Solid colors, no shadows, gradients or textures. The most flexible treatment: it prints, embroiders, screen-prints and scales without surprises.
cards.phrase: flat treatment: solid fills only, no gradients, shadows or texture

cards.name: Gradient
cards.desc: Color flows smoothly across the mark, often from warm to cool. It feels digital, optimistic and alive on screens, and needs a flat version for print.
cards.phrase: a smooth gradient treatment flowing from coral red through pink to gold, with a flat one-color fallback

cards.name: Chrome
cards.aka: Y2K chrome, liquid metal, airbrush metallic
cards.desc: Shiny metallic letters with a hard horizon line and bright highlights, from late-90s album covers and early web graphics. Loud, nostalgic and very online.
cards.phrase: a Y2K chrome treatment: glossy liquid-metal letters with a hard horizon reflection and starburst highlights

cards.name: Glitch
cards.desc: The mark looks like a corrupted signal: color channels shifted apart, slices displaced sideways. It suggests technology, disruption or something hacked.
cards.phrase: a glitch treatment: red and blue channels offset from the black letters, with horizontal slices shifted sideways

cards.name: Outline
cards.desc: Shapes and letters drawn as outlines with no fill, sometimes doubled into an inline. Light, airy and technical; often used as a secondary version over photography.
cards.phrase: an outline treatment: letters and shapes drawn as even strokes with no fill, like a neon tube

cards.name: Duotone
cards.desc: The whole identity uses exactly two inks, often a dark and a bright. Limits create character, and it prints cheaply on everything from posters to cups.
cards.phrase: a duotone treatment using only two inks, deep blue and soft pink, no other colors or tints

cards.name: Dimensional
cards.desc: The mark has depth: extruded sides, highlights, soft shadows or an inflated, puffy look. It feels tactile and toy-like, and suits screens and motion.
cards.phrase: a dimensional treatment: chunky letters extruded in a darker shade beneath a bright face, toy-like depth

cards.name: Organic blob
cards.desc: Soft, irregular shapes like pebbles or droplets, with rounded type to match. It feels calm, natural and gentle, the opposite of a sharp grid.
cards.phrase: an organic blob treatment: soft irregular pebble shapes and rounded lowercase type, calm natural colors

cards.name: Risograph
cards.desc: Bright spot inks printed one over another, slightly out of register, with a grainy finish. It feels independent, artsy and tactile.
cards.phrase: a risograph treatment: two bright spot inks overprinted and slightly misregistered, with fine grain

cards.name: Halftone
cards.aka: dot screen, Ben-Day dots, pop art dots
cards.desc: Tone made from dots that grow and shrink, as in newspaper printing and comic books. It adds texture and a printed, mechanical feel.
cards.phrase: a halftone treatment: tone built from dots that grow from small to large across the mark

cards.name: Cropped & bleeding
cards.aka: cut-off mark, edge bleed, cropped type
cards.desc: The mark runs off the edge of the frame so only part of it shows. Used big on posters, packaging and screens, it feels confident: you recognize it without seeing all of it.
cards.phrase: a cropped treatment: the mark scaled up so it bleeds off the frame edges, only part of it visible

cards.name: Custom lettering
cards.aka: bespoke wordmark, modified type, drawn letters
cards.desc: Letters drawn or redrawn for this one name, often starting from a typeface and changing the details: a tail, a terminal, the angle of a stroke. It is what makes a wordmark ownable.
cards.phrase: a custom-lettered wordmark redrawn from a serif typeface, with one distinctive drawn detail such as an extended tail

cards.name: Ligature
cards.aka: joined letters, connected pair, shared stroke
cards.desc: Two or more letters share a stroke and become one shape, like the "Th" or "fi" in fine typesetting. It ties a name together and gives the wordmark a signature moment.
cards.phrase: a wordmark with a custom ligature where two letters share one stroke and read as a single shape

cards.name: Cut letters
cards.desc: A single cut slices through the letters, or a notch is taken out of one. The cut adds movement or a hidden meaning (speed, a slope, a blade) without a separate symbol.
cards.phrase: a wordmark of heavy capitals with one clean diagonal cut slicing through every letter

cards.name: Tracked capitals
cards.desc: All capitals with generous space between letters, usually in a light or medium weight. It slows the reader down and reads as calm, expensive and confident.
cards.phrase: a wordmark in widely letterspaced capitals, light to medium weight, with a thin rule beneath

cards.name: All lowercase
cards.desc: The whole name in lowercase, often bold and rounded. It feels approachable, modern and unpretentious, the opposite of a capitalized corporation.
cards.phrase: an all-lowercase wordmark in a bold friendly sans, tight letterspacing, no symbol

cards.name: Script wordmark
cards.aka: cursive logo, signature script, connected script
cards.desc: The name written in joined-up script, often with a swash under it. It feels personal, nostalgic or celebratory depending on the hand.
cards.phrase: a connected script wordmark with a sweeping underline swash, warm and personal

cards.name: Stacked wordmark
cards.aka: stacked lockup, two-line logo, block of type
cards.desc: A two- or three-word name broken onto lines and set tight so it reads as one solid block. It fits square spaces like app icons, stamps and social avatars.
cards.phrase: a stacked wordmark: the name broken onto two tight lines in condensed capitals, forming a solid block

cards.name: Cropped wordmark
cards.desc: The tops or bottoms of the letters are cut away and the word is still readable. It feels editorial and bold, and creates a strong horizontal band.
cards.phrase: a cropped wordmark where the top third of every letter is cut away, still readable

cards.name: Swapped letter
cards.desc: One letter is replaced by a symbol that tells the story, like an O that is a sun or an A that is a mountain. The whole name stays readable and gains an icon you can pull out.
cards.phrase: a wordmark where one letter is replaced by a simple symbol that still reads as that letter

cards.name: Wordmark in a box
cards.aka: contained wordmark, label logo, knockout block
cards.desc: The name is knocked out of a solid rectangle, circle or tag shape. The container gives a simple word real presence and makes the logo easy to place on photos.
cards.phrase: a wordmark knocked out in white from a solid black rectangle, tight even padding

cards.name: Swoosh & underline
cards.aka: smile line, arrow underline, motion swash
cards.desc: A curved line, arrow or swoosh under or through the name adds motion or a hidden meaning, like a smile or a flight path. It turns a plain wordmark into something with a gesture.
cards.phrase: a wordmark with a single curved underline swash that suggests motion and ends in a small arrowhead

cards.name: Geometric sans
cards.desc: Built from circles and straight lines: round O, pointed A, single-story a. Clean, modern and optimistic, with a hint of the 1920s Bauhaus.
cards.phrase: set in a geometric sans-serif like Futura or Avenir: circular rounds, single-story a, clean and modern

cards.name: Humanist sans
cards.desc: A sans-serif with traces of the pen: varied stroke widths, open shapes and a two-story a. Friendly, readable and quietly human.
cards.phrase: set in a humanist sans-serif like Frutiger or Gill Sans: open shapes, gentle stroke contrast, warm and readable

cards.name: Grotesk
cards.desc: The neutral workhorse sans: even strokes, closed shapes, tight spacing. It says competent and no-nonsense, and lets the mark or the color do the talking.
cards.phrase: set in a neo-grotesque sans like Helvetica or Akzidenz-Grotesk: neutral, tight, bold weights

cards.name: Didone
cards.aka: Bodoni, Didot, high-contrast serif, fashion serif
cards.desc: Hairline thin strokes against heavy thick ones, with flat unbracketed serifs. It is the sound of fashion magazines and perfume counters.
cards.phrase: set in a high-contrast Didone serif like Didot or Bodoni: hairline strokes, vertical stress, elegant capitals

cards.name: Slab serif
cards.desc: Heavy rectangular serifs and low contrast. It feels sturdy, honest and a bit Western or industrial, like a wanted poster or a typewriter.
cards.phrase: set in a slab serif like Rockwell or Clarendon: heavy square serifs, sturdy and honest

cards.name: Rounded sans
cards.desc: A sans with rounded stroke ends and corners. It feels soft, safe and friendly, which is why so many kids' brands and fintech apps use it.
cards.phrase: set in a rounded sans-serif like VAG Rounded or Nunito: soft round terminals, friendly and safe

cards.name: Script
cards.desc: Joined-up handwriting, from formal copperplate to casual brush. Charming for a single word, tiring for a paragraph.
cards.phrase: set in a connected script face like Yellowtail or Lobster, for the name only, never for body text

cards.name: Blackletter
cards.desc: Dense, angular medieval letters made with a broad pen. It reads as tradition, newspapers, heavy metal or tattoo parlors, depending on the context.
cards.phrase: set in a blackletter face like Fette Fraktur: dense, angular broad-pen letters

cards.name: Monospace
cards.desc: Every character takes the same width, as on a typewriter or terminal. It signals code, technical honesty or a stripped-back editorial voice.
cards.phrase: set in a monospace face like IBM Plex Mono: fixed-width characters, technical and plain

cards.name: Extended
cards.desc: Very wide letters that take up a lot of horizontal room. It feels bold, futuristic and fashion-forward, like a sports car badge or a techno flyer.
cards.phrase: set in an extended wide sans like Druk Wide or Monument Extended: very wide, bold and futuristic

cards.name: Condensed
cards.desc: Tall, narrow letters that pack a lot of punch into little width. It is the voice of posters, headlines, sports and sale banners.
cards.phrase: set in a condensed poster sans like Bebas Neue or Knockout: tall narrow capitals, punchy

cards.name: Soft serif
cards.desc: A bold serif with rounded, bulbous shapes and soft terminals. It feels warm, nostalgic and a little playful, like a 70s cookbook.
cards.phrase: set in a soft chunky serif like Cooper Black or Recoleta: rounded serifs, warm and nostalgic

cards.name: Innocent
cards.aka: the dreamer, the optimist, the child
cards.desc: Wants to be happy and do things right. Promises simplicity, purity and a return to something good. Visuals are clean, soft and bright, with rounded shapes, white space and pale color.
cards.phrase: an Innocent brand archetype: optimistic, honest and simple, with soft rounded shapes, lots of white space and pale fresh colors

cards.name: Everyman
cards.aka: the regular guy or gal, the citizen, the neighbor
cards.desc: Wants to belong. Down to earth, unpretentious and fairly priced, it speaks to everyone and talks down to no one. The design is friendly and plain, with sturdy type and familiar color.
cards.phrase: an Everyman brand archetype: friendly, unpretentious and fair, with sturdy plain type, familiar primary colors and no luxury cues

cards.name: Hero
cards.aka: the warrior, the champion, the athlete
cards.desc: Wants to prove worth through courage and effort. The brand challenges you to be better and celebrates the win. Expect bold angles, strong upward motion, heavy type and high-contrast color.
cards.phrase: a Hero brand archetype: brave, driven and motivating, with bold upward angles, heavy type and high-contrast red and black

cards.name: Outlaw
cards.aka: the rebel, the revolutionary, the misfit
cards.desc: Wants to break what isn't working. It defines itself against the mainstream and trusts its fans to be in on it. Visuals run dark and raw: black, red, distressed texture, blackletter or stencil.
cards.phrase: an Outlaw brand archetype: rebellious, raw and anti-establishment, with black and red, rough texture and blackletter or stencil type

cards.name: Explorer
cards.aka: the seeker, the wanderer, the pioneer
cards.desc: Wants freedom and the experience of finding out for itself. The brand promises somewhere further, and respects your independence. Look for compasses, horizons, earthy greens and ochres, and rugged slab type.
cards.phrase: an Explorer brand archetype: independent, curious and outdoorsy, with horizon or compass motifs, earthy greens and ochres and a rugged slab serif

cards.name: Creator
cards.aka: the artist, the maker, the inventor
cards.desc: Wants to make something of lasting value. It hands people tools and invites them to make their own mark. The design is expressive and composed at once: primary shapes, considered color, an editorial serif.
cards.phrase: a Creator brand archetype: imaginative and expressive, with overlapping primary shapes, considered bright color and an editorial serif

cards.name: Ruler
cards.aka: the sovereign, the leader, the boss
cards.desc: Wants control, order and stability. The brand offers the assurance of being in charge, and it rarely discounts. Crests, crowns, symmetry, gold on black and high-contrast serifs in capitals.
cards.phrase: a Ruler brand archetype: commanding, stable and premium, with a symmetrical crest or crown, gold on black and a high-contrast serif in capitals

cards.name: Magician
cards.aka: the visionary, the alchemist, the shaman
cards.desc: Wants to make dreams real and transform how things are. It promises the moment where the impossible just works. Stars, orbits, glow, deep blues and violets, and an elegant display face.
cards.phrase: a Magician brand archetype: visionary and transformative, with a star or orbit motif, deep blue and violet with a pink glow, and an elegant display serif

cards.name: Lover
cards.aka: the romantic, the sensualist, the partner
cards.desc: Wants intimacy and pleasure. The brand is about how something feels, and it makes you feel desired. Warm reds and blush, flowing script, soft focus and close crops.
cards.phrase: a Lover brand archetype: sensual, warm and intimate, with flowing script, deep red and blush, and soft close-cropped imagery

cards.name: Caregiver
cards.aka: the nurturer, the parent, the helper
cards.desc: Wants to protect and care for others. The brand is generous, patient and reassuring, and puts the customer's wellbeing before its own image. Soft greens and blues, holding shapes, rounded friendly type.
cards.phrase: a Caregiver brand archetype: warm, protective and reassuring, with a holding or sheltering shape, soft greens and blues and rounded friendly type

cards.name: Jester
cards.aka: the entertainer, the trickster, the comedian
cards.desc: Wants to have a good time and lighten the mood. It wins with jokes, surprise and a little mischief. Wonky shapes, tilted type, loud saturated color and characters with faces.
cards.phrase: a Jester brand archetype: playful, irreverent and fun, with wonky tilted shapes, a character with a face and loud saturated yellow, pink and red

cards.name: Sage
cards.aka: the expert, the scholar, the mentor
cards.desc: Wants to understand the world and share the truth. The brand earns trust through knowledge, evidence and calm explanation. Books, lamps and lenses, deep blue and cream, and a bookish serif.
cards.phrase: a Sage brand archetype: knowledgeable, calm and trustworthy, with a book, lamp or lens motif, deep blue and cream and a bookish serif

cards.name: Sincerity
cards.desc: Down-to-earth, honest, wholesome and cheerful. The brand feels like a good neighbor: family-owned, plain-spoken, a little homespun. Warm color, friendly serifs and real photography of real people.
cards.phrase: a sincere brand personality: down-to-earth, honest, wholesome and cheerful, with warm color, a friendly serif and real unretouched photography

cards.name: Excitement
cards.desc: Daring, spirited, imaginative and up to date. The brand is young, cool and always doing something new. Saturated color, motion, wide or wild type and a lot of energy on every surface.
cards.phrase: an exciting brand personality: daring, spirited, imaginative and up to date, with saturated color, energetic motion and wide expressive type

cards.name: Competence
cards.desc: Reliable, intelligent and successful. The brand is the one you trust to get it right every time. Clean grids, restrained blue or neutral palettes, precise sans serifs and evidence on display.
cards.phrase: a competent brand personality: reliable, intelligent and successful, with a clean grid, a restrained blue and neutral palette and a precise sans serif

cards.name: Sophistication
cards.desc: Upper class, charming and glamorous. The brand is refined and a little out of reach, and it never shouts. Didone serifs, black and cream, generous margins and very little on the page.
cards.phrase: a sophisticated brand personality: refined, charming and glamorous, with a Didone serif, black and cream, generous margins and almost nothing on the page

cards.name: Ruggedness
cards.desc: Outdoorsy and tough. The brand looks built to take a beating and earns respect by lasting. Slab serifs, stamped badges, canvas and leather textures, browns, greens and safety orange.
cards.phrase: a rugged brand personality: outdoorsy, tough and durable, with a slab serif, a stamped badge, canvas and leather texture and brown, green and safety orange

cards.name: Quiet to loud
cards.desc: How much space the brand takes up. Quiet brands use small type, low contrast and a lot of air; loud ones fill the frame with size, color and exclamation. Setting the volume early settles a lot of later arguments.
cards.phrase: place the brand near the loud end of a quiet-to-loud scale: big type, saturated color and full-bleed layouts, with one quiet moment for contrast

cards.name: Classic to modern
cards.aka: timeless vs. contemporary, heritage vs. now
cards.desc: Whether the brand looks like it has always been here or just arrived. Classic leans on serifs, symmetry and crests; modern on geometric sans serifs, asymmetry and flat color. Many good brands sit in the middle: a modern classic.
cards.phrase: place the brand in the middle of a classic-to-modern scale: a modernized serif, simple symmetry and a restrained palette that feels both established and current

cards.name: Serious to playful
cards.aka: formal vs. fun, earnest vs. irreverent
cards.desc: How much the brand is willing to joke. Serious brands are straight, upright and careful; playful ones tilt, bounce and use characters. Insurance can be playful and toys can be serious, which is why it's worth saying out loud.
cards.phrase: place the brand near the serious end of a serious-to-playful scale: upright type, calm color and no characters, but warm rather than cold

cards.name: Challenger
cards.desc: A smaller brand that defines itself against the category leader and picks a fight on one point. It looks deliberately different from the leader: opposite color, sharper voice, fewer things said louder.
cards.phrase: a challenger brand stance: positioned against the category leader on one clear point, visually the opposite of the leader in color and tone

cards.name: Premium
cards.desc: Priced above the middle of the market and justified by quality, service or design. Premium is attainable, unlike luxury: the brand looks better made than its neighbors on the shelf, with fewer elements and richer materials.
cards.phrase: a premium brand stance: priced above the market and visibly better made, with fewer elements, deeper color and tactile materials

cards.name: Value
cards.aka: budget, low cost, everyday low price
cards.desc: Wins on price, and makes the savings obvious. Good value brands look honest and confident rather than cheap: plain packaging, big numbers, one bright color and nothing that looks like it cost money.
cards.phrase: a value brand stance: wins on price and says so plainly, with simple packaging, big confident numbers and one bright color

cards.name: Heritage
cards.desc: Sells its history: the founding date, the original recipe, the family name, the place. Design draws on archive material, badges and period type, and the best heritage brands update it rather than freezing it.
cards.phrase: a heritage brand stance: built on founding date, place and craft, with archive-inspired badges and period type updated for today

cards.name: Disruptor
cards.desc: Changes how the category works, not just how it looks: a new business model, channel or price structure. The identity usually breaks the category's visual codes on purpose, so it reads as a different kind of thing.
cards.phrase: a disruptor brand stance: introduces a new model to an old category and breaks the category's visual codes on purpose

cards.name: Category creator
cards.aka: category design, new category, blue ocean
cards.desc: Names and owns a category that didn't exist, so there is nobody to compare against. The brand has to teach the category as well as sell the product, which favors clear names and a simple, repeatable visual idea.
cards.phrase: a category-creator brand stance: names a new category and owns it, with a clear category name and one simple repeatable visual idea

cards.name: Luxury
cards.desc: Priced for rarity and desire rather than function. Luxury brands say almost nothing: a tiny tracked wordmark, an expanse of empty space, one material, a house code repeated for decades.
cards.phrase: a luxury brand stance: rare and desired rather than useful, with a tiny tracked wordmark, vast empty space, one rich material and a repeated house code

cards.name: Craft & indie
cards.desc: Small, independent and proud of the hands that make it. The look is tactile and specific: kraft paper, stamps, batch numbers, hand lettering, a named maker and a named place.
cards.phrase: a craft and independent brand stance: small batch and hand made, with kraft paper, rubber-stamp marks, batch numbers and hand lettering

cards.name: Mission-led
cards.desc: Exists to change something, and the product is how it pays for it. The mission shows up in the identity itself: a pledge mark, a counter, a certification, a cause color. It only works when the business actually does it.
cards.phrase: a mission-led brand stance: the cause is built into the identity with a pledge mark or impact counter, honest proof and a clear cause color

cards.name: Utility
cards.desc: Sells the thing itself, clearly labeled, with no story attached. Utility branding borrows from lab supplies, pharmacy and industrial labels: monospaced type, specs, numbers and a strict grid.
cards.phrase: a utility brand stance: no story, just a clearly labeled product, with monospaced type, specs and numbers on a strict label grid

cards.name: Signature color
cards.aka: ownable color, brand color, hero color
cards.desc: One hue the brand uses so often and so consistently that people recognize it before they read a word. It works because it is used with discipline: same value everywhere, in large areas, on everything.
cards.phrase: a single ownable signature color used in large flat areas on every touchpoint, so the brand is recognizable before the logo is read

cards.name: Primary palette
cards.desc: The two to four colors that do most of the work, usually the logo color, a background and an ink. Good guidelines give each one a proportion so layouts feel the same even when the content changes.
cards.phrase: a primary palette of three colors with set proportions: a warm cream background about 60%, a brand red about 30% and a dark ink about 10%

cards.name: Secondary palette
cards.desc: A wider set of colors that support the primaries: for charts, illustrations, seasonal campaigns and sub-brands. They are tuned to sit next to the core colors without fighting them, and they never replace the logo color.
cards.phrase: a secondary palette of four muted supporting colors (glaze blue, sage green, rose, sky) that sit beside the core cream, red and ink without competing with them

cards.name: Neutral scale
cards.aka: grays, warm neutrals, ink and paper
cards.desc: The run of off-whites, grays and near-blacks that carry most of the page: backgrounds, body text, borders and dividers. Warm or cool neutrals quietly set the mood of the whole brand.
cards.phrase: a warm neutral scale from a cream off-white to a soft near-black, tinted toward the brand red, carrying backgrounds, text and borders

cards.name: Accent color
cards.desc: One saturated color held back for the things that need attention: buttons, links, a sale tag, the key number. It only works because almost nothing else on the page uses it.
cards.phrase: a calm neutral layout with one saturated accent color reserved only for calls to action and key highlights

cards.name: Tint scale
cards.desc: The brand color stepped lighter and darker in even increments, so designers can make backgrounds, hover states and charts without inventing new colors. Usually named by number, 100 to 900.
cards.phrase: a tint scale of the brand blue in ten even steps from 50 to 900, used for backgrounds, states and charts

cards.name: Monochrome identity
cards.aka: black and white brand, one-color system
cards.desc: An identity built in black and white only, letting type, photography and layout carry everything. It reads as confident, editorial or luxurious, and it is cheap to print.
cards.phrase: a strictly monochrome identity in black and white only, where type, photography and layout do all the work

cards.name: Color blocking
cards.aka: blocks of flat color, panel color
cards.desc: Large, hard-edged areas of flat color laid side by side, with type sitting on top. Bold and graphic from a distance, and an easy system for posters, packaging and walls.
cards.phrase: bold color-blocked layouts: large hard-edged flat panels of red, ochre, blue and pink with type set directly on the blocks

cards.name: Multicolor system
cards.aka: rainbow palette, color family, flexible color
cards.desc: Many equal hues, any of which can lead, so the same logo and layout appear in a different color on every branch, issue or season. Variety comes from the color; consistency comes from everything else staying fixed.
cards.phrase: a multicolor system of six equal hues where any one can lead, applied to the same fixed layout and logo so each branch gets its own color

cards.name: Color coding
cards.aka: wayfinding color, product color, category color
cards.desc: Assigning a fixed color to each line, zone, product or category so people can navigate by color alone. The color carries meaning, so it must stay consistent everywhere and always come with a name or number.
cards.phrase: a color-coding system where each line or zone has one fixed color, always paired with a letter or number for accessibility

cards.name: Supergraphic
cards.aka: oversized graphic, cropped mark, brand shape
cards.desc: A shape from the logo, a letter or a simple form blown up far past normal size and cropped by the edges of the poster, wall or screen. It brands a surface without needing the full logo.
cards.phrase: an oversized supergraphic taken from the logo, scaled far past the frame and cropped by the edges of every poster and wall

cards.name: Brand pattern
cards.desc: A repeating motif, often built from part of the logo, used on packaging, linings, tissue paper and backgrounds. It gives large surfaces something to do and turns quiet products into branded ones.
cards.phrase: a repeating brand pattern built from a simplified piece of the logo, used on packaging, totes and backgrounds

cards.name: Framing device
cards.desc: A fixed shape that holds photos and text in every layout: corner brackets, a cut-off corner, an arch, a thick border. The images change; the frame says whose they are.
cards.phrase: a consistent framing device of thick corner brackets that holds every photo and headline across the campaign

cards.name: Holding shape
cards.desc: A shape, often taken from the logo, that holds a headline, price or logo on top of busy imagery. It keeps text legible and makes every ad recognizable from the outline alone.
cards.phrase: a slanted holding shape taken from the logo that sits over photography and contains every headline and price

cards.name: Brand illustration style
cards.desc: A defined way of drawing: line weight, color palette, how people and objects are simplified, how much texture. Any illustrator can follow it, so pictures look like they came from one hand.
cards.phrase: a brand illustration style with flat shapes, no outlines, a limited five-color palette, simplified rounded people and a little grain

cards.name: Icon style
cards.desc: A rulebook for icons: grid size, stroke width, corner radius, fill or outline, and how much detail. Following it makes icons from different designers look like one family.
cards.phrase: a consistent icon style on a 24px grid with a 2px stroke, round caps and joins, 2px corner radius and no fills

cards.name: Photography direction
cards.aka: art direction, photo style, image guidelines
cards.desc: Rules for what brand photos look like: subject, light, angle, color grade, how people are cast and posed, and what never appears. It lets many photographers shoot one consistent library.
cards.phrase: a photography direction of natural light, low camera angles, warm film grade, real people mid-activity, and no posed smiles at camera

cards.name: Motion principles
cards.aka: brand motion, motion language, animation guidelines
cards.desc: How the brand moves: its easing curves, speed, how things enter and leave, and a signature move for the logo. It keeps app transitions, video and social animation feeling like one personality.
cards.phrase: brand motion principles: a snappy ease-out curve, durations of 150, 300 and 600ms, and elements that slide up and settle like a page being placed

cards.name: Sonic logo
cards.aka: audio logo, mnemonic, sound ident, jingle
cards.desc: A short sound, usually two to five notes under three seconds, that plays wherever the logo would: end of an ad, app launch, a payment going through. Done well, people recognize it with their eyes closed.
cards.phrase: a sonic logo of four rising notes under two seconds, warm and acoustic, that plays at the end of every video and on app launch

cards.name: Data-driven identity
cards.aka: generative identity, dynamic system, algorithmic logo
cards.desc: A mark or graphic generated from real data, such as visitor counts, weather or the letters of a name, so it changes every time while following fixed rules. The system is the brand, not any single output.
cards.phrase: a data-driven generative identity where a radial mark is drawn from each event's data, with fixed color and typography holding the system together

cards.name: Custom typeface
cards.aka: brand typeface, proprietary font, house font
cards.desc: A typeface drawn or modified for one brand, so every headline and sign carries its voice even without the logo. Expensive up front but it saves licensing costs and is impossible to copy legally.
cards.phrase: a custom brand typeface with a few distinctive letters (a flat-topped t and a hooked y) used for all headlines and signage

cards.name: Layout grid
cards.aka: brand grid, modular grid, column system
cards.desc: A fixed set of columns, margins and baseline rhythm that every poster, page and screen sits on. It is the reason a brand's layouts feel related even when the content is completely different.
cards.phrase: a strict 6-column modular layout grid with generous margins and a baseline rhythm, used for every poster, report page and screen

cards.name: Stationery
cards.desc: Business cards, letterhead, envelopes and compliment slips: the oldest identity application and still a good test of whether the logo, type and color work small and in print.
cards.phrase: a stationery set of business card, letterhead and envelope with the logo top left, generous margins and the brand blue as a single edge stripe

cards.name: Wayfinding signage
cards.desc: Signs that help people find their way: directional arrows, destination names, pictograms and numbers on a consistent layout. Legibility at distance and speed matters more than personality.
cards.phrase: wayfinding signage on dark blue panels with large white sans-serif destinations, arrows on the left, pictograms and the brand mark small in the corner

cards.name: Packaging
cards.desc: Boxes, bags, labels and cans where the identity has to sell on a shelf in under a second. A strong system keeps the brand block fixed and lets flavors or variants change color or illustration.
cards.phrase: packaging with a fixed brand block at the top and a color band per variant, with a simple pictorial illustration and large flavor name

cards.name: Merchandise
cards.desc: Totes, caps, mugs, pins and shirts that people choose to wear or carry. The best merch treats the logo or a graphic device as something people would want even if they did not know the brand.
cards.phrase: merchandise that uses the mark small and a graphic device large: an embroidered cap, a screen-printed tote and an enamel pin

cards.name: Vehicle livery
cards.aka: fleet graphics, vehicle wrap, trade dress
cards.desc: The paint and graphics on boats, vans, planes, trucks and trains. Vehicles move, so the design must read from far away and work around doors, windows and curves.
cards.phrase: a vehicle livery with a broad brand-blue stripe sweeping along the hull, a white upper body, and the mark large near the bow

cards.name: Environmental graphics
cards.desc: Graphics applied to architecture: wall murals, window film, floor graphics, reception walls and dimensional letters. They turn a building into a branded place without a single sign.
cards.phrase: environmental graphics with a floor-to-ceiling wave supergraphic in brand blue across the terminal wall, dimensional letters and wood benches

cards.name: Social templates
cards.aka: social media kit, post templates, story templates
cards.desc: Ready-made layouts for posts, stories and banners, with fixed places for the logo, headline and image. They let anyone on the team post on-brand in minutes.
cards.phrase: a social template kit of square posts and vertical stories with a fixed logo corner, one headline zone and a photo window, in brand blue and cream

cards.name: Website
cards.desc: Often the most-seen application of all. It translates the identity into navigation, type sizes, color for links and buttons, and image crops that work from phone to desktop.
cards.phrase: a website homepage carrying the identity: a slim nav with the logo left, a full-width photo hero with a headline in the brand typeface, and brand-blue buttons

cards.name: App icon & splash
cards.aka: launch screen, app identity, home screen icon
cards.desc: The app icon on a home screen and the splash screen while it loads: the mark stripped down to one bold idea on a solid field. It is the most-seen version of the brand for many people.
cards.phrase: an app icon of the mark alone in white on a brand-blue rounded square, with a matching splash screen that shows the mark centered on solid blue

cards.name: Uniforms
cards.desc: What staff wear: jackets, shirts, aprons, name badges and hats. Uniforms carry the brand into every face-to-face moment and have to survive weather, washing and real work.
cards.phrase: crew uniforms in navy workwear with a small embroidered mark on the chest, a brand-red name tab and a knit cap

cards.name: Email signature
cards.desc: The few lines under every email: name, role, contact details and often a small logo. It is sent thousands of times a day, so it should be plain text first and survive any email client.
cards.phrase: a plain-text-first email signature with name in bold, role and phone on one line, a small logo image that is optional, and the brand blue only on links

cards.name: Design token
cards.desc: A named value that stands in for a raw one: color.action instead of #D9381E. Design files and code both point at the name, so changing it in one place changes it everywhere.
cards.phrase: define every color, size and spacing value as a named design token, and never hard-code raw values in components

cards.name: Primitive tokens
cards.aka: core, global or base tokens, the palette
cards.desc: The raw ingredients with neutral names: red-500, grey-100, space-4. They describe what a value is, not where it goes, and most components should never use them directly.
cards.phrase: start with a layer of primitive tokens named by value (red-500, grey-100, space-4) that components never use directly

cards.name: Semantic tokens
cards.desc: Tokens named for their job: color.text.danger, color.surface.raised, space.inset.card. Each one points at a primitive, so the meaning stays put while the value underneath can change.
cards.phrase: add a semantic token layer named for purpose (text.danger, surface.raised, border.subtle) that points at primitives

cards.name: Component tokens
cards.desc: The top layer: button.primary.background, card.padding. They let one component be tuned without touching the rest, and they point at semantic tokens underneath.
cards.phrase: expose component tokens (button.primary.background, card.padding) that alias semantic tokens, only where a component needs its own dial

cards.name: Color ramp
cards.aka: tonal scale, color scale, shades 50 to 900
cards.desc: One hue stepped from nearly white to nearly black in even, numbered stops. Good ramps step evenly in perceived lightness, so 500 on 50 and 50 on 900 both pass contrast.
cards.phrase: build each brand color as a ramp of 10 stops (50 to 900) evenly spaced in perceived lightness, using OKLCH

cards.name: Type scale
cards.desc: A fixed set of text sizes, each a step up from the last by a ratio such as 1.25. Every heading and label picks a step, so the hierarchy stays consistent from screen to screen.
cards.phrase: use a type scale with a 1.25 ratio and seven named steps (caption, body, body-lg, h4, h3, h2, display)

cards.name: Spacing scale
cards.desc: A short list of allowed gaps, usually multiples of 4 or 8. Padding, margins and gaps all come from it, which is why well-built screens feel evenly spaced without anyone measuring.
cards.phrase: use an 8pt spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64) for every padding, margin and gap

cards.name: Corner radius
cards.desc: A few named roundness values, from square to pill. Radius carries a lot of personality: sharp corners read serious and engineered, big round ones read friendly and soft.
cards.phrase: define radius tokens none, sm 4px, md 8px, lg 16px and full (pill), and use sm for buttons and inputs

cards.name: Elevation
cards.desc: A small set of depth levels, each a shadow (and sometimes a lighter surface in dark mode). Level 0 sits on the page, level 3 floats as a dialog, so depth tells you what is on top.
cards.phrase: define four elevation levels (flat, raised, overlay, modal) as shadow tokens, and lighten surfaces instead of adding shadow in dark mode

cards.name: Theming & modes
cards.aka: light and dark mode, color modes
cards.desc: Swapping the values behind semantic tokens to change the whole look at once. Light and dark are the common pair; high contrast is a third mode worth having.
cards.phrase: support light, dark and high-contrast modes by swapping the values behind semantic tokens, with dark mode designed on its own

cards.name: Multi-brand theming
cards.desc: One set of components dressed in several brands by swapping a theme file. Same buttons, same layouts, different colors, type and radius per brand.
cards.phrase: build one component library with a theme layer, so each brand swaps colors, typeface and radius without changing components

cards.name: Density
cards.aka: compact and comfortable modes, spacing modes
cards.desc: A setting that tightens or loosens padding and row height across the product. Dense views fit more on screen for experts; comfortable ones are easier to tap and scan.
cards.phrase: offer comfortable and compact density modes by swapping spacing tokens, keeping touch targets at least 44px on mobile

cards.name: Atomic design
cards.desc: Brad Frost's way of sorting a system by size: atoms (a label, a button) combine into molecules (a search field), which combine into organisms (a header). It gives teams a shared word for each level.
cards.phrase: organize the system with atomic design: atoms (button, input, label), molecules (search field), organisms (header, transaction list)

cards.name: Component library
cards.aka: UI kit, design library, Figma library
cards.desc: The shared, versioned set of ready-made components, kept in a design tool and in code. Teams pull from it instead of drawing their own button again.
cards.phrase: ship the components as one shared library in Figma and in code, with matching names and props in both

cards.name: Variants
cards.desc: Versions of one component chosen with a setting rather than drawn separately: primary, secondary, ghost, danger; small, medium, large. One component, a handful of switches.
cards.phrase: give each component a small set of variants (primary, secondary, ghost, danger; sm, md, lg) set by props, not separate components

cards.name: Interactive states
cards.desc: How a component looks in each moment: default, hover, pressed, focused, disabled, loading. Every state is designed on purpose, especially focus, which keyboard users rely on.
cards.phrase: design every interactive state (default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled, loading), with a visible 2px focus ring

cards.name: Component anatomy
cards.desc: A diagram that names every part of a component with numbered callouts: container, label, icon, helper text. It gives designers and engineers the same names for the same pieces.
cards.phrase: document each component with an anatomy diagram: numbered callouts for container, label, icon, helper text and their token names

cards.name: Slots
cards.desc: Empty, named spaces inside a component where teams drop their own content: a card with a header slot, a body slot and an actions slot. The frame stays consistent while the insides vary.
cards.phrase: build container components with named slots (leading, title, trailing, actions) instead of a prop for every possible content

cards.name: Patterns
cards.desc: Repeatable answers to common jobs, made from several components: sign-in, empty states, confirming a payment, filtering a list. A pattern documents the steps and the wording, not just the parts.
cards.phrase: document recurring patterns (sign-in, empty state, confirm a payment, error recovery) as step-by-step flows with real copy

cards.name: Page templates
cards.desc: Ready-made page shapes with the regions blocked out: a dashboard, a settings page, a detail view. New screens start from a template, so structure and spacing are already right.
cards.phrase: provide page templates (dashboard, list and detail, settings, form) with blocked-out regions built from the layout grid

cards.name: Icon set
cards.desc: One family of icons drawn to the same rules: grid size, stroke weight, corner style and a padding box. Consistent icons look like one hand drew them.
cards.phrase: use one icon set on a 24px grid with a 1.5px stroke, rounded joins and a 2px safe area, drawn to match the typeface weight

cards.name: Layout primitives
cards.desc: Tiny components whose only job is arrangement: Stack puts things in a column with even gaps, Cluster wraps things in a row, Grid makes columns. Most layouts are just these three nested.
cards.phrase: build layouts from layout primitives (Stack, Cluster, Grid) that own all spacing, so components carry no outer margins

cards.name: Breakpoints
cards.desc: The named widths where a layout changes shape: one column on a phone, two on a tablet, a sidebar on desktop. Components and templates say what they do at each one.
cards.phrase: define breakpoints sm 0, md 768px and lg 1200px, with a 4, 8 and 12 column grid, and document how each template reflows

cards.name: Handoff specs
cards.desc: The annotated version of a design that tells engineers exactly what to build: spacing, sizes, tokens, behavior. With a good token system, specs name tokens rather than pixel values.
cards.phrase: annotate designs for handoff with redlines that name tokens (space-4, radius-sm, color.action), not raw pixel values

cards.name: Brand guidelines
cards.aka: brand book, identity manual, brand standards
cards.desc: The rulebook for the identity: logo versions and clear space, colors with exact values, type, imagery, voice and real examples. The classic version is a bound manual; today it is usually a website or PDF.
cards.phrase: write brand guidelines covering logo versions and clear space, color values, typography, imagery, voice and do and don't examples

cards.name: Style guide
cards.aka: visual style guide, UI style guide
cards.desc: A lighter document than full guidelines: the colors, type styles, spacing and components on one page, ready to use. Often the first step before a real design system.
cards.phrase: produce a one-page style guide: color swatches with hex values, type styles, spacing scale, buttons and form fields

cards.name: Documentation site
cards.aka: design system site, zeroheight, Storybook docs
cards.desc: The website where the system lives: every token, component and pattern with live examples, usage notes and code. It is the front door most people actually use.
cards.phrase: publish a documentation site with a page per component: live example, usage do and don't, props table, tokens used and code

cards.name: Do and don't examples
cards.aka: misuse examples, correct and incorrect use
cards.desc: Paired pictures showing the right way and the common wrong ways: don't stretch the logo, don't put it on a busy photo, don't recolor it. People skim these first and remember them best.
cards.phrase: show do and don't examples side by side for the logo and key components: stretched, recolored, on busy backgrounds, crowded

cards.name: Single source of truth
cards.desc: Every value is defined in exactly one place, usually a token file, and a build step sends it out to Figma, CSS, iOS and Android. Nobody copies hex codes by hand.
cards.phrase: keep every token in one JSON source and generate CSS variables, Swift, Kotlin and Figma variables from it with Style Dictionary

cards.name: Versioning & changelog
cards.desc: Numbering releases so teams know what an update will do: 3.2.1 is a fix, 3.3.0 adds something, 4.0.0 breaks something. A changelog says what changed and how to migrate.
cards.phrase: version the system with semantic versioning and publish a changelog with migration notes for every breaking change

cards.name: Contribution model
cards.desc: The agreed route for adding to the system: propose, review, build, document, release. It decides whether one central team owns everything or product teams contribute too.
cards.phrase: define a contribution model: propose, review, build, document, release, with a core team that reviews and product teams that contribute

cards.name: Contrast & accessibility
cards.desc: Checking every text and background pair against WCAG: 4.5:1 for body text (AA), 3:1 for large text and icons, 7:1 for AAA. Systems publish the approved pairs so nobody guesses.
cards.phrase: publish approved text and background color pairs with their contrast ratios, all at least WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body text)

cards.name: Brand audit
cards.desc: Gathering every place the brand shows up, side by side, to see the drift: five blues, three logos, eleven button styles. It is usually the first step of a rebrand or a new design system.
cards.phrase: run a brand audit: collect every logo, color, type style and button in use today, group the duplicates and propose one of each

cards.name: Brand asset portal
cards.desc: A shared site where anyone can download approved logos, templates, photos and fonts in the right formats. It stops people screenshotting the logo from the website.
cards.phrase: set up a brand asset portal with approved logo files (SVG, PNG, EPS), templates, photos and fonts, each labelled with where to use it

cards.name: Naming conventions
cards.desc: Agreed rules for how things are named, so names are guessable: category, then property, then variant, then state. color-text-danger-hover tells you what it is without opening it.
cards.phrase: name tokens as category-property-variant-state (color-text-danger-hover) and components by purpose, never by appearance

cards.name: Adoption metrics
cards.desc: Measuring how much of the product actually uses the system: share of screens built from library components, number of hard-coded colors left, teams on the latest version. It shows where to help next.
cards.phrase: track adoption: share of UI built from library components, count of hard-coded values, and which teams are on the latest version

cards.name: Branded house
cards.desc: One master brand covers every product and division, each named with a plain descriptor. All the trust and spend goes into one name.
cards.phrase: a branded-house architecture: one master brand used on every product, with sub-products named by plain descriptors in the same typeface

cards.name: House of brands
cards.desc: A parent company owns many independent brands, each with its own name, look and audience. The parent stays in the background.
cards.phrase: a house-of-brands architecture: each product line has its own unrelated name and visual identity, and the parent company is mentioned only in small print

cards.name: Endorsed brand
cards.desc: Each product brand has its own name and look, with a small line from the parent ("by Atlas") for reassurance. Lends trust without taking over.
cards.phrase: an endorsed-brand lockup: the product brand dominant, with a small "by [parent]" endorsement line beneath in the parent's typeface

cards.name: Sub-brand
cards.aka: child brand, master brand plus modifier
cards.desc: A product carries the master name plus its own distinctive modifier, with its own color or mark. More personality than a descriptor, still clearly family.
cards.phrase: a sub-brand: the master brand name paired with a distinct product name and its own accent color, sharing the parent's typeface and lockup rules

cards.name: Hybrid architecture
cards.desc: Some products use the master brand, some are endorsed, some stand alone. Most large companies end up here through acquisitions.
cards.phrase: a hybrid brand architecture: core products under the master brand, one endorsed brand and one fully independent acquired brand, with written rules for each

cards.name: Ingredient brand
cards.desc: A branded part inside someone else's product, shown as a small badge on the host product. It sells the component to the end customer.
cards.phrase: an ingredient-brand badge: a compact mark for a component technology, designed to sit on other companies' products, with a short "inside" descriptor

cards.name: Family identity
cards.desc: A range of products shares one visual system (a band, a grid, a color code) so they read as a set on the shelf, even with different names.
cards.phrase: a product-family identity: every product uses the same band, grid and type, with one color per product so the range reads as a set

cards.name: Descriptive name
cards.desc: Says what the business does or sells, plainly. Instantly understood, but hard to trademark and easy to confuse with competitors.
cards.phrase: a descriptive brand name that plainly says what the business does, short and easy to say aloud

cards.name: Invented name
cards.desc: A new word with no prior meaning, chosen for its sound. Easy to trademark and to own, but it means nothing until the brand fills it.
cards.phrase: an invented brand name: a new two- or three-syllable word with no existing meaning, easy to pronounce, with a crisp sound

cards.name: Acronym
cards.desc: Initials of a longer name. Efficient once famous, but most acronyms start out meaningless and forgettable.
cards.phrase: an acronym name built from the initials of the full name, ideally pronounceable as a word

cards.name: Founder name
cards.desc: Named for the person or family who started it. Signals accountability, craft and heritage.
cards.phrase: a founder-name brand: the founder's surname, optionally with "& Daughters" or "& Co.", set like an old shop sign

cards.name: Evocative name
cards.desc: A real word that suggests a feeling or idea about the brand without describing it. Memorable and ownable in its category.
cards.phrase: an evocative brand name: one real word that suggests the brand's promise as a metaphor, not a description

cards.name: Compound name
cards.desc: Two whole words joined into one. Clearer than an invented word, more ownable than a phrase.
cards.phrase: a compound brand name made of two short, concrete words joined into one, with a clear image

cards.name: Portmanteau
cards.desc: Parts of two words blended, overlapping at a shared sound. Playful and often self-explaining.
cards.phrase: a portmanteau name blending two words at a shared sound, easy to spell after hearing it once

cards.name: Respelled name
cards.desc: A real word spelled differently so it can be trademarked and the domain bought. Says the meaning and stays ownable.
cards.phrase: a respelled brand name: a real word with one or two letters changed so it is distinctive, still pronounced the same

cards.name: Place name
cards.desc: Named for where the business is or came from. Grounds it in a landscape and a story.
cards.phrase: a place-name brand: named after a real-sounding lake, hill or street tied to the brand's origin

cards.name: Wordplay name
cards.desc: Uses sound devices like puns, alliteration, rhyme or onomatopoeia. Sticky and fun to say, best when it fits the brand's tone.
cards.phrase: a wordplay brand name using a pun, alliteration or rhyme that fits the brand's tone

cards.name: Spinner
cards.desc: A small animated character next to a status line that says "still working" when you can't know how long something will take. It is replaced by a ✓ or ✗ when the step ends.
cards.phrase: a braille-dot spinner beside the current step's label, replaced by a green ✓ or red ✗ when the step finishes

cards.name: Progress bar
cards.desc: A bar that fills as work completes, usually with a percentage, a rate and a time remaining. Use it when you can count the work.
cards.phrase: a determinate progress bar with percent, transfer rate and ETA, redrawn in place on one line

cards.name: Task checklist
cards.desc: Each step of a longer job gets its own line that moves from pending to running to done. Nested steps indent under their parent, and parallel steps can run at once.
cards.phrase: a live task checklist: one line per step with pending ◌, running spinner, done ✓ and failed ✗ states, nested sub-steps indented

cards.name: Semantic color
cards.desc: Color carries meaning, never decoration: green for success, yellow for warnings, red for errors, dim gray for secondary detail. The words still make sense with color turned off.
cards.phrase: semantic color only: green success, yellow warning, red error, dim secondary text; respect NO_COLOR and plain output when piped

cards.name: Aligned table
cards.desc: Rows of records in aligned columns with a header, so you can scan down a column. Plain whitespace columns stay easy to pipe into other tools.
cards.phrase: list output as an aligned table with an uppercase dim header row, status column colored, no borders so it pipes cleanly

cards.name: Helpful errors
cards.desc: An error that says what went wrong, points at the exact spot with a caret, and suggests the fix. The opposite of a stack trace dump.
cards.phrase: errors as diagnostics: a short red headline, the offending line with a caret underline, and a "help:" line with the likely fix

cards.name: Interactive prompts
cards.desc: Questions asked one at a time with arrow-key selection, checkboxes, text input and a y/N confirm. Answered questions collapse to a single line so the history stays readable.
cards.phrase: interactive prompts in the style of @clack/prompts: arrow-key select with a ❯ cursor, answered questions collapse to one line, every answer also settable by a flag

cards.name: Help & subcommands
cards.aka: git-style CLI, usage text, noun-verb commands
cards.desc: A tool organized as `tool <noun> <verb> [flags]`, with help text that leads with examples and groups commands by job. Every command answers --help.
cards.phrase: git-style subcommands (tool <noun> <verb>), --help on every command that leads with usage and 2–3 real examples, commands grouped by purpose

cards.name: Machine-readable output
cards.desc: A flag that swaps the pretty human output for stable JSON (or plain lines) that scripts can parse. Pretty for people, predictable for pipes.
cards.phrase: human-friendly output by default, plus --json for stable machine-readable output and --quiet for scripts; detect when stdout is not a TTY

cards.name: Tree output
cards.desc: Nested things drawn with box-drawing branches so parent and child relationships are clear at a glance.
cards.phrase: show the hierarchy as a tree with ├── and └── branches, directories in bold blue, sizes dimmed on the right

cards.name: Diff view
cards.desc: Changes shown as removed lines in red with − and added lines in green with +, with a few unchanged lines around them for context.
cards.phrase: show changes as a colored unified diff: red − removed lines, green + added lines, dim context lines and line numbers

cards.name: ASCII banner
cards.desc: A big title made of characters, printed once when a tool starts or a project is created. Pure personality; keep it to first run.
cards.phrase: a small ASCII-art wordmark banner on first run only, in one brand color, followed by a one-line tagline

cards.name: Log stream
cards.desc: Live log lines from several processes at once, each prefixed with a colored name and a timestamp so you can tell them apart.
cards.phrase: multiplexed log stream: each line prefixed with a fixed-width colored service name and dim timestamp, errors highlighted

cards.name: TTY-aware output
cards.aka: isatty check, NO_COLOR, plain mode, pipe-friendly output
cards.desc: The tool checks whether it is printing to a real terminal. On a terminal it uses color, spinners and redrawn lines; when piped to a file or another command it prints plain, one line per event.
cards.phrase: TTY-aware output: color, spinners and in-place redraws only when stdout is a terminal (isatty); plain line-by-line text with no ANSI codes when piped, when NO_COLOR is set, when TERM=dumb, or with --plain / --no-color

cards.name: stdout, stderr and exit codes
cards.desc: The result goes to stdout so it can be piped or saved; progress, warnings and errors go to stderr so they still show on screen. The exit code is 0 on success and non-zero on failure, so scripts and CI can react.
cards.phrase: write the primary result to stdout and all progress, warnings and errors to stderr; exit 0 on success, 1 on failure and 2 on bad usage, and document the exit codes in --help

cards.name: Dry run and confirm
cards.desc: Before a destructive or expensive action the tool shows exactly what it would do without doing it, and asks for confirmation. The riskiest actions make you type the name of the thing; scripts skip the question with --yes and fail safely with --no-input.
cards.phrase: a --dry-run flag that prints exactly what would change and changes nothing; destructive commands ask for confirmation on a TTY, the most dangerous ones require typing the resource name, --yes / --force skips the prompt, and --no-input makes it fail instead of hanging

cards.name: Suggest the next step
cards.aka: "did you mean", next-command hints, typo correction
cards.desc: When you mistype a command the tool suggests the closest real one, and after a command succeeds it tells you what you will probably want to run next. You learn the tool by using it.
cards.phrase: suggest the closest command on typos ("Did you mean deploy?", using edit distance) without running it automatically, and after each successful command print a dim "Next:" line with the most likely follow-up command

cards.name: Pager for long output
cards.desc: Output longer than the screen opens in a pager like less, so you can scroll and search, then quit back to a clean prompt. Short output prints directly, and nothing is paged when piped.
cards.phrase: page long output through $PAGER (default less -FIRX, which quits if it fits on one screen and keeps colors) only when stdout is a TTY, with --no-pager to turn it off

cards.name: Rendered markdown
cards.desc: Markdown shown in the terminal with real styling: colored headings, bullets, highlighted code blocks and wrapped paragraphs instead of raw # and ** characters.
cards.phrase: render markdown output with Glamour (Go) or Rich Markdown (Python): styled headings, bullets, syntax-highlighted code blocks, word wrap to the terminal width, and an auto dark/light style

cards.name: Split panes
cards.desc: The screen divided into bordered boxes, each showing one thing. The focused pane gets a brighter border, and Tab moves between them.
cards.phrase: full-screen TUI with tiled bordered panes, the focused pane's border highlighted, Tab to cycle focus

cards.name: List and detail
cards.desc: A list of items on one side and the selected item's details on the other. Moving the cursor updates the detail instantly.
cards.phrase: list-and-detail layout: scrollable list on the left with a highlighted cursor row, the selected item's details on the right, updating as the cursor moves

cards.name: Status line
cards.desc: A one-line strip pinned to the bottom (or top) showing mode, current item, position and background state. It is how a TUI says where you are.
cards.phrase: a bottom status line with colored segments: mode on the left, current file/item in the middle, position and background tasks on the right

cards.name: Key hint footer
cards.desc: A footer listing the few keys that work right now, with ? opening the full list. New users learn the tool without reading docs.
cards.phrase: a dim footer showing the 4–6 most useful key bindings for the current view, with ? toggling a full help overlay

cards.name: Terminal dashboard
cards.desc: Live meters, bar gauges and line graphs drawn with block and braille characters. Dense, glanceable and updating every second.
cards.phrase: a live terminal dashboard: labeled bar meters for CPU/memory, a braille line graph of history, and a sorted process table below

cards.name: Fuzzy finder
cards.desc: Type a few letters and a list narrows to fuzzy matches, with the matched letters highlighted and a preview of the selection. The fastest way to pick from hundreds of things.
cards.phrase: a fuzzy finder: query line at the bottom, results above with matched characters highlighted, a preview pane of the selected item

cards.name: Popup dialog
cards.desc: A bordered box drawn over the center of the screen to confirm an action or ask for input, with the background dimmed or left as is.
cards.phrase: a centered popup dialog with a double-line border over dimmed content, y/n buttons with the safe choice focused by default

cards.name: Tabs
cards.desc: A row of named views across the top, switched with number keys or Tab. Keeps several screens one keypress apart.
cards.phrase: a tab strip across the top with numbered views (1 Overview, 2 Logs, 3 Config), the active tab inverted, number keys to switch

cards.name: File tree
cards.desc: A tree of folders and files with ▸ and ▾ to collapse and expand, often docked on the left of an editor.
cards.phrase: a collapsible file tree sidebar with ▸/▾ toggles, the cursor row highlighted, git status markers beside changed files

cards.name: Inline TUI
cards.desc: Interactive UI drawn right below the prompt instead of taking over the screen, so earlier output stays in scrollback and the result remains visible afterwards.
cards.phrase: render the interactive UI inline below the prompt (not alternate-screen full-screen), so the final result stays in the terminal scrollback

cards.name: Vim keybindings
cards.desc: Navigation with h j k l, g/G for top and bottom, / to search and : for commands. Familiar to a lot of terminal users; offer arrow keys too.
