cards.phrase: keyboard-first navigation with vim keys (h/j/k/l, g/G, / search, : command mode) and arrow-key equivalents

cards.name: Terminal form
cards.aka: Huh form, gum prompts, multi-field input
cards.desc: Several fields on one screen, filled in order: text inputs, a select list and a yes/no confirm. The focused field gets a colored bar on its left, and Tab and Shift-Tab move between fields.
cards.phrase: a terminal form built with Charm Huh: a group of fields (text Input, Select, Confirm) with a thick left border on the focused field, validation shown inline, tab / shift+tab to move, and an accessible plain mode; use gum for the same in shell scripts

cards.name: Gauges and charts
cards.aka: sparklines, bar charts, braille plots, meters
cards.desc: Numbers drawn with block and braille characters: a filled gauge for a percentage, a thin line gauge, a sparkline for recent history, a bar chart for comparisons and a braille canvas for smooth line plots.
cards.phrase: charts drawn in the terminal with Ratatui widgets: Gauge for a percentage with a centered label, LineGauge for a thin meter, Sparkline for recent values, BarChart with labels, and Chart or Canvas with the braille marker for line plots

cards.name: Coding-agent TUI
cards.aka: AI chat TUI, agent REPL, terminal assistant
cards.desc: A scrolling transcript of what the agent read, ran and changed, with file edits shown as inline diffs and risky actions paused behind a permission prompt. A fixed input box sits at the bottom with a status line for model, token use and mode.
cards.phrase: a coding-agent TUI like Claude Code or Crush: scrolling transcript with tool calls as collapsible ● lines, edits as inline colored diffs, a bordered permission prompt (Yes / Yes, always / No) before running commands, a fixed rounded input box at the bottom, and a dim status line with model, token count and mode

cards.name: Box-drawing borders
cards.desc: Unicode line characters that draw boxes. Rounded corners feel friendly and modern, double lines feel classic, heavy lines feel bold.
cards.phrase: boxes drawn with rounded box-drawing borders (╭─╮ ╰─╯), double lines only for warnings

cards.name: Charm style
cards.desc: Rounded borders, generous padding, pink and purple accents and soft gray body text, the house style of Charm's Go libraries: Bubble Tea (app framework), Lip Gloss (styling and layout), Bubbles (lists, inputs, spinners), Huh (forms) and Glamour (markdown).
cards.phrase: Charm-style TUI built with Bubble Tea, styled with Lip Gloss (rounded borders, generous padding, hot-pink and violet accents, soft gray secondary text), using Bubbles components, Huh for forms and Glamour for markdown

cards.name: Dense & utilitarian
cards.desc: Every row and column used, minimal borders, many numbers at once. For power users who watch a screen all day.
cards.phrase: information-dense utilitarian layout: no wasted rows, minimal borders, many columns of numbers, color only for thresholds

cards.name: Retro phosphor
cards.desc: Green or amber text on black with a soft glow, like an old CRT monitor. Nostalgic and a little cinematic.
cards.phrase: retro phosphor look: monochrome green on black with a soft glow and faint scanlines, like a VT100

cards.name: Powerline prompt
cards.desc: A shell prompt built from colored segments joined by arrow-shaped separators, showing folder, git branch and status. Needs a Nerd Font for the icons.
cards.phrase: a powerline-style segmented prompt: colored blocks for directory, git branch and status joined by arrow separators, Nerd Font icons

cards.name: Named color themes
cards.aka: Dracula, Catppuccin, Nord, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night
cards.desc: Popular terminal palettes with names you can just say. Dracula is purple and pink, Catppuccin is pastel, Nord is icy blue, Gruvbox is warm retro, Tokyo Night is deep navy and neon.
cards.phrase: use the Catppuccin Mocha palette (or: Dracula / Nord / Gruvbox / Tokyo Night) for all UI colors

cards.name: Hero section
cards.aka: above the fold, jumbotron, header block
cards.desc: The first full-width block of a landing page: one big headline, a line of supporting text, one or two buttons, and usually a product screenshot. It answers "what is this and what do I do next" in a few seconds.
cards.phrase: a centered hero section: small announcement pill, a 2-line headline (text-5xl to text-6xl, tight tracking), one sentence of subtext, a primary and a secondary button, and a product screenshot below that bleeds off the fold

cards.name: Bento grid
cards.aka: bento box layout, feature grid, tile grid
cards.desc: Features shown as a grid of rounded tiles in mixed sizes, like a Japanese lunch box. Each tile holds one idea with a small visual, and the big tiles carry the most important ones.
cards.phrase: a bento grid of features: CSS grid with 4 columns and mixed tile spans (one 2x2 hero tile, a tall tile, wide tiles), rounded-2xl tiles with a subtle border, each tile one feature with a small live visual

cards.name: App shell with sidebar
cards.aka: admin layout, sidebar layout, application frame
cards.desc: The frame around a web app: a left sidebar of sections that stays put, a slim top bar with search and account menu, and a main area that changes. It makes a web app feel like a desktop app.
cards.phrase: an app shell: fixed 240px left sidebar with workspace switcher, icon + label nav items and the active item highlighted, a slim top bar with search and avatar menu, and a scrollable main content area; sidebar collapses to icons on narrow screens

cards.name: Dashboard
cards.aka: analytics overview, admin home, KPI page
cards.desc: A page of numbers at a glance: a row of stat cards with the trend for each, a large chart, and a short table of recent items. The aim is to answer "is everything OK" without clicking.
cards.phrase: a dashboard: a row of 4 KPI cards (label, big number, colored delta vs last period), one wide line chart with a date-range picker, a smaller breakdown chart beside it, and a recent-activity table below

cards.name: Docs layout
cards.aka: three-column docs, documentation site, on-this-page TOC
cards.desc: Three columns: a tree of all pages on the left, the article in the middle at a readable width, and an "On this page" list of headings on the right that highlights the section you are reading.
cards.phrase: a three-column docs layout: left sidebar page tree with collapsible sections, center article max-w-prose with headings, code blocks and callouts, right "On this page" TOC that highlights the current heading on scroll (scroll-spy), search with ⌘K in the header

cards.name: Pricing table
cards.desc: Two to four plans side by side as cards, each with a price, who it is for, a checklist of what it includes and a button. The recommended plan is raised or outlined, and a toggle switches monthly and yearly prices.
cards.phrase: a 3-tier pricing section: monthly/yearly toggle with a "save 20%" badge, three cards with plan name, big price per month, one-line audience, ✓ feature list and a button; the middle plan outlined in the accent color with a "Most popular" badge

cards.name: Split screen
cards.desc: The page cut into two halves: one side is a strong image, color or quote, the other holds the actual task, like a sign-in form. On phones the visual half shrinks to a banner or disappears.
cards.phrase: a split-screen layout: left half a full-height brand panel with a gradient or image and a customer quote, right half a centered sign-in form (max-w-sm) with email, password, primary button and "Continue with Google"; stack to a single column under md

cards.name: Masonry grid
cards.desc: Cards of different heights packed into equal-width columns with no row lines, so each column fills from the top like bricks. Good for images whose shapes you do not control.
cards.phrase: a masonry grid: 4 equal columns (CSS columns-4 or a JS masonry layout), cards keep their natural image aspect ratio, consistent gutters, caption on hover, infinite load at the bottom; 2 columns on mobile

cards.name: Long-form article
cards.aka: editorial layout, reading layout, blog post
cards.desc: A single narrow column of text set for reading: a big headline, byline, about 65 characters per line, generous line height, with pull quotes and wide images that break out of the column now and then.
cards.phrase: a long-form article layout: max-w-[65ch] centered column, serif or high-quality sans body at 18–20px with 1.6 line height, large headline, byline with avatar and reading time, a drop cap, pull quotes, and images that break out wider than the text; thin reading-progress bar at the top

cards.name: Alternating feature rows
cards.desc: Feature sections stacked down the page, each a picture beside a short block of text, with the picture switching sides every row. The alternation keeps a long page from feeling repetitive.
cards.phrase: alternating feature rows: each row a two-column section (screenshot + text with eyebrow, heading, 2 lines and a "Learn more →" link), image side flips every row, generous vertical spacing; stacks image-first on mobile

cards.name: Sticky header
cards.aka: fixed header, sticky nav, frosted header
cards.desc: The top bar stays pinned while the page scrolls under it, often turning translucent with a blur and a hairline border once you scroll. Navigation and the main button are always one click away.
cards.phrase: a sticky header (position: sticky; top: 0) with a translucent background and backdrop-blur, a 1px bottom border and slight shadow that appear only after the page scrolls; keep it short, about 56–64px

cards.name: Mega menu
cards.aka: large dropdown, flyout menu, full-width menu
cards.desc: Hovering or clicking a top nav item opens a wide panel with grouped links, each with an icon and a one-line description, often with a featured item on the side. It shows a large site at a glance.
cards.phrase: a mega menu on the "Products" nav item: a full-width panel with 3 labeled columns of links (icon, title, one-line description) plus a featured card on the right; opens on hover with a short delay and on click, closes on Escape (Radix NavigationMenu)

cards.name: Hamburger and off-canvas menu
cards.aka: drawer menu, mobile nav, slide-out menu, ☰ menu
cards.desc: On small screens the nav links hide behind a ☰ button; tapping it slides a panel in from the side (or drops one from the top) over a dimmed page. Tapping outside or ✕ closes it.
cards.phrase: below md, collapse the nav into a ☰ button that opens a left off-canvas drawer (shadcn/ui Sheet) with large tap targets, the current page highlighted, a primary button at the bottom; dim the page behind, close on ✕, outside click or Escape, and trap focus while open

cards.name: Breadcrumbs
cards.aka: breadcrumb trail, path nav, location trail
cards.desc: A one-line trail like Home › Projects › Atlas › Settings showing where the page sits in the hierarchy. Every part except the last is a link back up.
cards.phrase: breadcrumbs above the page title (nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"): ancestors as muted links separated by ›, the current page in bold and not a link (aria-current="page"), middle items collapsing into a … dropdown when the trail is long

cards.name: Tabs
cards.aka: tab bar, underline tabs, segmented control
cards.desc: A row of labels that switch between sibling views of the same thing without leaving the page. Underline tabs suit page sections; pill or segmented tabs suit small toggles like Day/Week/Month.
cards.phrase: underline tabs under the page title (Radix Tabs / shadcn/ui Tabs): active tab with a 2px accent underline and bold label, arrow keys move between tabs, the selected tab is reflected in the URL

cards.name: Pagination, load more, or infinite scroll
cards.aka: page numbers, load more, endless scroll
cards.desc: Three ways to show a long list. Pagination splits it into numbered pages you can link to and return to; a "Load more" button sits in the middle, adding the next batch only when asked so the footer stays reachable; infinite scroll loads on its own as you near the bottom, which suits endless browsing but loses your place and the footer.
cards.phrase: pick by task: numbered pagination for results and tables (‹ Previous, first page, pages around the current one, …, last page, Next ›, current page in the URL as ?page=3); a "Load more" button as the middle option for catalogs and lists with a footer (appends the next batch, shows "Showing 40 of 212", keeps scroll position and moves focus to the first new item); infinite scroll only for feeds (IntersectionObserver on a sentinel, skeleton rows while loading, restore scroll position on back)

cards.name: Fat footer
cards.aka: sitemap footer, mega footer, doormat footer
cards.desc: A large footer that works as a sitemap: several columns of grouped links, the logo with a short line, a newsletter field, then a bottom strip with copyright, legal links and social icons.
cards.phrase: a fat footer: brand column with logo, one-line description and newsletter email field, then 4 link columns (Product, Company, Resources, Legal) with small uppercase headings, and a bottom bar with © year, theme/language switcher and social icons

cards.name: Command palette
cards.aka: ⌘K menu, quick switcher, spotlight search, kbar
cards.desc: Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K) anywhere and a search box opens over the page. Type a few letters to jump to any page or run any action, with keyboard shortcuts shown beside each result.
cards.phrase: a ⌘K / Ctrl+K command palette (cmdk / shadcn/ui CommandDialog): centered dialog near the top with a search input, grouped results (Suggestions, Navigation, Actions) with icons and shortcut hints on the right, fuzzy matching, arrow-key selection and Enter to run

cards.name: Data table
cards.aka: data grid, table view, admin table
cards.desc: Rows of records with sortable column headers, a search or filter bar above, row checkboxes for bulk actions, status badges, a ⋯ menu per row and pagination below.
cards.phrase: a data table (TanStack Table with shadcn/ui): filter input and faceted filter buttons above, sortable headers with ↑↓ indicators, row selection checkboxes with a bulk-action bar, colored status badges, a ⋯ row-actions menu, sticky header, and pagination with "N of M selected"

cards.name: Toast
cards.desc: A small message that slides in at a corner of the screen to confirm something happened ("Changes saved"), optionally with an Undo, then disappears on its own after a few seconds. Several toasts stack.
cards.phrase: toasts with Sonner: bottom-right stack that expands on hover, success/error/info variants with icons, an Undo action on destructive operations, auto-dismiss after ~5s (paused on hover), announced with role="status"

cards.name: Modal dialog
cards.desc: A box in the center of the screen over a dimmed page that you must deal with before going back. Best for short decisions like confirming a delete; longer tasks deserve their own page.
cards.phrase: a modal dialog using the native <dialog> element opened with showModal() (top layer, styled ::backdrop, inert page and Escape for free), or Radix AlertDialog in React: dimmed backdrop, centered panel max-w-md with title, one-sentence description, and right-aligned Cancel + red destructive button; focus trapped, Escape and backdrop click close it, focus returns to the trigger

cards.name: Popover and dropdown menu
cards.aka: context menu, kebab menu, overflow menu, flyout
cards.desc: A small floating panel anchored to the button that opened it. A dropdown menu lists actions with icons, keyboard shortcuts and separators; a popover can hold anything, like a date picker or a small form.
cards.phrase: a dropdown menu (Radix DropdownMenu / shadcn/ui) anchored to a ⋯ button: items with leading icons and right-aligned shortcuts, separators between groups, a submenu with ›, the destructive item in red at the bottom; full keyboard support and collision-aware positioning; for simple popovers use the native popover attribute with popovertarget (light dismiss and Escape built in) and CSS anchor positioning (position-anchor, position-area) instead of Floating UI where supported

cards.name: Form with inline validation
cards.aka: field validation, form errors, live validation
cards.desc: Each field checks itself after you leave it and shows the problem right under the field in red, saying how to fix it, instead of one list of errors at the top after you submit.
cards.phrase: a form with inline validation (React Hook Form + Zod): labels above inputs, validate on blur and then on change, red border and a specific fix-it message under the invalid field (aria-describedby), a green check on valid fields, a password strength meter, submit disabled while submitting with a spinner

cards.name: Combobox / autocomplete
cards.desc: A text field with a list of options underneath that narrows as you type. You can pick with the arrow keys and Enter, and the matching letters are highlighted. Unlike a plain select, it scales to hundreds of options.
cards.phrase: a combobox (WAI-ARIA combobox pattern via Headless UI Combobox or shadcn/ui Command in a Popover): typing filters the list, matched letters bolded, arrow keys move the active option, Enter selects, a ✓ beside the current value, and a "Create …" option when nothing matches

cards.name: Accordion
cards.aka: collapsible sections, expander, disclosure, FAQ list
cards.desc: A stack of headings that each expand to reveal their content when clicked, with a chevron that flips. It keeps long, skippable content like FAQs short until someone needs it.
cards.phrase: an accordion (Radix Accordion / shadcn/ui, or native <details>/<summary>): full-width rows with a question and a chevron that rotates on open, smooth height animation, single item open at a time, buttons with aria-expanded

cards.name: Kanban board
cards.desc: Columns for stages (To do, In progress, Done) holding cards you drag from one column to the next. The whole state of a project is visible at once.
cards.phrase: a kanban board: horizontally scrolling columns with title and count, cards with title, label chips and assignee avatar, drag and drop between and within columns (dnd-kit) with a lifted, tilted card while dragging and a drop placeholder, keyboard dragging supported

cards.name: Stepper / wizard
cards.desc: A long task split into numbered steps with a progress indicator at the top showing done, current and upcoming steps, and Back / Continue buttons at the bottom.
cards.phrase: a multi-step wizard: horizontal stepper with numbered circles (✓ for completed, ring for current, gray for upcoming) joined by a progress line, one step's fields per screen, Back and Continue buttons, "Step 3 of 4" label, progress kept in the URL so refresh does not lose it

cards.name: Sheet and drawer
cards.aka: side sheet, slide-over, side panel, bottom drawer, Vaul drawer
cards.desc: A panel that slides in from an edge over the page instead of a centered box. On desktop it comes from the right and keeps the page visible beside it; on phones it rises from the bottom, can be dragged down to close, and the page behind shrinks slightly.
cards.phrase: a responsive sheet: on desktop a right side sheet (shadcn/ui Sheet, about 400 to 480px) with title, scrollable body and a sticky footer with Cancel and Save, page dimmed but visible; under the md breakpoint switch to a Vaul-style bottom drawer with a grab handle, drag to dismiss with velocity, snap points, and the page behind scaled to about 0.95 with rounded corners; focus trapped, Escape closes

cards.name: Resizable panels
cards.aka: split view, splitter, panel group, draggable divider
cards.desc: Side-by-side panels separated by thin dividers you can drag to give one panel more room. The cursor changes to a resize arrow over the divider, and the app remembers the sizes next time.
cards.phrase: resizable panels (react-resizable-panels / shadcn/ui Resizable): a horizontal PanelGroup with sidebar, editor and preview, thin 1px dividers with a wider invisible hit area and a small grip, col-resize cursor and accent highlight while dragging, min and max sizes, double-click to reset, collapsible sidebar, sizes saved to localStorage (autoSaveId), and arrow keys move a focused divider

cards.name: Date picker and range calendar
cards.aka: calendar popover, date range picker, datepicker
cards.desc: A field that opens a small calendar for choosing a date, or a start and end date with the days between shaded. Range pickers often show two months side by side and a list of quick presets like "Last 7 days".
cards.phrase: a date range picker (react-day-picker in a shadcn/ui Popover, or React Aria DateRangePicker): a trigger field showing "Mar 12 – Mar 18, 2026" with a calendar icon, a popover with presets on the left (Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month), two months side by side, start and end days as filled circles with the days between shaded, today marked, disabled past dates, arrow-key navigation, Cancel and Apply in the footer; the text field also accepts typed dates

cards.name: File upload dropzone with progress
cards.aka: drag and drop upload, dropzone, file uploader
cards.desc: A large dashed area you can drop files onto or click to browse, followed by a list of the chosen files, each with its own progress bar, a check when done, and a clear message and retry when one fails.
cards.phrase: a file upload dropzone (react-dropzone): a dashed rounded area with an upload icon, "Drag files here or browse", and the accepted types and max size, highlighted in the accent color while dragging over; below it a list of files with icon, name, size, a per-file progress bar and percent, cancel (✕) while uploading, a check when done, and an inline error with Retry for failed or too-large files; the browse link is a real button for keyboard users

cards.name: One-time code input
cards.aka: OTP input, verification code, PIN input, 2FA code field
cards.desc: A row of single-character boxes for the 6-digit code from an email, text or authenticator app. Typing moves to the next box, pasting the whole code fills all of them, and the phone can offer the code from Messages automatically.
cards.phrase: a one-time code input (input-otp / shadcn/ui InputOTP): six digit slots in two groups of three, one real <input> underneath with inputmode="numeric" and autocomplete="one-time-code" so iOS and Android offer the code and pasting fills every slot, the active slot ringed with a blinking caret, auto-submit on the sixth digit, a "Resend code in 0:24" countdown, and a clear error state that shakes and clears the slots

cards.name: Tooltip vs. hover card
cards.aka: tooltip, hint, title text, hover card, preview card, profile popover
cards.desc: A tooltip is a tiny dark label that names an icon button, appears on hover or keyboard focus, and holds no links. A hover card is a richer floating preview, such as a user profile behind an @mention, that opens after a short delay and can contain buttons.
cards.phrase: tooltips (Radix Tooltip) on every icon-only button: short label plus keyboard shortcut, dark, small, shown on hover and focus after ~300ms, never containing interactive content; and a hover card (Radix HoverCard) on @mentions showing avatar, name, handle, one-line bio, follower count and a Follow button, opening after ~500ms and staying open while the pointer moves into it; on touch the mention just links to the profile

cards.name: Stacked toasts, Sonner-style
cards.desc: When several toasts arrive, they pile up into a neat deck in the corner, the newest in front and older ones peeking out smaller behind it. Hovering the stack fans them out into a list so each one can be read or acted on.
cards.phrase: stacked toasts with Sonner: newest toast in front at the bottom-right, up to 3 visible with older ones scaled to 0.95 and 0.9 and offset upward behind it, the stack expands into a spaced list on hover or focus (expand on hover), timers pause while expanded, each toast swipe-to-dismiss with an optional action button, rich colors for success and error, aria-live polite

cards.name: View transitions
cards.aka: shared-element transition, page morph, hero animation, magic move
cards.desc: When you go from one page to another, an element that exists on both (a thumbnail that becomes the big photo) visibly grows and moves into its new place while the rest of the page cross-fades. It keeps you oriented, like an app rather than a page reload.
cards.phrase: view transitions between list and detail: give the thumbnail and the detail hero image the same view-transition-name (e.g. photo-42) so the browser morphs one into the other, cross-fade the rest; use the View Transition API (document.startViewTransition() for SPA updates, @view-transition { navigation: auto } for multi-page), tune ::view-transition-group() duration to about 300ms, and skip it under prefers-reduced-motion

cards.name: Scroll-driven animation and scrollytelling
cards.aka: scroll animations, scroll-linked effects, scroll reveal, scrollytelling, sticky storytelling
cards.desc: Animation whose progress is tied to the scroll position instead of a clock: a reading-progress bar fills, sections fade and rise as they enter, and in scrollytelling a pinned graphic changes step by step while the text scrolls past beside it.
cards.phrase: scroll-driven animation in CSS: a top reading-progress bar using animation-timeline: scroll(), sections that fade and rise into view using animation-timeline: view() with animation-range: entry 0% cover 30%; a scrollytelling section with a position: sticky chart on one side whose state changes per text step on the other (IntersectionObserver or view timelines); everything static under prefers-reduced-motion

cards.name: Scroll-snap carousel
cards.aka: snap carousel, swipeable row, slider, horizontal scroller
cards.desc: A horizontal row of cards you swipe or scroll through, where each card settles neatly into place instead of stopping half-way. The next card peeks in at the edge so people know there is more.
cards.phrase: a scroll-snap carousel in plain CSS: overflow-x: auto with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory, cards with scroll-snap-align: start and a fixed width so the next card peeks in, scroll-padding matching the page gutter, hidden scrollbar, ‹ › buttons that scroll by one card (scrollBy with smooth behavior) and dot indicators, keyboard and touch both work; no autoplay

cards.name: Microinteractions
cards.desc: Tiny, quick animations that confirm a single action: a heart that pops with a burst when liked, a switch whose knob slides and changes color, a Copy button that turns into "Copied ✓" for a moment. Each one answers "did that work?" without words.
cards.phrase: microinteractions: a like button that scales to 1.2 and back with a small particle burst and an animated count, a toggle whose thumb slides with a spring and whose track changes color, a copy button that swaps its icon to a check and its label to "Copied" for 2 seconds; 150 to 300ms each, transform and opacity only, respect prefers-reduced-motion

cards.name: Hover reveal and cursor effects
cards.aka: hover state, hover card actions, cursor spotlight, custom cursor, magnetic button
cards.desc: Moving the mouse over an item lifts it and reveals extra actions or detail, sometimes with a soft spotlight that follows the cursor. Touch screens have no hover, so the same actions must be reachable another way there, such as always-visible buttons or a ⋯ menu.
cards.phrase: hover reveal on cards: on hover the card lifts (translateY(-2px), larger shadow) and an action bar fades in over the image; a subtle radial spotlight follows the cursor via CSS variables set on pointermove; wrap hover-only styling in @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), and on touch devices show the actions permanently or behind a ⋯ button, and make them reachable by keyboard with :focus-within

cards.name: The Linear look
cards.desc: Near-black backgrounds, white-to-gray gradient headlines, hairline borders that catch light at the top edge, and a soft colored glow behind the hero. Calm, precise and very high contrast.
cards.phrase: the Linear look: near-black background (#08090A), Inter with tight tracking, headlines with a white-to-gray gradient (bg-clip-text), 1px borders as a white/10 gradient brighter at the top, a soft indigo radial glow behind the hero, muted gray body text and restrained indigo (#5E6AD2) accents

cards.name: Stripe look
cards.aka: mesh gradient, angled sections, fintech style
cards.desc: Bright, blended mesh gradients cut by a diagonal edge, deep navy text on white, a confident violet button, and crisp floating product cards with soft shadows. Polished and optimistic.
cards.phrase: the Stripe look: an animated mesh gradient (violet #A960EE, coral #FF333D, sky #90E0FF, yellow #FFCB57) in a section clipped at a skewed angle (clip-path or -skew-y-6), deep navy #0A2540 headlines in a heavy sans like Söhne or Inter, slate #425466 body, a #635BFF pill button with a › arrow, floating white UI cards with layered soft shadows

cards.name: Vercel / Geist monochrome
cards.aka: Geist style, black and white, developer minimal
cards.desc: Pure black and white with grays in between, the Geist sans and mono typefaces, thin grid lines with small + marks at the crossings, and a single triangle logo. Color only appears in status and code.
cards.phrase: the Vercel / Geist look: pure #000 background (and #FFF in light mode), Geist Sans for text and Geist Mono for code and labels, 1px #333 borders forming a visible layout grid with small + marks at intersections, tight-tracked large headlines, white primary button with black text and a dark outlined secondary, color reserved for status

cards.name: shadcn/ui look
cards.aka: shadcn style, zinc neutral, Radix + Tailwind default
cards.desc: The default look of shadcn/ui: neutral zinc grays, white cards with 1px borders, rounded-md corners, small medium-weight labels and a near-black primary button. Clean, quiet, and instantly familiar to developers.
cards.phrase: the shadcn/ui look: neutral zinc palette (bg-background white, border-zinc-200, text-zinc-950, muted text-zinc-500), Geist or Inter at text-sm, cards with border and shadow-sm, rounded-md inputs and buttons with h-9, a zinc-900 primary button, outline secondary, focus ring-2 ring-zinc-950/10, use the stock shadcn/ui components

cards.name: Neo-brutalism
cards.desc: Loud flat colors, thick black outlines, hard offset shadows with no blur, chunky bold type and slightly crooked stickers. Playful and deliberately unpolished.
cards.phrase: neo-brutalism: flat saturated fills (yellow #FFDC58, pink #FF90E8, cyan #A6FAFF), border-2 or border-[3px] solid black on everything, hard offset shadows (shadow-[4px_4px_0_0_#000]) with no blur that shrink on press, bold grotesque type like Archivo Black or Space Grotesk, rotated sticker badges

cards.name: Editorial / magazine
cards.desc: A print-inspired page: a big serif masthead, thin black rules, multi-column grids of headlines with clear hierarchy, small-caps labels and plenty of white space on a paper-tinted background.
cards.phrase: an editorial magazine look: off-white paper background (#F7F3EA), a high-contrast serif for headlines (Instrument Serif, Playfair Display or GT Sectra) with a clean sans for body, a centered masthead between double rules, a 12-column grid with 1px black rules between stories, small-caps section kickers in one red accent (#C8102E)

cards.name: Notion-clean
cards.aka: Notion style, document-like UI, soft minimal
cards.desc: Feels like a well-kept document: lots of white, warm grays, a big emoji page icon and a cover image, simple checkboxes and toggles, and quiet hover handles. Content first, almost no chrome.
cards.phrase: a Notion-clean look: white page with warm grays (text #37352F, muted #787774, sidebar #F7F7F5), Inter or the system UI font at 16px, a full-width cover image and large emoji page icon above a big bold title, property rows in muted gray, simple checkbox lists, gray callout blocks with an emoji, ⋮⋮ drag handles shown only on hover

cards.name: Aurora gradients and glass
cards.aka: glassmorphism, frosted glass, aurora UI, blurred blobs
cards.desc: Large soft blobs of color drifting on a dark background, with translucent frosted panels floating above them. The panels blur whatever is behind, so the page glows through.
cards.phrase: aurora gradients with glass: dark background (#0B0B1A) with 3 large blurred color blobs (violet #7C3AED, cyan #06B6D4, pink #EC4899) slowly drifting, content on frosted panels (bg-white/10, backdrop-blur-xl, border border-white/20, rounded-2xl) with white text; ensure text contrast stays above 4.5:1

cards.name: Y2K / retro web
cards.aka: Y2K aesthetic, Web 1.0, GeoCities style, chrome and bubble
cards.desc: Late-90s and early-2000s web nostalgia: chrome and bubble lettering, glossy beveled buttons, sky-blue and silver gradients, sparkles, marquees and a hit counter. Fun on purpose.
cards.phrase: a Y2K retro web look: sky-blue to silver gradient background with ✦ sparkles, chrome gradient display text (Arial Black with a metallic linear-gradient via bg-clip-text and a dark outline), glossy pill buttons with a white highlight and outset bevel, a scrolling marquee strip, pixel-perfect 1px borders, a black hit counter in green digits

cards.name: Oversized and kinetic typography
cards.aka: big type, kinetic type, type-led design, marquee text, outline text
cards.desc: Type is the main visual: headlines so large they run off the edge of the screen, words in outline, and lines of text that slide, scroll or react as you move. Few or no images.
cards.phrase: an oversized, kinetic type layout: a display headline in a variable grotesk at clamp(4rem, 14vw, 12rem) with tight -0.04em tracking that bleeds off the right edge, a second line as outlined text (-webkit-text-stroke with transparent fill), a slowly scrolling marquee band of repeated words, letters that shift weight on scroll via font-variation-settings; small 14 to 16px body copy for contrast, motion off under prefers-reduced-motion

cards.name: Terminal / dev-tool aesthetic
cards.aka: terminal style website, hacker aesthetic, monospace site, CLI-inspired web
cards.desc: A website styled like a terminal or code editor: dark background, everything in a monospace font, a blinking cursor, $ prompts, bracketed links and thin box borders. It signals "built for developers" at a glance.
cards.phrase: a terminal / dev-tool aesthetic for the web: near-black background (#0B0E14), a monospace font for everything (JetBrains Mono, Geist Mono or Berkeley Mono), one phosphor accent (green #7EE787 or amber), a hero that types out a command with a blinking block cursor, a copyable install command in a $ prompt box, links styled as [docs] [github], features in 1px bordered boxes with box-drawing headers like ┌─ deploy ─┐, and keyboard shortcuts shown inline

cards.name: Claymorphism
cards.aka: clay UI, soft 3D, puffy UI, inflated UI
cards.desc: Soft, rounded, pastel shapes that look inflated or made of modeling clay, using a soft drop shadow outside plus a light inner highlight and a darker inner shadow. Friendly and toy-like.
cards.phrase: claymorphism: pastel fills (lavender, mint, peach), very large radii (24 to 32px), each surface with three shadows (a soft outer drop shadow like 12px 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.12), an inset light highlight top-left and an inset darker shade bottom-right), chunky rounded type like Nunito or Baloo 2, puffy buttons that squash slightly on press, 3D clay-style illustrations; keep text contrast at WCAG AA despite the pastels

cards.name: Tab bar
cards.desc: A bar along the bottom with 3 to 5 icons and labels, one for each top-level section of the app. Each tab keeps its own navigation history, and in iOS 26 the bar floats above the content as a Liquid Glass capsule.
cards.phrase: a bottom tab bar (SwiftUI TabView with Tab items) with 4 top-level sections, SF Symbol icons with short labels and badges, each tab keeping its own NavigationStack, plus a search tab (Tab(role: .search))

cards.name: Large title navigation bar
cards.desc: The screen title starts big and bold at the top left, then shrinks into a small centered title in the bar as you scroll. In iOS 26 the bar has no solid background: its buttons float as Liquid Glass capsules over the content, and a soft edge effect keeps the small title readable once content scrolls under it.
cards.phrase: a large-title navigation bar (NavigationStack with .navigationTitle and .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.large)) that collapses to a small inline title when the list scrolls, toolbar buttons at the trailing edge

cards.name: Push navigation
cards.desc: Tapping a row slides the next screen in from the right, with a back button named after the previous screen. Swiping from the left edge goes back.
cards.phrase: drill-down push navigation with NavigationStack and NavigationLink: list rows with trailing chevrons push a detail screen, a back button labeled with the previous title, and edge swipe to go back

cards.name: Sheet with detents
cards.aka: half sheet, bottom sheet, modal sheet, page sheet
cards.desc: A card slides up over the current screen for a focused task, with a grabber at the top. It rests at a medium (about half height) or large detent. In iOS 26 a partial-height sheet is Liquid Glass, inset from the screen edges, with no dimming behind it; at the large detent it becomes opaque and the page behind recedes.
cards.phrase: a sheet presented with .sheet and .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]), a visible grabber (.presentationDragIndicator(.visible)), Cancel and Add buttons in its toolbar; Liquid Glass sheet inset from the edges at the medium detent, the page behind receding only at the large detent

cards.name: Full-screen cover
cards.desc: A modal that slides up and takes the entire screen, with nothing peeking behind it and no swipe down to dismiss. It always needs an explicit close or finish button.
cards.phrase: present the flow with .fullScreenCover so it covers the whole screen including the status bar area, with an explicit close (xmark) or End button and no swipe-to-dismiss

cards.name: Sidebar split view
cards.desc: On iPad the app shows a sidebar of sections, a list, and the selected item side by side. On iPhone the same view collapses into a push navigation stack automatically.
cards.phrase: an iPad layout with NavigationSplitView: a sidebar of sections, a content list and a detail pane, the sidebar collapsible, falling back to a stack on iPhone

cards.name: Search bar
cards.aka: searchable, search field, scope bar, search suggestions
cards.desc: A rounded search field with a magnifying glass and a Cancel button while active, optional scope buttons to narrow what is searched, and suggestions that update as you type. In iOS 26 search usually lives at the bottom, in the toolbar or as its own search tab at the trailing end of the tab bar, rather than at the top of the screen.
cards.phrase: search with .searchable(text:), placed at the bottom as in iOS 26 (in the bottom toolbar, or a Tab(role: .search) in the tab bar), scope buttons via .searchScopes for categories, and live .searchSuggestions with the typed text highlighted, results updating as you type

cards.name: Tab bar minimize and bottom accessory
cards.aka: collapsing tab bar, mini player bar, tabViewBottomAccessory
cards.desc: In iOS 26 the floating tab bar shrinks to a single button when you scroll down, giving the content more room. A bottom accessory, like a Now Playing mini player, sits above the tab bar and slides inline beside it when the bar shrinks.
cards.phrase: a TabView whose floating glass tab bar collapses to a single button on scroll (.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)), with a Now Playing mini player in .tabViewBottomAccessory that sits above the bar and moves inline when it minimizes

cards.name: Search tab
cards.aka: search role tab, bottom search, Tab(role: .search)
cards.desc: Search gets its own tab, drawn as a separate glass circle at the trailing end of the tab bar. Tapping it turns the bottom of the screen into a search field, with the other tabs collapsed to one button.
cards.phrase: a dedicated search tab (Tab(role: .search)) that iOS sets apart at the trailing end of the tab bar; selecting it shows a bottom search field with .searchable on the TabView, suggestions and recent searches above it

cards.name: iPadOS windowing and the menu bar
cards.aka: resizable windows, multiwindow, window tiling, iPad menu bar
cards.desc: Since iPadOS 26, apps run in freely resizable windows that can overlap, with close, minimize and tile controls at the top left. Swiping down from the top or moving the pointer there reveals a Mac-style menu bar listing every command the app has.
cards.phrase: iPadOS 26 windowing: multiple scenes (WindowGroup, UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes) with layouts that adapt to any window size, and a full menu bar defined with .commands (CommandMenu, CommandGroup) giving every action a keyboard shortcut

cards.name: Popover on iPad
cards.desc: On iPad a popover is a small rounded panel with an arrow that points at the button that opened it, and tapping outside closes it. On iPhone, or in a narrow iPad window, the same content becomes a sheet.
cards.phrase: a .popover(isPresented:attachmentAnchor:arrowEdge:) anchored to its toolbar button on iPad, adapting to a sheet in compact width on iPhone (tune with .presentationCompactAdaptation)

cards.name: Inset grouped list
cards.aka: grouped table view, Settings-style list, Form
cards.desc: Rows in rounded groups that float on a gray background, each row with an optional colored icon, a value, and a chevron or toggle. It is the standard look for settings and forms.
cards.phrase: an inset grouped List (.listStyle(.insetGrouped)) or Form: rounded sections on the grouped background, rows with white SF Symbols on colored rounded-square icons, trailing values, chevrons and toggles, plus section headers and footers

cards.name: Swipe actions
cards.aka: swipe to delete, row actions, leading and trailing actions
cards.desc: Swiping a list row sideways reveals colored buttons behind it, such as Delete, Flag or Archive. A full swipe performs the first action without lifting your finger.
cards.phrase: list rows with .swipeActions: trailing red Delete (role: .destructive) and orange Flag, leading blue Mark as Read, full swipe performs the first action

cards.name: Context menu
cards.aka: long-press menu, peek, contextMenu with preview
cards.desc: Pressing and holding an item lifts it into a larger preview while everything else blurs, with a menu of actions underneath. It is how iOS exposes secondary actions without visible buttons.
cards.phrase: a long-press .contextMenu with a preview (contextMenu(menuItems:preview:)): Copy, Share and Favorite, then a red destructive Delete in its own section

cards.name: Confirmation dialog
cards.desc: A short list of choices that rises from the bottom, or attaches to the button that opened it on iPad, usually to confirm a destructive action. Cancel sits apart from the rest.
cards.phrase: a .confirmationDialog with a short title, the destructive choice in red (role: .destructive) and a separate Cancel button

cards.name: Segmented control
cards.desc: A row of 2 to 5 equal segments in a gray track, with the selected one raised as a white pill. It switches between views or filters of the same content.
cards.phrase: a segmented control (Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented)) of 2 to 5 short options that switches the view of the same data below it

cards.name: Pickers
cards.aka: wheel picker, pop-up button, menu picker, date picker
cards.desc: Ways to choose a value: spinning wheels for times and short lists, a button that shows the current choice and opens a menu, and a calendar grid for dates. Compact styles show a small button that expands into the full picker.
cards.phrase: native pickers: Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) for a few options, DatePicker with .datePickerStyle(.graphical) for dates and .wheel for times

cards.name: Alert
cards.desc: A small centered card that interrupts with a title, a short message and one to three buttons. The screen behind dims and nothing else responds until you choose.
cards.phrase: an .alert with a short question as the title, a one-line explanation, a Cancel button (role: .cancel) and a red destructive action (role: .destructive)

cards.name: SF Symbols
cards.desc: Apple's library of thousands of icons, drawn to sit beside San Francisco text in nine weights and three scales. They render in monochrome, hierarchical, palette or multicolor modes and can animate with symbol effects.
cards.phrase: SF Symbols for every icon (Image(systemName:)), matched to the adjacent text weight, with .symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical) and .symbolEffect animations where they help

cards.name: Pull to refresh
cards.desc: Dragging the top of a list down reveals a spinning activity indicator, and letting go reloads the content. The list springs back up when loading finishes.
cards.phrase: pull to refresh on the list with .refreshable { await reload() }, showing the native spinner under the large title

cards.name: Pull-down menu
cards.aka: Menu button, pull-down button, UIMenu, overflow menu
cards.desc: Tapping a button, often a circle with three dots, opens a compact menu right where the button is, with grouped commands, checkmarks for the current choice and submenus. It is the standard way to tuck away secondary actions on iOS.
cards.phrase: a pull-down Menu from a toolbar button (SwiftUI Menu, or UIButton with .menu and showsMenuAsPrimaryAction): grouped Sections with SF Symbols, a Sort By submenu with a Picker for the checkmarked choice, and a destructive item last

cards.name: Share sheet
cards.desc: The system sheet that opens from the share button (a square with an arrow pointing up). It shows a preview of what is being shared, nearby people and recent contacts, apps to send to, and a list of actions like Copy and Save to Files.
cards.phrase: a share button using ShareLink(item:subject:message:preview:) (UIActivityViewController in UIKit) with the square.and.arrow.up symbol, sharing a URL or Transferable item with a title and thumbnail preview

cards.name: Page control and paged carousel
cards.aka: page dots, UIPageControl, paging TabView, carousel
cards.desc: Content you swipe through sideways one page at a time, with a row of small dots underneath that shows how many pages there are and which one you are on. The next card often peeks in from the edge to hint that there is more.
cards.phrase: a horizontally paged carousel (TabView with .tabViewStyle(.page) and .indexViewStyle(.page(backgroundDisplayMode: .always)), or a ScrollView with .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned) and peeking neighbors) with page dots showing the current page

cards.name: TipKit tips
cards.aka: feature tips, coach marks, popover tip, TipView
cards.desc: A small card that points out a feature the person has not tried yet, either as a popover with an arrow at the button it explains or inline in the content. It has a title, a short message and a close button, and it stops appearing once the feature is used.
cards.phrase: feature tips with TipKit: a Tip with a title, message and SF Symbol image, shown as a popover on the button it explains (.popoverTip(tip)) or inline (TipView(tip)), Tips.configure() at launch, with rules and invalidation so each tip shows once

cards.name: Grouped toolbar items
cards.aka: glass toolbar groups, ToolbarSpacer, prominent Done button
cards.desc: In iOS 26 toolbar buttons float as glass capsules, with related buttons sharing one capsule and spacers splitting the groups apart. The confirming action, such as Done, is a checkmark in a tinted, prominent circle at the trailing edge.
cards.phrase: iOS 26 toolbars with related buttons grouped in shared glass capsules (ToolbarItemGroup), ToolbarSpacer(.fixed) or ToolbarSpacer(.flexible) between groups, and the Done action as a tinted checkmark using .buttonStyle(.glassProminent) (or Button(role: .confirm)) at the trailing edge

cards.name: Home Screen widgets
cards.desc: Small, medium or large tiles on the Home Screen that show live information from an app without opening it. They are snapshots refreshed on a timeline, and can include simple buttons and toggles.
cards.phrase: a WidgetKit widget in small and medium sizes (.systemSmall, .systemMedium) showing one glanceable value, refreshed by a TimelineProvider, tapping deep-links into the app

cards.name: Live Activities and the Dynamic Island
cards.desc: A live card on the Lock Screen for something happening right now, like a delivery, a ride or a game. The same activity sits in the Dynamic Island around the camera and expands when you press it.
cards.phrase: a Live Activity (ActivityKit) with a Lock Screen card showing ETA and a progress track, plus Dynamic Island compact leading/trailing, minimal and expanded layouts

cards.name: Notifications
cards.desc: Banners on the Lock Screen and over other apps, with the app icon, a title and a short body, stacked by app or thread. They can carry actions and an interruption level from passive to time sensitive.
cards.phrase: local and push notifications (UserNotifications) with clear titles, thread grouping (threadIdentifier), actionable buttons, and the right interruption level (.passive, .active, .timeSensitive)

cards.name: App icon
cards.aka: Home Screen icon, Icon Composer icon
cards.desc: One square artwork that the system masks into a rounded squircle. Icons now ship in default, dark, clear and tinted appearances, and in iOS 26 they are built from layers that pick up the Liquid Glass look.
cards.phrase: an app icon built as layers in Icon Composer: one simple bold glyph on a gradient background, with default, dark, clear and tinted appearances, no text, no baked-in rounded corners

cards.name: Haptics
cards.desc: Short vibrations that confirm what happened: a crisp tick as a picker snaps, a double tap for success, a buzz for an error. Used sparingly, they make controls feel physical.
cards.phrase: subtle haptics with .sensoryFeedback: .selection on picker changes, .success after saving, .error on failure, .impact when something snaps into place; never on every tap

cards.name: Controls
cards.aka: Control Center controls, Lock Screen controls, Action button, ControlWidget
cards.desc: Small buttons and toggles an app can offer outside itself: in Control Center, in the two Lock Screen slots at the bottom, and on the Action button. Each is one icon, a short name and an on or off state that runs an app action without opening the app.
cards.phrase: a ControlWidget (WidgetKit, iOS 18 and later) with a ControlWidgetToggle or ControlWidgetButton backed by an App Intent, usable in Control Center, on the Lock Screen and with the Action button, with an SF Symbol, a short title and a tint for the on state

cards.name: Liquid Glass
cards.desc: Apple's design language since iOS 26: controls float above the content on translucent glass that bends and tints with whatever is behind it. Tab bars and toolbars are capsules that shrink as you scroll so content fills the screen.
cards.phrase: the iOS 26 Liquid Glass look: a floating glass tab bar that minimizes on scroll (.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)), toolbar buttons grouped in glass capsules, custom floating controls with .glassEffect() inside a GlassEffectContainer, content running edge to edge beneath

cards.name: Blur materials and vibrancy
cards.desc: Translucent layers that blur what is behind them, in thicknesses from ultra thin to thick, with vibrant text and icons that stay readable over any background. In iOS 26 Liquid Glass is for controls and navigation that float above content; these blur materials remain the choice for the content layer itself, such as cards and backgrounds.
cards.phrase: translucent backgrounds using SwiftUI Material (.ultraThinMaterial through .thickMaterial) with hierarchical foreground styles (.primary, .secondary) instead of fixed colors, so text stays readable over photos

cards.name: Dynamic Type
cards.aka: text size, accessibility text sizes, scalable fonts
cards.desc: People pick their text size in Settings, from xSmall up to five extra accessibility sizes, and apps scale with it. At the largest sizes layouts should reflow, stacking side-by-side items vertically instead of truncating.
cards.phrase: support Dynamic Type everywhere: semantic text styles (.font(.body), .headline) rather than fixed sizes, @ScaledMetric for icon sizes and spacing, and layouts that stack vertically at accessibility sizes (ViewThatFits or dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize)

cards.name: SF Pro and the type scale
cards.aka: San Francisco, text styles, system font
cards.desc: iOS text uses SF Pro in a fixed set of named styles, from Large Title at 34 pt down to Caption 2 at 11 pt, with Body at 17 pt. Using the style names instead of point sizes gets correct weights, spacing and Dynamic Type for free.
cards.phrase: the system font with semantic text styles only (.largeTitle, .title, .headline, .body, .subheadline, .footnote, .caption), bold large titles, no hard-coded font sizes

cards.name: Tint and semantic colors
cards.aka: accent color, system colors, dynamic colors
cards.desc: One app tint marks everything you can tap: buttons, links, toggles, the selected tab. Everything else uses semantic colors like label and systemBackground that adapt automatically to dark mode and increased contrast.
cards.phrase: a single app accent color set as the AccentColor asset and .tint, used only for interactive elements, with semantic system colors (Color(.label), .secondaryLabel, .systemBackground, .separator) everywhere else so dark mode works

cards.name: Spring animations and zoom transitions
cards.aka: spring animation, matched geometry, hero transition
cards.desc: Motion on iOS uses springs, described by a duration and a bounce, which can be interrupted mid-flight and carry the momentum of your finger. Zoom transitions grow a tapped thumbnail into the next screen and shrink it back when you leave.
cards.phrase: spring animations for all motion (.spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.2), withAnimation(.snappy)), and zoom transitions from thumbnails to detail screens (.navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:)) with .matchedTransitionSource)

cards.name: Scroll edge effect
cards.desc: In iOS 26 there is no solid bar behind floating controls. Instead, content fades and blurs softly as it scrolls under them, or, with the hard style, stops at a crisper edge that suits dense text and pinned headers.
cards.phrase: let content scroll under floating glass bars using the iOS 26 scroll edge effect: .scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.soft, for: .top) by default, .hard where pinned headers or dense text need a crisper edge, and custom bars added with .safeAreaBar(edge:) so they get the effect

cards.name: Concentric corners
cards.desc: Shapes nested inside each other share the same corner center, so an inner card's radius is the outer radius minus the gap between them. iOS 26 aligns controls, sheets and windows to the rounded corners of the hardware this way, and SwiftUI can compute it for you.
cards.phrase: concentric corners for nested shapes: ConcentricRectangle() or .rect(corners: .concentric) for cards and buttons inside sheets and containers, with .containerShape() setting the outer shape, instead of hard-coded corner radii

cards.name: Top app bar
cards.aka: app bar, toolbar, action bar (older Android)
cards.desc: The bar at the top of a screen with a navigation icon, the screen title and a few action icons. It comes in four sizes: small, center-aligned, medium and large, and the medium and large ones collapse into the small one as you scroll.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 top app bar: LargeTopAppBar on top-level screens that collapses to a 64dp small bar on scroll (TopAppBarDefaults.exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior), CenterAlignedTopAppBar or TopAppBar on detail screens, navigation icon on the left and at most 2 to 3 action icons on the right

cards.name: Navigation bar
cards.aka: bottom navigation, bottom nav bar, tab bar (iOS)
cards.desc: A bar along the bottom with three to five top-level destinations, each an icon with a short label, the current one inside a rounded pill called the active indicator. Material 3 Expressive adds a shorter flexible navigation bar that can put labels beside the icons in medium-width windows.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 navigation bar (Compose NavigationBar with NavigationBarItem) with 4 destinations, icon plus label on each, a tonal pill active indicator behind the selected icon, filled icon when selected and outlined otherwise

cards.name: Navigation rail
cards.desc: A narrow vertical strip on the left edge that holds the same top-level destinations as a navigation bar, plus an optional menu button and FAB at the top. It replaces the bottom bar once the screen is wide enough.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 navigation rail (Compose NavigationRail, or NavigationSuiteScaffold to switch automatically between bar and rail by window size class) on medium and expanded widths: 80dp wide, menu icon and FAB at the top, destinations with pill indicators below

cards.name: Navigation drawer
cards.aka: side drawer, hamburger menu, modal drawer
cards.desc: A panel that slides in from the left over a dimmed screen when you tap the menu icon, listing every destination with icons, counts and section headers. Material 3 Expressive is deprecating it in favor of the expanded navigation rail, which shows the same labeled list without hiding it behind a tap.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 modal navigation drawer (Compose ModalNavigationDrawer with ModalDrawerSheet and NavigationDrawerItem) opened from the top app bar menu icon or an edge swipe, scrim over the content, full-width rounded active indicator on the current item, section headers and item badges

cards.name: Predictive back
cards.desc: As you start the back swipe from the screen edge, the current screen shrinks and slides with your finger so you can see where back will take you before you let go. Release to go back, or drag back to cancel.
cards.phrase: support predictive back (android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true"): use Navigation Compose so screen transitions follow the gesture, and PredictiveBackHandler for custom surfaces like sheets and search, scaling and shifting the outgoing screen with the swipe progress

cards.name: Edge-to-edge
cards.aka: draw behind system bars, window insets, immersive layout
cards.desc: The app draws all the way under the transparent status bar and gesture bar, then pads only the content that must stay readable or tappable. Headers and photos bleed to the top edge; lists scroll underneath the gesture handle.
cards.phrase: edge-to-edge layout: call enableEdgeToEdge(), let the hero image and app bar background draw behind the status bar, apply WindowInsets.safeDrawing padding (Scaffold contentWindowInsets) to text and buttons, and let lists scroll under a transparent gesture navigation bar

cards.name: List-detail layout
cards.aka: canonical layout, adaptive layout, two-pane, master-detail
cards.desc: On a phone the list and the detail are separate screens; on a tablet or unfolded foldable they sit side by side, and selecting an item fills the right pane instead of navigating. One of Material's three canonical layouts, with supporting pane and feed.
cards.phrase: an adaptive list-detail layout (Compose ListDetailPaneScaffold from material3-adaptive): single pane on compact widths, list and detail side by side at 600dp and up, the selected list item highlighted, navigation rail on the left, back from detail returns to list on phones

cards.name: Floating and docked toolbars
cards.aka: floating toolbar, docked toolbar, bottom app bar (older M3)
cards.desc: A row of actions for the current screen. The floating kind is a short pill that hovers above the content near the bottom, often with a FAB beside it; the docked kind is a full-width strip at the bottom. Material 3 Expressive uses these in place of the bottom app bar.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 Expressive floating toolbar: HorizontalFloatingToolbar centered near the bottom (offset FloatingToolbarDefaults.ScreenOffset) with 4 to 5 icon toggles and a FAB attached via the floatingActionButton slot, hiding on scroll down (FloatingToolbarDefaults.exitAlwaysScrollBehavior); use a docked toolbar (FlexibleBottomAppBar) instead of BottomAppBar when the actions should span the full width

cards.name: Window size classes and the supporting pane
cards.aka: breakpoints, adaptive layout, responsive layout (Android), canonical layouts
cards.desc: Android sorts the window width into five classes: compact below 600dp, medium from 600dp, expanded from 840dp, large from 1200dp and extra-large from 1600dp. The layout changes at each step: the bottom bar becomes a rail, one pane becomes two, and a supporting pane can appear beside the main content.
cards.phrase: an adaptive layout driven by window size classes (currentWindowAdaptiveInfo().windowSizeClass, breakpoints 600 / 840 / 1200 / 1600dp): NavigationSuiteScaffold to switch from navigation bar to rail automatically, ListDetailPaneScaffold for list and detail at expanded width, and SupportingPaneScaffold to show related content in a side pane on wide windows that moves below or into a sheet on compact ones

cards.name: Foldable postures
cards.aka: tabletop mode, book mode, flex mode, hinge-aware layout
cards.desc: A half-folded phone can stand like a laptop (tabletop) or be held open like a book. Hinge-aware apps put the content on one half and controls on the other, like a video above and playback controls on the flat half, and never place a button across the fold.
cards.phrase: hinge-aware layouts using Jetpack WindowManager (WindowInfoTracker.windowLayoutInfo): when a FoldingFeature is HALF_OPENED and HORIZONTAL (tabletop), put the video or viewfinder above the fold and controls below it; when VERTICAL (book), split into two panes at the fold bounds; keep touch targets and text off the hinge when isSeparating is true

cards.name: Floating action button
cards.desc: A rounded-square button that floats above the content in the bottom-right corner for the single most important action on the screen, like compose or create. The extended version adds a label and shrinks back to an icon as you scroll.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 floating action button bottom-right with 16dp margins for the primary action: ExtendedFloatingActionButton with icon and label that collapses to a 56dp FloatingActionButton on scroll (expanded = !listState.isScrollInProgress), primaryContainer color, 16dp corner radius

cards.name: Bottom sheet
cards.aka: modal bottom sheet, action sheet (iOS), standard bottom sheet
cards.desc: A surface that slides up from the bottom edge with a small drag handle on top, holding actions or extra detail for the current screen. The modal kind dims the screen behind it; the standard kind sits alongside the content and can be dragged between heights.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 modal bottom sheet (Compose ModalBottomSheet with rememberModalBottomSheetState) with a drag handle, 28dp top corners, surfaceContainerLow color and a scrim; swipe down or tap the scrim to dismiss, and it supports predictive back

cards.name: Snackbar
cards.desc: A short message in a dark strip near the bottom of the screen that confirms what just happened, often with one action like Undo. It disappears on its own after a few seconds.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 snackbar via Scaffold snackbarHost and SnackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message, actionLabel = "Undo"), inverse surface colors, one action at most, shown above the navigation bar and pushing the FAB up

cards.name: Chips
cards.aka: filter chips, tags, pills, input chips
cards.desc: Small 32dp rounded-rectangle buttons in four kinds: assist chips suggest an action, filter chips toggle a filter with a checkmark, input chips hold an entered value like a contact, and suggestion chips offer quick replies.
cards.phrase: Material 3 chips: a horizontally scrolling row of FilterChip with a leading checkmark when selected, AssistChip with a leading icon for contextual actions, InputChip with avatar and trailing close for entered values, SuggestionChip for quick replies; 32dp tall, 8dp corners

cards.name: Cards
cards.aka: elevated card, filled card, outlined card
cards.desc: A container for one item, like a place, a post or a product, with 12dp rounded corners. Material 3 has three kinds that differ only in how they separate from the background: a soft shadow, a tinted fill, or a thin outline.
cards.phrase: Material 3 cards with 12dp corners: Card (filled, surfaceContainerHighest) for grouped content, ElevatedCard for items that need to lift off a busy background, OutlinedCard in dense layouts; the whole card is one tap target with a ripple

cards.name: Dialog
cards.desc: A rounded panel in the middle of a dimmed screen that asks for a decision before you continue, with an optional icon, a headline, a sentence of detail and text buttons at the bottom right.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 basic dialog (Compose AlertDialog) with 28dp corners and surfaceContainerHigh color: optional centered icon, a question as the headline, one sentence of supporting text, and text buttons bottom-right with the confirming verb ("Discard") on the right and "Cancel" on its left

cards.name: Segmented buttons (legacy)
cards.aka: segmented control (iOS), toggle button group, button group
cards.desc: A pill-shaped row of two to five joined options where the selected ones are tinted and get a checkmark, allowing one choice or several. Material 3 Expressive deprecates them in favor of connected button groups, so prefer those in new designs.
cards.phrase: Material 3 segmented buttons: SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow with SegmentedButton for a Day / Week / Month switcher, MultiChoiceSegmentedButtonRow for multi-select filters, 40dp tall, checkmark icon on selected segments

cards.name: Search bar and search view
cards.aka: search bar, docked search, full-screen search
cards.desc: A tall pill-shaped field at the top of the screen with a leading icon and often your avatar. Tapping it expands into a full-screen search view with a back arrow, recent searches and live suggestions.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 search bar (Compose SearchBar) at the top: 56dp pill on surfaceContainerHigh with a leading icon and the account avatar trailing; on tap it expands to a full-screen search view with back arrow, recent searches with history icons and suggestions; use DockedSearchBar on tablets

cards.name: Ripple and state layers
cards.aka: ink ripple, touch feedback, hover and pressed states
cards.desc: Every tappable thing answers a touch with a ripple that spreads from your finger, and hover, focus, press and drag each lay a faint tint of the content color over the element. It is how Material shows that something is interactive and was hit.
cards.phrase: Material 3 interaction states on every clickable element: a bounded ripple from the touch point (Modifier.clickable with ripple()) and state layers of the content color at 8% hover, 10% focus, 10% pressed and 16% dragged, plus a visible focus ring for keyboard users

cards.name: Button groups
cards.aka: connected button group, toggle button group, segmented buttons (older M3)
cards.desc: A row of related buttons that react to each other: when you press one it widens and its corners square off, and its neighbors shrink to make room. The connected kind joins the buttons with small gaps and rounds only the outer ends; the selected one turns fully round.
cards.phrase: Material 3 Expressive button groups: a standard ButtonGroup of icon ToggleButtons that widen and morph from round to square when pressed (animateWidth), and a connected button group for single-select view switching, built from ToggleButtons with ButtonGroupDefaults.connectedLeadingButtonShapes(), connectedMiddleButtonShapes() and connectedTrailingButtonShapes(), 2dp apart, the checked button fully rounded with a check icon

cards.name: Split button
cards.aka: split dropdown button, menu button with default action
cards.desc: A button cut into two halves: the main part runs the usual action and the small arrow part opens a menu of related choices. When the menu opens, the arrow half turns into a circle and the chevron flips.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 Expressive split button (Compose SplitButtonLayout with SplitButtonDefaults.LeadingButton and SplitButtonDefaults.TrailingButton): the leading half runs the default action, the trailing chevron half toggles a DropdownMenu of variants, the trailing half morphs to a circle and the chevron rotates 180 degrees while open; filled, tonal, outlined and elevated variants

cards.name: FAB menu
cards.aka: speed dial, expandable FAB, floating action menu
cards.desc: Tapping the floating action button opens a short stack of labeled pill buttons above it, and the FAB itself turns into a round close button. It replaces the old speed dial of tiny unlabeled circles.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 Expressive FAB menu (Compose FloatingActionButtonMenu with a ToggleFloatingActionButton and FloatingActionButtonMenuItem entries): 2 to 6 labeled pill items stacked above the FAB in primaryContainer color, the FAB morphing from rounded square to a circle with a close icon when expanded, predictive back and tapping outside collapse it

cards.name: Carousel
cards.aka: image carousel, horizontal scroller, hero carousel
cards.desc: A horizontal row of rounded image cards that change width as they scroll, so a large item sits next to smaller ones that peek in and show there is more. Variants keep one big centered hero item, or let items keep one size and run off the edge.
cards.phrase: a Material 3 carousel: HorizontalMultiBrowseCarousel (rememberCarouselState, preferredItemWidth 186dp) with items clipped by Modifier.maskClip(MaterialTheme.shapes.extraLarge) so large, medium and small items reshape as they scroll; HorizontalCenteredHeroCarousel for one featured item and HorizontalUncontainedCarousel for equal-width items; text over images only on the large item

cards.name: Loading indicator
cards.aka: shape-morphing loader, expressive spinner, contained loading indicator
cards.desc: A small shape that spins while morphing through rounded shapes like a burst, a cookie, a pill and an oval. It is Material 3 Expressive's replacement for the indeterminate circular spinner, and the contained version sits on a colored circle for pull to refresh.
cards.phrase: the Material 3 Expressive LoadingIndicator for short indeterminate waits (shape morphing through MaterialShapes), ContainedLoadingIndicator on a primaryContainer circle as the pull-to-refresh indicator (PullToRefreshBox with indicator = PullToRefreshDefaults.LoadingIndicator), and wavy LinearWavyProgressIndicator when progress is known

cards.name: Dynamic color
cards.desc: Android picks a source color from the wallpaper and builds a whole palette from it, so every app that opts in shares the same tones as the home screen. Buttons, chips, pills and surfaces all take a tint of it, in light and dark.
cards.phrase: Material You dynamic color: on Android 12+ use dynamicLightColorScheme(context) / dynamicDarkColorScheme(context) in MaterialTheme, with a fallback color scheme generated from the brand color in Material Theme Builder; style everything with color roles (primary, primaryContainer, surfaceContainer, onSurfaceVariant) instead of hex values

cards.name: Material 3 Expressive
cards.desc: The 2025 update to Material 3 that makes apps feel livelier: bigger and bolder headlines, a library of playful shapes that morph into each other, buttons that change shape when pressed, and spring-based motion that slightly overshoots and settles.
cards.phrase: the Material 3 Expressive style (MaterialExpressiveTheme with MotionScheme.expressive()): emphasized bold headlines, MaterialShapes such as Cookie9Sided and Clover4Leaf for avatars and accents, ButtonGroup buttons that morph from pill to square when pressed, LoadingIndicator and wavy progress indicators, spring motion with a slight overshoot

cards.name: Shape scale
cards.desc: A fixed set of corner radii from square to fully round, and every component uses one of them: small things get small corners and big surfaces get big ones. Picking from the scale keeps corners consistent across the app.
cards.phrase: use the Material 3 shape scale only (MaterialTheme.shapes): extraSmall 4dp for menus and snackbars, small 8dp for chips, medium 12dp for cards, large 16dp for FABs and navigation drawers, extraLarge 28dp for dialogs and bottom sheets, full (CircleShape) for buttons and search bars

cards.name: Tonal elevation
cards.aka: surface tint, surface containers, elevation overlay
cards.desc: In Material 3, a surface that sits higher gets a slightly stronger tint of the primary color rather than a bigger shadow. It shows up most when you scroll and the top app bar quietly changes tone to separate from the content.
cards.phrase: tonal elevation instead of drop shadows: use the surface container roles (surface, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer, surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest) for stacked layers, and let the top app bar switch to surfaceContainer when content scrolls under it (TopAppBarDefaults scrolledContainerColor)

cards.name: Type scale
cards.desc: Fifteen named text styles in five roles: Display, Headline, Title, Body and Label, each in Large, Medium and Small. You choose a role by job, not by pixel size, so text stays consistent and scales with the user's font setting.
cards.phrase: text styled only with Material 3 type roles (MaterialTheme.typography): displayLarge for hero numbers, headlineMedium for screen headings, titleLarge for app bar and section titles, bodyLarge for reading text, labelLarge for buttons; sizes in sp so they follow the system font scale

cards.name: Material Symbols
cards.desc: Google's icon set of over 3,000 glyphs in Outlined, Rounded and Sharp styles, built as a variable font so you can tune fill, weight, grade and optical size. A common convention is outlined when inactive and filled when selected.
cards.phrase: icons from Material Symbols Rounded, imported as vector drawables and shown with Icon(painterResource(...)), 24dp, weight 400; outlined (FILL 0) for unselected and filled (FILL 1) for selected navigation items

cards.name: Widgets and themed icons
cards.aka: home screen widgets, app widgets, Glance widgets, monochrome icons
cards.desc: Resizable panels of live app content on the home screen, with large rounded corners and colors taken from the wallpaper. Themed icons are the matching home screen app icons drawn as single-color glyphs on tinted circles.
cards.phrase: a home screen widget built with Jetpack Glance (GlanceAppWidget with GlanceTheme for dynamic colors): rounded corners matching system_app_widget_background_radius, resizable layouts for small and large sizes, tapping opens the matching screen; plus a monochrome layer in the adaptive launcher icon for themed icons

cards.name: Container transform
cards.aka: shared element transition, hero transition, shared bounds
cards.desc: Tapping a card or FAB makes that container grow smoothly into the next screen, keeping its edges continuous, so you see the item become its own detail page instead of a new screen sliding in. Back shrinks it to where it came from.
cards.phrase: a container transform from list card to detail screen using Compose SharedTransitionLayout with Modifier.sharedBounds on the card and the detail container, sharedElement on the image, corner radius animating from 12dp to 0, and the reverse on back

cards.name: Smart Stack widgets
cards.aka: widget stack, watchOS widgets, relevant widgets
cards.desc: Turning the Digital Crown from the watch face scrolls up a stack of widget cards, with the most relevant one for this moment on top. Each card shows one live value, like the weather, a timer or the next meeting, and tapping it opens the app.
cards.phrase: a watchOS Smart Stack widget (WidgetKit, .accessoryRectangular) showing one glanceable value in the app's color, with relevance (RelevanceConfiguration in watchOS 26, or RelevantIntent) so it rises to the top of the stack when timely; tapping opens the app

cards.name: Complications
cards.aka: watch face complications, accessory widgets, ClockKit (legacy)
cards.desc: Tiny pieces of app data that live right on the watch face, in fixed shapes: a curved corner gauge, a small circle, a rectangle, or a single line of text. They update quietly through the day and open the app when tapped.
cards.phrase: watch face complications built with WidgetKit accessory families (.accessoryCircular, .accessoryCorner, .accessoryRectangular, .accessoryInline), using Gauge and .widgetLabel, and rendering well in the tinted watch face mode (widgetRenderingMode .accented)

cards.name: Vertical paging with the Digital Crown
cards.desc: Screens stack vertically, and turning the Digital Crown or swiping moves one full page at a time, with a small page indicator by the crown. Each page shows one idea, and the first page holds the most important thing.
cards.phrase: a vertically paged layout (TabView with .tabViewStyle(.verticalPage)) that the Digital Crown moves page by page, one full-screen view per page with a containerBackground color, and .digitalCrownRotation for any value the crown should adjust directly

cards.name: Glanceable list and detail
cards.aka: watchOS list, NavigationStack on watch, primary action button
cards.desc: A short list of big rounded rows, each with a title and one line of detail, that pushes to a detail screen. The detail screen leads with its one main action as a large full-width button, which double tap on newer watches can press for you.
cards.phrase: a watchOS NavigationStack with a List of large rows (title plus one detail line) that pushes a detail screen whose main action is a big full-width button (.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)) that also responds to double tap (.handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction)), with secondary actions in the toolbar

cards.name: Short look and long look notifications
cards.aka: watchOS notifications, short look, long look
cards.desc: A notification first appears as a short look: just the app icon, a title and the app name, readable in a glance. If the wrist stays raised, it becomes a long look with the full message, any image, and big action buttons.
cards.phrase: watchOS notifications: a short look with the app icon, title and app name, and a long look (default, or a custom SwiftUI interface via WKUserNotificationHostingController) with the full message, an optional image, and a few action buttons from the notification category

cards.name: Edge-hugging button
cards.desc: The main action on a Wear OS screen sits at the very bottom in a button with a flat top and a bottom that follows the round edge of the display, so it uses the space a rectangle would waste. There is one per screen.
cards.phrase: a Wear OS Material 3 EdgeButton for the main action, placed in the edgeButton slot of ScreenScaffold below a TransformingLazyColumn so it hugs the bottom bezel and works with the list scroll; EdgeButtonSize.Medium with a short label or a single icon, primary color

cards.name: Curved, transforming list
cards.aka: scaling list, round-screen list, curved list
cards.desc: A vertical list where items shrink, fade and morph as they move toward the top and bottom of the round screen, so the item in the middle is always the largest and easiest to read. A scroll indicator curves along the right edge, and the crown scrolls it.
