cards.phrase: in harmonic minor, dark and exotic

cards.name: Major pentatonic
cards.desc: Five notes with no half steps, so nothing clashes. Folk melodies, country licks, "Amazing Grace", "My Girl". Instantly sweet and open.
cards.phrase: a simple major pentatonic melody, open and folk-like

cards.name: Minor pentatonic
cards.desc: Five notes that underlie blues, rock riffs and countless folk tunes worldwide. Earthy and strong.
cards.phrase: riffs built on the minor pentatonic scale

cards.name: Blues scale
cards.desc: Minor pentatonic plus the flat fifth "blue note" that lives between the cracks. Bent, crying, gritty.
cards.phrase: bluesy melodies with bent blue notes

cards.name: I–IV–V
cards.aka: three-chord song, three chords and the truth
cards.desc: The three most important chords in a key. Folk, country, blues, early rock'n'roll, gospel: thousands of songs use nothing else.
cards.phrase: a simple I–IV–V three-chord progression

cards.name: I–V–vi–IV
cards.desc: The most-used progression in modern pop, uplifting with a touch of wistfulness from the minor vi.
cards.phrase: an uplifting I–V–vi–IV pop progression

cards.name: I–vi–IV–V
cards.desc: The doo-wop progression: sweet, nostalgic, a little innocent. "Stand by Me", "Earth Angel", and every 50s prom slow dance.
cards.phrase: nostalgic 1950s I–vi–IV–V changes

cards.name: ii–V–I
cards.desc: The basic move of jazz harmony: a minor seventh, a dominant seventh, then home. Smooth and sophisticated.
cards.phrase: jazzy ii–V–I changes with seventh chords

cards.name: 12-bar blues
cards.desc: Twelve bars of I, IV and V in a fixed order (I I I I / IV IV I I / V IV I V). The skeleton of blues, rock'n'roll and rockabilly.
cards.phrase: a 12-bar blues progression with dominant sevenths

cards.name: Andalusian cadence
cards.desc: Four chords stepping down to a major V: dramatic, Spanish, fatalistic. Flamenco, "Hit the Road Jack", "Walk Don't Run", spaghetti westerns.
cards.phrase: a dramatic descending Andalusian cadence, i–♭VII–♭VI–V

cards.name: i–♭VI–♭III–♭VII
cards.desc: A minor loop that keeps lifting without resolving: cinematic, yearning, heroic in a sad way. Trailer music and arena ballads.
cards.phrase: a yearning cinematic minor loop, i–♭VI–♭III–♭VII

cards.name: I–♭VII–IV
cards.desc: A major chord, then the chord a whole step below, then the IV. Swaggering, open, Americana. "Sweet Home Alabama", "Gloria", "Hey Jude" outro.
cards.phrase: a swaggering I–♭VII–IV vamp

cards.name: Plagal cadence
cards.desc: Ending by moving from IV straight home to I, as in the "A-men" at the end of a hymn. Gentle, warm, reverent.
cards.phrase: ends on a warm IV–I "amen" cadence

cards.name: Circle of fifths
cards.desc: Chords that each lean to the next a fifth down, usually as dominant sevenths. Old-timey and jaunty: ragtime, Western swing, "Salty Dog", "Alice's Restaurant".
cards.phrase: jaunty old-timey ragtime changes moving around the circle of fifths

cards.name: vi–IV–I–V
cards.aka: sensitive female chord progression, minor-start axis
cards.desc: The axis progression started on its minor chord, so it leans sad and searching instead of triumphant.
cards.phrase: a wistful vi–IV–I–V progression

cards.name: I–III–IV–iv
cards.desc: A major chord, a surprising major III, then IV turning minor. Bittersweet and aching; the minor iv is the gut punch.
cards.phrase: a bittersweet I–III–IV–iv progression ending on the aching minor four

cards.name: Suspended chords
cards.desc: Chords with the third replaced by a second or fourth, so they sound open and unresolved, as if waiting. Jangle-pop and folk players love them.
cards.phrase: open suspended chords that hang unresolved

cards.name: Major seventh
cards.desc: A major chord plus the note a half step below the octave: soft, dreamy, wistful, a little sophisticated. Bossa, yacht rock, city pop, lo-fi.
cards.phrase: dreamy major-seventh chords

cards.name: Extended jazz chords
cards.desc: Chords stacked past the seventh, so each one is rich and blurry rather than plain. Neo-soul, jazz, lo-fi and sophisticated pop.
cards.phrase: lush extended chords, minor ninths and thirteenths

cards.name: Minor four
cards.desc: In a major key, turning the IV chord minor for a moment. One of the most reliably heartbreaking moves in pop and hymns.
cards.phrase: a heartbreaking turn to the minor four chord

cards.name: Drone & pedal tone
cards.desc: One note held or repeated under changing harmony. Ancient and hypnotic: bagpipes, dulcimers, Indian music, psych folk and post-rock builds.
cards.phrase: melodies moving over a constant low drone

cards.name: Truck-driver key change
cards.desc: Lifting the whole song up a half or whole step for the last chorus, like a truck shifting gears. Pure uplift; cheesy if you're not careful.
cards.phrase: a key change up a whole step into the final chorus

cards.name: Open tunings
cards.desc: Retuning the guitar so the open strings form a chord, which gives huge droning resonance and easy slide playing. Celtic, Delta blues, Joni Mitchell, Keith Richards.
cards.phrase: acoustic guitar in an open tuning, ringing drone strings

cards.name: Hook
cards.desc: A short, catchy phrase (sung, played or produced) that the whole song is built to deliver. Usually short, repeated, and placed in the chorus or intro.
cards.phrase: a short, instantly memorable hook repeated in the chorus

cards.name: Riff
cards.desc: A repeated instrumental figure, usually low and rhythmic, that a song is built on. Rock, blues, funk and surf all run on riffs.
cards.phrase: built on a repeating low guitar riff

cards.name: Ostinato
cards.desc: A short pattern repeated persistently while other things change around it. Film scores, minimalism and trailer music use it to build tension.
cards.phrase: a persistent string ostinato that builds tension

cards.name: Arpeggio
cards.desc: Playing the notes of a chord one after another instead of together. Fingerpicked guitar, harp, synth arps: motion without strumming.
cards.phrase: gently arpeggiated chords

cards.name: Countermelody
cards.desc: A second melody played against the main one, often answering in the gaps. Strings or horns weaving around a vocal.
cards.phrase: a countermelody on strings weaving around the vocal

cards.name: Harmony in thirds
cards.desc: A second voice or instrument following the melody three notes above or below: sweet, close and very Southern. Twin fiddles, Everly-style vocals, mariachi trumpets.
cards.phrase: melody doubled in sweet parallel thirds

cards.name: Unison & octaves
cards.desc: Several instruments playing the same line together (or an octave apart) for weight. Fiddle and banjo in old-time music; strings in octaves at a film climax.
cards.phrase: fiddle and banjo playing the tune in unison

cards.name: Call and response
cards.desc: One voice or instrument plays a phrase and another answers. From work songs, gospel and the blues (voice then guitar) to sea shanties.
cards.phrase: call and response between the lead and the band

cards.name: Intro
cards.desc: Sets the mood before the voice arrives, often a stripped-down version of the main riff or chords. Describe it: "[Intro: solo fingerpicked guitar]".
cards.phrase: a short instrumental intro that sets the mood before the vocal enters

cards.name: Verse
cards.desc: Tells the story. Same melody each time, new words each time, usually lower in energy and range than the chorus.
cards.phrase: verses that tell the story in a lower, conversational register

cards.name: Pre-chorus
cards.desc: A short section that builds tension between verse and chorus: rising melody, new chords, drums building.
cards.phrase: a pre-chorus that climbs and builds tension into the chorus

cards.name: Chorus
cards.desc: The emotional and melodic peak, with the same words every time and usually the title. Biggest energy, highest notes.
cards.phrase: a big, singable chorus that repeats the title

cards.name: Post-chorus
cards.desc: A short extra hook right after the chorus, often wordless ("oh-oh-oh") or a repeated phrase, to keep the energy up.
cards.phrase: a chanted wordless post-chorus right after each chorus

cards.name: Bridge
cards.desc: A contrasting section, usually once, two-thirds of the way in: new chords, new angle, before the last chorus lands harder.
cards.phrase: a contrasting bridge with new chords before the final chorus

cards.name: Instrumental break
cards.desc: A section with no vocal where an instrument takes the lead. Name it: "[Instrumental: pedal steel solo]", "[Fiddle break]".
cards.phrase: an instrumental break where the pedal steel takes a solo

cards.name: Breakdown
cards.desc: Most of the band drops out, leaving one instrument, the voice, or a beat. Creates intimacy or tension before the big return.
cards.phrase: a breakdown where everything drops out except voice and one guitar

cards.name: Build & drop
cards.desc: Dance music's version of a chorus: tension rises (snare rolls, filter sweeps, risers) then releases into the full beat. Name both parts.
cards.phrase: a build-up with a snare roll and rising filter, then a drop into the full beat

cards.name: Outro
cards.desc: How the song leaves: a repeated chorus line, the intro riff again, a slow-down or a solo instrument alone. Say which.
cards.phrase: an outro that returns to the opening guitar and slows to a stop

cards.name: Verse–chorus
cards.desc: Verses alternate with a repeating chorus, usually with a bridge before the last chorus. The default for pop, rock and country since the 1960s.
cards.phrase: classic verse–chorus form with a bridge before the last chorus

cards.name: AABA
cards.desc: Four 8-bar sections: a main melody twice, a contrasting bridge, then the main melody again. Jazz standards, Beatles ballads, classic Hollywood songs.
cards.phrase: 32-bar AABA form: main melody twice, a contrasting bridge, then the main melody again

cards.name: Strophic ballad
cards.desc: The same melody repeated for every verse, with no chorus, maybe a short refrain line at the end of each. Story ballads, murder ballads, hymns, Dylan's long songs.
cards.phrase: a strophic folk ballad: many verses on one melody, no chorus, each verse ending on a short refrain line

cards.name: 12-bar blues form
cards.desc: Each verse is twelve bars with a line sung, repeated, then answered: "I woke up this morning... (repeat)... and my baby was gone."
cards.phrase: twelve-bar blues verses with an AAB lyric: a line sung twice, then answered

cards.name: Through-composed
cards.desc: Each section is new; nothing repeats. Art songs, film cues, prog epics and multi-part folk suites.
cards.phrase: through-composed: a sequence of distinct sections with no repeating chorus

cards.name: Loop-based
cards.desc: One short progression loops the whole way, with sections made by adding and removing layers. Hip-hop, house, afrobeat, krautrock.
cards.phrase: built on a single repeating loop, with sections made by adding and removing layers

cards.name: Cold open
cards.desc: The song begins with the voice (or the chorus) immediately, no instrumental lead-in. Grabs attention in the first second.
cards.phrase: starts cold on the vocal with no intro

cards.name: Fade-out
cards.desc: The band keeps playing the last chorus or vamp while the volume slowly drops to silence, as if it goes on forever somewhere.
cards.phrase: ends on a repeating chorus that slowly fades out

cards.name: Cold ending
cards.desc: Everyone stops together on one hit. Tight and punchy; the opposite of a fade.
cards.phrase: ends abruptly with the whole band stopping on one hit

cards.name: False ending
cards.desc: The song seems to end, a beat or two of silence, then it crashes back in for one more chorus.
cards.phrase: a false ending: silence for two bars, then the band crashes back in for one last chorus

cards.name: A cappella break
cards.desc: Instruments drop away and the voices sing alone, usually for a final chorus before the band slams back in.
cards.phrase: the band drops out for an a cappella chorus, then slams back in

cards.name: Spoken-word section
cards.desc: A passage spoken instead of sung, often over a quiet bed. Old country records, 60s girl groups and modern folk storytelling all use it.
cards.phrase: a quiet spoken-word section over a soft instrumental bed

cards.name: Quiet–loud dynamics
cards.desc: Hushed verses and explosive choruses, the contrast doing the emotional work. Pixies, Nirvana, post-rock, indie folk anthems.
cards.phrase: hushed whispered verses that explode into loud choruses

cards.name: Tag ending
cards.desc: Repeating the last line of the chorus two or three times to end, often slowing down on the final one. Country and gospel love it.
cards.phrase: ends by repeating the final chorus line three times, slowing on the last

cards.name: Final chorus lift
cards.desc: The last chorus gets more: a key change, a gospel choir, double-time drums or every instrument at once. Say which.
cards.phrase: the final chorus lifts with a full choir and double-time drums

cards.name: Breathy
cards.desc: Lots of air around the note, close to the mic. Intimate, vulnerable, sensual. Dream pop, bedroom pop and bossa.
cards.phrase: a soft breathy vocal close to the mic

cards.name: Deep baritone
cards.desc: A low, resonant voice that sounds steady and grave. Cowboy balladeers, crooners, Johnny Cash and Matt Berninger.
cards.phrase: a deep resonant baritone

cards.name: Falsetto & head voice
cards.desc: A light, high voice above the normal chest range: fragile, longing, ghostly. Bon Iver, Bee Gees, Jeff Buckley, Fleet Foxes harmonies.
cards.phrase: a fragile soaring falsetto

cards.name: Raspy & gravelly
cards.desc: A rough, cracked texture from strain, age or whiskey. Instantly worn and honest. Tom Waits at the far end, Chris Stapleton in the middle.
cards.phrase: a raspy gravelly worn-in voice

cards.name: Country twang
cards.desc: Bright nasal resonance and Southern vowels, with little catches and breaks. The voice of honky-tonk and classic country.
cards.phrase: a bright twangy country vocal with Southern vowels

cards.name: Pure & clear
cards.desc: A clean, bell-like voice with little vibrato or grit. Traditional folk singers, choirboys, early music.
cards.phrase: a pure clear bell-like vocal with little vibrato

cards.name: Smoky contralto
cards.desc: A low, dark, velvety voice with weight and mystery. Torch songs, noir jazz, fado and dark folk.
cards.phrase: a smoky velvety contralto

cards.name: Belting
cards.desc: Chest voice pushed loud and high, the big final-chorus voice of gospel, soul and power ballads.
cards.phrase: a powerful belted vocal on the final chorus

cards.name: High lonesome
cards.desc: A piercing, strained high tenor with hard vowels, sitting above the melody. Bill Monroe's sound; "lonesome" is the point.
cards.phrase: a piercing high lonesome bluegrass tenor

cards.name: Yodel
cards.desc: Flipping rapidly between chest voice and falsetto. Swiss alpine, Jimmie Rodgers' blue yodel and singing-cowboy songs.
cards.phrase: a cowboy yodel flipping between chest voice and falsetto

cards.name: Melisma
cards.desc: Several notes sung on one syllable, sliding through runs. Gospel, R&B and pop divas; also Middle Eastern and Irish sean-nós singing.
cards.phrase: soulful melismatic runs on the held words

cards.name: Straight tone
cards.desc: Notes held perfectly still, without vibrato. Sounds innocent, ancient or cold. Early music, folk, indie and Nordic singers.
cards.phrase: held notes sung with a still straight tone and no vibrato

cards.name: Wide vibrato
cards.desc: A pronounced, slow wobble on held notes. Old-time crooners, Roy Orbison, opera and vintage French chanson.
cards.phrase: a dramatic wide vibrato on held notes

cards.name: Talk-singing
cards.desc: Somewhere between speaking and singing, with loose pitch and conversational rhythm. Lou Reed, Johnny Cash late, Bob Dylan, Kurt Vile.
cards.phrase: a half-spoken talk-sung delivery, loose and conversational

cards.name: Whispered
cards.desc: Almost no voiced tone, just breath and consonants. Unsettling or very intimate; use for a line, not a whole song.
cards.phrase: a hushed, nearly whispered vocal

cards.name: Scat
cards.desc: Improvised nonsense syllables sung like a horn solo. Jazz singers' instrument.
cards.phrase: playful improvised jazz scat singing

cards.name: Sibling harmony
cards.desc: Two voices, usually a third apart, so closely matched they sound like one. The Everly Brothers, the Louvin Brothers, First Aid Kit.
cards.phrase: two closely matched voices singing in tight sibling harmony

cards.name: Three-part harmony
cards.desc: Three voices stacked into full chords on the chorus. Bright and rich: Crosby, Stills & Nash; bluegrass trios; Fleet Foxes.
cards.phrase: rich stacked three-part harmonies on the chorus

cards.name: Gang vocals
cards.desc: A crowd of untrained voices singing or shouting together, a bit ragged. Indie folk choruses, shanties, punk and arena chants.
cards.phrase: ragged gang vocals shouting the chorus together

cards.name: Lead and choir
cards.desc: A solo voice calls a line and a choir answers or sustains under it. Gospel, spirituals and big soul.
cards.phrase: a lead singer answered by a full gospel choir

cards.name: Duet
cards.desc: Two lead singers trading verses and joining on the chorus, often as characters in the song.
cards.phrase: a duet: two voices trade verses and join in harmony on the chorus

cards.name: Wordless vocals
cards.desc: A voice used as an instrument, singing melody on vowels with no words. Morricone westerns, Sigur Rós, film scores.
cards.phrase: a soaring wordless vocal used like an instrument

cards.name: Distant & reverb-drenched
cards.desc: The voice placed far back in a big reverb, as if singing across a lake or a canyon. Haunting and cinematic; a signature of cosmic Americana and dream pop.
cards.phrase: a vocal placed far back in a cavernous reverb, as if sung across a lake

cards.name: Double-tracked
cards.desc: The singer records the same part twice and both are played together, slightly out of sync. Thicker and more confident; Beatles, Elliott Smith.
cards.phrase: a double-tracked vocal, two takes stacked

cards.name: Slapback vocal
cards.desc: A single quick echo (around 100 ms) right behind the voice. Instantly 1950s: Elvis at Sun, rockabilly, retro country.
cards.phrase: a vocal with 1950s slapback echo

cards.name: Old-radio vocal
cards.desc: The voice squeezed through a narrow band of frequencies, like a phone line or old radio. Used for intros, bridges and in-world broadcasts.
cards.phrase: a lo-fi vocal filtered like an old AM radio

cards.name: Hard Auto-Tune
cards.desc: Pitch correction set so fast that the voice jumps between notes like a synth. Trap, hyperpop and 2000s pop. Ask for "no autotune" when you don't want it; generators sometimes add it.
cards.phrase: a vocal with hard robotic Auto-Tune

cards.name: Vocoder
cards.desc: A voice shaping a synthesizer so the synth "speaks". Daft Punk, Kraftwerk, Boards of Canada and 80s electro.
cards.phrase: a robotic vocoder voice

cards.name: Chopped vocal samples
cards.desc: Short slices of a vocal re-pitched and played like an instrument. Future bass, house, folktronica.
cards.phrase: chopped and re-pitched vocal samples played as a melody

cards.name: 1920s–30s shellac
cards.desc: Recorded into a horn or one early microphone and cut to a 78: narrow, honky midrange, hiss and crackle, no real bass or treble.
cards.phrase: sounds like a scratchy 1920s 78 rpm record: narrow, honky midrange, surface crackle and hiss

cards.name: 1950s mono
cards.desc: A small band around a few tube microphones, recorded live to mono tape with slapback echo. Punchy, warm and immediate.
cards.phrase: 1950s mono recording: live band around a few tube mics, slapback echo, warm and punchy

cards.name: 1960s studio
cards.desc: Four-track tape, plate reverb or real echo chambers, bright midrange and hard stereo panning (drums left, vocals right) on early stereo mixes.
cards.phrase: 1960s studio sound: four-track tape, echo-chamber reverb, bright midrange, slightly lo-fi drums

cards.name: 1970s analog
cards.desc: Twenty-four-track tape, close-miked drums with dampened toms, warm saturated tape and a dry, intimate sound. Laurel Canyon, soul and Southern rock.
cards.phrase: warm 1970s analog production: dry close-miked drums, saturated tape, intimate and rich

cards.name: 1980s digital
cards.desc: Digital reverbs, drum machines, chorused everything and the famous gated-reverb snare that booms then cuts off. Big, bright, glossy.
cards.phrase: glossy 1980s production: gated-reverb snare, chorused guitars, bright digital reverb

cards.name: Home 4-track
cards.desc: Recorded at home on a cassette Portastudio: hiss, wobble, saturated tape and charming mistakes. Indie lo-fi and early bedroom recordings.
cards.phrase: lo-fi home 4-track cassette recording: tape hiss, slight wobble, intimate and unpolished

cards.name: Live in one room
cards.aka: live off the floor, one take
cards.desc: The whole band playing together in a room with the mics catching each other. Spill, room sound and real interplay.
cards.phrase: recorded live off the floor in one room, natural room sound and bleed between mics

cards.name: Modern polished
cards.desc: Pristine digital production: tight edited timing, tuned vocals, wide stereo, loud and bright master. Say this or its opposite explicitly.
cards.phrase: modern polished production: tight, wide, bright and loud

cards.name: Field recording
cards.desc: Recorded where the musician lives: a porch, a kitchen, a church, with crickets or traffic in the background. Archival folk and modern lo-fi folk.
cards.phrase: a field recording on a porch at night: crickets and room noise in the background

cards.name: Dry & close
cards.desc: No reverb at all, the source right against the mic. Intimate, confessional and very present. Modern pop vocals and 70s records use it.
cards.phrase: bone-dry and close, no reverb

cards.name: Room reverb
cards.desc: A short, natural sense of a real room around the sound. Makes things feel live and together without washing them out.
cards.phrase: a short natural room reverb

cards.name: Plate reverb
cards.desc: A vibrating steel sheet: bright, smooth and dense, with no sense of a real room. Classic on vocals and snare from the 60s on.
cards.phrase: a bright smooth plate reverb on the vocal

cards.name: Spring reverb
cards.desc: A metal spring inside a guitar amp: boingy, drippy and twangy. Surf rock, dub, Western twang and lo-fi.
cards.phrase: drippy spring reverb on the guitar

cards.name: Hall reverb
cards.desc: A long, smooth tail like a concert hall. Grand and lush on strings, piano and big ballads.
cards.phrase: a lush concert-hall reverb

cards.name: Cathedral
cards.desc: An enormous stone space where every note hangs for seconds. Sacred, haunting, distant. Choirs, organs and far-away voices.
cards.phrase: an enormous cathedral reverb where every note hangs for seconds

cards.name: Slapback echo
cards.desc: One single, short echo right after the note (about 80 to 140 ms). Rockabilly, 50s vocals and country guitar.
cards.phrase: a single short slapback echo

cards.name: Tape echo
cards.desc: Repeats that get darker, wobblier and more saturated as they fade, because each one is copied from tape. Dub, psych and dreamy guitar.
cards.phrase: warm wobbly tape echo repeats trailing off into the distance

cards.name: Ping-pong delay
cards.desc: Echoes that bounce from left speaker to right and back. Wide, playful and dizzy in headphones.
cards.phrase: echoes bouncing left and right in a ping-pong delay

cards.name: Gated reverb
cards.desc: A big reverb cut off abruptly by a noise gate, so the snare booms huge and then stops dead. The defining 80s drum sound.
cards.phrase: a huge 1980s gated-reverb snare

cards.name: Chorus
cards.desc: A slightly detuned, delayed copy mixed with the original so one instrument sounds like several. Shimmery and watery: 80s guitars, dream pop, post-punk bass.
cards.phrase: shimmering chorus on the clean guitar

cards.name: Flanger
cards.desc: A very short, sweeping delay that makes a jet-plane whoosh through the sound. Psychedelic 60s and 70s rock.
cards.phrase: a sweeping jet-plane flanger

cards.name: Phaser
cards.desc: A gentler swirl than flanging, like the sound turning slowly in space. 70s funk, outlaw-country guitar, psych keys.
cards.phrase: a slow swirling phaser

cards.name: Tremolo
cards.desc: Volume pulsing up and down rhythmically: "wah-wah-wah". Built into old amps; the throb of Western twang and swampy blues.
cards.phrase: throbbing amp tremolo pulsing in time

cards.name: Rotary speaker
cards.desc: A spinning speaker that adds both swirl and pitch wobble, fast or slow. Hammond organ's best friend, also used on guitars and vocals.
cards.phrase: swirling rotary-speaker effect

cards.name: Wow & flutter
cards.desc: Pitch drifting slowly (wow) and jittering fast (flutter), like a stretched cassette or warped record. Nostalgic and slightly seasick; lo-fi and hauntology.
cards.phrase: warped wobbly tape with wow and flutter

cards.name: Tape saturation
cards.desc: Gentle soft clipping from pushing tape or tubes: thicker, rounder, glued together. What people usually mean by "warm".
cards.phrase: warm tape saturation gluing the mix together

cards.name: Overdrive
cards.desc: An amp pushed until it breaks up: crunchy and responsive, cleaning up when played softly. Blues, classic rock, country rock.
cards.phrase: a crunchy overdriven amp

cards.name: Fuzz
cards.desc: Clipping so hard the wave turns nearly square: buzzy, woolly and thick. Garage, psych, stoner and shoegaze.
cards.phrase: thick buzzing fuzz distortion

cards.name: Bitcrush
cards.desc: Lowering the digital resolution so the sound turns crunchy and steppy. Chiptune, glitch and lo-fi beats.
cards.phrase: crunchy bitcrushed digital texture

cards.name: Wide stereo
cards.desc: Instruments spread hard left and right with space in the middle. Lush and immersive in headphones.
cards.phrase: a wide spacious stereo mix

cards.name: Mono
cards.desc: Everything from one point in the middle, as on records before about 1967. Punchy and focused, with a vintage feel.
cards.phrase: mixed in punchy vintage mono

cards.name: Vocal up front
cards.desc: The voice loud, clear and present over the band, every word audible. Country, pop and singer-songwriter records.
cards.phrase: the vocal mixed loud and up front, every word clear

cards.name: Buried vocal
cards.desc: The voice sunk into the instruments like another texture, words half-heard. Shoegaze, dream pop, early R.E.M.
cards.phrase: the vocal buried low in the mix, words half-heard

cards.name: Music from the next room
cards.desc: Highs rolled off so the music sounds like it's coming through a wall or from a party next door. A favorite film and transition trick.
cards.phrase: muffled as if heard from the next room

cards.name: Telephone EQ
cards.desc: Lows and highs both cut so only a narrow midrange remains, like a phone or transistor radio. Use on a vocal intro or a whole bridge.
cards.phrase: narrow telephone-style EQ on the intro

cards.name: Vinyl crackle
cards.desc: Surface crackle and pops from an old record laid under the music. Lo-fi hip-hop's signature and instant nostalgia.
cards.phrase: warm vinyl crackle underneath

cards.name: Sidechain pump
cards.desc: Pads and bass duck out of the way every time the kick hits, so the whole mix breathes in time. House, French touch, EDM.
cards.phrase: pads pumping with sidechain compression on every kick

cards.name: Punchy low end
cards.desc: Kick and bass compressed and shaped so they hit your chest without getting muddy. Modern rock, hip-hop and dance.
cards.phrase: a tight punchy low end that hits hard

cards.name: Wind in the pines
cards.desc: Soft rushing wind with gusts rising and falling, through trees or across open ground. Lonesome and wide.
cards.phrase: soft wind rushing through pines, gusts rising and falling

cards.name: Lake at night
cards.desc: Small waves lapping against a dock or rocks, a distant loon, deep quiet. Perfect for Lord Huron-style lakeside intros.
cards.phrase: water lapping against a wooden dock at night, a distant loon

cards.name: Summer night
cards.desc: Crickets chirping in a warm field or on a porch. Instant small-town summer.
cards.phrase: crickets chirping on a warm summer night

cards.name: Rain & distant thunder
cards.desc: Steady rain with drops on a surface, and thunder rolling far away. Cozy indoors, ominous outdoors.
cards.phrase: steady rain on a tin roof with thunder rolling in the distance

cards.name: Campfire
cards.desc: Wood crackling and popping, a low rumble of flame. Campfire songs, cabins, storytelling.
cards.phrase: a crackling campfire close by

cards.name: Ocean waves
cards.desc: Big waves rolling in and drawing back over sand, in slow cycles. Calming, vast and a little lonely.
cards.phrase: slow ocean waves rolling in and drawing back

cards.name: Loon call
cards.desc: The haunting rising wail of a loon across a still lake. Shorthand for wilderness, northern lakes and loneliness.
cards.phrase: the haunting wail of a loon echoing across a still lake

cards.name: Distant train
cards.desc: A train horn chord fading in the distance and wheels clacking on the rails. Americana's favorite sound effect.
cards.phrase: a freight train horn in the distance and wheels clacking on the rails

cards.name: Radio between stations
cards.desc: Static and squeals while a dial turns, then a song faintly emerging. A classic intro for in-world radio and found-footage feel.
cards.phrase: AM radio static as the dial turns, then a faint old song comes through

cards.name: Room tone
cards.desc: The quiet sound of an empty room: hum, air, faint traffic. Under dialogue or between songs it makes silence feel real.
cards.phrase: quiet room tone with a faint electrical hum

cards.name: Riser
cards.desc: A sound that climbs in pitch and volume to build tension toward a moment: noise sweeps, rising synths, accelerating rolls.
cards.phrase: a white-noise riser building tension into the drop

cards.name: Sub drop
cards.desc: A deep sine tone that falls in pitch, felt more than heard. Marks a downbeat or a transition with weight.
cards.phrase: a deep sub drop on the downbeat

cards.name: Impact
cards.desc: A huge layered hit (low boom, crack, reverb tail) for a cut, a title card or a punch.
cards.phrase: a huge cinematic impact with a long reverb tail

cards.name: Whoosh
cards.desc: Air rushing past from one side to the other. Transitions, fast camera moves, logos flying in.
cards.phrase: a fast whoosh passing from left to right

cards.name: Stinger
cards.desc: A short, sharp musical hit that punctuates a moment: a brass stab, a chord hit, a jump scare.
cards.phrase: a sharp orchestral stinger on the reveal

cards.name: Reverse swell
cards.desc: A sound played backwards so it swells up into the next note instead of decaying from it. Dreamy transitions and pre-chorus lifts.
cards.phrase: a reverse swell sucking into the downbeat

cards.name: Drone
cards.desc: A sustained, slowly shifting tone under a scene. Low and dark for dread, bright and airy for awe.
cards.phrase: a low dark drone slowly shifting underneath

cards.name: Shepard tone
cards.desc: Overlapping tones an octave apart that seem to rise forever without getting higher. Endless, inescapable tension; "Dunkirk".
cards.phrase: an endlessly rising Shepard tone

cards.name: Glitch
cards.desc: Sound chopped into stutters, skips and digital errors. IDM, hyperpop, tense UI and broken-machine moments.
cards.phrase: stuttering glitchy edits and buffer repeats

cards.name: Heartbeat
cards.desc: A low double thump in a steady pulse. Suspense, intimacy or a clock running out.
cards.phrase: a low heartbeat pulse under the silence

cards.name: Sine wave
cards.desc: The purest tone, a single frequency with no harmonics. Soft, round, sub bass, test tones, flutes and whistles.
cards.phrase: a pure soft sine tone

cards.name: Square wave
cards.desc: Hollow and buzzy, with only odd harmonics. Chiptune leads, clarinet-like tones, retro bass.
cards.phrase: a hollow buzzy square-wave lead

cards.name: Sawtooth wave
cards.desc: Bright and buzzy with every harmonic. The raw material of synth strings, brass, leads and supersaw pads.
cards.phrase: a bright buzzing sawtooth synth

cards.name: White, pink & brown noise
cards.desc: Random sound with different tilts: white is hissy, pink is rain, brown is a low roar like surf. The basis of wind, snares and risers.
cards.phrase: filtered noise like a distant roar

cards.name: FM bell
cards.desc: Frequency modulation makes metallic, glassy, bell-like tones. The 80s DX7 electric piano and bell presets.
cards.phrase: glassy FM synth bells

cards.name: Granular texture
cards.desc: A recording sliced into tiny grains and scattered into a shimmering cloud. Ambient, experimental and modern scores.
cards.phrase: a shimmering granular cloud made from plucked guitar

cards.name: Supersaw pad
cards.desc: Many detuned sawtooth waves stacked into one huge, shimmering chord. Trance, EDM drops and synthwave pads.
cards.phrase: a huge shimmering detuned supersaw pad

cards.name: Warm
cards.desc: More low-mids, softened highs, a little saturation. What people usually want from "analog" or "vintage".
cards.phrase: a warm rounded tone with soft highs

cards.name: Bright
cards.desc: Boosted highs and upper mids so it cuts through. Clean pop vocals, acoustic guitars, cymbals.
cards.phrase: a bright crisp sparkling tone

cards.name: Dark
cards.desc: Highs rolled right off. Moody, distant, old; also muddy if overdone.
cards.phrase: a dark muted tone with no top end

cards.name: Airy
cards.desc: Extra extreme highs (above 10 kHz) so breath and shimmer come through. Expensive-sounding vocals and acoustic guitars.
cards.phrase: an airy open top end with breath and shimmer

cards.name: Gritty
cards.desc: Distortion and noise left in on purpose. Rough edges that feel human and unpolished.
cards.phrase: a gritty raw tone with dirt left in

cards.name: Glassy
cards.desc: Clear, bright, ringing tones with pure upper harmonics: celesta, FM bells, clean chorused guitar.
cards.phrase: glassy crystalline tones

cards.name: Hollow
cards.desc: Missing some midrange so it sounds like it's inside a tube or box. Old radios, clarinets, cheap speakers.
cards.phrase: a hollow boxy tone

cards.name: Metallic
cards.desc: Inharmonic ringing overtones like struck metal or a short comb filter. Bells, robots, industrial textures.
cards.phrase: a metallic ringing clang

cards.name: Lush
cards.desc: Layered, chorused and reverberant, filling the whole space. Strings, pads and stacked harmonies.
cards.phrase: lush layered chorus and reverb filling the space

cards.name: Thin
cards.desc: Missing the low end, so it sounds small, distant or cheap. Useful on purpose for intros, transistor radios or contrast before a big drop.
cards.phrase: a thin tinny tone with no low end
